**GenInfer prefilter v1.4: soundness repair, exact fallback stages, fast-path prevalence (2026-10-06):** the v1 three-build panel (480 workers, 15/15) used only single-predicate fixtures. An exploratory differential run then showed the v1 prefilter diverging from the historical enumerator on two-predicate, id-bearing inputs at the seed's `max_dims=2`, in 145–701 of 1,488 cases per family. The enumerator accepts per-predicate shift residuals that the affine proof does not model. v1.4 restricts the affine proof to inputs where it coincides with the enumerator. Before the enumerator it now tries two exact stages: a row-factorized search for frames with a unique pre-coordinate prefix (O(n·(2b+1)²) per row) and a correspondence-complete generator for frames without one (O(n_p³) hypotheses, each judged by the enumerator's own validator). A 37,500-case finite census, the frozen v1.2 oracle (unchanged digest), and 914/914 real or production-shaped Term-level pairs all match the enumerator exactly. Prevalence is the main limit: 0/10 production `dim_types` declarations have an identity slot, so the exact solve is reachable only from fixtures. On production-shaped inputs the gains are fast refusal (Omniglot `["cell", r, c]`: 265/300 pairs by relation count, 33/300 by correspondence; median 196 ms → 0.03 ms) and the correspondence stage on `sdloop_vision` bars (16×16: 17.8 s → 93 ms, 27.8 s → 373 ms). The correspondence stage still grows cubically: 12.6 s at 324 relations. The panel's expensive fallbacks resolve in under 1 ms at Term level (rank-deficient was 73 s). No real handwriting pair was related by a nonsingular integer map. This is a dispatch-equivalence and cost result, not natural-task learning or rung-three induction; full-seed closure and default-on remain unmeasured. See [results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_PREFILTER_PREVALENCE_V1_4_RESULTS_20261006.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_PREFILTER_PREVALENCE_V1_4_PREREG_20261006.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_PREFILTER_PREVALENCE_V1_4B_AMENDMENT_20261006.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/geninfer_prefilter_prevalence_v1_4b_analysis_20261006.json).

**Recursive mint closure current-source replay (2026-09-26):** a provenance-only v1.1 rerun preserves the 18-cell `add_node`/keyed-dedup fixture comparison at sizes 1/2/4, three repeats, and a 32-step cap. The existing restricted termination theorem and parser crosswalk establish a finite-key finite-universe sublanguage, but no mandatory engine gate enforces it. The current-source audit now covers direct rule authoring, checkpoint import, graph-rule compilation, self-minted rules, and rule revision; the next gate is a fail-closed admission design and production-route validation, not another restatement of the proof ([results](SUBSTRATE_MINT_TERMINATION_ENVELOPE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260926.md), [theorem](SUBSTRATE_FINITE_KEY_CLOSURE_TERMINATION_20260926.md), [parser crosswalk](SUBSTRATE_FINITE_KEY_RUNTIME_PARSER_CROSSWALK_20260926.md), [current-source admission audit](SUBSTRATE_FINITE_KEY_CLOSURE_FRAGMENT_SOURCE_AUDIT_V1_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_mint_termination_envelope_v1_1.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_mint_termination_envelope_v1_1_20260926.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_mint_termination_envelope_v1_1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**Finite-key closure fragment source audit (2026-09-28):** source review formalizes the current checker's narrow finite-universe argument: fixed literal `AddNodeIfAbsent` signatures plus empty-attribute `AddEdge` effects yield at most `S + T(N₀+S)² − M₀` progressing graph mutations. With fixed rule and pattern sizes this is polynomial data complexity, but it is not weak acyclicity and does not bound rule families whose patterns grow with input. The native loader accepts computed effect Terms, general `where` Terms, and a wider effect language. A three-worker runtime probe confirms that direct authoring, checkpoint import, rule-patch revision, and explicit graph-rule self-mint all accept an out-of-fragment fresh-mint rule. Arbitrary production termination remains unproved. The next gate is designing and validating fail-closed admission across those routes, or a separately specified weak-acyclicity fragment ([source audit](SUBSTRATE_FINITE_KEY_CLOSURE_FRAGMENT_SOURCE_AUDIT_V1_20260928.md), [runtime results](SUBSTRATE_MINT_FRAGMENT_ADMISSION_PATH_PROBE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260928.md)).

# Substrate capability and tractability measurement plan

## Current programme status (2026-10-03)

The raw-residual handoff now has a bounded native-execution result. A branch-only graph rule consumed raw `actual`/`expected` fields and supplied opposite-action ontology facts, derived the existing `flip_comparison` cue in all four positive cases, and enabled held-out-correct graph composition; eight ambiguity/non-inversion controls had no false cue or proposal. The primary remained unchanged until a compact residual return in all 13 cases. This moves one mapping from Python into substrate execution, but the inference rule, action ontology, cue vocabulary, and target class were supplied by the experiment. The next rung is for the substrate to induce a reusable relation or mapping from examples without that rule/ontology being hand-authored per experiment; evaluate the induced rule on a separately held-out relation family and include false-mint and abstention controls ([protocol](RESIDUAL_TO_COMPOSER_NATIVE_CUE_V1_PREREG_20261003.md), [results](RESIDUAL_TO_COMPOSER_NATIVE_CUE_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md)).

The latest A8 bridge now supplies prospective held-out evidence for a limited responsibility transfer. Given an explicit residual cue and the existing EditOp vocabulary, graph-resident composition generated a rule that solved both withheld navigation directions in 4/4 workers; no-cue composition abstained in 4/4. The strict preregistered identity check failed in every worker because the generated rule differed from its host reference in metadata beyond the permitted generated-name normalization. Graph-route median cost (133.20 ms including shared task setup) also exceeded the host default-order route (77.51 ms). This is a useful capability boundary: substrate-owned composition and evaluation can work when task diagnosis and operator vocabulary are supplied, but the current path neither matches the reference representation exactly nor beats its host baseline. Next measure raw residual-to-cue generation and metadata normalization as separate, explicit stages before treating this route as general self-improvement ([v1.3 results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_A8_PROPOSAL_BRIDGE_V1_3_RESULTS_20261003.md)).

**Fresh-signature relation transfer (2026-10-03):** The source-locked full-seed GenInfer panel acquired `[2,1,1,1]` before heldout insertion and used that exact generator on a distinct heldout signature in 3/3 repeats. The strict 3-map gate failed: `[1,0,1,1]` appeared only after heldout insertion, and `[1,1,0,1]` used an existing `cycle4` route with GenInfer disabled as well as enabled. Identity controls added no generator; corrupted-heldout exact matches were 0/9. This is measured bounded induction and transfer for one map, not general self-improvement. Next prospectively select maps without existing-route aliases, lock their absence before training, and require exact generator acquisition and attributed heldout reuse before scoring transfer ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_RELATION_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_RELATION_TRANSFER_V1_PREREG_20261003.md)).

**Prospective relation transfer v2 (2026-10-03):** A disclosed task-development pilot identified three maps that the full-seed path acquires rather than explaining through existing routes. The preregistered 30-case capture passes all gates: exact generator acquisition and distinct-signature reuse are 9/9; disabled acquisition, identity minting, and corrupted exact matches are 0/9, 0/3, and 0/9. Median training closure is 9.84 ms; held-out closure is 0.74 ms. This upgrades the evidence from one map to three maps in one bounded synthetic operator family. Next measure search scaling against relation count and the data-derived coefficient bound, including candidate checks, wall/CPU time, peak memory, and false acceptance under structured nulls. Then repeat transfer on a structurally distinct task family to test whether learning composes beyond this authored geometric path ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_RELATION_TRANSFER_V2_RESULTS_20261003.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_RELATION_TRANSFER_V2_PREREG_20261003.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_relation_transfer_v2_analysis_20261003.json)).

**Full-seed relation-count × coefficient-bound scaling (2026-10-03):** The 84-worker source-locked panel passes. Positive acquisition/transfer is 60/60; disabled and predicate-corrupt acquisition are each 0/12. Coordinate-corrupt heldouts are recognized through the acquired generator plus an explicit local shift in 60/60 cases, with exact matrix-only match 0/60. Across N=4–64 and B=3–6, median closure cost follows the expected `N×(2B+1)^4` workload approximately, reaching 1.78 s at N=64/B=6; reuse on that cell is 4.67 ms. HWM deltas are coarse and measured above an already booted process baseline. This closes the single-frame, low-dimensional scaling gate for one family; next test multiple eligible frames/codebook parts, broader structured nulls, actual peak memory, and a structurally distinct task family ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_FULLSEED_SCALING_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_FULLSEED_SCALING_V1_PREREG_20261003.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_fullseed_scaling_v1_analysis_20261003.json)).

**Shared versus frame-isolated codebook cost (2026-10-03):** The paired v1.1 comparison passes for 93/93 frame outputs. At K=16, one shared GenInfer closure is 1.053 s versus 164 ms summed for isolated single-part closures (6.42×); the non-mutating diagnostic sees 16× more candidate checks in shared scope. This is a measured locality opportunity, not a production speedup: current GenInfer scans all eligible shape parts and ignores `frame_id`; isolated execution uses independent graphs and excludes boot, scope selection, scheduling, and data movement. Next add an explicit, provenance-bearing codebook scope and compare exact outcomes plus complete selection/maintenance/closure cost against the shared baseline. Also measure when scoping is wrong or unavailable, so no benefit is assumed without reliable boundaries ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_FRAME_ISOLATION_COMPARISON_V1_1_RESULTS_20261003.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_FRAME_ISOLATION_COMPARISON_V1_1_PREREG_20261003.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/geninfer_frame_isolation_v1_1_analysis_20261003.json)).

The thought-experiment path now has a measured candidate-repair lifecycle in addition to the existing snapshot, scoring, and receipt work. A hand-authored conflict guard ran only in a CoW branch, abstained on contradictory accepted claims, preserved the unique-claim and mismatch controls, and returned its conflict residual to primary in all six conflict trials; branch rules and graph state remained isolated until that explicit return. This is a branch-execution/adoption-mechanism result, not substrate-led rule discovery: the rule itself was supplied by the experiment author. The next capability gate is to measure generation, held-out probe selection, branch evaluation, and adoption as separate stages, and then establish whether the substrate can generate and select repairs without LLM-authored candidates ([protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_POLAR_CONFLICT_GUARD_V1_PROTOCOL_20261003.md), [results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_POLAR_CONFLICT_GUARD_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md)).

The programme has moved beyond inventory into source-locked engine and learning measurements. The thoughtexperiment substrate can isolate candidate branches, compare controlled outcomes, return residual receipts, and guard adoption against stale revisions; measured branch performance depends on backend, topology, and exposed boundary, and the predeclared 10× marginal-evaluation target is still unmet. On the learning side, code-write acquisition transfers across the measured parity/clamp cases, while the finite-probe coverage study shows that an accepted receipt only supports adequacy over its caller-declared probes: a narrow aliasing domain accepted a false candidate in all three repetitions, and a distinguishing domain rejected it in all three ([thoughtexperiment scale/objective evidence](#thoughtexperiment-harness-isolated-rust-cow-experiments), [code-write transfer and coverage results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROBE_COVERAGE_AB_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md)).

This is evidence for a useful isolated experimentation and held-structure application regime, not for autonomous general self-improvement. Candidate proposal quality, probe-domain adequacy, deployment-grade provider trust, and broad transfer remain material gaps. Across two authored Term families, maximum-entropy challenger selection reduced broad-domain one-label false acceptance from 54/60 and 56/60 to 0/60, used one label to reject each wrong candidate, and preserved all 30/30 correct adoptions per family. The new `domains/adequacy_probe_selection.py` helper composes with provenance-bound requests/receipts and the real `teach()` adoption boundary. A matched full-seed spoof study showed caller-asserted provider IDs do not authenticate labels. An optional HMAC wrapper blocks unsigned, tampered, replayed, unknown-provider, and empty-probe evidence before `teach()`. The source-locked live-route adversarial panel demonstrates the remaining epistemic gap: a trusted provider’s HMAC-valid, candidate-consistent but false identity label was adopted in 3/3 runs and failed 9/9 held-out square cases, while the truthful condition passed 9/9 ([trusted-signer live-route results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_TRUSTED_SIGNER_LIVE_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_trusted_signer_live_v1_analysis_20261002.json)). The live `WorldAdapter` now has an opt-in strict code-example route: provider keys are copied into adapter-owned configuration at construction and evidence is supplied separately to `converse`; missing evidence refuses before any graph mutation. The strict policy survives checkpoint save/load, while shared secrets are never serialized; if the trusted registry is not reinjected on load, the route fails closed. A fresh-process adoption-surface panel adopted exactly one typed code-write shape in 3/3 valid-signature workers, refused all 3/3 tampered-signature cases despite internally accepted receipts, refused 3/3 direct receipt-only calls on strict adapters, and refused all 6/6 published-curriculum function attempts without evidence; the current-source analyzer passes 9/9 checks ([adoption-surface v1.2 results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_ADOPTION_SURFACE_V1_2_RESULTS_20261002.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_adoption_surface_v1_2_analysis_20261002.json)). The route gate is opt-in: non-strict agents and lower-level direct `teach()` calls remain outside it; process-local key configuration is not key isolation. The preregistered agreement/domain panel shows why both controls are needed: conflicting authenticated providers are rejected, but two distinct IDs sharing the same false answer still cause adoption in 3/3 runs; two truthful providers on an alias-only domain also cause adoption in 3/3 and fail all nine held-outs ([results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROVIDER_AGREEMENT_AND_DOMAIN_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_provider_agreement_domain_v1_analysis_20261002.json)). An opt-in selected-probe adoption gate now recomputes the challenger selector and refuses the tested zero-entropy alias domain: 0/3 alias candidates were adopted despite accepted receipts, while the honest square control adopted and passed 9/9 held-outs. It still permits a trusted false label when that label matches the candidate at the selected probe (3/3 false adoptions, 0/9 held-out), and caller-supplied challenger/domain completeness remains unverified ([selected-probe adoption results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_SELECTED_PROBE_ADOPTION_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_selected_probe_adoption_v1_analysis_20261002.json)). Next test the gate on independently authored families and realistic domain distributions; separately measure provider correlation and key ownership before any quorum claim. Keep operating-cost claims separate from the cost and capability of acquiring new structure. Keep operating-cost claims separate from the cost and capability of acquiring new structure ([probe-selection results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROBE_SELECTION_V1_2_RESULTS_20261002.md), [early-stop transfer results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_EARLY_STOP_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [receipt/adoption integration results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_SELECTOR_RECEIPT_ADOPTION_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [provider spoof results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROVIDER_SPOOF_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [provider-auth v1.1 results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROVIDER_AUTH_V1_1_RESULTS_20261002.md)).

The latest thoughtexperiment gate adds graph-resident evidence aggregation and candidate choice through [`select_candidate_from_graph_evidence`](../../../domains/contract_query.py). After the direction-free composer abstained, the host enumerator supplied fault and two ordered swaps. In 32/32 conditions, a native Term scored per-probe candidate evidence inside a disposable snapshot branch, selected the unique forward repair after oracle release, and returned a compact residual to primary. Tie and all-wrong controls abstained; malformed evidence was rejected; candidate/evidence nodes did not leak into primary. This is a bounded substrate-owned decision over host-supplied candidates and labels, not rule invention or oracle verification. Graph evidence materialization plus Term selection averaged 0.205 ms, branch fork 0.0238 ms, and residual return 0.0150 ms, compared with about 148 ms for 100-input active query over three hypotheses; candidate enumeration remained host-side at 0.404 ms. The first v2 pilot is censored for a malformed tie control and writing evidence to primary; v3 corrects both and passes its preregistered gate. The scorer also transfers to a second, recurrence task family in a retrospective replay, but the corrected per-worker sample audit shows it does not meet the original literal sample-size claim. A fresh prospective recurrence panel uses four train and four held-out episodes per candidate and worker. The graph Term selects the unique useful rule in all four workers and the chosen rule reaches fixed point on all held-outs. Five alternatives hit the 100-call cap in all 160 of their train/held-out episodes, so the original full all-candidate closure gate fails. A paired bounded-evaluation follow-up preserves pass/fail outcomes on all 256 candidate episodes and selects the same repair in all four workers, while reducing mean panel runtime 20.6× (116.384 s to 5.643 s) and rule work 5.46× (176,288 to 32,288 units) through a 200-call stage budget and early rejection. This is a harness-level result on one fixture; it does not change general engine closure semantics or prove the capped alternatives nonterminating. Corrected baseline episode means are 459 ms training and 467 ms held-out (the earlier 115–117 ms estimate was low by four); candidate enumeration averages about 109 ms per worker. The preregistered budget-calibration replication now passes its 12/12 analysis checks: at arities 2/4/8 and budgets 200/400/800, graph-Term choice is stable, all selected repairs succeed on held-outs, candidate pass/fail parity is exact, and no reference-resolved proposal is falsely rejected. Pooled held-out episode medians improve 18.3×/5.7×/1.5× at budgets 200/400/800 for arity 2; the selected repair itself shows no speedup, while work rises 4/8/16 units with arity. The repeated poor proposals all exhaust at stage one, so this confirms harness-level savings on one proposal distribution, not general tractability. Next test candidate diversity and false-rejection behavior on a distinct rule family and non-synthetic task family ([results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_RECURRENCE_BUDGET_CALIBRATION_V1_1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_RECURRENCE_BUDGET_CALIBRATION_V1_1_PREREG_20261002.md)). Supporting evidence: [attribute-site v3 results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_ATTRIBUTE_SITE_GRAPH_SELECTION_V3_RESULTS_20261002.md), [early-rejection results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_RECURRENCE_EARLY_REJECTION_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [early-rejection protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_RECURRENCE_EARLY_REJECTION_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [recurrence v1.1 results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_RECURRENCE_GRAPH_SELECTION_V1_1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [analysis amendment](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_RECURRENCE_EARLY_REJECTION_V1_AMENDMENT_20261002.md), [retrospective sample amendment](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_RECURRENCE_GRAPH_SELECTION_RETRO_V1_AMENDMENT_20261002.md), [corrected analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_recurrence_graph_selection_v1_3_analysis_20261002.json)).

## Real-data thoughtexperiment matcher transfer: Omniglot v1.1 (2026-10-02)

The graph Term uniquely selects PointSetDist on background-alphabet training episodes in all three workers, then scores 62.5%, 66.8%, and 60.4% on alphabet-disjoint evaluation episodes, with zero regret to the held-out hindsight-best of three supplied matchers. The independent 12-check analysis verifies full dataset/source/native hashes, sealed orders, matched episodes, branch-local evidence, and compact residual return. PointSetDist aggregates to 63.2% over 20 evaluation alphabet clusters (descriptive cluster-bootstrap 95% interval 58.0–68.6%; chance 5%). This demonstrates transfer of substrate-owned ranking over provided matchers on real handwritten glyphs, not autonomous matcher invention or broad vision. Branch fork median is 8.5 µs; graph evidence scoring is 25.1 ms over 800 training queries. The frozen analyzer had a held-out-order schema bug; the corrected post-capture v1.2 analysis and amendment are disclosed. The earlier v1 pilot preloaded evaluation features and omitted fork timing and is not the confirmatory result ([v1.1 results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_OMNIGLOT_MATCHER_SELECTION_V1_1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_OMNIGLOT_MATCHER_SELECTION_V1_1_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_omniglot_matcher_selection_v1_1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_omniglot_matcher_selection_v1_2_analysis_20261002.json)).

## Real-data thoughtexperiment matcher transfer: FSDD v1.2 (2026-10-02)

On six-speaker Free Spoken Digit data, the substrate selected ordered DTW in two speaker-disjoint folds and abstained on an exact DTW/PointSetDist training tie in the third. Ordered DTW transferred to fresh held-out recordings at 43.0% and 64.5% against 10% chance, and matched the held-out hindsight-best in both selected folds. Across all three folds, ordered DTW scored 51.2%, PointSetDist 38.7%, and XCorrPeak 35.8%. The corrected analysis passes 9/12 checks; the three failed end-to-end gates reflect abstention in one fold, not data-integrity failures. This is selection among three harness-supplied Terms, not matcher invention or general speech understanding. Earlier captures are retained as disclosed invalid pilots: v1 omitted the gallery while scoring held-outs, and v1.1 failed before reading held-out audio. The v1.2 capture uses fresh held-out recording indices 10–19 with a frozen training gallery. See [results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_FSDD_MATCHER_SELECTION_V1_2_RESULTS_20261002.md), [preregistration](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_FSDD_MATCHER_SELECTION_V1_2_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_fsdd_matcher_selection_v1_2.py), [orders](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_fsdd_matcher_selection_v1_2_orders_20261002.json), [scores](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_fsdd_matcher_selection_v1_2_scores_20261002.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_fsdd_matcher_selection_v1_3_analysis_20261002.json).

## Thoughtexperiment harness: isolated Rust CoW experiments

The target loop is substrate-led improvement from explicit residual evidence, not a claim that the current system already improves itself generally. The LLM currently supplies much of the meta-level direction; the gradual handoff requires the substrate to consume experiment outcomes and take over bounded decisions under measurement.

The next systems capability is the **thoughtexperiment harness**: fork a primary substrate revision into an isolated copy-on-write candidate state, apply a candidate rule/representation or policy there, run the same frozen probe on primary and branch, then return a compact residual and outcome record to the primary graph. Candidate mutations must never leak into the primary before an explicit adoption step. The primary receives evidence (candidate identity, input/probe identity, baseline and branch predictions, residual delta, cost, validity, and provenance), not a wholesale branch merge. Adoption remains a separate, attributable decision.

The thoughtexperiment harness now has an implemented Linux process-CoW prototype: a guarded child runs the candidate in place and returns a residual receipt to the primary graph. This is OS page-level CoW supplied by `fork`, not a native Rust overlay or a portable substrate fork API. The source audit confirms `TypedGraph` in [`graph.rs`](../../../runners/dsl/src/graph.rs) has Vec-backed node/edge slabs plus derived adjacency, type, edge, and attribute indices. More importantly, [`Substrate`](../../../runners/dsl/src/substrate.rs) owns much more than the graph: the interner, checker/grammar, term arena, rewrite rules, evaluator caches, incremental cursors, counters, and transient queues. The prototype's fail-closed eligibility checks cover selected hooks, pending effects, handles, and external-reading rules in a single-threaded Linux process; they are not a security boundary or proof of full-state isolation.

Copy-on-write is a reusable substrate capability in its own right, not merely an optimization for thoughtexperiments. It gives callers an explicit isolation boundary for speculative execution, parallel search, simulations, and independent consumers of a shared revision; it also lets the substrate evolve its storage backend without changing those callers. A vLLM-style interface is a useful compatibility target because it can share immutable prefix state among requests while isolating divergent continuations. That analogy does not mean this substrate already implements a KV cache or is integrated with vLLM. The design requirement is a backend-neutral snapshot/branch contract, with consumer-specific adapters and their own lifetime, concurrency, cancellation, and memory tests.

Accordingly, the CoW workstream has two independent acceptance dimensions: **semantic capability** (revision identity, read-only sharing, nested and sibling branch isolation, explicit discard/adoption, deterministic residuals, and compatibility with at least two distinct consumers) and **resource behavior** (branch latency, bytes copied or dirtied, peak RSS/PSS, reclamation after cancellation/drop, and throughput as fan-out grows). Passing the semantic gate establishes a useful isolation and compatibility feature even when a workload does not become faster; performance claims require the resource gate on that workload. A vLLM-style or other shared-prefix adapter should be measured as a consumer integration, including prefix reuse, branch-local writes, request cancellation, and memory reclamation.

The Rust and Python consumer APIs now begin with `Substrate.snapshot()` and hide the selected storage backend from `SubstrateSnapshot`; backend-selecting access is private to measurement code. The 5,000-node fanout capture passes primary, sibling, and captured-revision isolation for all three measured implementations at fanouts 1/4/16, five repeats per cell. At fanout 16, median branch fork is 1.10 ms for full copy, 0.79 ms for shared slabs, and 0.0043 ms for shared graph pages. This is an API-contract and local cost result. It does not yet establish complete-state CoW, concurrent consumers, cancellation/reclamation under pressure, RSS/PSS, or a serving adapter. Next work should validate lifecycle and concurrency semantics against the consumer-neutral API before implementing a shared-prefix adapter ([design](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_COW_SUBSTRATE_DESIGN.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_snapshot_fork_contract_v1.py), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_consumer_neutral_snapshot_api_v1.json)).

**Reusable snapshot memory lifecycle v2 (2026-10-01):** 45 measured fresh-process workers plus 9 warmups sample full-process RSS/PSS at primary baseline, snapshot capture, branch fork, branch write, branch drop with snapshot retained, verification-fork drop, snapshot drop, and primary drop. All 8 analyzer gates pass, including current source/native provenance, full randomized worker grid, primary and branch isolation, and a later fork that excludes the discarded branch write. At 50,771 total nodes, median PSS deltas at snapshot/branch-live stages are 10,996/27,832 KiB full copy, 3,004/11,844 KiB shared slabs, and 284/772 KiB shared graph pages. This supports a much lower resident footprint for shared graph pages on the large fixture. PSS after drop does not reliably return to baseline: full-copy process pages remain resident and shared-page readings fluctuate below baseline. Therefore semantic disposal is established while allocator/kernel reclamation and bounded-memory behavior remain open. The study is one host and one synthetic fixture without inference, concurrency, or active cancellation ([results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_SNAPSHOT_RECLAMATION_V2_RESULTS_20261001.md), [preregistration](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_SNAPSHOT_RECLAMATION_V2_PREREG_20261001.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_snapshot_reclamation_v2.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_snapshot_reclamation_v2.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_snapshot_reclamation_v2_analysis.json)).

**Native concurrent snapshot branches v1 (2026-10-01):** `ExperimentSnapshot` satisfies Rust `Send + Sync`; one immutable snapshot is shared across worker threads. A source-captured paired panel completes 9 size × fanout cells (771/10,771/50,771 nodes; fanout 1/4/16; five arm-order-alternated repeats). All 7 semantic/provenance gates pass. Concurrent fork-plus-one-node-write loses at every 771-node cell and at 10,771/fanout 1; it wins 5/5 paired repeats at fanouts 4 and 16 on 10,771 nodes, and fanouts 4 and 16 at 50,771 nodes. Median serial/concurrent ratios are 2.77× at 10,771/fanout 16 and 4.28× at 50,771/fanout 16. This establishes safe parallel branch creation and a measured crossover for a tiny mutation workload, not concurrent live-Substrate mutation, rule inference, or thoughtexperiment throughput. Next measure parallel rule execution and memory under fanout, cancellation, and branch drop with multiple concurrent consumers before adopting this as an open-ended search executor ([results](COW_SNAPSHOT_CONCURRENT_FORK_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [protocol](COW_SNAPSHOT_CONCURRENT_FORK_V1_PREREG_20261001.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/cow_snapshot_concurrent_fork_v1.py), [probe](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/fixtures/cow_snapshot_threads/src/main.rs), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/cow_snapshot_concurrent_fork_v1_analysis.json)).

The portable design candidate is an immutable, revisioned base plus branch-local mutation overlays, exposed through a graph-view interface to reads and a branch mutation API to writes. A partial Rust implementation now stores `TypedGraph` node and edge slabs in `CowPagedVec`; `clone_sharing_slabs()` shares those pages but still copies indexes and the rest of `Substrate`. The source-locked graph v2 probe covers path/star/grid at four sizes, clone-only, one-write, and 1%-write workloads, with 25 repeats per cell; divergent sibling values and primary isolation pass in all 12 cells. At 50,771 nodes, shared/eager clone times are 2.41–2.42/6.45–10.65 ms across the three topologies; with 1% writes, shared/eager are 2.27–3.42/7.65–10.38 ms. The separate full candidate-batch comparison still has no stable end-to-end win. CoW remains independently useful for branch isolation, parallel consumers, storage-backend compatibility, and future interfaces; a vLLM-like shared-prefix consumer is a design possibility, not an implemented or measured integration. Next measure index and full-state copy costs, touched-page allocation and memory, then extend the snapshot/fork/receipt interface without exposing storage layout. Keep external effects disabled or explicitly sandboxed; a branch must be replayable from a primary revision plus candidate patch and probe. See the [v2 graph capture](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_probe_v2.json) and [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/typed_graph_cow_probe_v2.py).

The allocator-accounting follow-up covers the same 12 topology/size cells with seven repeats, and every branch returns requested live bytes to the pre-operation baseline after drop. At 50,771 nodes, clone-only retained heap is 8.23–10.22 MiB eager versus 5.84–7.03 MiB shared-slab; one write to a shared branch adds 3,936 bytes, and spaced writes to 1% of nodes add about 1.08 MiB. This shows meaningful but partial memory savings and exposes the remaining eager graph-index/state cost. The figures exclude allocator overhead, RSS/PSS, page residency, and all non-graph `Substrate` fields. See the [memory capture](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_memory_probe_v1.json) and [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/typed_graph_cow_memory_probe_v1.py).

Adjacency-page sharing is the latest measured engine increment. The Rust API and Python thoughtexperiment fork now expose `native_shared_graph_pages_scoped`, sharing node/edge records plus top-level `out`/`in` pages while retaining eager hash-index clones. The source-locked graph-only benchmark passes edge-query and branch-isolation gates on path/star/grid at four sizes. At 50,771 nodes, graph-page clone medians are 0.89–1.58 ms vs 7.14–9.62 ms records-only; 1% edge insertion is 1.63–2.66 ms vs 8.10–9.68 ms. Its allocation probe reports clone-only retained heap of 3.26–4.70 MiB vs 6.68–7.87 MiB records-only, with the branch reclaimed on drop in all 12 cells. An initial three-repeat full candidate-batch capture was inconclusive. The higher-repeat replay then used five measured blocks plus two warmups at baseline/+10k/+50k and passed exact nested output and primary-isolation gates across all three branches. Baseline is tied; at +10k graph-page batch time is 866 ms versus 1,009 ms eager and 966 ms records-only, winning all five paired blocks. At +50k it is 912 ms versus 1,426/2,030 ms and wins all five blocks, with 1.65×/2.15× median paired ratios against eager/records-only. This is an end-to-end win on one synthetic task family and host, not a natural-task or independent-host result. Next measure RSS/PSS and complete Substrate memory, then replicate workloads and hosts. See the [graph probe](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_graph_pages_probe_v1.json), [allocation probe](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_graph_pages_memory_probe_v1.json), [initial batch capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_shared_graph_pages_batch_v1.json.gz), and [higher-repeat batch capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_shared_graph_pages_batch_v2.json.gz).

**Sparse mutation-journal readout v1 (2026-09-30):** [implementation](../../../domains/imagination.py) now uses a Rust before-image journal to form `conclusions` and `derived_only` from touched graph objects rather than serializing and diffing the full detached graph. A source-locked nonzero-inference probe executes a held graph rule against an injected hypothesis and requires exact output parity, unchanged primary state, and nonempty coverage of all five mutation classes: added/changed/removed nodes and added/removed edges. Three paired repeats plus one warmup pass at 0/1k/10k/50k/100k unrelated nodes. Journal versus legacy whole-graph readout medians are 0.129/2.698 ms (20.9×), 0.241/15.504 ms (64.3×), 1.080/257.302 ms (238.3×), 4.394/1,412.152 ms (321.4×), and 9.661/3,139.056 ms (324.9×). At 100k nodes this is about 103 timed branch operations/s versus 0.32/s for the legacy branch/readout route. This isolates sparse branch/readout work on one synthetic, one-rule family; it is not a general system speedup or a natural-task throughput result, and excludes fresh fixture construction. A matched self-correction runner exposes each nested baseline and candidate forward-look residual. At baseline and +10k, two measured repeats plus one warmup pass exact nested `conclusions`/`derived_only` parity across serialization, native copy, scoped copy, and scoped legacy-diff backends; positive and negative outcomes and primary-graph/rule preservation also pass. At +10k, journal scoped rehearsal takes 239.62/215.52 ms (positive/negative) versus 2,009.23/1,930.24 ms with legacy whole-graph readout, or 8.4×/9.0× faster. Against the previous serialization backend it is 5.4×/5.8× faster; against full native copy it is 3.2×/3.5×. At baseline the gain is 1.9×/1.7×. This validates a substantial corrected-rehearsal gain on one synthetic family and host under a small exploratory repeat count, not a broad natural-task rate. The next harness gate is experiments completed per wall-clock budget across a diverse candidate panel, with exact branch residuals, useful-outcome rate, memory, and fixed-revision isolation reported together. See the [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_delta_journal_inference_v1.py), [nonzero-inference capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_delta_journal_inference_v1.json), and [matched self-correction capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_branch_delta_journal_v1.json).

**Bounded candidate-diversity expansion v1 (2026-09-30):** `_default_candidates` now adds up to four deterministic `swap_term_leaf` mutations over attribute keys already used by the target effect. This changes the measured `sd_mint_quantum` panel from two candidates to six while retaining a hard per-target generation cap. The source-locked [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_candidate_diversity_v1.py) evaluates each candidate on a fresh positive/negative fixture at baseline and +10k through journal and legacy-diff modes; two repeats plus one warmup per cell pass exact top-level and nested forward-look residual parity, candidate-application, primary graph/rule isolation, and designated positive/negative controls. At +10k, summed per-candidate medians are 1.12 s for journal mode versus 12.34 s for legacy diff (about 11× potential panel throughput, with fixture generation excluded). Only the designated dedup fix converges (2/2); the negative guard and all four key swaps diverge (0/2 each). Thus the faster substrate buys six checked candidates for roughly the former legacy route's time, while this expansion adds no new useful candidate on the current task. This is candidate-by-candidate timing, not a shared-baseline batch, and one target rule is not a general search distribution. Next test other target-rule/task families, extend bounded edits only when their outcomes can be independently scored, and report useful discoveries per unit CPU/memory rather than candidate count alone. See the [candidate-diversity capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_candidate_diversity_v1.json).

**Unrelated graph-topology replication v1 (2026-09-30):** positive dedup and negative guard controls were repeated against 10k unrelated-node path, star, and 100×100 grid backgrounds. Each cell uses two measured repeats plus one warmup; exact top-level and nested residual parity, expected outcomes, and primary graph/rule isolation pass in all six cells. Journal versus legacy-diff medians range from 8.7× to 11.4× across these three topologies (path: 9.4×/11.4×; star: 10.9×/10.5×; grid: 8.7×/10.3×, positive/negative). This shows the readout gain is not specific to the path noise graph, but remains a single-host synthetic test with unchanged local correction frame; it does not establish prevalence on natural tasks. See the source-locked [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_topology_scaling_v1.py) and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_topology_scaling_v1.json).

### Source-derived state partition and adoption contract

**CoW design intent (2026-09-30):** copy-on-write is a core substrate capability with value beyond making thoughtexperiments faster. It provides a clean isolation boundary for speculative branches, preserves compatibility with consumers that need snapshot-like state (including a future vLLM-style serving interface), and keeps the branch model explicit in the Rust API. Performance is a further benefit, not the feature's only justification. The Linux `fork()` prototype below is evidence for one backend and must not define the public interface: expose backend-neutral snapshot/fork, branch mutation, discard, and residual operations so Rust-managed page/arena or persistent-data-structure CoW can replace or coexist with process CoW. Any serving adapter must have its own ownership, lifetime, concurrency, and memory-accounting contract; compatibility is an architectural target, not yet an implemented vLLM integration.

**Generated version-space integration pilot (2026-09-30, exploratory):** `domains/generator.synthesize` now has an opt-in bounded collection mode that separates labeled training rows from unlabeled probe environments. It can collect the smallest behaviorally distinct fitting terms over a fixed probe set, and `include_output_constants=False` holds the literal grammar fixed so labels cannot expand the search vocabulary. For triangular numbers, five single-example anchors (`n=1..5`) produced pools of 126, 38, 14, 9, and 4 terms after enumerating 7,905 candidates per anchor. In each case the known closed form was present; entropy ranking selected one unlabeled query (`n=11`, `11`, `11`, `3`, `2`) whose single oracle response left exactly that term in the pool. This shows a concrete substrate path from enumerative generation to active query selection on one authored arithmetic task. It is a deterministic exploratory probe on one family, not an independent held-out task evaluation; the probe inputs participate in behavior deduplication, and the fixed grammar, size cap, and one-example anchors limit the claim. Next lock a multi-family protocol and compare generated-pool ranking with fixed/random query selection, including exact held-out behavior, CPU time, memory, and oracle calls, before integrating it into the CEGIS driver.

**Generated-pool scaling probe (2026-09-30, exploratory negative result):** on the existing list-variance task, the same collector with a fixed arithmetic grammar, one training row, 12 unlabeled candidate inputs, and a 20-second cap explored 102,703 terms and retained 277 fitting behaviors before timeout (39,628 distinct observed behaviors total). This does not establish that the complete bounded version space is inherently too costly; it does establish that the current collector can return a partial pool under realistic resource caps. Query selection must therefore expose `halt_reason`, explored count, and completeness, and evaluation must report both query value and pool-generation cost. Any apparent one-query identification from a timed-out pool is provisional until compared with the full bounded pool or an explicit uncertainty-aware stopping rule. The next multi-family protocol should treat timeout as an outcome and include a smaller/fixed-budget task where complete-pool controls are possible.

**Generated-pool confirmatory pilot v1 (2026-09-30):** five preregistered triangular-number anchors (`n=6..10`) completed their bounded searches in a median 0.647 s after 7,905 term evaluations, returning 1–3 hypotheses each. Entropy selected `n=2` and uniquely identified the held-out-correct behavior in 5/5 anchors. Fixed-first did the same in 5/5; seeded random did so in 50/50 draws. Oracle-best selected the same query at a cost of 10 labels per anchor. This is a negative comparative result: the family is too easy to demonstrate a benefit from entropy, and no cross-task claim follows. The source-locked [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENERATED_VERSION_SPACE_V1_PREREG_20260930.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_generated_version_space_v1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_generated_version_space_v1_20260930_analysis.json), and [results](SUBSTRATE_GENERATED_VERSION_SPACE_V1_RESULTS_20260930.md) require a harder independent task next; the variance timeout above shows the current full enumerator may exceed bounded budgets there.

**Generated Euler active-query v1.1 (2026-09-30):** three complete generated pools (218–662 hypotheses) each contain a hypothesis correct on six separate holdout complexes. Iterative entropy uniquely identifies a holdout-correct survivor in 3/3 anchors at a median 3 oracle calls, versus 7 fixed-first calls and 4 seeded-random calls. However, current ranking expends a median 6,026 native prediction evaluations and 31.6 ms per policy run, versus 705 / 2.9 ms for fixed-first; the local grounded oracle costs only about 0.2–0.5 ms per complete policy run. Thus query reduction is real on this finite family but does not pay for itself in local compute as currently implemented. The [v1.1 amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENERATED_EULER_ACTIVE_QUERY_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260930.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_GENERATED_EULER_ACTIVE_QUERY_V1_1_RESULTS_20260930.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_generated_euler_active_query_v1_1.py), and [analysis capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_generated_euler_active_query_v1_1_20260930_analysis.json) make the next optimization measurable: cache the hypothesis × query prediction matrix or update entropy counts incrementally, including its one-time memory and compute cost.

**Generated Euler cache-index v1.2 (2026-09-30):** a new immutable `QueryRankingIndex` precomputes one prediction matrix and reuses it across iterative query selection. It exactly matches the uncached query sequence on all three anchors. Median repeated decision work falls from 32.29 ms to 4.76 ms, but the one-time 29.0 ms build raises single-episode total to 34.05 ms; the fixed-order baseline is 4.33 ms. The matrix retains about 642 KB of estimated Python heap at the median pool size. Reuse across two independent episodes is projected to amortize the cache build against uncached ranking, but has not yet been measured. See the amended [v1.2 results](SUBSTRATE_GENERATED_EULER_ACTIVE_QUERY_V1_2_RESULTS_20260930.md) and [analysis capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_generated_euler_active_query_v1_2_20260930_analysis.json). Next measure real repeated branch reuse and RSS, rather than claiming the projected break-even as an observed speedup.

**Cache tolerance correction and branch-reuse outcome (2026-09-30):** a synthetic alternative-target replay found an exact-float versus `1e-9` tolerance mismatch in cached filtering, which could retain different hypotheses than the existing CEGIS path. The API now applies the same tolerance; v1.2.1 has exact cached/uncached query-sequence and survivor parity. Its corrected single-episode total (44.15 ms) is slightly slower than uncached (42.95 ms). A separate 1/5/20 serial hypothesis-branch study directly measures amortization: cached batch medians are 59/81/128 ms versus 40/200/823 ms uncached (0.74×/2.70×/6.53× speedup), with ~642 KB estimated Python heap per index. The targets are synthetic alternate hypotheses and the forks are Python hypothesis states, not live graph branches. See the corrected [v1.2.1 results](SUBSTRATE_GENERATED_EULER_ACTIVE_QUERY_V1_2_1_RESULTS_20260930.md), [branch-reuse protocol](SUBSTRATE_QUERY_INDEX_BRANCH_REUSE_V1_PREREG_20260930.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_QUERY_INDEX_BRANCH_REUSE_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260930.md), and [branch-reuse results](SUBSTRATE_QUERY_INDEX_BRANCH_REUSE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260930.md). The next gate is to reuse branch-invariant predictions behind the actual Rust thought-experiment interface and include RSS/concurrency costs.

Source review of [`Substrate`](../../../runners/dsl/src/substrate.rs), [`TypedGraph`](../../../runners/dsl/src/graph.rs), [`Interner`](../../../runners/dsl/src/sym.rs), [`TermArena`/`EvalCache`](../../../runners/dsl/src/term.rs), [`ConsistencyChecker`](../../../runners/dsl/src/checker.rs), and [`RewriteRule`](../../../runners/dsl/src/rewrite.rs) implies four distinct classes:

| State class | Current examples | Thoughtexperiment treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Semantic primary state | Graph facts/attrs and indices; grammar; rules; terms; concept resolver; shape target. | Immutable base plus branch-local overlay. Candidate additions/revisions remain branch-local. |
| Derived execution state | Rule dirty bits, dependency indexes, cursors, evaluator/shape caches, mutation versions, counters and cost telemetry. | Rebuild or invalidate at branch start; keep telemetry branch-local. Never merge cache/cursor internals into primary. |
| Deferred effects | Rule-edit/patch, framebuffer sample, identity-track, and net-collapse queues; attr-write logs. | Start empty. Drain only against branch-local state. Reject or record any effect that crosses the sandbox boundary. |
| External resources | Attached shared-memory framebuffers, process/global registries, host I/O, clocks/randomness. | Exclude by default. Tests that need them must use deterministic captured inputs and explicit fake/sandbox adapters. |

Symbol and node handles are only meaningful in their originating state. The residual protocol must therefore use stable semantic references (for example primary node IDs plus branch-local temporary IDs with an explicit namespace), candidate/probe digests, primary revision, and measured outputs; it must not copy raw branch handles into the primary. Adoption is replay, not branch merge: check that the primary revision still matches, apply the candidate patch through ordinary admission/mutation paths, rerun the validation probe on the primary, and commit atomically only if it still passes. A stale primary revision requires reevaluation from a fresh branch. This is necessary to avoid importing branch-local IDs, derived indices, or effects into live state.

**Current field-level fork boundary (2026-09-30):** a source inspection of the live struct declarations finds 25 `TypedGraph` fields and 50 `Substrate` fields. `TypedGraph` combines semantic slabs (`nodes`, `edges`, edge attributes) with mutation-maintained indices (`by_type`, adjacency/type maps, target indexes, and `attr_indices`), freelists/version counters, and seven pending/logging fields. The core semantic substrate state is spread across `graph`, `interner`, `checker`, `terms`, `concepts`, `rules`, `gamma_epoch`, `gamma_graph_root`, and shape target; it cannot be reproduced by the current graph serializer alone. Rule execution state includes dependency/readers indexes, dirty bits, cursors, evaluator/JIT/shape caches, incremental-mode flags, and cost/trace counters. The graph and substrate also contain deferred mutation/perception queues, while `framebuffers` holds handles to shared external resources. Those resources must be excluded or replaced by captured deterministic inputs in a branch. Counters and traces must be branch-local; derived indexes/caches must be rebuilt or invalidated; pending effect queues must begin empty. The [source-locked field census runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_state_inventory_v1.py) fails closed on unclassified, added, or removed fields and writes the [current capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_state_inventory_v1.json). Its policy labels are a design checklist, not proof of semantic isolation; runtime behavior must still validate them at the locked revision.

### Staged implementation and evidence gates

1. **Specify branch semantics and API:** define a backend-neutral Rust snapshot/fork, branch mutation, discard, and residual interface; define primary revision, branch identity, allowed mutation surface, ID allocation, deletion/reuse behavior, symbol/rule/term isolation, cache invalidation, external-effect prohibition, crash/discard behavior, and the residual schema. Verify that discarding a branch leaves primary state byte-for-byte or semantically unchanged. Keep process `fork()` behind an implementation adapter. This API is also the future integration point for serving systems that benefit from shared immutable state and per-request CoW, subject to an explicit concurrent lifetime and memory budget.
2. **Measure the representation:** compare the existing graph serialization/restore route with an independent full-substrate-copy control and a CoW branch on the same source-locked rehearsal probe. Require parity across the semantic state above and fail closed if any external handle/effect is touched. Then compare the CoW fork, branch execution, and residual readout at increasing node/edge counts and 0.1%, 1%, and 10% mutation density. Record fork and end-to-end latency, peak/RSS memory, write amplification, branch operation cost, and residual readout cost. Include concurrent branches and long-lived branches. A process fork is optional and platform-specific; it is not a substitute for proving substrate state isolation.
3. **Wire a bounded experiment runner:** fork candidates from one immutable primary revision; run identical probes and resource caps; return residual deltas with source locks, candidate digest, probe digest, and branch revision. Do not merge candidate state.
4. **Teach the primary to use returned evidence:** persist each result as a typed experience record; author a graph policy that ranks the next bounded candidate from prior outcome/residual/cost records. Compare that policy with fixed ranking and frozen/no-learning controls on fresh correction families. LLM may choose the outer task initially, but must not silently choose candidate order, score interpretation, or adoption within the measured delegated boundary.
5. **Transfer responsibility incrementally:** first let substrate rank; then allocate a fixed search budget; then propose a policy update. At every step report decision provenance, intervention/veto rate, paired held-out utility, false acceptance, forgetting, total CPU/memory, and exact rollback. Durable self-modification remains gated on repeated held-out gains and existing custody/release prerequisites.

**First acceptance gate:** on small representative graph sizes, branches produce the same probe outcomes as independent full-copy controls; primary state is unchanged before adoption; residuals exactly identify the preregistered branch-vs-primary differences; fork-plus-run-plus-readout costs less than full-copy evaluation at the declared scale. Performance alone is insufficient if state isolation or provenance fails. No general self-improvement claim follows from this systems result.

**Current snapshot baseline v1 (2026-09-30):** the executable [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_snapshot_baseline_v1.py) measures the existing native `graph_to_dict` + `graph_from_dict` detached-copy route on a chain-plus-skip graph, with seven timed repeats after two warmups. The [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_snapshot_baseline_v1.json) source-locks the runner, graph/persistence/PyO3 and imagination/correction paths, and loaded native binary (`sha256:a5aa1ea0…`). Export-plus-restore medians are 10.33 ms for 1,000 nodes/1,991 edges, 124.56 ms for 10,000/19,991, and 729.14 ms for 50,000/99,991; the largest JSON representation is 12,017,262 bytes. At 50,000, export accounts for 402.89 ms and restore 319.20 ms. This is a single-host graph-only synthetic baseline: it excludes rule-store import, candidate application, inference/closure, residual extraction, RSS, and external resources. It is not a CoW result and does not yet show an end-to-end thoughtexperiment speedup. Next compare a real full-copy experiment and the CoW branch on the exact same source-locked probes, reporting full substrate state and residual parity as well as latency and memory.

**Matched serialization vs native deep-copy rehearsal v1 (2026-09-30):** the [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_self_correction_copy_comparison_v1.py) executes the same fresh positive/negative correction fixtures through the existing graph serialization/restore route and a new native deep-copy control. The control copies graph slabs and indexes, interner, grammar/checker, Term arena, concepts, rewrite rules, and active execution configuration; it detaches the Γ epoch, resets branch telemetry/caches, and refuses pending effects, attribute-write observations, framebuffer handles, Python hooks, a live agent thread, or an initialized Python memory faculty. A focused probe also copies the full identity space and prunes edges outside the same focus aperture as serialization. All six size × candidate parity gates pass at baseline, +1k, and +10k unrelated chain nodes: positive converges 3/3 and wrong diverges 3/3 with matching prediction metrics, step counts, conclusion counts, primary graph counts, and rule counts. The runner additionally confirms that all pre-existing primary node values/types, edge instances, and native rewrite rules remain unchanged; only allowed durable trace node types are added. Median full rehearsal times are 788.98/800.81 ms at 771 nodes, 972.52/974.08 ms at 1,771 nodes, and 3,329.29/3,179.42 ms at 10,771 nodes for serialization positive/negative; native deep copy is 424.87/384.57 ms, 560.40/572.55 ms, and 2,870.60/2,796.89 ms respectively. This is a single-host three-repeat result with fixed backend order; it compares full rehearsal routes, not isolated fork time. It records no RSS/peak memory or concurrent branches, and it does not establish full semantic parity across all 74 audited fields. Native deep copy is still O(graph + substrate state) and is a control arm, not CoW. The current loaded-engine/source fingerprint and per-file locks are in the [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_self_correction_copy_comparison_v1.json). The next gate is an actual shared-base/branch-delta implementation with mutation and read parity, then the same rehearsal probe plus sparse/dense mutation, memory, and counterbalanced-order measurements.

**Self-correction rehearsal pilot v1 (2026-09-30, superseded diagnosis):** the first direct fixture replay found both candidate arms nonconvergent. Source tracing identified two missing pieces in detached execution: `imagine()` copied graph data but not the separate native rewrite-rule store, and forward-look recovery subsequently called the Default `tick()` plan, which can skip graph-resident rules. The old run was a valid diagnostic of the incomplete route, not a candidate-quality result. The code now copies active native rules into every detached branch, applies candidate deltas there, and executes an explicit graph-then-struct plan; `self_correction` no longer performs a duplicate rule import, and `collapse_model` no longer performs a structural-only re-tick.

**Linux process-CoW thoughtexperiment harness v1 (2026-09-30):** the [source-locked runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_process_cow_self_correction_v1.py) forks the guarded substrate, executes correction in-place in the child, returns the residual over a pipe, and writes a namespaced `ThoughtexperimentReceipt` in the parent without merging branch state. Six size × candidate comparisons at baseline, +1k, and +10k nodes match predictions and residuals against serialization and native deep-copy controls; the positive candidate converges and the wrong candidate remains divergent, with all six explicit semantic, control-outcome, and parent-isolation gates passing. The runner now executes three seeded randomized complete blocks per graph size (order seed `20260930`), with both candidate arms and all three backends in each block. Process-CoW total medians at baseline/+1k/+10k are 407/439, 700/621, and 2,930/2,881 ms (correct/wrong), against same-run native deep-copy 389/394, 587/538, and 2,810/2,764 ms. It is 5–11% slower at baseline, 15–19% slower at +1k, and about 4% slower at +10k. Same-run serialization medians are 786–789, 965–985, and 3,291–3,542 ms. This establishes isolation, parity, receipt return, and a randomized-block comparison; it does not deliver the large per-experiment speedup needed for open-ended search. At +10k, model-before alone costs 1.16–1.19 s per run; the child dirties 22–107 MB. Source tracing finds additional whole-graph work in focus pruning and graph-diff readout. The [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_process_cow_self_correction_v1.json) separately reports model-before, child, fork-plus-pipe, and receipt costs. This remains one synthetic fixture family, one host, three repeats, no concurrent branches, and no OS sandbox.

**Thoughtexperiment scale objective and implementation gates:** treat “massively faster” as a stretch target of at least 10× lower marginal candidate-evaluation time than the current native deep-copy route on sparse experiments over the same fixed primary revision. For the current 10,771-node matched probe, this sets an initial target near 300 ms per candidate after one reusable baseline, versus the prior measured ~2.95 s full rehearsal. Keep baseline/setup amortization separate from candidate marginal cost and preserve exact semantic/residual parity. Baseline reuse remains measured at 1.15×–1.27× on the two-candidate fixture. The Rust residual journal, frame visibility scope, and six-candidate generation panel are now implemented and measured: at +10k the journal rehearsal is 3.2×/3.5× faster than full native copy and 8.4×/9.0× faster than scoped native copy with whole-graph readout; all nested residuals match, but the 10× target relative to native copy is not reached. Six candidates take a summed 1.12 s in journal mode versus 12.34 s in legacy mode, but only the designated dedup fix converges on this probe. Next reduce per-candidate O(state) branch work with a portable immutable-base/overlay experiment, and test independent graph/task families with useful-outcome-per-time and memory accounting. The existing `imagine_candidate_batch` computes one traced baseline for a fixed primary revision, suppresses per-candidate primary traces, reuses that baseline across isolated native-deep-copy branches, then verifies graph/rule identity after the candidate batch. On its original two-candidate fixture it matches standalone positive/negative outcomes and residual metrics, leaves the primary unchanged during the candidate phase, and yields 1.15×/1.25×/1.27× median speedups at baseline/+1k/+10k nodes. This baseline-amortization result is real but modest and remains distinct from the newer journal measurements. See the source-locked [amortization runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_candidate_batch_amortization_v1.py), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_candidate_batch_amortization_v1.json), and [candidate-diversity capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_candidate_diversity_v1.json).

**Frame-scoped edge-read experiment v1 (2026-09-30):** the Rust graph now has an opt-in sparse edge-read scope that retains full node identity while exposing only edges and adjacency indexes in the chosen aperture. Existing unrestricted graph behavior is unchanged when no scope is active. Candidate rehearsal now accepts explicit experiment focus nodes. In two matched repeats per cell, the native deep-copy scoped route exactly matches physical-prune/serialization outputs, including canonical conclusion and derived-only diffs; all six size × positive/negative parity gates and primary-state checks pass. At +10k unrelated nodes, median full rehearsal is 2.23/2.25 s (positive/negative) with sparse scoped indexes versus 2.68/2.80 s for native full copy, about 1.20×/1.24× faster. This is a modest gain; it remains a full graph copy and the scope index itself costs time. See the [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_self_correction_copy_comparison_v1.py) and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_frame_aperture_v1.json).

**Scoped process-CoW experiment v1 (2026-09-30):** the same aperture is now exercised inside the forked child, alongside the previous physical-prune child and copy controls. One fresh randomized block per size and candidate at baseline/+10k passes exact residual parity across all five execution routes, expected positive/negative controls, and parent graph/rule isolation. At +10k, scoped process-CoW end-to-end totals were 2.49/2.82 s (positive/negative); native full-copy scoped controls were 2.30/2.40 s. The process route therefore did not show a speed advantage. Child private-dirty growth remained about 100/108 MB, so page-level CoW did not make this rehearsal cheap. These one-repeat numbers are exploratory, not stable estimates. The [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_process_cow_self_correction_v1.py) and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_process_cow_scoped_v1.json) lock the route and residuals. The likely remaining cost is baseline prediction and whole-state traversal/diff; the next optimization gate is a branch mutation journal or reusable frame-local indexes that avoid full-graph copies and repeated graph serialization/diff, measured with a broader candidate panel and randomized repeats. The 10× marginal-time objective is not met.

**Zero-step candidate-base readout ablation v1 (2026-09-30):** `imagine_and_check_convergence` creates a candidate base by calling `imagine` with zero steps, no hypothesis, and no grounding cut. That branch cannot have a graph delta, but the old route still serialized it twice and ran two empty graph diffs. A narrowly guarded fast path now returns the exact empty diff shape without those whole-graph reads; other imagination modes retain the ordinary execution and readout path. The randomized paired ablation uses the same scoped native-copy backend for both modes, with two timed repeats and one warmup per cell. Exact prediction, candidate application, conclusion/derived-only outputs, and primary-state checks pass in all four size/candidate cells. At +10k unrelated nodes the median improvement is 1.21×/1.27× for positive/negative candidates (1,868/1,888 ms versus 2,255/2,393 ms); at baseline it is 1.11×/1.14×. This removes redundant work but leaves full deep copying, baseline prediction, and post-collapse graph diff in place. See the [ablation runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_noop_readout_ablation_v1.py) and [source-locked capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_noop_readout_ablation_v1.json).

**Scoped process-CoW replay after readout optimization v2 (2026-09-30):** one randomized complete block at baseline and +10k confirms exact conclusion and derived-only residual parity against serialization, native deep copy, and scoped native deep copy, with expected positive/negative outcomes and parent graph/rule isolation. At +10k, the scoped CoW child totals 2.22/2.26 s, versus 1.96/2.03 s for the scoped native deep-copy control; child private-dirty growth is 96–105 MiB. One repeat is exploratory, but it does not suggest a CoW speed advantage. The [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_process_cow_scoped_v2.json) locks the updated imagination path and residual outputs.

**Fixed-revision process-CoW batch amortization v1 (2026-09-30):** two candidates (the designated positive correction and matched negative control) are forked sequentially from the same primary state after one baseline prediction. The parent defers both receipt writes until the two branches finish and verifies the graph/rule digest remains fixed between branches. Three randomized paired repeats plus one warmup pass exact prediction and complete residual parity, fixed-primary isolation, and positive/negative outcome gates at baseline, +1k, and +10k nodes. Total batch / sum-of-standalone medians are 782/892 ms, 1,186/1,226 ms, and 4,484/5,819 ms, yielding 1.14×/1.03×/1.30× speedups. The gain is largest at +10k and is not monotonic across the three sizes; fixed overhead and timing noise are visible at +1k. This supports baseline amortization on the largest measured fixture, but not a general scaling law. This is sequential Linux fork work on one synthetic family and one host, and the 10× target remains unmet. See the [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_process_batch_amortization_v1.py) and [source-locked capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_process_batch_amortization_v1.json).

**Corrected self-correction rehearsal v1 (2026-09-30):** on the same fixture and newly rebuilt source-matched native engine (`sha256:7bf9a7cb…`), the designated `dedup_identity_fix` converges in 3/3 repeats at each graph size, while the matched wrong candidate remains divergent in 3/3. Frontier growth changes 3.0→0.0 for the positive arm and stays 3.0→3.0 for the negative; measured forward-look steps are 15 and 12 respectively. Full candidate-rehearsal median time (fixture construction excluded) is 551.91/542.30 ms at 771 nodes/744 edges, 651.38/673.78 ms at 1,771/1,743, and 2,387.90/2,438.23 ms at 10,771/10,743 (positive/negative arms). The 10k unrelated-chain increase costs roughly 1.84 s over the base fixture in both arms, despite the correction frame being unchanged; this is consistent with full-graph detached copying and whole-state prediction cost, and provides a concrete target for CoW/overlay evaluation. This is one host and one synthetic load shape; no speedup claim is made. The [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_self_correction_baseline_v1.py) locks twelve source files plus runner and binary; the [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_self_correction_baseline_v1.json) records all 3/3 outcomes, graph sizes, residuals, candidate application, and timings. No pytest suite was run.

**Term access-dependency coverage v1 (2026-09-28):** the generated crosswalk covers all 237 `TermNode` variants and finds evaluator and child-walk entries for each. It classifies 36 unconditional wildcard readers, 5 finite-key readers, 5 conditional readers, and 191 generic child-walk fallbacks. **Stateful shared-callback order/replay probe v1.3 (2026-09-28):** all 10 independent checks pass in three fresh workers. A shared callback returning true once makes the first inserted rule win; reversing insertion order reverses the marker. Each first settle makes three calls (two by the first rule, one by the second), then resetting callback state without changing the graph causes the second settle to make zero calls and zero progress. **Predicate-use migration impact and design gate (2026-09-28):** a reproducible source inventory scans all 828 flat `seeds/*.json` files and finds 18 syntactic `UseTool` nodes in `where` fields across nine rules in `figure_grounding.json`; it finds zero in rule effects. Every referenced tool name is present in `domains.symbolic_perception.HANDLERS`. `load_all_seeds()` documents full-corpus behavior when no selection arguments are supplied, so a blanket predicate ban would affect this existing seed on full-corpus boot; profile and selective boots may differ. The optional `domains.ast_to_rule.Migrator` seam also maps nested `np.<module>.<function>(...)` calls to `UseTool`, and translates no-else `if` guards through `_value(st.test)`, so generated rules can enter the same predicate position; the located `scripts/migrate_curious_agent.py` caller is opt-in. This is a syntactic compatibility census, not a runtime-frequency or handler-purity census ([audit runner](../../../scripts/audit_use_tool_predicate_surface_v1.py), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/use_tool_predicate_surface_v1_20260928.json)).

**Decision recommendation:** do not implement an unconditional ban or treat registration as proof of purity. Add explicit handler contracts separating predicate-safe deterministic handlers from effect-capable handlers; reject or quarantine unclassified handlers in predicates, and represent mutable external data through versioned graph facts or an explicit invalidation key. Before changing runtime behavior, run a source-locked full-boot compatibility probe for the nine `figure_grounding` rules, exercise each handler for repeatability/order effects on fixed inputs, and compare predicate results and final graph against the current path. Preserve a compatibility arm for handlers that cannot yet satisfy the contract. The unresolved tractability issue is invalidation: external changes must wake affected predicates without restoring global rescans. Record call counts and affected-rule counts across repeated and externally changed settles, then measure the false-stability and recomputation tradeoff.

**Handler-source qualification:** the registered symbolic handlers are read-only in their intended lookup semantics, but their results depend on external corpus files and some first-use paths have process or filesystem effects. `domains.dict_teacher._wordnet()` downloads WordNet and OMW when absent and caches the corpus in `_WN`; `text_valence` goes through `_opinion()`, which downloads the NLTK opinion lexicon on a miss and caches it in `_OPINION`. Wiktionary and ConceptNet handlers query local mmap slabs; a missing slab can produce empty/negative lookup results. Thus “predicate-safe” requires a pinned resource snapshot and controlled initialization, not just absence of graph writes. The fixed-corpus lexical/set handlers (`is_extreme`, `is_minimizer`, `is_intensifier_spike`, `text_severe`) have no such resource dependency. This is source review, not a dynamic repeatability audit; the next probe must vary resource availability/version and cold versus warm process state ([WordNet loader](../../../domains/dict_teacher.py), [symbolic handlers](../../../domains/symbolic_perception.py), [Wiktionary lookup](../../../domains/wiktionary_reference.py), [ConceptNet lookup](../../../domains/conceptnet_reference.py)).

**UseTool handler resource probe v1.2 (2026-09-28):** three fresh offline workers pass all seven gates with source and resource fingerprints stable. Fourteen of 15 handlers return the same output twice and across all workers for the frozen representative inputs. `text_valence` errors on both calls in every worker and attempts `nltk.download("opinion_lexicon")` twice, because failed initialization does not cache the result. The corpus probe corrected an earlier false absence report: WordNet and OMW are present as ZIP archives and their representative handlers succeed offline; the opinion lexicon is absent. SentiWordNet fallback behavior is untested by the chosen early-exit derive-opposes case. v1's failed import pilot and v1.1's incomplete resource lock remain preserved; v1.2 is the analyzed capture. **External resource invalidation probe v1 (2026-09-28):** three fresh locked workers pass all nine integrity and behavioral gates. With a file-backed `UseTool` predicate, an initial external value `0` is evaluated once and rejected. Changing only the file to `1` causes zero callbacks, zero graph progress, and no accepted marker. Changing it back to `0` while adding a new matching graph edge causes two callbacks for two matches, both reading the current value. Static access marks the rule `reads_any=true`, so graph changes can wake the predicate; external file changes have no corresponding engine event. This directly establishes missing external invalidation for this synthetic rule path and means “resource-versioned input” must be represented in graph state or explicitly trigger reevaluation. Next compare a resource-version fact plus scoped reevaluation against the current wildcard path, including correctness on positive-to-negative changes and effect retraction/compensation semantics ([results](SUBSTRATE_EXTERNAL_RESOURCE_INVALIDATION_PROBE_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/external_resource_invalidation_probe_v1_20260928.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/external_resource_invalidation_probe_v1_analysis_20260928.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_external_resource_invalidation_probe_v1.py)).

**Resource-version plus scoped invalidation v1.2 (2026-09-28):** all nine preregistered gates pass in three fresh workers at N=4/16/64, with paired global and caller-selected per-Microtheory closure. Global update callback counts are 2N (8/32/128); scoped counts remain four. At N=64 median update time is ~3.05 ms global and ~0.245 ms scoped, descriptive only. This demonstrates a viable explicit representation and scheduling seam for this authored partition, not an automatic watcher or a total engine complexity bound. Scoped closure still enumerates active rules, and callback invocation is repeated within fixpoint execution. v1.1's initial/external-only analyzer gate failed because it inspected final state; the capture and correction are disclosed and v1.2 adds phase-local graph snapshots. **External effect compensation v1 (2026-09-28):** all eight gates pass in three fresh workers. **T2 trace/work counter reconciliation v1 (2026-09-28, post-hoc):** an independent analyzer crosswalks the retained `describe_scene` whole-request capture against aggregate trace rows and native counters. All three audited workers reproduce 1,140,892 weighted trace events and five effect-event families exactly match their separate counters (edge upsert/delete, node mint/delete, attribute write). The capture also exposes 419/678,432 unattributed candidate tests and 2,461/3,676,862 unattributed Term evaluations; scheduler slot/enumeration/pass and deferred queue counters are reported separately because the trace has no matching scheduler event family. **T2 live operation-work attribution diagnostic v1 (2026-09-28):** on a full `describe_scene` request, three workers reproduce 21 `run_rules` operation IDs and identical scoped work totals. **T3 finite-key closure status (2026-09-28):** the restricted finite-key monotone insertion gate now has a finite-progress proposition, conservative checker, generated accepted/refused grammar execution, parser crosswalk, hardening, and same-schema native scaling through N=64. Remaining T3 work is scheduler/access completeness, least-fixed-point semantics, construction-time integration, and broader interaction/dependency families; unrestricted fresh-name minting remains open.
