**Code-composition refusal gate (2026-09-28):** two workers pass 2/2 supported positives and typed-refuse all ten authored negative checks, including ambiguous/dynamic module names, recursion/depth, unsupported helper shapes, and bool/string/out-of-i64 bitwise inputs. The effectful helper’s sentinel remains absent. This closes the named emitter refusal probes only; it is not an OS containment result or general guarantee. The preregistered module-held-out and independent licensed-project panels are now complete; their low candidate diversity is documented, so the next code gate needs a broader justified AST grammar or a task sample whose eligibility is independent of current emitter coverage ([refusal results](SUBSTRATE_CODE_COMPOSITION_REFUSAL_PANEL_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [same-project held-out results](SUBSTRATE_CODE_MODULE_HELDOUT_PANEL_V1_1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [independent-project results](SUBSTRATE_INDEPENDENT_PROJECT_CODE_PANEL_V1_1_RESULTS_20260928.md)).

Four runtime source files and one loaded seed differ from v1, and the ambiguous-name refusal path remains untested. The adversarial refusal panel is now complete, and the module-held-out panel returns 27/27 exact outputs on three functions from one CPython module. **Borrowed scoped-rule optimization confirmation (2026-09-26):** both scoped APIs now use ordered borrowed references rather than clone active rule bodies. No-op setup slopes fall 8.1–8.5× with audit off (180→21 ns/rule basic; 189→23 ns/rule report). The v2 no-op, topology, and per-rule analyses pass 294/294, 480/480, and 180/180 gates respectively, including exact projections, notification/omission controls, original indices `{0,2,3,4}`, and counter conservation. At N=64 the event/full candidate-work ratios are unchanged at 1.88×/17.79×/68.61× for chain/tree/star, so the optimization closes setup-copy cost but leaves topology-sensitive repeated matching untouched. See [results](SUBSTRATE_BORROWED_SCOPED_RULES_RESULTS_20260926.md), [confirmation lock](SUBSTRATE_BORROWED_SCOPED_RULES_CONFIRMATION_PREREG_20260926.md), and the linked v2 analyses.

**Scoped local-candidate seeding (2026-09-26):** a narrowly gated one-edge ownership seed passes 606/606 amended gates with source/native provenance. At N=64 event/full candidate ratios are 0.080 chain, 0.809 binary tree, and 15.89 star; audit-instrumented wall ratios are 0.357, 3.077, and 18.53. The chain benefits; tree candidate savings do not overcome scheduler cost, and star fanout remains a regression. Deletions, edge-slot reuse, and multiedge rules exercise the conservative full-match fallback. Next attribute queue turns, notifications, and repeated ownership requeues, then test hub-aware batching/coalescing with full semantic parity. Do not generalize these authored topologies to natural frames ([results](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_LOCAL_CANDIDATES_RESULTS_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_LOCAL_CANDIDATE_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_frame_topology_local_candidates_v3_1_20260926_analysis.json)).

**Scoped notification/requeue attribution (2026-09-26):** five-repeat per-turn and per-owner traces pass 666/666 gates with exact provenance and counter conservation. All topologies take four frame turns per frame over the two transitions, half no-progress; duplicate notification suppression is zero, while each frame self-requeues after its scoped call. At N=64, star queue depth reaches 64 and the root owns 6,337/14,123 candidates and 48,329/106,927 Term evaluations. This points to two targets: verify safe suppression of same-frame notifications after local fixpoint, and reduce repeated high-degree hub scans. These are synthetic attribution results only ([results](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_NOTIFICATION_REQUEUE_ATTRIBUTION_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_NOTIFICATION_REQUEUE_ATTRIBUTION_PREREG_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_scoped_notification_requeue_attribution_v1_20260926_analysis.json)).

**Guarded self-requeue suppression pilot (2026-09-26):** the runner-only guard suppresses a current-owner enqueue only when the owner Microtheory and direct `has_concept` membership are unchanged across the scoped call. Five repeats over chain/tree/star at 8–64 frames pass against the frozen baseline raw/analysis and exact full-closure projections; all non-self notifications remain unchanged. The ownership-change control adds a new `has_concept` member, retains the self-requeue, processes that member, and matches full closure. A delayed-writer adversary makes B notify previously settled A; the guarded run processes A→B→A and matches both baseline and full closure. At N=64, per-transition candidate reductions are 29.3%/27.4%/5.4% and audit-on wall ratios 0.619/0.621/0.760 for chain/tree/star. This supports the guarded policy on the measured fixtures only. Next test edge/node deletion and reuse, dynamic dependency changes, deferred effects, and multi-frame feedback, then verify an equivalent owner-saturation contract at a real scoped call site before any opt-in engine integration ([results](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_SELF_REQUEUE_SUPPRESSION_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_SELF_REQUEUE_SUPPRESSION_PREREG_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_scoped_self_requeue_suppression_v1_20260926_analysis.json)).

**Production call-site audit (2026-09-26):** there is no production consumer of `run_rules_scoped_delta_report` under `domains/`, `substrate/`, or `worlds/`. The existing CAN `scoped_settle` wrapper makes one `run_rules_scoped` call per Microtheory and has no cross-frame notification queue, so there is no production self-enqueue to optimize. The self-requeue result remains harness-only; creating a production scheduler solely to apply it would not advance the substrate's current capability envelope. Continue adversarial notification measurements and move to the next open tractability/capability gate unless a real queued caller is introduced ([source audit](SUBSTRATE_SELF_REQUEUE_CALLSITE_AUDIT_20260926.md)).

**GenInfer pattern-structure factorial (2026-09-26):** a 4×3 design varies four asymmetric 2-D point sets and shared/paired/unique predicate labels at fixed four relations, B=4, and 6,560 candidates. All 60 calls recover `[2,1,1,1]`; the independent analyzer passes 10 integrity/semantic/schedule checks. Median-of-cell latencies are 7.40 ms shared, 7.59 ms paired, and 11.50 ms unique predicates (unique/shared ≈1.55×); geometry spread within grouping is ≤6.5% in these five-repeat samples. This suggests predicate matching complexity may matter more than these small coordinate-set changes, but timing is exploratory. Next replicate with more repeats and a negative control, then test a distinct transform family and full seed/automatic mint acquisition cost before making rung-three claims ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_PATTERN_STRUCTURE_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_PATTERN_STRUCTURE_PREREG_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_pattern_structure_v1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**GenInfer transform-family extension (2026-09-26):** four invertible 2-D integer matrices over one four-relation unique-predicate signature are tested at fixed B=4/6,560 candidates, five calls each. All 20 calls recover the exact locked matrix and all 11 integrity/semantic/schedule checks pass. Median latencies range 11.18–11.68 ms with small overlapping ranges and no resolved transform-family ordering. This expands positive operator coverage without testing noise or acquisition cost. Next add null/noise arms across transform families and measure full recognize/mint/reuse cost, rather than extrapolating from direct calls ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_TRANSFORM_FAMILY_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_TRANSFORM_FAMILY_PREREG_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_transform_family_v1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**GenInfer selected-null refusal and semantic boundary (2026-09-26):** two retained 100-call factorial captures test positive recovery and four selected null classes over the same four maps. Both captures recover positives 20/20 per family and refuse predicate corruption, missing relation, and extra relation 60/60 each. Both fail the all-null gate because every coordinate perturbation is still `explained=true` and returns the positive matrix. The initial origin perturbation is translation-equivalent under coordinate normalization; an amended p1 perturbation is also accepted, indicating that the boolean denotes a generator-plus-residual decomposition rather than matrix-only exact fit. This sharpens the next step: expose and measure residual transforms, then preregister distinct matrix-fit and decomposed-explanation criteria before calibrating broader noise. See [results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_NOISE_REFUSAL_RESULTS_20260926.md), [preregistration and amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_NOISE_REFUSAL_PREREG_20260926.md), and [v2 analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_noise_refusal_v2_analysis_20260926.json).

**GenInfer residual-semantics confirmation (2026-09-26):** a locked four-family × two-condition × five-repeat field audit passes all six gates. Exact positives have no residual transforms; each p1-perturbed target is decomposed into the expected recovered matrix plus one predicate-local `shift(+1)` residual on dimension 1. This resolves the previously ambiguous boolean semantics for this fixture: `explained=true` is decomposition acceptance, not exact fit by the matrix alone. This is a semantic contract result, not a broader soundness or noise-calibration claim ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_RESIDUAL_SEMANTICS_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_RESIDUAL_SEMANTICS_PREREG_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_residual_semantics_v1_analysis_20260926.json)). Next quantify residual decomposition precision/recall across perturbation families and integrate that distinction into full-seed mint/reuse measures.

**Repeated-predicate recovery factorial (2026-09-26):** a 3×5 geometry/perturbation sweep with five repeated calls per cell shows all positives recover the known matrix, while only 4/12 perturbed cells do so; 11/12 still return `explained=true`. Uniform perturbations preserve the generating matrix for two point groupings but select an alternate for the third; inconsistent perturbations yield alternate matrices or refusal. The v1 fixed `checked=6,560` gate failed on one data-dependent search-bound cell (14,640); the failed analysis is retained and a v1.1 amendment validates positivity and within-cell stability instead. This makes the matrix-recovery/decomposition distinction operational but does not establish natural-noise accuracy. Next use more relations and held-out relations to separate generator identification from residual fitting, then carry the scoring into full-seed acquisition ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_REPEATED_PREDICATE_RECOVERY_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_REPEATED_PREDICATE_RECOVERY_PREREG_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_REPEATED_PREDICATE_RECOVERY_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_repeated_predicate_recovery_v1_20260926.json), [amended analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_repeated_predicate_recovery_v1_1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**GenInfer held-out relation diagnostic (2026-09-26):** across three predicate geometries, three training conditions, two held-out conditions, and five repeats (90 calls), every clean-training/clean-holdout case predicts both unseen relations. A learned p0 shift transfers to shifted p0 holdouts and systematically mispredicts clean p0 holdouts. Under inconsistent training, two geometries refuse; the third retains the true matrix plus a shift that does not predict clean heldouts. A separate scorer applies the returned matrix/residuals to withheld rows, so these are actual held-out relation outcomes rather than `explained` proxies. This remains a tiny controlled evaluator result. Next score the same distinction through production full-seed recognition/mint/reuse and measure acquisition cost and false residual transfer ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_HELDOUT_RELATION_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_HELDOUT_RELATION_PREREG_20260926.md), [runner](../../../scripts/geninfer_heldout_relation_probe_v1.py), [independent analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_geninfer_heldout_relation_probe_v1.py), [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_heldout_relation_v1_20260926.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_heldout_relation_v1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**Full-seed GenMint held-out transfer (2026-09-26):** 180 production-path sequences cover three predicate layouts, three training conditions, two held-out conditions, induction on/off, and five repeats. Every clean-training/clean-heldout enabled case mints `[1,1,0,2]`, re-decodes without a quantum, selects that acquired generator on the separately staged held-out base, and predicts both held-out rows. Uniform-shift training also transfers the generator to clean heldouts in all 15 paired sequences; inconsistent training mints it in only one layout. Route-aware analysis finds every heldout status `recognized_transformed`, including induction-disabled controls, because the two-row heldout pattern is also explained by held `scale2`; each shifted heldout selects `scale2` rather than the learned matrix. Median clean training closure is 32.79 ms enabled vs 1.21 ms disabled, descriptive on this run. The initial analyzer's denominator issue is preserved and corrected by a disclosed v1.1 amendment. Evidence is a controlled acquisition/transfer mechanism plus a serious baseline-confounding finding, not general capability gain. Next enlarge and discriminate the heldout pattern, then measure a paired reuse/amortization curve and memory cost ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_HELDOUT_TRANSFER_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_HELDOUT_TRANSFER_PREREG_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_HELDOUT_TRANSFER_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [runner](../../../scripts/genmint_heldout_transfer_probe_v1.py), [amended analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_genmint_heldout_transfer_probe_v1_1.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_heldout_transfer_v1_20260926.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_heldout_transfer_v1_1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**Full-seed GenMint four-relation transfer confirmation v2 (2026-09-26):** the 180-sequence follow-up uses four held-out relations, two under each predicate, and a matched no-induction arm. All 15 clean-training/clean-heldout enabled sequences use the matrix minted during training and predict all four held-out relations (60/60 rows); disabled controls mint a quantum at both stages and acquire no expected matrix. Uniformly shifted training transfers the matrix to clean heldouts in another 15/15 sequences. Inconsistent training acquires the expected matrix in 10/30 enabled sequences and mints a quantum in the other 20. Median clean closure is 24.69 ms enabled vs 0.80 ms disabled in this run. The initial analyzer used a two-row denominator and its source snapshot was not retained; this provenance failure is disclosed, its initial analysis preserved, and route-aware v2.1 reanalysis passes all checks. This remains one authored matrix family; the `scale2` alias is absent from the clean positive arms but other held dimensions still affect perturbed cases. Next vary matrices/geometries and reuse count, including source-complete analyzer snapshots and acquisition/application cost ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_HELDOUT_TRANSFER_V2_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_HELDOUT_TRANSFER_V2_PREREG_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_HELDOUT_TRANSFER_V2_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [runner](../../../scripts/genmint_heldout_transfer_probe_v2.py), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_genmint_heldout_transfer_probe_v2_1.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_heldout_transfer_v2_20260926.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_heldout_transfer_v2_1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**Matrix × predicate-layout fixture-selection pilot (2026-09-26):** one clean full-seed run across three matrices and three layouts acquires the prior matrix and `shearA` in all layouts; `shearB` is acquired in two layouts but not `adjacent_01`, despite that observation reaching `recognized_transformed`. This unregistered pilot provides no rate estimate, but it identifies a necessary negative cell and confirms that capability scoring must inspect the minted matrix rather than terminal status. Preserve it as fixture-selection only; preregister the full matrix/layout/held-out/reuse factorial before any confirmatory expansion ([exploratory results](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_MATRIX_LAYOUT_EXPLORATORY_RESULTS_20260926.md), [runner](../../../scripts/genmint_matrix_layout_exploratory_v1.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_matrix_layout_exploratory_v1_20260926.json)).

**Full-seed GenMint matrix/layout and reuse-cost confirmation (2026-09-26):** the preregistered 360-worker sweep passes all 14 integrity/analysis gates. The expected matrix is acquired in 40/45 enabled training sequences per K prefix: all prior-matrix and `shearA` layouts, and two of three `shearB` layouts; `shearB × adjacent_01` again fails acquisition despite its recognized status. Every one of 280 held-out calls routed to a training-acquired matrix exactly predicts all four held-out rows (1,120/1,120); application-minted or application-reused generators and no-generator routes are not credited as training transfer. Enabled runs avoid CapabilityAxis quanta in the measured sequence, while disabled controls use a median 1/2/3/5 quanta for K=0/1/2/4. Median cumulative closure remains higher with induction enabled at each K (3.80/4.61/5.64/7.61 ms vs 0.87/1.73/2.78/5.64 ms); only 1/45 matched pairs are faster by K=4, with no median crossover in any matrix/layout stratum. This demonstrates authored-family acquisition and exact reuse, but not amortized runtime savings, natural-task prevalence, or asymptotic scaling. Next extend reuse count, separate training induction from held-structure application and fixed closure, broaden matrices/geometries, and measure actual separator width/factorized execution on representative workload graphs ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_MATRIX_REUSE_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_MATRIX_REUSE_PREREG_20260926.md), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/genmint_matrix_reuse_lock_20260926.json), [runner](../../../scripts/genmint_matrix_reuse_probe_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_genmint_matrix_reuse_probe_v1.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_matrix_reuse_v1_20260926.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_matrix_reuse_v1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**Full-seed GenMint extended-horizon v2 (2026-09-26):** a 540-worker extension measures K={0,1,2,4,8,16} with 16 deterministic held-out shapes and records training and held-out closure stages separately. The first analyzer incorrectly expected 90 instead of 108 cells; its failed output is preserved, and a separate corrected v2.1 analyzer passes all 16 checks without changing raw data or outcome criteria. Expected-matrix training acquisition again occurs in 40/45 cases per K. Conditional on acquiring during training, all 1,240 held-out calls across the sweep predict their four rows exactly (4,960/4,960). Median training closure is about 3.8 ms enabled vs 0.88 ms disabled; application-only medians at K=16 are 27.4 vs 42.0 ms. The pooled paired runtime median crosses at K=16 (−9.94 ms), while the acquisition-conditional comparison crosses at K=8 (−0.21 ms); prior-matrix strata do not cross through K=16. In the persistent `shearB × adjacent_01` miss, acquisition is deferred to the first held-out task and costs 548–595 ms before later tasks reuse the new generator at roughly 0.8–1.6 ms. This supports amortization on selected authored families and exposes a substantial latency tail; it does not establish natural-task frequency or general learning economics. Next vary transform families/geometries and preregister the deferred-acquisition distribution, while separately executing the planned structural census on representative workloads ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_MATRIX_REUSE_V2_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_MATRIX_REUSE_V2_PREREG_20260926.md), [analysis amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_MATRIX_REUSE_V2_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/genmint_matrix_reuse_v2_lock_20260926.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_matrix_reuse_v2_20260926.json), [corrected analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_matrix_reuse_v2_1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**GenInfer residual-envelope extension (2026-09-26):** 110 field observations across five repeats pass all 12 integrity/semantic gates. Evidence now covers numeric global shifts, symbolic substitution, two residual entries under `max_dims=2`, refusal at `max_dims=1`, and refusal of a conflicting symbolic mapping. A repeated-predicate numeric corruption instead selects a stable alternative matrix `[-2,-2,0,2]` with p0/p1-local residuals, although the target was generated from `[1,1,0,2]`. Thus residual support can trade off with the inferred generator; decomposition acceptance is not generator-recovery accuracy under inconsistent observations. Next sweep repeated-predicate geometry and corruption magnitude, then quantify exact-matrix recovery separately from decomposition acceptance and test downstream mint/reuse effects ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_RESIDUAL_ENVELOPE_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_RESIDUAL_ENVELOPE_PREREG_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_residual_envelope_v1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**GenInfer repeated-predicate robustness surface (2026-09-26):** the preregistered 3-layout × 4-condition × 5-repeat sweep passes all eight integrity/determinism gates. All 15 positives recover `[1,1,0,2]`; among 45 localized numeric corruptions, 20 are accepted, 25 refused, and only 5 accepted cases retain the generating matrix. Acceptance and matrix recovery vary non-monotonically with corruption magnitude and geometry: in the original geometry +2 recovers the generator while +1/+3 select other matrices; orthogonal-pair corruptions all refuse; paired-square +2 accepts an alternate matrix while +1/+3 refuse. Candidate count is 624 for both bounded geometries and 6,560 for the original. This is a measured synthetic surface, not a natural-noise error estimate. Next characterize the matching/ranking cause for the non-monotonic transitions and test end-to-end mint/reuse sensitivity ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_REPEAT_PREDICATE_ROBUSTNESS_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_REPEAT_PREDICATE_ROBUSTNESS_PREREG_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_repeat_predicate_robustness_v1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**GenInfer robustness mechanism audit (2026-09-26):** source-linked analysis rules out search-bound exclusion for this suite: B is 2 or 4 and the generating matrix coefficients all lie within the enumerated cube. The observed non-monotonicity follows the combination of canonical positional pairing after separately sorting held and observed relations, predicate-local residual consistency, and the Occam ranking by residual count then matrix L1 norm. In the original layout, +1/+3 perturbations reorder duplicate-predicate rows into inconsistent aligned deltas, while +2 yields a consistent +1 residual; the paired-square +2 alternative wins with one residual and smaller matrix norm. This is a mechanism-level explanation grounded in source and fixture arithmetic, not a general theorem about recovery. The paired stable-ID ablation then partially changes the corrupted outcomes but leaves 15/45 alternate-matrix acceptances, including all original-layout corruptions. Next enumerate and score candidate decompositions under explicit identity alignment, then test downstream mint behavior ([robustness results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_REPEAT_PREDICATE_ROBUSTNESS_RESULTS_20260926.md), [identity-ablation results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_RELATION_IDENTITY_ABLATION_RESULTS_20260926.md), [implementation](../../../runners/dsl/src/shape_decode.rs), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_repeat_predicate_robustness_v1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**GenInfer stable-relation-identity ablation (2026-09-26):** the paired 120-observation capture preserves the prior no-ID arm exactly and passes positive, input, deterministic-repeat, and provenance gates, but fails the prediction that an unchanged ID field forces every corruption to refuse. Adding IDs reduces accepted corruptions from 20/45 to 15/45, yet all 15 accepted stable-ID cases use alternative matrices; the original geometry accepts all three corruptions in both modes, and its +2 case shifts from the true generator without IDs to an alternate with IDs. Stable alignment affects outcomes but does not remove generator/residual trade-offs. Preserve the failed prediction. A source-derived enumeration now matches all 18 native corrupted cells: stable IDs can make the true matrix ineligible; without IDs, paired-square +2 leaves 25 candidates and the L1 tie-break chooses an alternative over an eligible generator. Search bounds include the generator in every cell. See the [candidate-ranking reconstruction results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_CANDIDATE_RANKING_RECONSTRUCTION_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_CANDIDATE_RANKING_RECONSTRUCTION_PREREG_20260926.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_candidate_ranking_v1_analysis_20260926.json); next measure end-to-end mint/reuse effects.

**Full-seed GenInfer residual-robustness evaluation (2026-09-26):** 240 fresh-core sequences (two closure stages each; five replicates across 3 layouts x 2 identity modes x 4 input conditions x GenInfer on/off) pass all nine integrity/provenance gates. The production seed's earlier held rungs preempt GenInfer on many cases; among 90 enabled corrupted first members, 35 finish transformed recognition, 55 mint a quantum, and 25 acquire a linear matrix (5 exact, 20 alternative). Every later clean M-squared member is recognized transformed in all 120 enabled sequences, including cases with a wrong first matrix; the 20 alternative-first cases have an additional generator by the end. Disabled controls mint 180 quanta versus 55 enabled across 120 two-observation sequences, while paired-square held transforms account for 40 no-difference controls. Enabled clean-M-squared closure latency has 0.572 ms median and 221.757 ms p90 (252.208 ms max), a small-fixture long tail consistent with occasional inference/search. This measures an authored seed path, not general learning accuracy. See [results](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_RESIDUAL_ROBUSTNESS_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_RESIDUAL_ROBUSTNESS_PREREG_20260926.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_residual_robustness_v1_analysis_20260926.json).

**Direct scoped snapshot clone timing and mutation audit (2026-09-26):** the diagnostic repeats the exact active-rule enumerate/filter/clone collection and drops the snapshot without executing rules. Across 60 same-build cells, snapshot timing is 86–95% of full scoped no-match call medians. For 1→8 effects/rule, snapshot-only increments are 4.1/18.6/36.4 μs versus full-call increments 4.2/16.6/37.5 μs at 64/256/512 rules. The source audit finds public direct mutation of `rules` and `active` in `cognitive_cycle.rs` and `wave_stencil.rs`, making retained cache invalidation unsafe without broader encapsulation. Next prototype a borrowed-rule scoped path (immutable rule refs plus disjoint mutable state fields), then gate with exact parity, stable original indices, tombstone, and mutation controls ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_SNAPSHOT_CLONE_COST_PREREG_20260926.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_SNAPSHOT_CLONE_COST_RESULTS_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_scoped_snapshot_clone_cost_v1_20260926_analysis.json)).

**Scoped rule-body factorial (2026-09-26):** 60 cells independently pass exact active/slot counts, zero-progress fixed point, unchanged graph, and zero candidate/Term/audit work. Increasing effects/rule from 1→8 adds 5.5/22.3/52.9 μs per call at 64/256/512 rules; increasing match edges/rule from 1→8 adds 3.1/10.1/19.8 μs. Both dimensions scale with rule count; effect payload is the stronger signal. The positive interaction is noisy. Because end-to-end calls include both snapshot cloning and matcher setup, this still does not isolate clone cost. Next instrument a narrow native clone-only diagnostic, compare against the measured end-to-end deltas, then choose whether snapshot reuse merits invalidation complexity ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_RULE_BODY_FACTORIAL_PREREG_20260926.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_RULE_BODY_FACTORIAL_RESULTS_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_scoped_rule_body_factorial_v1_20260926_analysis.json)).

**Scoped snapshot attribution follow-up (2026-09-26):** a 60-cell, five-repeat no-match sweep independently validates active/slot counts, unchanged state, zero progress, and zero candidate/Term work. Adding an equal number of tombstoned slots does not produce a stable cost increase. Increasing each active rule from one match edge/one effect to eight/eight adds 4.3, 28.0, and 63.9 μs/call at 64/256/512 active rules. Because pattern size and effect payload change together, this implicates active rule-body processing but does not isolate clone cost. Next run a factorial pattern-edge × effect-count probe, then select a clone/snapshot optimization only if the payload axis supports it. See [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_RULE_SNAPSHOT_ATTRIBUTION_PREREG_20260926.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_RULE_SNAPSHOT_ATTRIBUTION_RESULTS_20260926.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_scoped_rule_snapshot_attribution_v1_20260926_analysis.json).

**Scoped audit parity and no-op setup envelope (2026-09-26):** the audit-on/off chain/tree/star probe passes 135/135 checks for semantic parity; measured instrumentation ratios are 1.12×–1.23× on this N=64 synthetic workload. A separate seven-repeat no-match sweep passes 294/294 checks and shows scoped-call latency rising roughly linearly with active-rule count: fitted slopes are 180–210 ns/rule through 512 rules, while warmed full-report calls stay around 3.3–4.2 μs. This is setup/dispatch scaling; no candidate or Term evaluation occurs, and the measurement does not attribute cost exclusively to cloning. Next profile and prototype a reusable eligible-rule view/cursor with invalidation controls, then rerun the matched topology matrix with instrumentation-off timing and exact parity gates. See [audit parity results](SUBSTRATE_SCOPE_AUDIT_ON_OFF_PARITY_RESULTS_20260926.md), [no-op setup results](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_NOOP_SETUP_COST_RESULTS_20260926.md), their protocols, and independent analyses ([audit](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_scope_audit_on_off_parity_v1_20260926_analysis.json), [no-op](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_scoped_noop_setup_cost_v1_20260926_analysis.json)).

**Scoped cost-attribution instrumentation audit and repair (2026-09-26):** the v1 capture confirmed no per-rule rows on the scoped path despite nonzero global work; v1.1 adds current-rule accounting keyed by original rule slots. A tombstoned-slot control confirms active indices `{0,2,3,4}` remain correctly attributed, per-rule candidate/where/Term sums conserve global counters, and all 30 N=64 event/full pairs preserve state parity and settlement. Per-rule work attributes the tree/star cost gap primarily to repeated propagation-rule matching (up to 127.5× candidate work for star `propagate_on`). The v1 failed capture and source/binary snapshots remain archived. Next directly compare audit-on/off state, then measure empty/no-match scoped-call setup versus active-rule count; do not infer active-rule clone overhead from the existing timing ratios ([v1.0 gap and v1.1 results](SUBSTRATE_FRAME_TOPOLOGY_COST_ATTRIBUTION_RESULTS_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_FRAME_TOPOLOGY_COST_ATTRIBUTION_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [v1.1 analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_frame_topology_cost_attribution_v1_1_analysis_20260926.json)).

**Matched topology scaling gate (2026-09-26):** 60 five-repeat event/full pairs across chain, binary-tree, and star graphs (N=8/16/32/64) pass state parity, exact changed-owner coverage, omission sensitivity, fixed-point, and audit-integrity gates. The native counters expose a topology-sensitive cost failure: event candidate work is 907→60,995 and is identical across shapes at each N, while full closure at N=64 is 32,385/3,429/889 candidates for chain/tree/star. Event/full candidate ratios are 1.88×/17.79×/68.61× respectively; instrumented wall ratios are 1.90×/16.57×/46.89×. The current scoped runner full-matches and filters most rules, clones the active rule list per call, and has no scoped cursor reuse (source comments mark it correct but not fast); event turns are 4N. Next quantify which cost component dominates with a scoped-matching implementation experiment: compare current path to a per-scope eligible-candidate index/cursor with parity and invalidation controls, then rerun this locked topology matrix and instrumentation-off timings. Keep natural-task partition quality as a separate later gate ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_FRAME_TOPOLOGY_MATCHED_SCALE_PREREG_20260926.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_FRAME_TOPOLOGY_MATCHED_SCALE_RESULTS_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_frame_topology_matched_scale_v1_20260926_analysis.json), [scoped runner source](../../../runners/dsl/src/rewrite.rs)).

**Scoped notification fanout scaling (2026-09-26):** five-repeat N=2/4/8/16/32/64 star-fanout probes pass exact owner notification, omission sensitivity, event/full projection parity, and termination gates. Event scheduling is slower than full closure at every size (median 0.152 ms vs 0.083 ms at N=2; 9.445 ms vs 0.724 ms at N=64); report turns rise 8→256 while full progress steps remain 5 on this tiny generated workload. This separates scheduler correctness from efficiency and shows that complete notifications do not imply tractable speedup. Next compare sparse/local, bounded-separator, and high-fanout topologies at matched node/rule counts, capture candidate/evaluation counters, then test structurally generated partitions on authored tasks. No natural workload or asymptotic claim follows ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_NOTIFICATION_FANOUT_SCALE_PREREG_20260926.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_NOTIFICATION_FANOUT_SCALE_RESULTS_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_scoped_notification_fanout_scale_v1_20260926_analysis.json)).

The first pilot exposed a symmetric-binding ambiguity, preserved with its exact runner and raw failure; the preregistered v1.1 amendment adds role guards without changing gates. Arbitrary-degree effects and general scheduler completeness remain open. All 40 per-cell gates pass: exact birth/deletion notification owners, event/full projection parity, queue completion, dependency creation/removal, full fixed points, and sensitivity to omission of each individual target notification. Birth/deletion queue turns each scale 6/10/18/34; candidate and Term counts are zero for this small fixture, so this is owner-dispatch mechanism evidence, not a speedup result. In both transitions, A/B notifications are exact; consuming them settles the event queue to the same projected state as monolithic closure, while omitting the external trigger's initial A seed stays detectably stale. This closes only the controlled ownership/effect/queue mechanism case. Caller seeding of external changes, root-frame deletion/repartitioning, arbitrary deferred effects, general scheduler completeness, and natural-task prevalence remain open. Next extend controlled mutation coverage to multiple incident dependency edges and then validate automatically generated frame partitions against full closure on matched task distributions ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_NODE_LIFECYCLE_PREREG_20260926.md), [result](SUBSTRATE_SCOPED_NODE_LIFECYCLE_RESULTS_20260926.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_scoped_node_lifecycle_probe_v1.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_scoped_node_lifecycle_probe_v1_20260926.json), [independent analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_scoped_node_lifecycle_probe_v1_20260926_analysis.json)).

**Status:** active measurement programme. The inventory, benchmark protocol, source-linked evidence map, and multiple structural, engine, learning, and scaling gates now have executable artifacts and bounded results recorded below. Open phases and unresolved gates remain; no current result supports an unqualified claim that the whole substrate is tractable or generally capable.

**Phase A entrypoint and ownership audit (2026-09-25):** the source-linked map now contains callable entrypoints, activation/path notes, canonical state owners, and host-shadow/index notes for all 15 capability rows. The generated JSON resolves 70 source references and the audit records 82 normal/measurement entrypoints plus 69 alternate or diagnostic paths. The builder rejects missing row-level callable, owner, or resolvable source-anchor data. This closes the inventory's callable/ownership checklist items; it does not establish that each route is complete, default in every application, or covered by current tests. Test/evidence provenance and complete host/native route verification remain open. See [`SUBSTRATE_CAPABILITY_MAP.md`](SUBSTRATE_CAPABILITY_MAP.md), [`capability_map.json`](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/capability_map.json), and [`build_substrate_capability_map.py`](../../../scripts/build_substrate_capability_map.py).

Current map validation covers all 15 rows, with 41 test references, 119 result-document references, 50 protocol/lock references, 107 raw/analysis references, and 168 runner/analyzer references; no row lacks a linked test, source link, or required evidence field. These are references, not unique artifacts or coverage claims: every row remains marked `linked_tests_present; coverage not audited`. After source-anchor repair, 13/16 capability rows have candidate call-name matches, two have only generic-name matches, and one (planning/action selection) has no linked-test call matching its source-linked bounded-planner functions. Its linked Python tests validate proposal/runtime-closure protocol records; they are not planner execution tests. **Seed-index cold/warm full-state verification (2026-09-25):** after the schema-v5 serialization-order repair, the V3 frozen-corpus probe confirms equality of seed-load order, active rule order, ProblemShape indices, complete serialized graph state, grammar, exported rule store, and rule access sets across separate cold and warm boots. The corpus produced 24,784 nodes, 11,090 edges, 2,289 active rules, and 11 identical seed-load failures. This establishes cold/warm state parity for this corpus, not all loader lifecycle behavior. Next isolate schema/source invalidation, truncated or digest-invalid cache rebuild, and simultaneous cold writers; retain exact boot-state fingerprints as the oracle ([repair results](SUBSTRATE_SEED_INDEX_CACHE_ORDER_FIX_V2_RESULTS.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_seed_index_cache_state_probe_v3.py), [report](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_seed_index_cache_state_probe_v3_20260925.json)).

**Seed-index cache recovery/concurrency follow-up (2026-09-25):** on an isolated hardlink copy of the same corpus, v4-schema, malformed-JSON, and bad-payload-digest cache entries all rebuild to the baseline complete graph/grammar/rule/access/order fingerprints. Two simultaneous cold builders produce the same state, leave a usable cache, and a subsequent warm load matches. A separate content-invalidation probe appends a JSON whitespace newline to one manifest, verifies that the source digest changes, and confirms the complete boot-state fingerprint remains identical after rebuild. Concurrent writers during independent source mutation and downstream order-sensitive task parity remain open. This is focused loader reliability evidence, not application-level semantic parity ([repair results](SUBSTRATE_SEED_INDEX_CACHE_ORDER_FIX_V2_RESULTS.md), [lifecycle runner](../../../scripts/substrate_seed_index_cache_lifecycle_probe_v1.py), [lifecycle report](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_seed_index_cache_lifecycle_probe_v1_20260925.json), [invalidation runner](../../../scripts/substrate_seed_index_source_invalidation_probe_v1.py), [invalidation report](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_seed_index_source_invalidation_v1_20260925.json)).

**Seed-index cache application parity gate (2026-09-25):** a new-source-locked four-worker comparison checks cold and warm cache boots on recognition and recurrent-residual ProblemShape workloads at N=32. All four fresh processes pass authored task/fixed-point criteria; within each mix, full task/order/work projections match exactly. Candidate pairs, Term evaluations, task outcomes, mints, and final codebook size are identical across cache states. Boot takes 24–29 seconds and summed task observations 0.8–1.1 seconds per process; this is one run per cell and not a cache speedup estimate. Loader stage profiling and repeated startup measurements become explicit scaling work; broad corpus/domain parity remains open ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_SEED_INDEX_COLD_WARM_PROBLEM_SHAPE_PREREG_20260925.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_SEED_INDEX_COLD_WARM_PROBLEM_SHAPE_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_seed_index_cold_warm_problem_shape_v1_20260925.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/seed_index_cold_warm_problem_shape_lock_20260925.json)).

**Full seed-boot stage profile (2026-09-25):** four profiled cold/warm/warm/cold boots over the locked 833-manifest corpus produce identical full state. cProfile attributes 3.63–4.38 s to cold index read/build versus 0.37–0.39 s warm, while 748 native manifest loads take 9.83–11.82 cumulative seconds and the boot-time self-model mirror takes 12.51–13.86 seconds (overlapping profiler intervals). JSON decoding and native `export_rules` are also material. This says cache rebuild is only one part of startup and identifies post-load provenance as a cost worth evaluating against its capability contract; it does not show that the work is unnecessary. Stage wall times include cProfile overhead. A source consumer audit and six-run unprofiled startup repeat now follow; test any lazy alternative only under exact self-query and boot-state parity ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_SEED_BOOT_PROFILE_PREREG_20260925.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_SEED_BOOT_PROFILE_RESULTS.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_seed_boot_profile_v1.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_seed_boot_profile_v1_20260925.json)).

**Self-model mirror consumer audit (2026-09-25):** source review finds RuleSummary consumers in real self-query, conversation action, reflective rule/threshold/edit selection, frozen-core provenance gates, collapse checks, and rule/seed signature enrichment. Some reflective call paths can mint a narrower summary on demand, but that does not establish parity with the full native-rule and graph-rule mirror or ProgramSummary population. This is source-path evidence, not exhaustive runtime demand or a claim that eager construction can be removed. Any deferral experiment must preserve all those behavior and fail-closed provenance contracts ([consumer audit](SUBSTRATE_SELF_MODEL_BOOT_CONSUMER_AUDIT.md)).

**Unprofiled startup repeats (2026-09-25):** three cold and three warm fresh processes on the same frozen corpus all produce identical full boot state. Median wall startup is 32.18 s cold and 26.75 s warm; observed ranges are 30.57–33.32 s and 26.13–27.96 s. Imports and domain tasks are excluded. This is a small single-host repeat envelope, not a general speedup or scaling claim; warm startup remains costly. Broader corpus-size sweeps and attribution by import, install, and self-model mirror remain open ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_SEED_BOOT_UNPROFILED_REPEATS_PREREG_20260925.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_SEED_BOOT_UNPROFILED_REPEATS_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_seed_boot_unprofiled_repeats_v1_20260925.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/seed_boot_unprofiled_repeats_lock_20260925.json)).

**Nested prefix boot scale envelope (2026-09-25):** 16 fresh boots across 128/256/512/737 indexed IDs (two cold and two warm per size) preserve exact full state within each size. The locked 833 physical manifests map to 737 bulk-index IDs; the largest subset retains all physical files. N=128/256 use 3,725/6,264 graph nodes, 390/615 active rules, and ~571 MiB process peak RSS. N=512 jumps to 20,757 nodes, 1,806 active rules, 1,837 RuleSummary nodes, and ~1.56 GiB RSS; median wall rises from 1.86 s at N=256 to 26.78 s cold / 22.70 s warm. The full 737-ID corpus reaches 24,784 nodes, 2,289 active rules, 2,331 RuleSummary nodes, and ~1.67 GiB RSS; its observed boot is faster than N=512, so timing is non-monotone and does not establish asymptotic growth. The independent source census attributes a major payload covariate to IDs 257–512 (258,992,525 bytes); `grounded_lexicon.json` alone is 110,731,329 bytes and contains a nested 2,501-node graph. Source confirms the entire manifest is generic-JSON-converted at the PyO3 call boundary before Rust consumes a narrower documented field set. This is a candidate decoding/serialization cost, not yet causal or safe-to-remove evidence. Next compare a native-boundary projection that retains full Python manifests under complete state and self-model parity, then remeasure matched prefix composition and repeat upper points under controlled host load ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_SEED_BOOT_PREFIX_SCALE_PREREG_20260925.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_SEED_BOOT_PREFIX_SCALE_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_seed_boot_prefix_scale_v1_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_seed_boot_prefix_scale_v1_analysis_20260925.json), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_substrate_seed_boot_prefix_scale_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/seed_boot_prefix_scale_lock_20260925.json)).

**Native seed-boundary projection intervention (2026-09-25):** a source-locked control/projection comparison at N=512/737 (three fresh workers per arm/size) passes exact boot report, graph, grammar, rule store/access/order and self-model parity. Projecting the full Python manifest to the fields consumed by the PyO3 loader reduces serialized boundary payload by 68–70%, median measured boot wall by 19–22%, and median CPU by 18–22% in this instrumented corpus run. This localizes avoidable work to the native conversion boundary; it does not validate production change or explain the entire earlier non-monotonic scale jump. The diagnostic retains manifests until after the measured interval, inflating RSS to ~2.1–2.25 GiB, so peak memory is not an uninstrumented estimate. A source-hashed caller audit now identifies the common PyO3 seam, and the native implementation has passed the contract matrix and exact uninstrumented full-corpus parity gate; follow with representative domain-consumer parity and a quiet-host same-source before/after repeat ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_NATIVE_SEED_PROJECTION_PREREG_20260925.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_NATIVE_SEED_PROJECTION_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_native_seed_projection_probe_v1_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_native_seed_projection_probe_v1_analysis_20260925.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_native_seed_projection_probe_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_substrate_native_seed_projection_probe_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/native_seed_projection_lock_20260925.json)).

**Native seed manifest caller audit (2026-09-25):** a source-hashed AST census finds 922 direct syntactic calls across 633 Python files (173 under `domains/`, `substrate/`, and `worlds/`), with 356 test calls and 376 script calls including six calls in the contract probe. The PyO3 function was the shared seam and now applies the ten-key projection; the contract matrix and full cold/warm corpus parity pass. Static call counts do not establish runtime reachability or dynamic argument types. Continue with representative domain-consumer parity and a quiet-host same-source before/after repeat before making a durable speed claim ([audit](SUBSTRATE_NATIVE_SEED_CALLER_AUDIT.md), [raw census](../../../evaluation/reports/native_seed_manifest_caller_audit_v1_20260925.json), [auditor](../../../scripts/audit_native_seed_manifest_callers_v1.py)).

**Native seed projection integration (2026-09-25):** the release extension now projects at the PyO3 boundary; four no-wrapper full-corpus cold/warm workers exactly match the frozen pre-change report, graph, grammar, rule store/access/order, and active-rule state. A 28-case optional-field/error matrix passes, including unknown non-JSON metadata and unchanged caller dicts. Median startup is 14.33 s cold and 11.65 s warm with ~1.67 GiB whole-process high-water RSS. Several Python source files differ from the historical baseline, so this is a compatibility gate and current operating envelope rather than a controlled speed comparison; the equal-instrumentation experiment provides the narrower performance evidence ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_NATIVE_SEED_PROJECTION_INTEGRATION_PREREG_20260925.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_NATIVE_SEED_PROJECTION_INTEGRATION_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_native_seed_projection_integration_v1_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_native_seed_projection_integration_v1_analysis_20260925.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_native_seed_projection_integration_probe_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/native_seed_projection_integration_lock_20260925.json)).

**Purpose:** convert the tractability assessment into an executable research programme that measures what the substrate can do, where it works, how it fails, and how cost grows. The scope is the substrate as a whole: graph and rule execution, inference, perception/shape operations, memory, learning, planning, transfer, interfaces, reliability, and resource use. This plan complements [`TRACTABILITY_SUBSTRATE_ASSESSMENT.md`](TRACTABILITY_SUBSTRATE_ASSESSMENT.md); it does not replace the broader safety and progressive-agency gates in [`GENERAL_INTELLIGENCE_EXPANSION_PLAN.md`](GENERAL_INTELLIGENCE_EXPANSION_PLAN.md).

**Execution status (2026-09-24):** the initial capability inventory, benchmark protocol, schemas, and instrumentation audit exist. The first closure pilot exposed a cursor bug; the fix, focused regression, incremental-matching regression run, and path recheck are recorded in [`SUBSTRATE_CLOSURE_PILOT_RECHECK_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_CLOSURE_PILOT_RECHECK_RESULTS.md). Isolated path/banded-DAG/complete-DAG workers pass an independent oracle at small sizes, and an exploratory size sweep reaches n=96 on bounded-width families and n=64 on the dense control (see [`SUBSTRATE_CLOSURE_ISOLATED_PILOT_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_CLOSURE_ISOLATED_PILOT_RESULTS.md) and [`SUBSTRATE_CLOSURE_SCALE_PILOT_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_CLOSURE_SCALE_PILOT_RESULTS.md)). Candidate partitions and per-family native graph-effect counters reconcile; the existing graph_writes counter remains Python-boundary scoped. Edge, node, attribute, delete, and replacement effects have focused instrumentation coverage. A five-repeat audit-on/off overhead pilot preserves semantics on eight closure cases; observed ratios sit near 1 but are inconclusive and do not estimate the dormant instrumentation floor (see [`SUBSTRATE_AUDIT_OVERHEAD_PILOT_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_AUDIT_OVERHEAD_PILOT_RESULTS.md)). The harness records per-worker post-import, post-setup, and post-run RSS high-water marks; a new CAN fresh-process sweep provides three repeats per point through N=256 on sparse/banded graphs and N=128 on complete graphs, while higher-resolution allocation/heap measures remain open ([`SUBSTRATE_CAN_PROCESS_SCALE_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_CAN_PROCESS_SCALE_RESULTS.md)). The first broader rule-family pilot covers transitive closure, duplicate no-op, and bounded deduplicated minting across three graph topologies and two sizes; all 18 instances match their independent expected state and settle under a terminal probe ([`SUBSTRATE_RULE_FAMILY_PILOT_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_RULE_FAMILY_PILOT_RESULTS.md)). A follow-up repeated envelope adds duplicate no-op and bounded mint at n=16/32/64 with three workers per point; all 54 states settle exactly, and dense candidate/time costs rise with graph density ([`SUBSTRATE_RULE_FAMILY_SCALE_PILOT_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_RULE_FAMILY_SCALE_PILOT_RESULTS.md)). A two-rule cyclic diagnostic found pass-boundary overshoot and exercised the additive typed runner report. The PyO3 API labels all five capped cases `progress_budget_reached` with correct overshoot, labels the opt-in repeat as `repeated_graph_state`, and matches the legacy progress count and graph state across six comparisons ([`SUBSTRATE_CYCLIC_CAP_PILOT_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_CYCLIC_CAP_PILOT_RESULTS.md)). A seven-repeat caller-visible overhead pilot measured 5.93 µs/call for the typed dictionary path versus 2.28 µs for the legacy integer path (median ratio 2.72×) on one very short synthetic cycle; the absolute delta is 3.65 µs and the result is not an end-to-end cost claim ([`SUBSTRATE_RULE_RUN_REPORT_OVERHEAD_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_RULE_RUN_REPORT_OVERHEAD_RESULTS.md)). The public report implementation is recorded in [`SUBSTRATE_RULE_RUN_OUTCOME_CONTRACT.md`](SUBSTRATE_RULE_RUN_OUTCOME_CONTRACT.md); focused unit tests and report overhead on representative workloads remain open. Unrestricted minting, broader cyclic families, compiled-out instrumentation comparison, and preregistration remain open.

**Structural census pilot (2026-09-24):** 24 synthetic graph inputs across six families and four sizes were measured with exact width on n=8 and min-fill upper bounds through n=64. Each graph received one ID-contiguous and five seeded shuffled recursive partitions. Ordered path, banded, and modular families show small cut boundaries under the ID-contiguous hierarchy; complete and sparse-random controls remain high-boundary. A star has treewidth 1 yet a large boundary under balanced disjoint bisection, demonstrating that treewidth, cut definition, and frame aperture are distinct measures. This pilot does not establish locality on natural workload graphs or semantic validity of a partition ([`SUBSTRATE_STRUCTURAL_CENSUS_PILOT_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_STRUCTURAL_CENSUS_PILOT_RESULTS.md)).

**E1 graph-authored episodic task and cue robustness pilots (2026-09-25):** a fresh-process, pre-locked six-arm task run tested 6/24/78 episode loads, same-cue collisions, reset-memory, no-memory, and unknown-cue controls. The three unique-cue arms returned 18/18 exact answers with `recalled` provenance; six ambiguous tasks all reported confidence/uncertainty 0.5 and abstained at the fixed 0.75 threshold. Negative controls behaved as specified. Single-run median tick latency was 0.17/0.35/1.98 ms as episode count increased from 6 to 78; these are descriptive microbenchmark values, not a scaling curve. A second pre-locked probe found exact-key retrieval on 12/12 exact forms, including 6/6 with lexical near-neighbor memories, while 12/12 truncated and 12/12 paraphrased forms returned explicit `insufficient_information`. The seed's `partial_cue_completion` is exact-key collision handling, not fuzzy or semantic cue matching. Both locks matched under independent raw-record audits. This covers synthetic symbolic cue retrieval/interference only; retention, eviction, durable restart, corruption recovery, and natural-task utility remain open. See [`SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_MEMORY_TASK_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_MEMORY_TASK_RESULTS.md), [`SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_ROBUSTNESS_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_ROBUSTNESS_RESULTS.md), [task raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_memory_task_pilot_20260925.json), [cue raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_cue_robustness_20260925.json), and the two preregistrations/locks linked in those reports.

**E1 working-memory capacity/expiry mechanism probe (2026-09-25):** a pre-locked four-scenario live run with a two-slot policy accepted two same-task items and refused the third, replaced the lowest-priority foreign-task slot while preserving the higher-priority item, expired an unmaintained slot at epoch 9, and extended a maintained slot to epoch 16 before expiry. Held content was removed on expiry in both cases. The independent audit matched all eight amended-lock hashes. This measures authored working-memory slot mechanics only; it does not establish useful eviction, episodic retention, persistence, or scale. The first harness invocation failed before scoring on NodeID serialization; the unchanged protocol was rerun under a disclosed amendment and new lock. See [`SUBSTRATE_WORKING_MEMORY_CAPACITY_TTL_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_WORKING_MEMORY_CAPACITY_TTL_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_working_memory_capacity_ttl_amended_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_working_memory_capacity_ttl_analysis_20260925.json), and [amended lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/working_memory_capacity_ttl_amended_lock_20260925.json).

**E1 episodic graph checkpoint restart/corruption (2026-09-25):** across distinct writer/reader processes, `WorldAdapter.save/load` restored six bound episodes, all 18 memory rules, and each Episode→event/context/schema relation; intact exact-cue retrieval succeeded 6/6. Removing one `recorded_episode` edge caused an explicit insufficient-information result only for that key. Malformed JSON was rejected with `JSONDecodeError`. However, changing one event summary in valid JSON led to that corrupted content being returned as `recalled` at confidence 0.85 without a warning, and `WorldAdapter.close()` raised `AttributeError` on every successfully loaded reader because `_vision_illumination_nodes` was absent after load. The independent v3 audit matched all nine source/input hashes. This is evidence for graph checkpoint round-trip plus content-integrity and cleanup gaps; it is not evidence for long-term MemoryFaculty durability, crash consistency, or adversarial security. The first two harness invocations failed after/beside measurement and are disclosed; v3 preserved outcomes without changing tasks or criteria. See [`SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERY_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERY_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_checkpoint_recovery_amended_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_checkpoint_recovery_analysis_20260925.json), and [v3 lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/episodic_checkpoint_recovery_amended_v3_lock_20260925.json).

**E1 checkpoint cleanup repair and rerun (2026-09-25):** `WorldAdapter.load` now initializes the missing session-local `_vision_illumination_nodes` list. A fresh-process save/load/close check and a pre-locked v5 rerun across all four checkpoint variants pass clean close. Intact retrieval, missing-link refusal, and malformed-JSON rejection reproduce; valid-JSON semantic corruption remains silently retrievable as recalled content. The v5 independent audit matched all ten locked inputs. This closes the lifecycle cleanup defect only; checkpoint integrity/recovery policy is still open. See [`SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERY_POSTFIX_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CHECKPOINT_RECOVERY_POSTFIX_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_checkpoint_recovery_postfix_v5_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_checkpoint_recovery_postfix_v5_analysis_20260925.json), and [v5 lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/episodic_checkpoint_recovery_postfix_v5_lock_20260925.json).

**E1 episodic graph-checkpoint scale envelope (2026-09-25):** two fresh writer/reader replicates at N=6/24/78/192 restored all episodes and rules, retrieved all 600 exact keys correctly, and closed cleanly. Checkpoint size rose from 55.3 KB to 358.2 KB; median save/load reached 22.5/16.5 ms at N=192. Median retrieval tick rose from 0.168 ms (N=6) to 12.0 ms (N=192), while one reader's 192-key workload totaled 2.31 s. These small synthetic measurements are a tractability warning, not a complexity classification: operation attribution and larger repeated envelopes remain open. This is full WorldAdapter graph checkpointing, not the separate long-term JSON index. See [`SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CHECKPOINT_SCALE_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CHECKPOINT_SCALE_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_checkpoint_scale_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_checkpoint_scale_analysis_20260925.json), and [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/episodic_checkpoint_scale_lock_20260925.json).

**E1 episodic query-cost attribution (2026-09-25):** a paired native scale-audit run at N=6/24/78/192 (three replicates each, one query/reader) localizes the steep retrieval growth to `episodic_mark_overlapping_cues_for_conservative_completion`. It enumerates exactly `2*N*(N+1)` candidate tests for every query on this all-unique-cue workload; by N=192 it contributes 74,112/75,278 rule candidate tests and 73,344/73,729 where evaluations. Control and audited answers/provenance agree. The current mechanism performs a global pair scan even when there are no cue collisions. Per-rule instrumentation reaches 2.87× control wall at N=192, so the operation counts—not audited timing—are the attribution evidence. This is a concrete rule-level quadratic-work source and the next optimization target; an isolated request-count variant now removes the pair-scan cost on a synthetic workload; see the E1 variant result below. The production seed remains unchanged. See [`SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_QUERY_ATTRIBUTION_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_QUERY_ATTRIBUTION_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_query_attribution_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_query_attribution_analysis_20260925.json), and [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/episodic_query_attribution_lock_20260925.json).

**E1 episodic query cost variant (2026-09-25):** an amended, pre-locked isolated request-count variant passed all checks across 32 cells (unique/collision workloads; N=6/24/78/192; two replicates; baseline/request-count; separate control and audit readers). Exact target identity and response confidence matched at all sizes. At N=192, the baseline pair rule made 74,112/73,344 candidate tests; request-count made none. Total candidate tests fell by 98.4% and total term evaluations by 96.2%. Uninstrumented median query time fell from 11.98 to 0.72 ms (unique) and 12.31 to 0.80 ms (collision). The prototype moves ambiguity to recall time and does not persist episode collision marks, so only response-level parity is established. Its Count/Filter and Argmax still scan recorded episodes; N≤192 and two replicates do not establish a general bound. This attributes and removes one specific quadratic operation, not the whole tractability problem. Next: indexed cue lookup with persistence/duplicate/update correctness; then natural workload frame locality and higher-rung learning frequency. See [`SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_INDEX_VARIANT_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_INDEX_VARIANT_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_cue_index_variant_v3_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_cue_index_variant_v3_analysis_20260925.json), and [lock](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_INDEX_VARIANT_LOCK_V3_20260925.json).

**E1 native indexed cue lookup (2026-09-25):** a second locked experiment compared baseline, request-count, and `NodesWhere` exact-cue variants in 48 cells, including separate checkpoint readers that redeclared the derived native attribute index. All responses and confidence values matched the synthetic unique/collision expectations. At N=192, indexed lookup preserved response-count candidate tests and where evaluations exactly versus request-count (1,166/1,167 candidates; 385/386 where checks), while reducing retrieval-rule term evaluations about 73% and total term evaluations about 20%; median tick improved 6–12%. The index works within Terms, but the rule matcher still enumerates the Episode population. The index is not declared by the standard memory adapter and must be rebuilt after load. Next engine measurement: indexed join pruning of the retrieval rule's own match edge, including duplicate and update semantics. See [`SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_NATIVE_INDEX_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_NATIVE_INDEX_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_cue_native_index_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_cue_native_index_analysis_20260925.json), and [lock](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_NATIVE_INDEX_LOCK_V2_20260925.json).

**E1 indexed episodic retrieval join (2026-09-25):** the native matcher now uses `IndexJoinHint` when one match-edge endpoint is already bound, probes the exact attribute index, and verifies graph-edge identity. A current-source, provenance-recorded engine build was run through 48 fresh-process cells. Exact responses/confidence, automatic cue-index declaration after rule import, collision side-effect boundaries, and closure all passed; independent source-hash audit passed on v2. At N=192 the retrieval rule's candidate tests fell 97.4% (196→5) for unique cues and 95.4% (197→9) for one collision; hinted candidate pairs stayed at 2 and 6 respectively from N=6 through 192. Total candidate tests fell ~16%, term evaluations ~27%, while other rules still account for the remaining work. Median tick improved descriptively 22%/14% at N=192 with only two replicates and no gain at N=6. This is one measured indexed join, not general tractability evidence; prototype collision marks remain nonpersistent. See [`SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_INDEXED_JOIN_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_INDEXED_JOIN_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_cue_native_index_join_v2_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_episodic_cue_native_index_join_analysis_20260925.json), and [lock](SUBSTRATE_EPISODIC_CUE_INDEXED_JOIN_LOCK_V2_20260925.json).

**Current-source paired CAN inference envelope (2026-09-25):** 24 deterministic synthetic 3-state graphs (n=5/7/9; path, cycle, complete, sparse-random; two replicates) were run through the current exact solver, integrated width gate, max-product BP, native 20-start relaxation, and independent exhaustive MAP. Junction-tree MAP and native scoring matched the independent oracle in all cases; the width-4 gate attempted 16 and refused 8. BP converged 20/24 times and matched the optimum in 19/24; one converged run was suboptimal, and all four n=9 complete cases failed to converge. Native multi-start relaxation produced stable terminal states in 24/24 but matched the optimum in 11/24; its selector minimizes frustration, and this comparison uses the separate energy objective. Costs include extraction, width, triangulation, exact messages, BP, exhaustive search, seed loading, and relaxation. Python tracemalloc excludes native memory. This is a synthetic correctness/cost pilot only: no natural-task locality, frame factorization, useful-scale inference, or memory claim follows. See [`SUBSTRATE_CAN_INFERENCE_COST_QUALITY_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_CAN_INFERENCE_COST_QUALITY_RESULTS.md) and [raw report](../../../evaluation/reports/can_inference_cost_quality_envelope_20260925.json).

**Authored Bigville CAN inference envelope (2026-09-25):** all 100 deterministic cast residents were constructed through `worlds.bigville_can_beliefs`, given the authored shared scenario evidence, and run through exact MAP, max-product BP, 20-start native relaxation, and an independent exhaustive 243-state oracle. Every graph had 5 concepts/5 undirected pairs and width upper bound 2; exact MAP matched the oracle 100/100. BP converged 35/100 and was optimal 37/100; native relaxation passed the terminal fixed-point probe 100/100 but was optimal 16/100. Median exact cost was 0.111 ms, BP 35.0 ms, and 20-start relaxation 5.19 ms (native seed loading 2.82 ms separately). The same five-node topology is used for every resident, and this is deterministic authored simulation data, not natural-world validation. See [`SUBSTRATE_BIGVILLE_INFERENCE_ENVELOPE_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_BIGVILLE_INFERENCE_ENVELOPE_RESULTS.md) and [raw report](../../../evaluation/reports/can_bigville_inference_envelope_20260925.json).

**Runtime-generated authored CAN inference envelope (2026-09-25):** 80 N=8 complete models (2-state/3-state, coarse/fine, 20 matched seeds per cell) were first settled by the native rules, then compared with direct exact MAP, BP, and 20-start relaxation against independent exhaustive energy enumeration. Closure and terminal checks passed 80/80; direct exact MAP matched the oracle 80/80; baseline native fixed points and multi-start were MAP-optimal 29/80 each, BP 38/80 and converged 42/80. Measured min-fill width is 7, so direct junction-tree here is diagnostic beyond the production width-4 gate. This runtime-derived but authored synthetic complete-graph workload supplies no natural-task or frame-locality evidence. See [`SUBSTRATE_CAN_RUNTIME_GENERATED_INFERENCE_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_CAN_RUNTIME_GENERATED_INFERENCE_RESULTS.md) and [raw report](../../../evaluation/reports/can_runtime_generated_inference_envelope_20260925.json).

**Exact separator-factorization envelope (2026-09-25):** 96 synthetic modular CAN graphs varied frame count (2/4/8), private frame size (2/4), shared boundary dimensions (0–3), and domain size (2/3), through 35 nodes. Global junction-tree MAP matched a separate conditional-frame exact solver in all 96; all measured widths matched the constructed clique bound. At fixed local dimensions, local assignment work and conditional solver time approximately doubled with each doubling of frame count; increasing boundary scope raised cost exponentially. Python traced peak memory was much lower for the conditional implementation on the tested cases, but it remains a Python prototype. This validates exact factorization only when the shared-separator construction is given; no learned-cut or runtime-scheduler guarantee follows. See [`SUBSTRATE_CAN_SEPARATOR_FACTORIZATION_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_CAN_SEPARATOR_FACTORIZATION_RESULTS.md) and [raw report](../../../evaluation/reports/can_separator_factorization_envelope_20260925.json).

**Current-source treewidth-analysis envelope (2026-09-25):** a repeat benchmark measured 36 exact-search runs at n=8/9/10 and 95 min-fill runs on deterministic path, banded, complete, and sparse-random graphs through n=512 (complete through n=80). Exact median time rises from roughly 34–47 ms at n=8 to 3.6–4.9 s at n=10; min-fill stays below 0.6 s through 512 nodes in these families. Returned exact/min-fill order widths match an independent replay of each elimination order. This isolates analysis cost; it is not junction-tree inference cost, proof of exact minimum beyond the permutation-search implementation, or evidence that natural workload graphs have low width. See [`SUBSTRATE_TREEWIDTH_COST_ENVELOPE_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_TREEWIDTH_COST_ENVELOPE_RESULTS.md) and [raw report](../../../evaluation/reports/graph_treewidth_cost_envelope_20260925.json).

**External-effect route source audit (2026-09-25):** host effects have multiple owners: typed `use_tool` handlers, a separate process-global native `UseTool` callback registry, WorldAdapter pending-I/O fulfillment, and explicit ToolBox file/shell capabilities. Graph-visible ToolSpec/ToolCall/Action records do not authorize, isolate, or receipt those effects. Native callback failures can collapse to integer zero; `ToolBox.run_command` uses `shell=True` with inherited environment, reads are not workspace-limited, and direct-I/O denial is active only inside the P0-A ContextVar context. This is a source finding, not a dynamic route census or containment result. Before action/planning efficacy trials, inventory all registered handlers and adapter routes at runtime, run denial/interception probes in the evaluator boundary, and reconcile each executed effect with authorization and a durable receipt. The exact source ownership and limitations are in [`SUBSTRATE_CAPABILITY_MAP.md`](SUBSTRATE_CAPABILITY_MAP.md).

**External-effect AST census (2026-09-25):** a read-only scanner parsed 832 runtime-owned Python files with no syntax errors and recorded 37 process call sites, 19 network API/construction sites, 14 tool-registration call sites, and 6 explicit P0-A guard calls. Two process calls share an enclosing function with a guard; the fetch materialization guard is separate from the fallback `urlopen` call. These are source-placement observations, not proof of guard dominance or activation. Counts are not reachable-route totals: the scan intentionally does not import code or invoke handlers and can miss indirect/dynamic/native effects. See [`SUBSTRATE_EXTERNAL_EFFECT_CENSUS_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_EXTERNAL_EFFECT_CENSUS_RESULTS.md) and the [raw hashed report](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_external_effect_census_20260925.json). Next, add runtime registry enumeration and route-by-route denial/receipt probes inside the evaluator-owned activated P0-A context, preserving the existing no-action prerequisite.

**P0-A compatibility denial probe (2026-09-25):** in a fresh process, the eight names in `ROUTE_INVENTORY` each raised the typed denial, and nine patched API attempts (socket, URL, process, file-open/read, and exec) were blocked before the original operation: 17/17 blocked, zero unexpected returns, zero handler invocations. A separate read-only default `WorldAdapter` core boot produced 747 graph nodes, zero ToolSpecs, zero Python/native handler registrations, and four introspection capabilities. On an isolated substrate, explicit registration of the demo tool pack created five ToolSpecs and five Python/native callbacks but no ToolCall; the native fire counter remained zero before and after the probes. The explicit ToolBox pack advertises three optional capabilities. This is local monkeypatch/audit-hook behavior plus a seed-load-only core snapshot and configuration-only demo registration. It is not an OS sandbox, a custody-attested P0-A launch, an optional-profile/daemon registry snapshot, or proof that each adapter route reaches the guard. See [`SUBSTRATE_P0A_DENIAL_PROBE_RESULTS.md`](SUBSTRATE_P0A_DENIAL_PROBE_RESULTS.md) and [raw result](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_p0a_denial_probe_20260925.json). Next: under the gated evaluator launcher, snapshot the booted registries and exercise each enabled route with an intercepted sentinel request plus durable receipt verification; retain the no-action prerequisite until the containment gate passes.

**Source-derived workload structure (2026-09-24):** authored dependency projections have been extracted from active CAN discrete-inference and conversation-deliberation seeds. A PyO3 `rule_access_sets()` diagnostic and a fresh release extension were used to compare the extractor with native `derive_access` over all 16 active rules: resource keys and `reads_any`/`writes_any` flags match exactly.
