**ProblemShape event/index recovery (2026-09-25):** at N=8, a checkpoint taken with one residual event and support count 1 loaded with all five rules and event productions intact; the graph index was deleted/rebuilt from observations, the host lookup reconstructed, and resumed closure matched uninterrupted final state by goal ID. Both arms reached the same eight recognized observations, minted shape/support, codebook epoch, support index, empty event queues, and fixed point. Full-adapter checkpoint was 113.9 MB; one save/load took 9.74/5.48 s, while the one-key index rebuild took 0.124 ms and peak RSS was 3.02 GB. This establishes one recovery path, not crash durability; full-graph checkpoint cost now becomes a measured scaling concern. Next test larger observation counts, checkpoint points, interruption/corruption, and whether the application requires the full adapter graph ([recovery results](SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_SHAPE_EVENT_INDEX_RECOVERY_RESULTS.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_problem_shape_event_index_recovery_20260925.json)).

**ProblemShape checkpoint scale follow-up (2026-09-25):** fresh writer/reader processes at N=2/8/16/32 all reproduce exact goal-keyed observation, shape, index, event, epoch, rule, and fixed-point state. The ~78 KB artifact growth across 30 more observations shows these small ProblemShape structures are dwarfed by the full default graph; it is not an asymptotic fit. **Minimal ProblemShape checkpoint probe (2026-09-25):** a three-process N=8 full-control / compact-writer / compact-reader comparison preserves exact goal-keyed continuation through mint and re-decode. This is only a format-level probe and does not prove arbitrary-crash/power-loss durability, concurrency safety, hostile-input safety, migration, or general solver recovery. Next define the actual consumer restart boundary and compatibility policy, then exercise kill points and concurrent writers on the target filesystem before any production adoption ([hardening protocol](SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_SHAPE_MINIMAL_CHECKPOINT_HARDENING_PREREG_20260925.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_SHAPE_MINIMAL_CHECKPOINT_HARDENING_RESULTS.md), [schema](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/problem_shape_checkpoint.schema.v1.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_problem_shape_minimal_checkpoint_hardening_20260925.json)).

**F3 Program IR retention/reuse follow-up (2026-09-25):** a preregistered three-fresh-adapter run on one known-success reverse-string task exercises P4 acceptance and the actual reflected-IR `ProgEval` route. All three runs return identical accepted IR and match 4 revealed plus 3 held-out examples before and after IR graph export/restore. Median setup is 29.75 ms wall / 29.88 ms process CPU; route is 16.00 ms wall / 54.04 ms process CPU; combined setup+route is 45.48 ms wall / 81.83 ms process CPU; seven-row verification is 432 µs; the 161-byte IR exports/restores in 7.59/21.49 µs and applies in about 48–50 µs/call. The route is exemplar retrieval, not induction. More consequentially, root-only `remove_node` leaves four child Term nodes; repeated temporary add/remove retains +4/+40/+400 nodes after 1/10/100 cycles, and compact graph JSON grows +316/+3,160/+31,600 bytes from a 545,973-byte baseline. Current RSS deltas after 100 cycles vary 0–304 KiB and are inconclusive; shared-subgraph references remain untested. This identifies an ownership-aware cleanup gap in repeated reflection helpers. Whole-graph JSON growth is now measured, while the RSS signal is inconclusive. Next add external-reference and shared-child controls, then implement an ownership-aware subgraph cleanup API or explicit helper and verify it preserves shared children before rerunning the lifecycle curve ([protocol](SUBSTRATE_P4_PROGRAM_IR_REUSE_PREREG_20260925.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_P4_PROGRAM_IR_REUSE_RESULTS.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_p4_program_ir_reuse.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_p4_program_ir_reuse_20260925.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/p4_program_ir_reuse_lock_20260925.json)).

The prototype walks `child.*`, protects externally referenced nodes and their child closure, then deletes unshared nodes deepest-first. It passes unshared-tree, shared-subtree, and shared-leaf cases; after deleting each owner, later cleanup returns to the empty baseline (3/3). **TermArena lifecycle measurement (2026-09-25):** a source-locked Rust harness parsed/reflected/cleaned the fixed four-node Term 1,000 times. Ownership-aware cleanup kept graph growth at zero at 1/10/100/1,000 cycles but `TermArena.len()` grew by 4/40/400/4,000 nodes. Root-only deletion grew the graph by 3/30/300/3,000 and had the same arena growth. One 1,000-cycle timing was 29.32 ms versus 20.73 ms; this is one small-tree run and not a performance estimate. Arena length is logical AST count, not RSS or allocated capacity. This establishes that graph reclamation does not bound memory-bearing arena state on repeated temporary parses. Before implementing reclamation, map all persisted `TermIdx` owners (rules, concepts, and other retained structures), then evaluate scratch-arena execution or safe arena lifetime boundaries against the full P4 route. The focused probe does not yet exercise P4’s complete Python path or retained rule/concept references ([results](SUBSTRATE_TERM_ARENA_GROWTH_RESULTS.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_TERM_ARENA_GROWTH_PREREG_20260925.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_term_arena_growth_20260925.json), [Rust harness](../../../runners/dsl/examples/term_arena_growth_probe.rs), [orchestrator](../../../scripts/substrate_term_arena_growth_probe.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/term_arena_growth_lock_20260925.json)).

**Term cleanup hook delivery follow-up (2026-09-25):** a pre-locked native-binding probe measured deletion callbacks for an unshared Term tree, a shared leaf, and a raising callback followed by a second observer. Success arms delivered exactly one `node_deleted` event per removed node and none for the protected leaf. The initial probe found that callback failure stopped later node notifications after graph deletion. `fire_hook` and the cleanup binding now attempt all callbacks/events, retain the first error, and report it after dispatch; the confirmatory run delivered all four events to both callbacks, removed all Term nodes, then surfaced the first `RuntimeError`. The hook, ownership, and P4 cleanup probes pass on the rebuilt native extension. This does not cover reentrant or mutating callbacks, concurrency, arena reclamation, or realistic callback cost. Next characterize mutation/reentrancy policy and TermArena growth under repeated temporary parsing before making any long-run memory claim ([results](SUBSTRATE_TERM_CLEANUP_HOOKS_RESULTS.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_TERM_CLEANUP_HOOKS_PREREG_20260925.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_term_cleanup_hooks_20260925.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_term_cleanup_hooks_probe.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/term_cleanup_hooks_lock_20260925.json)).

**Native Term cleanup and P4 recheck (2026-09-25):** the ownership policy is implemented as `Substrate::remove_term_subgraph` and exposed through PySubstrate. **TermArena shape-API retention repair (2026-09-25):** an exploratory probe showed repeated public `shape_of_term` JSON calls retained one Term node per call because each parse received a new TermIdx; `add_shape_node_for_term` had the same temporary-Term retention despite its graph Shape node being the durable output. Both APIs now compute from a scratch suffix and release it on success or partial parse failure; the JSON path bypasses the TermIdx cache, while stable-index internal callers keep it. A rebuilt-extension diagnostic confirms zero arena growth and exact Shape equality at 10/100/1,000 repeated calls, 100/100 malformed partial-parse rollbacks per API, and 1,000 persistent graph Shape nodes with zero arena growth. This is post-change engineering verification, not a preregistered performance claim. The source-linked owner map records rule/grammar/concept/cache constraints on general reclamation. Next audit the remaining parse-and-truncate call sites, then measure retained arena length and process memory under repeated real synthesis/P4 use ([results](SUBSTRATE_TERM_ARENA_SHAPE_CLEANUP_RESULTS.md), [ownership audit](SUBSTRATE_TERM_ARENA_OWNERSHIP_AUDIT.md), [raw report](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_term_arena_shape_cleanup_20260925.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_term_arena_shape_cleanup_probe.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/term_arena_shape_cleanup_lock_20260925.json)).

**TermArena parse-failure rollback follow-up (2026-09-25):** a source census found partial-parse retention in scratch operations and malformed reflected-Term reads. Rollback is now explicit for `evaluate`, `relax_to_fixpoint`, `search` preparation, `term_subgraph_json`, and failed `define_concept` parsing. Three replicates × 100 attempts across seven API error paths all raised as expected and preserved logical arena length. This is post-change engineering verification, not a performance result. Failed `add_rule` can still retain a partial Term suffix, and failed `import_rules` can leave an earlier prefix of rules installed; transactional import remains open. Next make rule parsing failure-atomic, then measure repeated real synthesis/P4 reuse and process memory ([results](SUBSTRATE_TERM_ARENA_FAILURE_ROLLBACK_RESULTS.md), [ownership audit](SUBSTRATE_TERM_ARENA_OWNERSHIP_AUDIT.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_term_arena_failure_rollback_20260925.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_term_arena_failure_rollback_probe.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/term_arena_failure_rollback_lock_20260925.json)).

**Rule parsing/import atomicity follow-up (2026-09-25):** `add_rule` now rolls back its TermArena and interner suffix on malformed input; `import_rules` stages every parsed rule before installing the rule store and restores both suffixes on a late parse error. The public Rust `parse_rule_json_pub` helper also rolls back its own failed parse. Three replicates with 25 fresh substrates per case verify 75/75 failed adds and 75/75 late import failures preserve arena length, rule count, and subsequent Sym IDs. A successful control preserves two-rule order and the inactive tombstone. This is post-change correctness evidence, not a performance result. The separately locked direct wrapper probe now confirms 25/25 late unknown-Term failures preserve both suffixes and a valid control parses afterward. **ProblemShape rule-order preservation V1.4 (2026-09-25):** 12 fresh-process pairs (six each for recognition and recurrent-residual, N=32) pass semantics and exact seed-load/pre-observation rule-name order. Both arms use immutable copies of the same locked 831-file corpus; the baseline copy matches the corpus lock byte for byte. With eventized rules held in their original slots, every non-ProblemShape rule's audited counters are identical pair by pair. Whole-seed Term evaluations fall 0.48%, candidate tests 0.96%, and rule enumerations do not change; graph writes double. Paired wall medians are 1.009 and 1.003 with broad ranges crossing parity. This establishes localized work reduction, not a timing gain. The prior append-arm collateral counter increases are consistent with a rule-order effect but remain unproven because they were not measured against the same frozen corpus. Next run baseline, append-order, and original-slot arms against one immutable corpus with randomized balanced order ([results](SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_SHAPE_RULE_ORDER_PRESERVATION_V1_4_RESULTS.md), [protocol amendment](SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_SHAPE_RULE_ORDER_PRESERVATION_V1_4_AMENDMENT_20260925.md), [raw report](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_problem_shape_rule_order_preservation_v1_4_20260925.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_problem_shape_rule_order_preservation_v1_4_analysis_20260925.json)).

**ProblemShape rule-placement three-arm control V1.7 (2026-09-25):** twelve randomized baseline/append/original-slot triads on one immutable 833-file corpus pass semantic, exact seed-load, cache-integrity, and treatment-order gates. Append placement reproduces the six collateral rule Term-evaluation increases exactly on both authored N=32 mixes; original-slot placement leaves every non-ProblemShape rule counter unchanged. It recovers 1,536/2,094 Terms beyond append, but only changes whole-seed Term work from −0.43%/−0.41% to −0.48%/−0.48%. Candidate work drops about 0.8–1.0%; enumerations are unchanged, writes double, and timing is too variable to show a CPU gain. Separately, identical seed bytes produce different rule order on cold vs warm index-cache loads because the cache serializes an insertion-ordered mapping with sorted keys and `_topo_order` traverses mapping order; the five ProblemShape rules shift by five slots. Next resolve the seed-loader cold/warm order contract (including exact rule-order and semantic parity), then measure the eventization on larger N and a held-out workload before making a general tractability claim ([V1.7 results](SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_SHAPE_RULE_ORDER_PRESERVATION_V1_7_RESULTS.md), [cold/warm diagnostic](SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_SHAPE_RULE_ORDER_PRESERVATION_V1_5_DIAGNOSTIC.md), [probe report](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_seed_index_cache_order_probe_20260925.json)).

**Seed-index cache-order repair verification (2026-09-25):** the cold/warm mismatch was traced to insertion-ordered seed metadata being serialized with sorted JSON keys. This repairs the specific reproducibility defect, not every order-sensitive workload or concurrent cache lifecycle. A benchmark-only addressee-guard candidate now reproduces the fixture's two intended sequences and preserves owner-queue parity at every checkpoint, but same-addressee concurrent goals remain unresolved. This is not a production fix or general task-identity result. Phase C/C2a remains open for more task families, dynamic boundaries, and production integration evidence. See [v2 results](SUBSTRATE_CONVERSATION_SCOPED_OWNER_WAKEUP_V2_RESULTS_20260926.md), [v3 candidate results](SUBSTRATE_DISCOURSE_GOAL_ASSOCIATION_V3_RESULTS_20260926.md), [v3 protocol](SUBSTRATE_DISCOURSE_GOAL_ASSOCIATION_V3_PREREG_20260926.md), and [v3 analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_discourse_goal_association_v3_analysis_20260926.json).

**Same-addressee Goal identity scale v4 (2026-09-26):** a 15-worker 2/4/8 concurrent-goal sweep separates temporal, addressee-only, explicit `for_goal` identity, owner-queue, and omitted-notification arms. Only explicit event-to-goal links match the intended transitions for all Goals; both temporal and addressee guards assign every Goal to the first task sequence. Explicit owner-queue closure matches full graph state at all 56 checkpoints and exact task provenance; omitted notification stales result receipts and final global recovery restores parity. At N=8 the queue requires 1.30× the full candidate pairs, 1.26× the Terms, and 2.35× the aggregate wall in this single capture. This is a generated fixture, identity edges are caller supplied, and RSS includes the large interpreter floor. Next validate an independently authored workload and extend above eight Goals before any production or scaling claim. See [v4 results](SUBSTRATE_DISCOURSE_GOAL_IDENTITY_SCALE_V4_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_DISCOURSE_GOAL_IDENTITY_SCALE_V4_PREREG_20260926.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_discourse_goal_identity_scale_v4_analysis_20260926.json).

**Same-addressee Goal scale extension v4.1 (2026-09-26):** a separate locked N=16/32/64 run adds 15 fresh processes to v4's 2/4/8 sweep. Explicit-link full and caller-owner schedules meet the task oracle and exact graph parity at all 448 checkpoints; omitted notifications stale receipts and global recovery restores parity. From N=16 to 64, candidate pairs rise 15.6× and Terms 15.5× for a 4× goal increase, consistent with near-quadratic work on this generated sequence family over 16–64. At N=64 owner queue costs 1.27× candidate pairs, 1.19× Terms, and 1.59× the single-capture wall time of explicit full closure. No formal bound follows, and input task links are harness-supplied. Next use an independently authored producer-integrated task and repeat timings plus allocation-level memory accounting before runtime claims. See [v4.1 results](SUBSTRATE_DISCOURSE_GOAL_IDENTITY_SCALE_V4_1_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_DISCOURSE_GOAL_IDENTITY_SCALE_V4_1_PREREG_20260926.md), and [independent analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_discourse_goal_identity_scale_v4_1_analysis_20260926.json).

**Same-addressee Goal identity replicated scale v4.2 (2026-09-26):** three fresh processes per arm and N=16/32/64 (45 total) reproduce exact candidate/Term counts and pass independent task, checkpoint-parity, notification, omission, recovery, and scoped-completion gates. Owner-queue/full ratios at N=16/32/64 are 1.281/1.272/1.268× candidates, 1.221/1.202/1.192× Terms, and 2.148/1.936/1.730× median wall time. Current-RSS event-to-settlement deltas grow from 3.8 to 12.5 MiB for global closure and 3.9 to 12.9 MiB for owner queue; peak RSS is noisy and not allocator attribution. The N-doubling operation counts remain near-quadratic on this one generated fixture. The identity relation is still harness-supplied and no runtime advantage is shown. Next: integrate identity from an independently authored production producer, test multiple task/frame topologies and boundary widths against global closure, and attribute memory before drawing natural-workload or commodity-scale conclusions. See [v4.2 results](SUBSTRATE_DISCOURSE_GOAL_IDENTITY_REPLICATED_SCALE_V4_2_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_DISCOURSE_GOAL_IDENTITY_REPLICATED_SCALE_V4_2_PREREG_20260926.md), and [independent analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_discourse_goal_identity_replicated_scale_v4_2_analysis_20260926.json).

**Phase 4A producer-emitted Goal identity (2026-09-26):** a corrected locked 18-worker N=2/4/8 comparison drives the existing `materialize_from_live_thought_manifold` path and native `cm4a_begin_execution` writer. All nine full/scoped pairs produce one task-correct `DeliberationExecutionTrace.for_goal` and matching resolved settle-back; normalized task projections match. At N=8 repeated scoped closure costs 6.11× candidate pairs, 4.67× Terms, and 2.97× median wall time versus full closure. Raw whole-graph digests differ; a locked structural follow-up over N=2/4/8 and three replicates (nine pairs) confirms exact typed-edge isomorphism after descriptor mapping in every pair, including the one ambiguous Deliberation class via ID-order pairing. The main sweep also passes its preregistered task-projection gates. An initial recursive-worker CLI defect was stopped before data capture and disclosed in the amendment; corrected captures and independent analyses pass. This verifies explicit identity emitted by one existing producer but not natural frame locality or all task producers. Next apply the graph-isomorphism diagnostic to other producer families, then vary event-driven boundary mutation and independently authored task/evidence families. See [graph-isomorphism results](SUBSTRATE_PHASE4A_GOAL_IDENTITY_GRAPH_ISOMORPHISM_RESULTS_20260926.md) and [independent analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_phase4a_goal_identity_graph_isomorphism_v1_analysis_20260926.json). See [results](SUBSTRATE_PHASE4A_PRODUCED_GOAL_IDENTITY_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_PHASE4A_PRODUCED_GOAL_IDENTITY_PREREG_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_PHASE4A_PRODUCED_GOAL_IDENTITY_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_phase4a_produced_goal_identity_v1_analysis_20260926.json).

**Common-ground same-addressee Goal identity replication (2026-09-26):** a separately authored two-origin fixture runs temporal-only, addressee-guarded, and explicit-link arms in three fresh processes each. The two controls reproducibly assign events 4/5/6 to both Goals (0/3 task-oracle passes); fixture-supplied `for_goal` links assign 4/5/6 and 7/8/9 correctly (3/3). Every closure reaches fixed point and CommonGround semantics pass in all arms. This independently reproduces the task-identity failure without a broad discourse-state failure. The identity links remain harness-supplied, so this is not a production correction or prevalence estimate. Next trace the missing task identity across the production event path and test whether a producer-generated relation can satisfy the oracle without harness links. See [results](SUBSTRATE_COMMON_GROUND_TASK_IDENTITY_REPLICATION_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_COMMON_GROUND_TASK_IDENTITY_REPLICATION_PREREG_20260926.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_common_ground_task_identity_replication_v1_analysis_20260926.json).

**Live action event identity producer audit (2026-09-26):** three fresh full-seed workers run the production `converse("Check the pressure.", speech_act="instruction")` path. Each creates one inbound `instruction` DiscourseEvent and an action Goal linked to that Message/origin; each creates zero `selection`, `execution`, or `action_result` DiscourseEvents and zero Goal lifecycle transitions. Associated Phase 4A Deliberations reach `no_candidate`. Source review shows `record_event` has no Goal parameter; Phase 4A `DeliberationExecutionTrace.for_goal` is a distinct internal trace and does not satisfy the discourse event consumer. This confirms that the separately benchmarked operation-event sequence is not produced by this live path. It is bounded to one live instruction route, not proof no other producer emits those event kinds. Full-seed boot median is 12.17 s and turn median 3.37 s, descriptive only. Next define the production event writer/identity owner and evaluate a producer-integrated multi-goal path without harness-authored links. See [results](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_ACTION_EVENT_IDENTITY_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_ACTION_EVENT_IDENTITY_PREREG_20260926.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_live_action_event_identity_v1_analysis_20260926.json).

**Repeated live Goal origin identity (2026-09-26):** the follow-up runs two identical instruction turns for the same recipient in each of three fresh full-seed processes. All six turn records have distinct Message/event/Goal IDs and preserve the one-to-one Goal `comprehends` and `originated_in` mapping; producer structure repeats across processes. All runs still have zero `selection`, `execution`, and `action_result` events and zero Goal transitions. Median full-seed boot is 12.27 s and median turn time 2.08 s, descriptive only. This closes the repeated-ingress identity question while confirming the downstream event producer gap. Next implement or identify the production lifecycle writer, then rerun a multi-goal end-to-end path with independently produced selection/execution/result identity and omission/cross-assignment controls. See [results](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_MULTI_GOAL_ORIGIN_IDENTITY_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_MULTI_GOAL_ORIGIN_IDENTITY_PREREG_20260926.md), and [independent analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_live_multi_goal_origin_identity_v1_analysis_20260926.json).

**Lifecycle producer source audit (2026-09-26):** the two production `record_event` ingress call sites (text-turn and semantic-event) do not accept Goal identity and do not emit selection/execution/result events. The lifecycle rules consume those kinds using temporal ordering without requiring `event --for_goal--> goal`, which leaves cross-Goal assignment possible. The live conversation-action router and separate operational-planning executor were not found to bridge their outcomes into this lifecycle stream. Next choose an authoritative live action route and specify its Goal-carrying event contract, including errors and partial outcomes; add identity-constrained transition rules; then test a two-Goal sequence with omission, swapped-link, duplicate-result, and execution-failure controls. See [source audit](SUBSTRATE_DISCOURSE_LIFECYCLE_PRODUCER_SOURCE_AUDIT_20260926.md).

**Live held-faculty lifecycle producer replication (2026-09-26):** three fresh full-seed processes each run two same-recipient `report your organisation` turns through the real `self_report` route. All six replies carry organisation evidence; each Goal has exactly its own Message/origin identity and distinct IDs. Yet each state has only two instruction events, zero selection/execution/action-result events, and zero Goal transitions. An initial capture is retained but excluded because `world_adapter.py` changed during its capture window; confirmatory v1.1 locks the source and verifies per-worker start/end plus post-run fingerprints. Median boot is 13.32 s, per-turn 2.21 s, descriptive only. The next gate is to add or identify a production event owner that emits identity-bound selection/execution/outcome for a real action path, constrain the lifecycle rules to that identity, and pass omission, swapped-link, duplicate-result, and execution-failure controls. See [results](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_SELF_REPORT_LIFECYCLE_PRODUCER_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_SELF_REPORT_LIFECYCLE_PRODUCER_PREREG_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_SELF_REPORT_LIFECYCLE_PRODUCER_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_live_self_report_lifecycle_producer_v1_1_analysis_20260926.json).

**Goal-bound self-report lifecycle integration (2026-09-26):** the live held self-report action owner records exact Goal-bound selection → execution → result events; native transitions require `event --for_goal--> goal`, and terminal rules remove active membership. Adapter rebinding preserves closed/active mutual exclusion. V1.6 re-confirms the route against the owner-uniqueness guarded seed in three full-seed processes and passes all five controls; median boot is 11.82 s and turn time 1.98 s, descriptive only. V1.3–v1.5 remain preserved as earlier source-state evidence; v1–v1.2 failed captures remain disclosed and excluded. This route is sequential only. See [results](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_SELF_REPORT_LIFECYCLE_IDENTITY_INTEGRATION_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_SELF_REPORT_LIFECYCLE_IDENTITY_INTEGRATION_PREREG_20260926.md), [v1.6 amendment](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_SELF_REPORT_LIFECYCLE_IDENTITY_V1_6_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), and [current independent analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_live_self_report_lifecycle_identity_integration_v1_6_analysis_20260926.json).

**Native lifecycle owner uniqueness (2026-09-26):** the v1 three-process interleaving probe passed explicit A/B event identity and missing-owner rejection, but found that a single event linked to two Goals transitioned both. The four native lifecycle rules now guard against any distinct second `for_goal` neighbor. Three source-stable v1.1 workers preserve all six interleaved checkpoints and reject both missing-owner and ambiguous-owner selection events. Same-thread reentrant live describe calls also pass: B completes while A remains selected/active, then A resumes with distinct Goal/event ownership and both baseline replies. A controlled two-thread call on one adapter reaches the correct Goal transitions but fails in B at `WorldAdapter.converse`'s message node read with `RuntimeError: Already mutably borrowed`, reproduced in three source-stable workers. Source indicates that `run_rules(&mut self)` holds an exclusive PyO3 borrow while releasing the GIL. A per-adapter `RLock` now serializes complete `WorldAdapter.converse` calls and preserves same-thread reentry; this is a scoped mitigation, not a native borrow/API repair. Three source-locked v1.2 workers confirm B blocks at lock acquisition, A and B then complete sequential Goal lifecycles, both baseline replies return, and no thread errors occur. Paired sequential full-turn timing (20 guarded/control pairs) now gives a guarded-minus-control median of +18.1 ms around 1.7 s/turn, but deltas span −67.1 to +109.2 ms; this is inconclusive because timing variance and evolving graph state swamp the median. Next use randomized fresh-adapter blocks and an uncontended lock microbenchmark, while auditing other adapter operations and native entry points for the same borrow boundary. See [native v1.1 results](SUBSTRATE_NATIVE_GOAL_LIFECYCLE_INTERLEAVING_V1_1_RESULTS_20260926.md), [same-thread reentrant results](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_REENTRANT_INTERLEAVING_PREREG_20260926.md), [threaded v1.1 results](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_THREADED_INTERLEAVING_V1_1_RESULTS_20260926.md), and [threaded v1.2 confirmation](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_THREADED_INTERLEAVING_V1_2_RESULTS_20260926.md). Paired latency protocol and [results](SUBSTRATE_CONVERSATION_LOCK_OVERHEAD_V1_RESULTS_20260926.md) record the inconclusive 20-pair estimate. The adapter now serializes all public methods through one per-instance RLock. A three-worker cross-entrypoint capture confirms public `tick()` waits while a live `converse()` transaction is paused, then both complete with preserved lifecycle/reply and no thread errors. A shared native-call facade now serializes direct calls through adapter-owned `s`, `inner`, and `s._inner`; a source-locked four-contender capture passes across three workers. A shared-native identity registry now gives multiple native facades the same RLock; a five-contender, three-worker capture and a registry cleanup probe pass. Raw handles retained before wrapping, complete adapters sharing Python-side indexes, autonomous workers, and other schedules remain open. See [shared-facade results](SUBSTRATE_SHARED_NATIVE_FACADE_SERIALIZATION_V1_RESULTS_20260926.md), [direct-access results](SUBSTRATE_DIRECT_NATIVE_ACCESS_SERIALIZATION_V1_RESULTS_20260926.md), [public cross-entrypoint results](SUBSTRATE_ADAPTER_API_SERIALIZATION_V1_RESULTS_20260926.md), and the updated [concurrency surface audit](SUBSTRATE_CONCURRENCY_SURFACE_AUDIT_20260926.md).

**Second-route identity correction and producer confirmation (2026-09-26):** the initial repeated-request probe confirmed that `describe_scene` reused one scene-level parent Goal, attached both Messages to it, and emitted no lifecycle events. V1.1 now creates a request-scoped Scene view, gives the authored rule the actual inbound Message, links the minted Goal to that Message, selects the unique newly minted owner, and applies parent-only lifecycle while retaining per-percept utterance subgoals as internal decomposition. Three source-stable fresh workers pass distinct Goal/origin ownership, exact selection → execution → result ownership, terminal closure, three-child structure, normalized graph replication, and reply-text equality against baseline under v1.2 of the owner-uniqueness guarded seed. Sequential and same-thread reentrant operation are confirmed; controlled threaded overlap preserves Goal lifecycle but causes B to fail at a PyO3 node read. Other thread schedules, request-route missing/ambiguous-owner controls, complete projection parity, other routes, and scaling remain open. See [source audit](SUBSTRATE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_LIFECYCLE_PRODUCER_SOURCE_AUDIT_20260926.md), [v1.2 results](SUBSTRATE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_LIFECYCLE_IDENTITY_V1_2_RESULTS_20260926.md), [reentrant results](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_REENTRANT_INTERLEAVING_PREREG_20260926.md), and [threaded results](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_THREADED_INTERLEAVING_V1_1_RESULTS_20260926.md).

**High induced-boundary width sweep (2026-09-26):** the corrected 72-case chain/cycle/clique Bigville augmentation passes exact global-MAP parity and independent checks through k=8, across N=12/20 and three workers. At k=8, chain/cycle/clique induce widths 1/2/7 and require 66/174/9,840 VE row evaluations respectively, against 6,561 exhaustive boundary assignments. A source-locked v1.1 rerun preserves the design and independently verifies all 72 cases, the shared manifest, parent log, and child stdout hashes; at N=20,k=8, message+VE medians are 5.81/6.47/51.26 ms for chain/cycle/clique, versus 5.24/5.79/35.71 ms for global JT. The high-width clique remains slower. An initial 24-case undercoverage failure is preserved and disclosed. This supports width-sensitive complexity under controlled factor topology only. Next run connected task families, derive runtime cuts/dependencies, and include native scheduler plus memory costs. See [v1.1 results](SUBSTRATE_BIGVILLE_HIGH_BOUNDARY_WIDTH_V1_1_RESULTS_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_BIGVILLE_HIGH_BOUNDARY_WIDTH_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [raw report](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_bigville_high_boundary_width_v1_1_20260926.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/bigville_high_boundary_width_v1_1_lock_20260926.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_bigville_high_boundary_width_v1_1_analysis_20260926.json); the original [v1 result](SUBSTRATE_BIGVILLE_HIGH_BOUNDARY_WIDTH_V1_RESULTS_20260926.md) remains preserved.

**Connected conversation boundary panel (2026-09-26):** a 12-case native census covers one authored common-ground stress sequence and generated same-addressee concurrent-goal workloads at N=2/4/8, with three fresh workers per workload. Every event reaches fixed point, every Goal resolves with the intended transitions, and graph/counter captures reproduce. In the generated family, direct cross-frame edges rise 3/7/15 and shared boundary incidences 8/16/32, while the pairwise frame projection has exact widths 1/3/7 because each shared global node connects all touched frames into a clique. Candidate pairs rise 119/386/1,364 and Term evaluations 404/1,160/3,728; no partitioned route was run. This is an authored/generated task panel, not a natural-conversation population estimate. It shows why the boundary representation should retain shared hyperedges and why one pairwise treewidth number can overstate independent interactions. Next preserve bus/hyperedge structure and measure additional independently authored task families and runtime-derived cut costs. See [protocol](SUBSTRATE_CONNECTED_CONVERSATION_BOUNDARY_PANEL_PREREG_20260926.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_CONNECTED_CONVERSATION_BOUNDARY_PANEL_V1_RESULTS_20260926.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_connected_conversation_boundary_panel_v1_analysis_20260926.json).


**GenInfer data-derived bound scaling (2026-09-26):** a 24-call direct-Term sweep (12 scale-by-condition cells) across three fresh workers and scales s=1–4 validates the normalized bound B=3s and exact candidate count (2B+1)^4−1. All positive cases recover `[1,1,0,1]` with zero residual; a same-geometry predicate-corruption control is refused at every scale. Median positive wall time grows from 3.01 ms at 2,400 candidates to 452.55 ms at 390,624, about 1.15–1.25 µs/candidate over the measured range. Null cases check the same candidate counts but are faster, showing `checked` is search cardinality rather than a complete cost predictor. This is a one-transform, one-codebook-part, 2-D direct-kernel envelope only; no extrapolation or end-to-end learning claim follows. Next vary transform/geometry and predicate structure, then pair the kernel envelope with full-seed acquisition, residual, and reuse costs ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_BOUND_SCALING_V1_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_BOUND_SCALING_PREREG_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_bound_scaling_v1_analysis_20260926.json)).


**GenMint matrix-family transfer and reuse (2026-09-26):** a preregistered 324-worker, six-matrix × three-layout × enabled/disabled × K={0,4,16} × three-replicate full-seed capture broadens the earlier positive-shear family to a coefficient-2 shear, coordinate swap, and signed quarter-turn. The corrected independent analysis passes 16 checks. All 54 enabled training cases say `recognized_transformed`, but only 33 acquire the intended matrix (9/9 prior, shearA, shearC; 6/9 shearB; 0/9 swap and quarter-turn). Of 651 applications routed through the exact training-acquired matrix, all 2,604 held-out rows are predicted exactly; the remaining calls use other seed generators, mint/reuse an application generator, or select no generator. At K=16, per-family median paired cost ranges from −11.44 ms for shearA to +12.14 ms for shearC; pooled median paired difference is −0.056 ms with 27/54 enabled-faster pairs, effectively parity rather than a stable crossover. The v3 analyzer seed mismatch and v3.1 correction are disclosed, with raw and initial analysis retained. This is selected synthetic 2-D coverage, not general transfer or natural-task prevalence ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_MATRIX_FAMILY_REUSE_V3_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_MATRIX_FAMILY_REUSE_V3_PREREG_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_MATRIX_FAMILY_REUSE_V3_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_genmint_matrix_family_reuse_v3_1_analysis_20260926.json)). Next expand to non-linear-transform families and independently authored geometry; keep status, exact acquisition, route selection, prediction, and stage cost as separate outcomes.


**Nonlinear DimInfer codebook-dependence panel (2026-09-26):** a locked 72-worker full-seed comparison tests five held primitives (rotation, two reflections, scale2, cycle4) and three two-generator compositions on three asymmetric six-relation geometries, with GenInfer disabled and the required generator(s) removed in the paired control. All 14 independent checks pass. Exact intended routes are 9/9 for rotation, both reflections, scale2, cycle4, rotation→cycle4, and rotation→scale2; reflection→cycle4 is selected in 6/9 because cycle4 k=2 is equivalent on the other three. Ablation causes one quantum in 51/72 cases; the remaining 18 stay recognized by alternate generators, exposing reflection/rotation/cycle aliases. All intact cases mint zero quanta. Median closure is ~0.7 ms for primitives and 1.6–1.7 ms for compositions; boot/setup excluded. This measures held operator application, not nonlinear induction or natural-task prevalence. The initial harness/scorer/quantum-count defects are preserved and corrected in disclosed amendments; only v1.3 supports quantum outcomes ([results](SUBSTRATE_DIMINFER_NONLINEAR_CODEBOOK_ABLATION_V1_3_RESULTS_20260926.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_DIMINFER_NONLINEAR_CODEBOOK_ABLATION_PREREG_20260926.md), [amendments](SUBSTRATE_DIMINFER_NONLINEAR_CODEBOOK_ABLATION_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [v1.2](SUBSTRATE_DIMINFER_NONLINEAR_CODEBOOK_ABLATION_V1_2_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [v1.2.1](SUBSTRATE_DIMINFER_NONLINEAR_CODEBOOK_ABLATION_V1_2_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [v1.3](SUBSTRATE_DIMINFER_NONLINEAR_CODEBOOK_ABLATION_V1_3_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_diminfer_nonlinear_codebook_ablation_v1_3_analysis_20260926.json)). Next sample independently authored geometry to estimate residual-alias frequency. Exact reflection identities cannot be resolved from endpoint coordinates, so test sequence identification only when history, intervention, or another independent signal is available; separately test actual nonlinear induction.


**Nonlinear DimInfer geometry-distribution extension (2026-09-26):** 576 fresh workers cover 24 distinct six-point geometries sampled from a locked 4×4 lattice, eight held primitive/composition families, paired required-generator ablations, and three repeats; all 16 amended analysis checks pass, including repeat-semantic determinism. The geometry-level counts show exact intended routes on 24/24 cases for all five primitives; `rotation90→cycle4` is exact on 21/24 and `reflection_r→cycle4` on 12/24, with residual-bearing alternatives or Rung 1-only residuals accounting for the rest. Ablation of `cycle4` leaves a `reflection_r` plus local shifts route on 6/24 geometries and mints on 18/24. Exact D4 reflection identities remain endpoint-indistinguishable; the analyzer separates those from geometry-dependent residual routes. All intact calls recognize without quanta; status remains insufficient to score route identity. This is a bounded synthetic lattice sample and held-structure application, not nonlinear induction or natural prevalence ([results](SUBSTRATE_DIMINFER_NONLINEAR_GEOMETRY_DISTRIBUTION_V2_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_DIMINFER_NONLINEAR_GEOMETRY_DISTRIBUTION_V2_PREREG_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_DIMINFER_NONLINEAR_GEOMETRY_DISTRIBUTION_V2_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_diminfer_nonlinear_geometry_distribution_v2_1_analysis_20260926.json)). Next extend the geometry population and provide sequence-identification signals (history/intervention); evaluate nonlinear induction separately.


**Restricted closure termination result (2026-09-26):** formalized a finite-key monotone insertion fragment admitted by the existing conservative analyzer. For initial N nodes, M literal mint signatures, E edge types and e0 initial edge facts, at most `B=M+E(N+M)^2-e0` novel graph facts can be inserted; each progressing firing inserts at least one, so the fixed-rule closure terminates after at most B progressing firings and one final no-progress pass, provided external mutation is absent. The native finite-recursion fixture reaches fixed point in two firings/three passes against B=9, with exact state and access-set checks. This is a polynomial fixed-rule data-complexity result for the syntactic fragment, not weak acyclicity or unrestricted closure. See [formal statement and assumptions](SUBSTRATE_FINITE_KEY_CLOSURE_TERMINATION_20260926.md), [native capture](../../../evaluation/reports/mint_termination_fragment_native_20260926.json), and [analyzer fixture capture](../../../evaluation/reports/mint_termination_fragment_selfcheck_20260926.json). Next expand multi-signature/multi-rule accepted programs and validate admission against the runtime rule syntax before using this as a trusted gate.


**Finite-key closure family replication (2026-09-26):** expanded native validation from one recursive mint rule to 18 cells crossing M=1/2/4 fixed literal mint signatures and sparse-cycle/dense initial graphs, with three separate substrate constructions per cell. All analyzer admissions, independently recomputed exact terminal node/edge sets, fixed-point statuses, and progress-bound checks pass. Bounds range 14–64; each run settles in three passes. The independent analyzer hashes the raw capture and reconstructs expected closure. This is stronger evidence for the scoped finite-key fragment, still at N=4 and with one positive rule schema. See [the theorem/update](SUBSTRATE_FINITE_KEY_CLOSURE_TERMINATION_20260926.md), [runner](../../../scripts/verify_mint_termination_families_v1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/mint_termination_families_v1_analysis_20260926.json), and [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/mint_termination_families_v1_20260926.json). Next vary initial graph size and admitted rule interactions, then check analyzer-runtime grammar equivalence.


**Finite-key closure scale and key-equality gate (2026-09-26):** the amended v1.1 native sweep passes all 54 cells over N=4/16/64, cycle/dense initial topologies, M=1/2/4 authored signatures, and three constructions per cell. The run remains one positive rule schema and no wall-time study ([results](SUBSTRATE_FINITE_KEY_CLOSURE_SCALE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260926.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_FINITE_KEY_CLOSURE_SCALE_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260926.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/mint_termination_scale_v1_1_20260926.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/mint_termination_scale_v1_1_analysis_20260926.json)). **Finite-key closure rule-interaction gate (2026-09-26):** a preregistered 36-case family executes three interacting native rule bodies (one-edge match, two-edge join, downstream two-edge join) over five edge types, N=4/8 cycle/path graphs, three rule orders, and three substrate constructions. **Finite-key closure self-join gate (2026-09-26):** amended independent analysis passes 72 native cases using repeated-variable `loop(x,x)`, reciprocal-edge self-joins, and three-edge cycle joins. **Rung 3 nonlinear capability boundary (2026-09-26):** current source and existing measurements delimit `GenInfer` to 2-D integer-matrix induction. Nonlinear DimInfer panels establish application of preinstalled operators; they do not establish induction. The full-seed GenMint result explicitly leaves its nonlinear warp outside the linear inducer, while held-out relation results show residual explanation can fail clean holdouts despite a recovered matrix. The next gate is a frozen, independently scored production-path contrast with a linear positive control, held-operator control, frozen/no-induction control, and held-out nonlinear families; record proposal/mint/adoption separately from fit and prediction. A detailed source-linked boundary and protocol requirements are in [`SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_NONLINEAR_CAPABILITY_BOUNDARY_20260926.md`](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_NONLINEAR_CAPABILITY_BOUNDARY_20260926.md). This closes an inventory ambiguity, not the Rung 3 capability gap.
**Nonlinear induction protocol lineage:** the initial v1 protocol and failed JSON-string harness capture are preserved; the admitted v1.1 protocol, runner, source/input lock, raw data, and independent analysis are linked in [`SUBSTRATE_NONLINEAR_DIMENSION_INDUCTION_V1_1_RESULTS_20260926.md`](SUBSTRATE_NONLINEAR_DIMENSION_INDUCTION_V1_1_RESULTS_20260926.md).

**Nonlinear dimension induction v1.1 (2026-09-26):** the corrected and pre-locked 60-case production-path comparison passes all ten admission checks, including the linear positive control. GenInfer acquires the exact linear map and recognizes the separate transfer shape in 10/10 cases; frozen controls acquire none. Neither the quadratic-shear nor piecewise-shear family induces a transform in 10/10 production cases; both observations fall back to quantum minting. The quadratic miss path has 1.013 s median and 2.042 s maximum per closure on this capture, versus sub-millisecond frozen controls. The earlier v1 JSON-string encoding failure is retained and excluded. A second fresh-process v1.1 execution reproduces all semantic records exactly; quadratic-miss medians are 1,013.06/1,013.38 ms across the two processes. This is a narrow demonstrated linear induction boundary and nonlinear miss-cost result, not a general learning estimate. See [`SUBSTRATE_NONLINEAR_DIMENSION_INDUCTION_V1_1_RESULTS_20260926.md`](SUBSTRATE_NONLINEAR_DIMENSION_INDUCTION_V1_1_RESULTS_20260926.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_NONLINEAR_DIMENSION_INDUCTION_V1_1_PREREG_20260926.md), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_1_lock_20260926.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_1_20260926.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_1_analysis_20260926.json). Next: independent replication, then specify and compare a bounded richer hypothesis class; characterize and potentially budget the costly nonlinear miss path.

**Cross-family induction-surface audit (2026-09-26):** source review widened the GenInfer-only result to include `TimeInfer`/order-N dynamics, `DepthInfer`, `SupportInfer`, `BlinkBridge`, `RatioInduce`, `MetaShapeMint`, and bounded `SynthEnumerate`. These have different input classes and integration status: order-N dynamics and meta-shape growth have seeded acquisition evidence; depth/blink are gated/schema-specific; support and ratio are direct-call paths without seed consumers, and RatioInduce has a documented application-semantics defect; bounded synthesis can produce executable programs only inside caller-supplied grammars and budgets. This prevents the nonlinear GenInfer negative result from being generalized to all substrate induction while preserving the open question of a residual-triggered, validated, adopted general learner. Next: activation/input-path census, then test MetaShapeMint transfer and production residual-to-SynthEnumerate adoption.

**Runtime activation census v1 (2026-09-26):** a single-process, three-fresh-adapter comparison of default core (17 seeds), selected conversation profile (70, no failures), and explicit MetaShape-growth dependency closure establishes the actual activation boundary for the teaching route. Chat (27 core+chat seeds) and embodied (7 seeds) exclude the growth path and stay pending. Thus v1's core-only/conversation-profile inertness does not imply that the ordinary full daemon is inert; it describes those specific profiles. The selected Phase 7 conversation evaluation profile still excludes growth. All eight analyzer gates pass. A source trace then found that daemon graph-selected teacher dispatch materializes `TeacherEvidence` and candidate nodes but does not call `teach()` or `meta_shape.observe`; the observation helper is invoked only when another caller explicitly uses `teach()`. Next: map the production callsites that can feed `teach()` and identify any evidence-adoption bridge; instrument real daemon conversations for compatible shape residuals, teach invocations, recognized reuse, and mint outcomes before measuring false-mint/transfer effects. **Multi-schema MetaShape transfer panel v1/v1.1 (2026-09-26):** the preregistered four-schema panel and exact fresh-process replication reproduce the same failures. Only 3/4 schemas mint support-2 patterns; only 3/4 positive holdouts use their target pattern; only 1/4 fixed-field negatives remain residual and refused. ResourceTransfer and GoalTrace negatives with changed fixed values are selected by `recognized_prior`/`covered_by`; the preexisting `spatial_dynamics` prior absorbs all MotionRule inputs. Source tracing distinguishes these from structural `recognized`: `recognized_prior` is the weakest keyword-prior rung and scores principle keywords in relation predicates/arguments rather than exact fixed-value equality. These are controlled structural matcher failures, not a measured semantic error rate. Next: characterize rung-specific false attribution on a broader locked corpus, add conflicting prior/tie cases, and only score downstream “recognition” after task utility is established. **Fixed-value/prior sensitivity v1/v1.1 (2026-09-26):** a 40-observation, four-schema sweep plus exact fresh-process replication resolves the prior-attribution boundary. Among 28 controls, 12 are `recognized_prior` attributed to the target minted shape despite fixed-value changes (ResourceTransfer/GoalTrace), seven are attributed to the unrelated `spatial_dynamics` prior (all MotionRule controls), three extra-field cases are structurally recognized by the target shape, and six remain residual. No controls mint another MetaShape. The stable result confirms that rung and shape identity must be reported separately; recognition labels alone do not establish decision quality. Next gate: pair the ladder outcomes with an independently labeled downstream task oracle, measuring action/value/abstention utility per rung and fixed-field control. **Downstream filing-category utility v1.1/v1.2 (2026-09-26):** a 20-query paired evaluation of the real `categorise_by_shape` consumer, using a fixed family/abstain oracle, replicates exactly in a fresh process. Adding three minted MetaShapes raises non-abstain coverage 25%→75% but lowers exact accuracy 65%→55% and abstention recall 90%→30%. ResourceTransfer/GoalTrace labels now fire on positives but also fixed-value, missing-field, and changed-type controls; FrameBinding's new shape is not selected by this keyword scorer; the existing MotionRule prior remains stable. V1 had two oracle-label coding errors and is marked inadmissible; v1.1 corrected only those labels and v1.2 replicates. This is task-conditional evidence that structural decode labels and the actual teach filing decision diverge. No independent real-world MetaShape gold set is present in the inspected repository scope. Keep natural filing utility explicitly open; do not relabel fixture outcomes as natural performance. Continue the wider capability programme with task families that have independent expected outputs and preserve source, split, negative-control, acquisition-cost, and held-structure application measures ([audit](SUBSTRATE_METASHAPE_INDEPENDENT_LABEL_AUDIT_20260926.md)).

**Default filing integration census (2026-09-26):** an AST scan found 36 in-repository `teach()` call expressions: 31 pass a `category=` keyword directly, one more passes it through a kwargs dict, and four omit both visible `category` and `categorise` in actor-goal codebook helpers. Those four helpers have only test call sites in the repository; several of the direct keyword arguments are dynamic variables that may be `None`. `teach()` always emits `ShapeObservation`; a non-None explicit category bypasses `categorise_by_shape`, while `None` reaches it. Thus the direct utility probe measures a real function, but the runtime frequency and production reachability of its default branch remain unknown. Next: trace runtime values and branch outcomes at actual `teach()` call sites, then select broader capability measurements by independent task oracles rather than assuming this filing consumer is an operational bottleneck ([source census and limits](SUBSTRATE_METASHAPE_INDEPENDENT_LABEL_AUDIT_20260926.md)).

Ordered captures match byte-for-byte, all 19 invocations are recorded, and the full seed-tree digest is unchanged. **Finite-key closure scale-cost sweep v1/v1.1 (2026-09-26):** the same recursive finite-key insertion rules were measured on directed cycles at N=16–1,024 with M=1/2/4 literal mint signatures, seven fresh substrates per cell and separate setup/closure timing. **Degree-skew and closure-cost gate v1 (2026-09-26):** 126 source/native-locked cells pass 1,013/1,013 checks at fixed output cardinality. At `M=64`, 1,024 balanced decoys produce 332,354 vs 642 writer candidate tests; three-replicate plain closure medians are 2.257 ms vs 0.557 ms. Source inspection explains why global relation counts miss the costly tie: bound-source lookup enumerates outgoing local neighbors, bound-target lookup enumerates incoming neighbors, and the both-bound matcher branch still enumerates outgoing neighbors before filtering the target. The active store grows from 2,316 slots at boot to 2,340 during the closures. An exact pre-action graph snapshot has 25,142 nodes and 11,762 edges. Independent enumeration of `rule_intent_about_mentioned_concept` counts 2+8+22=32 candidate visits per pass and 22 bindings; native counters report 64 tests over two scheduler passes in all three repeats. This is real runtime state and native work evidence for one rule, not a passing task-quality result or full `converse` cost attribution. The same fixture records median full-call A/B wall times of 20.66/18.13 s and thread CPU times of 20.57/11.44 s across three workers; B wall time exceeds its CPU time by about 6.7 s under the deliberate serialized schedule. These audit-instrumented timings are diagnostic only, not uninstrumented latency or throughput evidence. Next attribute matcher work across the complete request boundary, prioritizing binary joins, and track the reply-quality failure separately ([results](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_TASK_RUNTIME_JOIN_CAPTURE_V1_RESULTS_20260927.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_TASK_RUNTIME_JOIN_CAPTURE_V1_PREREG_20260927.md), [reply amendment](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_TASK_RUNTIME_JOIN_CAPTURE_V1_AMENDMENT_20260927.md), [integrity analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_live_task_runtime_join_capture_v1_2_analysis_20260927.json), [runtime graph join analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_live_task_runtime_join_snapshot_v1_analysis_20260927.json)).

**Two-sheet vision closure-pass trace v1.8 (2026-09-27):** seven independent checks pass. Full closure and one-pass-sliced execution match exactly in terminal graph, termination class, progress work, and pass count for a root-scoped B-only cycle and a global both-gratings fixed point. The full panel gives exact cycle periods: root-scoped B-only 8, A-only 6, both 24 passes; global B-only 8, with global A-only and both-gratings fixed points. `act`/`act_step` first change on pass 2; `rate`/`rate_step` first change on pass 3 and never update again, while act continues changing through later settling passes. The v1.9 pass cap was an instrumentation horizon, not unresolved engine termination. Combined distribution on this single learned graph is root-scoped 5 fixed points/20 cycles and global 9 fixed points/16 cycles. Cycle periods from these native reports are unavailable. Next repeat the phase-aware panel across independently adapted seeds and visual task families before prevalence or scale claims ([v1.9.1 results](SUBSTRATE_VISION_SHARED_SUBSTRATE_MULTI_SHEET_TASK_PILOT_V1_9_1_RESULTS_20260927.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_VISION_SHARED_SUBSTRATE_MULTI_SHEET_TASK_PILOT_V1_9_1_AMENDMENT_20260927.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_vision_shared_substrate_multisheet_task_pilot_v1_9_1_analysis_20260927.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_vision_shared_substrate_multisheet_task_pilot_v1_9_1_20260927.json)).


**Vision multi-seed response replication v2.1 (2026-09-27):** three independently adapted checkpoints completed the same 25-condition orientation/phase panel under the v1.9 response contract. The 11/11 analysis gates pass across 75 trials: phase-appropriate rate equations and stamps hold, all inputs match pixel counts, every outcome is an exact fixed point or cycle, and none hits the 512-pass/1.6M progress bound. Adaptation work is similar (429k/442k/439k progress), and response medians are 194/192/192 passes; yet termination class differs by seed in 9/25 matched conditions (seed fixed/cycle counts 4/21, 4/21, 7/18). This supports bounded progress counts on the small fixture and exposes seed-sensitive attractors; no reliable per-condition wall-clock or peak-memory capture was made, so it is not a commodity-CPU latency result. It does not establish natural-task prevalence, cheap-cut locality, scaling, or learning tractability. Next test independent visual task families and grow frame size while recording graph width/separator and CPU/memory costs, then isolate rung-3/4 induction rather than extrapolating from closure ([results](SUBSTRATE_VISION_MULTI_SEED_RESPONSE_REPLICATION_V2_1_RESULTS_20260927.md), [response preregistration](SUBSTRATE_VISION_MULTI_SEED_RESPONSE_REPLICATION_V2_1_PREREG_20260927.md), [checkpoint preregistration](SUBSTRATE_VISION_MULTI_SEED_CHECKPOINT_REPLICATION_V2_0_PREREG_20260927.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_multiseed_response_replication_v2_1_analysis_20260927.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_multiseed_response_replication_v2_1_20260927.json)).


**Vision multi-seed timed response replay v2.2 (2026-09-27):** the 75-trial replay passes seven integrity gates and exactly reproduces all v2.1 response vectors, work counts, termination classes, and cycle indices. Across three isolated seed workers, median native `run_rules_report(1, False)` call time is 60–62 ms per stimulus (about 1.50–1.56 s summed across 25 trials); peak process RSS is 228–237 MiB. The full exact-cycle audit loop takes 426–446 s per seed because it materializes/hashes the graph after every pass and extracts state; the non-engine portion is not separately attributed and must not be called substrate latency. The evidence narrows the small-fixture CPU/memory envelope only. Next repeat call-level time and memory under a current-source size/rule-count sweep with exact output parity, then compare the audit hash implementation separately ([results](SUBSTRATE_VISION_MULTI_SEED_RESPONSE_COST_REPLAY_V2_2_RESULTS_20260927.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_VISION_MULTI_SEED_RESPONSE_COST_REPLAY_V2_2_PREREG_20260927.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_multiseed_response_cost_replay_v2_2_analysis_20260927.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_multiseed_response_cost_replay_v2_2_20260927.json)).


**Vision two-sheet current-source scale sweep v2.3 (2026-09-27):** 96 isolated cells cross 3 seeds, 4 frame sizes, global/root-scoped fold, two B-sheet states, and audit counters off/on. All eight analysis gates pass; all audit-on/off outputs and progress counts match exactly, and the independent equation oracle and counter conservation pass. At 512 total SUnits, global `NodesOfType` work is 524,800 (`T(2T+1)`) versus 512 (`T`) under root scoping. Counter-off median closure time is 24.846 ms global versus 11.391 ms scoped; peak process RSS medians rise from 42 to 51 MiB through this limited size range. The selected global fold therefore defeats execution locality even though the two frame roots are disjoint. Root scoping removes cross-root traversal but leaves dense within-sheet coupling. This is controlled one-rule evidence at 512 SUnits, not a natural workload or large-scale bound. Next grow local frame size and capture the runtime dependency width, then test independently authored rules from a second task family ([results](SUBSTRATE_VISION_TWO_SHEET_CURRENT_SOURCE_SCALE_V2_3_RESULTS_20260927.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_VISION_TWO_SHEET_CURRENT_SOURCE_SCALE_V2_3_PREREG_20260927.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_two_sheet_current_source_scale_v2_3_analysis_20260927.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_two_sheet_current_source_scale_v2_3_20260927.json)).


**Vision two-sheet current-source scale extension v2.4 (2026-09-27):** 144 isolated worker cells extend the same controlled factor to 8,192 SUnits across 3 seeds, 6 sizes, 2 scopes, 2 B states, and audit off/on. Nine analysis gates pass, including exact counter-off/on semantic parity, equation oracle, work-count reconciliation, and stable per-worker source locks. From 2,048 to 8,192 units, total Term evaluations increase 15.9× as unit count increases 4×, for both global and root-scoped folds; counter-off call time rises about 15.4×. At 8,192 units, global/scoped times are 6.297/2.786 s and process peak RSS is about 207 MiB. Root scoping halves this one rule's constant factor but retains quadratic work within each sheet because every output reads a whole-sheet mean. These are controlled-rule measurements, not natural workload prevalence or arbitrary-rule scale. The master completion flag was stale at 96; the complete 144-cell aggregate was independently rebuilt from each locked worker file and that reconciliation is included in analysis. Next measure a second task family and dynamic dependency widths, then run broader rule sets at larger graph sizes ([results](SUBSTRATE_VISION_TWO_SHEET_CURRENT_SOURCE_SCALE_V2_4_RESULTS_20260927.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_VISION_TWO_SHEET_CURRENT_SOURCE_SCALE_V2_4_PREREG_20260927.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_two_sheet_current_source_scale_v2_4_analysis_20260927.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_two_sheet_current_source_scale_v2_4_20260927.json)).

**Live conversation dynamic locality v1 (2026-09-27):** a derived analysis of three complete, identical traces from the source-locked live describe-scene capture passes seven integrity gates. The request-owned lifecycle projections have 6–7 nodes and min-fill induced-width upper bound 2, but cuts expose 18–20 external nodes. Request B records 2,081 weighted accesses touching A's lifecycle core, and each request has over 900,000 selected events touching neither lifecycle core; `term_attr_read` dominates. The capture's projection omits the attached Scene and Percept inputs, so these outside-core counts do not separate scene-local work from shared-state access or unrelated scans. The result shows that lifecycle width is not a valid proxy for complete task-frame width; it does not settle live-conversation dynamic locality. Next amend the projection to include scene inputs and explicit rule-produced descendants, then rerun paired workers under a fresh current-source lock before attempting causal dependency interventions ([results](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_CONVERSATION_DYNAMIC_LOCALITY_V1_RESULTS_20260927.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_live_conversation_dynamic_locality_v1_20260927.json), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_substrate_live_conversation_dynamic_locality_v1.py)).

**Live conversation scene-boundary trace v2.2 censored runs (2026-09-27):** the first six-worker capture's lock detected concurrent changes to four conversation source/seed files; pair 0 retained semantic parity, but pairs 1 and 2 mixed source snapshots. The same prompt passed all gates in an earlier v1.2 capture, but source locks differ for four shared conversation modules; this is a source-state discrepancy, not causal attribution. Next inspect the differing source states, revalidate the task stimulus on an immutable snapshot, then collect selected access counts ([censored record](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_ACCESS_TRACE_V2_2_CENSORED_20260927.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_LIVE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_ACCESS_TRACE_V2_2_PREREG_20260927.md), [raw worker record](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_live_describe_scene_access_trace_v2_2_workers_raw_20260927.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_live_describe_scene_access_trace_v2_2_censored_analysis_20260927.json), [prior successful capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_describe_scene_lifecycle_identity_v1_2_20260926.json)).

**Live describe-scene trace isolation and v2.4 replication (2026-09-27):** a same-snapshot native trace-only isolation passes seven gates: both arms complete two concurrent describe-scene requests with resolved Goals, source hashes are stable, and the traced arm records 2,138,740 events without drops. The full paired v2.4 driver then passes all eight gates across six fresh workers, resolving the v2.3 driver failure on a new source snapshot without retroactively repairing v2.3. Thus a small induced lifecycle width is not evidence of a small cut or dynamic factorization. Public replies match the expected scene description while graph-visible outbound Messages fail to match them in every traced run, a separate output-alignment gap. **Five-process uninstrumented timing and OS memory cross-check (2026-09-27):** five fresh processes on the exact v2.4 source/native lock pass all seven lifecycle and integrity gates. Per two-call concurrent schedule, median combined caller CPU is 11.370 s (10.961–12.467 s), the median maximum caller wall interval is 11.463 s (11.069–12.631 s), boot wall/CPU medians are 12.284/13.248 s, and process peak RSS median is 2.508 GiB (range 2.508–2.509 GiB). The timing runner field at boot is a high-water RSS (1.673 GiB), not current RSS; a phase profile measures current RSS as 1.342 GiB after boot and 0.352 GiB after the two requests, despite a transient 2.508 GiB peak. A sixth fresh worker under GNU `time -v` independently reports 2,630,800 KiB peak RSS, matching `resource.getrusage`; it is a method cross-check, not part of the five-sample distribution. The A/B label with high CPU varies, and no outer batch timer was captured, so report caller wall with this schedule boundary. This shows a large boot-associated footprint and transient request peak at only 25,201 final graph nodes, not a persistent memory floor; ownership remains unknown. Next attribute the peak among seed/graph components, repeat phase samples and minimal profiles, capture outer schedule wall, then perform graph/rule sweeps and independent task families ([results](SUBSTRATE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_UNINSTRUMENTED_TIMED_REPLICATION_V2_RESULTS_20260927.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/describe_scene_uninstrumented_timing_v2_analysis_20260927.json), [RSS cross-check](../../../evaluation/reports/describe_scene_uninstrumented_timing_v2_os_rss_crosscheck_20260927.json)).


**Boot-versus-request memory phase attribution (2026-09-27):** an independently analyzed source-locked worker measures current RSS at 0.037 GiB before adapter creation, 0.039 GiB after construction, 1.342 GiB after full seed boot, 1.344 GiB after scene attachment, and 0.352 GiB after both requests. Anonymous RSS grows by 1.295 GiB during boot; scene attachment adds about 1.2 MiB. Request handling raises process high-water RSS by another 0.835 GiB to 2.508 GiB, then RSS drops by about 0.992 GiB before the post-run sample. This corrects the v2 runner's `rss_after_boot_bytes` interpretation: it is `ru_maxrss` high-water, not current RSS. Independent phase gates pass, and GNU `time -v` confirms the high-water measurement. Next determine which seed families/data structures dominate boot memory and what is released or trimmed during request completion; repeat the profile, add exact outer schedule timing, then compare reduced seed profiles ([phase results/correction](SUBSTRATE_DESCRIBE_SCENE_BOOT_MEMORY_PROFILE_V1_RESULTS_20260927.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/describe_scene_boot_memory_profile_v1_analysis_20260927.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_describe_scene_boot_memory_profile_v1.py)).


**Seed-manifest footprint and selective-profile capability frontier (2026-09-27):** 837 seed JSON files occupy 288.15 MB; the top three account for 73.7% of bytes and the top ten 89.4%. `grounded_lexicon.json` alone is 110.73 MB and stores 2,501 nodes under a legacy nested `graph` key, showing that direct top-level node counts miss a major payload. Same-source selective probes load 4 or 8 of 742 indexed seeds and reduce peak RSS to 0.129 GiB, versus 2.508 GiB full-profile peak, but both lose the scene-description Goal lifecycle: the conversation-only profile reports ungrounded identity; the instruction+identity profile answers only “I am Jabberwock.” Reduced profile capability gates fail, so these savings are not a successful lightweight operating mode. **Observed seed/runtime-rule provenance on the current live route (2026-09-27):** ten independent gates pass on `world_adapter.py` hash `517cec9914d600ca…`. Full seed boot loads 731 seeds, reports 11 manifest failures, and installs 2,325 native rules. The successful two-request trace reconciles 2,138,740 accesses. Per-seed loader intervals attribute 872,784 accesses (40.8%) to seed-installed rules; 18 rules are added by lazy describe-faculty construction on the first request and account for 1,265,388 accesses (59.2%); six further conceptualizer rules are added on that request and account for 568 accesses. The second request adds no rules. Source order invokes `_ensure_describe` before the new request is tested against the held recognition rules, so this path-specific implementation mints on first use without an observed held-basis failure. This qualifies the report's “rare minting” economic assumption for actual route startup; it does not establish how often other tasks pay the cost. Explicit prebuild costs 10.907/10.910 s, then the first request costs 0.388/0.384 s and the second 0.282/0.283 s. The lazy route adds 24 rules on first use (18 faculty plus six conceptualizer); prebuild adds 18 before the request and the first request adds the same six conceptualizer rules. **Cold prompt-family capability and construction v1 (2026-09-27):** ten fresh full-seed processes (two per condition) pass lock and capture-integrity analysis, but the prompt-family capability gate fails. Only `describe what you see` reliably completes scene description. `tell me what you see` and `report what you observe` both build the 18-rule faculty (+24 total rules), then return “I am Jabberwock” on the self-report route without a scene Goal. `describe the scene` returns a gap reply without action or Goal. **ProblemShape BP parameter semantics v1.1 (2026-09-27):** six source-locked workers compare `max_product` and `sum_product` on three resident CAN networks, two replicates each. Both settings share the same structural ProblemShape key in every pair, yet all six belief maps differ (maximum absolute per-variable delta 2.0); `sum_product` converges in all six, while `max_product` reports nonconvergence in four. Using `add_node_if_absent` plus `add_edge` to surface both proposals reaches fixed point under either insertion order and preserves A=1/B=2 without choosing. This is the strongest measured representation, with selection still open. **Conflict proposal lifecycle scale v1.2 (2026-09-28):** three fresh workers pass all gates through N=64. Existing `Count(Filter(score == MaxOver(...)))` Terms support a stable graph-rule resolver that selects unique maxima and explicitly flags ties without selecting. Generation work is linear in this fixture (progress N, candidate tests 2N); resolver Term evaluations rise from 80 to 26,058 for unique maxima and 58 to 17,480 for tied maxima over N=2..64, roughly quadratic in the measured range. This closes the basic tie-handling construction gap but leaves a material resolver-cost question; compare or optimize alternate graph-native formulations under identical semantics before claiming cheap arbitration. **Rule-run progress-budget overshoot v1.1 (2026-09-28):** three workers show that `max_steps=1` applies every eligible independent rule in the selected scheduler batch: at N=64, 64 writes occur and reported overshoot is 63; the next call is an idempotent fixed point. **Budgeted revision stage-order probe v1 (2026-09-28):** three workers reproduce a false commit when max/count/decision/commit rules are installed in reverse order without readiness guards: a budget-one pass advances revision 1 with `top_count=0` and empty selection despite a unique oracle winner; full settle remains fixed at the wrong result. Guarding count on the current max stamp and decision on the current count stamp keeps the prior commit intact at the cut and recovers correctly on the next closure. Favorable normal order succeeds even unguarded, showing that ordering can hide the defect. This proves authored revision stamps need prerequisite guards, not merely equal terminal version numbers; the substrate supplies no automatic stage dependency contract ([results](SUBSTRATE_BUDGETED_REVISION_PIPELINE_ORDER_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_BUDGETED_REVISION_PIPELINE_ORDER_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/budgeted_revision_pipeline_order_v1_analysis_20260928.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/budgeted_revision_pipeline_order_v1_20260928.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/budgeted_revision_pipeline_order_v1_lock_20260928.json)).

**Budget-cut recovery across process restart v1 (2026-09-28):** 106 gates pass across three workers, N=2/64, and reverse guarded, reverse unguarded, and normal guarded arms. Reverse guarded cuts preserve the prior resolved and consumed revision and resume to the oracle; normal guarded order completes correctly within the selected pass.
