This means a downstream-reuse benchmark cannot yet exercise a real consumer. Before adding one, specify a test-only consumer contract with parameter preservation, abstention, output oracle, and a cost comparison against direct dispatch; only consider production integration after a held-out probe shows value ([results](SUBSTRATE_PROBLEM_SHAPE_PRODUCTION_CONSUMER_AUDIT_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [AST scanner](../../../scripts/audit_problem_shape_production_consumers_v1.py), [record](../../../evaluation/reports/problem_shape_production_consumer_audit_v1_20260928.json)).

**Native typed-graph storage scale v1.1 (2026-09-28):** the corrected source-locked panel passes eight worker gates and the independent analyzer passes 11/11 checks at N=10k/100k/1M/10M, two processes each. At 10M nodes plus 9,999,999 chain edges, median construction is 15.66 s CPU and RSS increases 2.15 GB (2.393–2.394 GB process peak). This closes a storage-only 10⁷-node measurement gap for one host and an empty-attribute sparse chain; it says nothing about rule closure or inference scaling. The first capture's six-worker aggregate assertion defect is preserved and disclosed. Next add representative attributes and rule density, then measure exact closure work and parity; keep graph construction separate from closure ([results](SUBSTRATE_GRAPH_STORAGE_SCALE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GRAPH_STORAGE_SCALE_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [extension](SUBSTRATE_GRAPH_STORAGE_SCALE_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260928.md), [correction](SUBSTRATE_GRAPH_STORAGE_SCALE_V1_1_CAPTURE_CORRECTION_20260928.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_graph_storage_scale_v1_1_analysis_20260928.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/graph_storage_scale_v1_1_lock_20260928.json)).

**Single-rule native closure scale v1 (2026-09-28):** the 16-worker source-locked panel passes all runner gates; an independent analyzer passes 11/11 checks across N=10k/100k/1M/10M, audit off/on, and two replicates. In the attributed ring, all nodes reach `done` at exact fixed point; audit counters are exactly 2N candidate tests, N attribute writes, and 8N Term evaluations with zero unattributed tests. Audit-off closure at 10M takes 8.85 CPU seconds (8.90 s wall); live post-closure RSS increase is 3.29 GB and validation-inclusive process peak is 6.13 GB, the latter including an N-entry `done` ID readback. This is a favorable single monotone rule, not a general closure theorem or inference result. Its interacting-topology follow-up is now measured through 1M nodes ([results](SUBSTRATE_RULE_CLOSURE_SCALE_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_RULE_CLOSURE_SCALE_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_rule_closure_scale_v1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_rule_closure_scale_v1_analysis_20260928.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/rule_closure_scale_v1_lock_20260928.json)).

**Interacting two-rule closure on tree topologies v1 (2026-09-28):** 36 fresh workers across N=10k/100k/1M, balanced binary tree/star, audit off/on, and three replicates pass every runner gate; the independent analyzer passes 11/11. Exact fixed points and per-rule counters reconcile. At 1M, audit-off medians are 6.11 s on the balanced tree and 1.68 s on the star; audit-on candidate tests are about 40M versus 4M, and the balanced tree needs 20 passes versus 2. This demonstrates strong topology dependence for one monotone propagation program, not a general bound. Validation-inclusive peak RSS differs from closure live RSS and includes terminal readback. See [results](SUBSTRATE_INTERACTING_TREE_CLOSURE_SCALE_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_INTERACTING_TREE_CLOSURE_SCALE_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_interacting_tree_closure_scale_v1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_interacting_tree_closure_scale_v1_analysis_20260928.json), and [source lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/interacting_tree_closure_scale_v1_lock_20260928.json).

**Interacting-tree graph-construction cost v1 (2026-09-28, post-hoc):** reanalysis of the same source-locked raw workers separates edge construction from closure. From N=100k to 1M, median star edge-build time grows 163.2× (2.80 s to 456.86 s), versus 11.0× for balanced trees; at 1M, star edge construction is 272.5× its closure time. This matches the current source's linear `(source, edge type)` bucket scan during duplicate detection, though the source/timing correspondence is not separately instrumented. A new 10M star pilot was interrupted after >9 minutes without a result and is excluded. Next address high-degree duplicate detection or provide a semantically equivalent bulk builder, then repeat paired topology construction and closure measurements before making high-fanout scale claims ([results](SUBSTRATE_INTERACTING_TREE_CONSTRUCTION_COST_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_interacting_tree_construction_cost_v1_analysis_20260928.json), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_substrate_interacting_tree_construction_cost_v1.py)).

**Adaptive high-degree edge index replay v1.2 (2026-09-28):** an adaptive target map activates for high-degree `(source, edge type)` buckets while low-degree adjacency retains the compact scan. The 12-worker paired replay passes graph, closure, source-lock, and semantic controls for duplicate replacement, deletion, demotion, reinsertion, and sparse lookup; independent analysis passes 29/29. At N=1M star, edge construction falls from 456.86 s to 1.66 s (275.6×), with about 13.9 MiB higher peak RSS; balanced construction remains effectively unchanged. V1/v1.1 gate defects are preserved and disclosed; v1.2 is the confirmatory replay. This causally supports the duplicate-scan bottleneck for the tested fixture, not general graph performance ([results](SUBSTRATE_INTERACTING_TREE_EDGE_INDEX_V1_2_RESULTS_20260928.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_INTERACTING_TREE_EDGE_INDEX_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_interacting_tree_edge_index_v1_2_20260928.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_interacting_tree_edge_index_v1_2_analysis_20260928.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_interacting_tree_edge_index_v1.py)).

**Adaptive edge-index 10M interacting star scale v1.3 (2026-09-28):** three fresh locked workers pass all graph, sampled-attribute/parent, fixed-point, source, and phase-timing gates; independent analysis passes 11/11. For N=10M and 19,999,998 directed edges, medians are 23.07 s node construction, 19.93 s edge construction, 17.78 s two-rule closure, 0.69 s validation, 4.14 GB live post-closure RSS, and 7.02 GB peak RSS. From the 1M indexed star, node/edge/closure times grow 10.25×/12.02×/10.58×. This is near-linear descriptive scaling for one high-fanout topology and fixed monotone rule pair on one host, not a general tractability result; at the time, balanced interacting closure was measured only through 1M, and its subsequent 10M extension is recorded below ([results](SUBSTRATE_INTERACTING_TREE_EDGE_INDEX_V1_3_SCALE_RESULTS_20260928.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_INTERACTING_TREE_EDGE_INDEX_V1_3_SCALE_PREREG_20260928.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_interacting_tree_edge_index_v1_3_20260928.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_interacting_tree_edge_index_v1_3_analysis_20260928.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_interacting_tree_edge_index_scale_v1_3.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/interacting_tree_edge_index_v1_3_lock_20260928.json)).

**Adaptive edge-index balanced-tree 10M scale v1.4.1 (2026-09-28):** three fresh workers and 9/9 independent checks pass after a v1.4 worker-source-lock defect was disclosed and corrected in a separate amendment. On 10M nodes/19,999,998 directed edges, medians are 23.17 s node construction, 20.92 s edge construction, 77.89 s two-rule closure, 0.67 s validation, 5.10 GB live post-closure RSS, and 6.33 GB peak RSS. From the 1M balanced tree, node/edge/closure grow 10.11×/12.26×/12.56×. At 10M, balanced and star construction costs are similar but balanced closure is 4.38× slower, showing topology-sensitive propagation after the high-fanout construction issue is removed. This is one fixed monotone two-rule program on one host; audit is off and per-rule candidate counters at 10M are not available ([results](SUBSTRATE_INTERACTING_TREE_EDGE_INDEX_V1_4_BALANCED_SCALE_RESULTS_20260928.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_INTERACTING_TREE_EDGE_INDEX_V1_4_BALANCED_SCALE_PREREG_20260928.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_interacting_tree_edge_index_v1_4_1_balanced_analysis_20260928.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_interacting_tree_edge_index_v1_4_1_balanced_20260928.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_interacting_tree_edge_index_scale_v1_4_balanced.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/interacting_tree_edge_index_v1_4_1_balanced_lock_20260928.json)).

**High-degree edge delete/reinsert churn v1 (2026-09-28):** nine locked workers and 11/11 independent checks pass for full deletion and reinsertion of one hub's 5k/20k/80k typed-edge bucket. Delete-all medians are 35.15 ms/550.73 ms/8.70 s; each 4× size increase costs 15.67×/15.79× more. Per-edge deletion cost rises from 7.03 µs to 108.69 µs, while reinsertion remains approximately linear (1.83/8.57/37.87 ms). Exact delete/empty/reinsert lookup and edge-count oracles pass. Source inspection finds repeated `retain` scans over source adjacency, typed adjacency, and the global edge-type vector. This identifies a quadratic-looking deletion path, not a theorem. The v1 follow-up compares stable batch compaction with repeated single-edge calls; position-aware reordering remains a separate option only if the engine's iteration-order contract is relaxed ([results](SUBSTRATE_HIGH_DEGREE_EDGE_DELETE_CHURN_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_HIGH_DEGREE_EDGE_DELETE_CHURN_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_high_degree_edge_delete_churn_v1_analysis_20260928.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_high_degree_edge_delete_churn_v1_20260928.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_high_degree_edge_delete_churn_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/high_degree_edge_delete_churn_v1_lock_20260928.json)).

**Stable-order edge deletion batch v1 and public node removal v1.1 (2026-09-28):** paired sequential and batch runs pass all 12 runner gates and 16 independent checks across 5k/20k/80k edges. The batch API preserves canonical graph state, duplicate/missing-request results, `edge_deleted` hook ordering, and remaining neighbor iteration order. Median batch deletion is 3.53/9.16/42.71 ms versus 35.94/569.54/8,740 ms sequential (10.2×/62.1×/204.6×). A separate three-worker-per-size public `remove_node` replay passes 8 runner gates and 13 independent analysis checks at the same sizes. Median node removal is 0.559/2.68/13.36 ms, or 112/134/167 ns per incident edge; at 80k this is about 651× faster than repeated single-edge deletion. The APIs differ: `remove_edges_batch` fires per-edge hooks and reports per-edge outcomes, while `remove_node` follows the existing node-deletion hook contract. Stable compaction preserves order without a permanent position table. Next measure mixed source/type buckets and rule-heavy dirty propagation, cursor invalidation, and mutation-log parity ([batch results](SUBSTRATE_HIGH_DEGREE_EDGE_DELETE_BATCH_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [node-removal results](SUBSTRATE_HIGH_DEGREE_REMOVE_NODE_SCALE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [node-removal analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_high_degree_remove_node_scale_v1_1_analysis_20260928.json), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_HIGH_DEGREE_EDGE_DELETE_BATCH_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [batch analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_high_degree_edge_delete_batch_v1_analysis_20260928.json), [raw batch capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_high_degree_edge_delete_batch_v1_20260928.json), [batch runner](../../../scripts/substrate_high_degree_edge_delete_batch_v1.py), [source lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/high_degree_edge_delete_batch_v1_lock_20260928.json)).
**Mixed-topology node deletion semantics v1.1 (2026-09-28):** three fresh workers pass all 7 runner gates and 8 independent checks for public `remove_node` on a fixture with incoming/outgoing edges, five incident edge types, a self-loop, attributed edges, and an unrelated survivor. Canonical post-state matches an independent filtering oracle; every incident lookup is absent, the unrelated edge remains, and hook behavior is exactly one `node_deleted` event with no `edge_deleted` events. This closes semantic corner cases for one fixture, not active-rule invalidation or mutation-log parity. Next measure deletion under rules that read affected edge types, including exact fixed-point refresh, cursor rescan work, and dirty propagation ([results](SUBSTRATE_MIXED_NODE_DELETE_SEMANTICS_V1_1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_MIXED_NODE_DELETE_SEMANTICS_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_MIXED_NODE_DELETE_SEMANTICS_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_mixed_node_delete_semantics_v1.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_mixed_node_delete_semantics_v1_1_20260928.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_mixed_node_delete_semantics_v1_1_analysis_20260928.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/mixed_node_delete_semantics_v1_1_lock_20260928.json)).
**Active-rule node deletion invalidation v1 and fix v1.1 (2026-09-28):** the pre-fix source-locked replay exposed a default-mode stale derived count after deleting the only edge read by a typed `Edges` Term; default mode returned fixed point with zero rule enumeration and retained count 1 against graph count 0. Precise mode correctly refreshed. The native implementation now snapshots incident edge types and dirties those readers in both modes, while retaining precise-mode node type/attribute invalidation. A fresh post-fix three-worker replay passes 8 runner gates and 8 independent checks: both modes enumerate one rule/candidate and refresh to zero. This closes the direct typed-`Edges` node-delete counterexample, not all deletion invalidation semantics. Next test where-only negation readers, additional Term families, mixed-type batches, and increasing reader-rule counts ([pre-fix results](SUBSTRATE_DELETE_ACTIVE_RULE_INVALIDATION_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [fix results](SUBSTRATE_DELETE_ACTIVE_RULE_INVALIDATION_V1_1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_DELETE_ACTIVE_RULE_INVALIDATION_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_DELETE_ACTIVE_RULE_INVALIDATION_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_delete_active_rule_invalidation_v1.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_delete_active_rule_invalidation_v1_1_20260928.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_delete_active_rule_invalidation_v1_1_analysis_20260928.json), [source](../../../runners/dsl/src/substrate.rs)).
**Where-only cursor behavior after node deletion v1.1 (2026-09-28):** nine workers compare full rescan, sound incremental, and unsound type-local invalidation across N=8/32/128 stable match edges. All three conditions open every newly unblocked slot and produce identical graphs. Candidate work is N in every arm, with one reader enumeration, because generic `mark_node_mutation` clears all where-rule cursors on `remove_node`; this is a correct but linear fallback. The initial expectation that the unsound type-local switch would diverge was masked by that generic fallback and is disclosed in the amendment. This does not isolate type-local cursor clearing. Next vary the edge-delete route and reader count under controlled fallback conditions ([results](SUBSTRATE_DELETE_WHERE_CURSOR_INVALIDATION_V1_1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_DELETE_WHERE_CURSOR_INVALIDATION_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_DELETE_WHERE_CURSOR_INVALIDATION_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_delete_where_cursor_invalidation_v1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_delete_where_cursor_invalidation_v1_1_analysis_20260928.json), [source](../../../runners/dsl/src/substrate.rs)).
**Edge-only where-reader cursor invalidation v1 (2026-09-28):** nine source-locked workers isolate `remove_edge` on a type read only by a where-clause while match edges remain stable, at N=8/32/128. Full rescan and sound incremental outputs are identical and reopen all slots; the unsound cursor falsifier opens zero, confirming type-local cursor clearing is required. Sound candidate work remains N with one rule enumeration, so this operation is correct but still incurs a linear full rematch. All 9 runner gates and 7 independent analysis checks pass. This closes one `Count(Edges)` where-reader shape, not all Term families or fan-out ([results](SUBSTRATE_DELETE_EDGE_WHERE_CURSOR_INVALIDATION_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_DELETE_EDGE_WHERE_CURSOR_INVALIDATION_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_delete_edge_where_cursor_invalidation_v1.py), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_delete_edge_where_cursor_invalidation_v1_20260928.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_delete_edge_where_cursor_invalidation_v1_analysis_20260928.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/delete_edge_where_cursor_invalidation_v1_lock_20260928.json)).

**Where-reader fan-out v1 (2026-09-28):** 36 fresh workers cross two where-only read families (`Count(Edges)` and `Count(InNeighbours)`), N=32/128 stable match bindings, and R=1/4/16 rules. Full-rescan and sound incremental graphs agree; the unsound falsifier misses all newly enabled slots. Candidate work and enumerations are exactly N×R and R, respectively, in each family: deletion invalidation is sound here but induces a full reader rescan whose work grows linearly with both binding count and reader fan-out. At N=128,R=16, settle medians are 0.828 ms for `Edges` and 0.805 ms for `InNeighbours`. All 10 runner gates and 7 independent checks pass. This remains a synthetic two-Term panel with R≤16 ([results](SUBSTRATE_WHERE_READER_FANOUT_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_WHERE_READER_FANOUT_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_where_reader_fanout_v1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_where_reader_fanout_v1_analysis_20260928.json)).

**Expanded where-reader Term/fan-out v1.1 (2026-09-28):** 36 workers cross `ReachableFrom` and `Not Exists` readers, N=128/512 and R=1/16/64. All 10 runner gates and 7 independent checks pass; sound incremental matches full rescan, and the unsound falsifier misses all newly enabled bindings. At N=512,R=64 both families enumerate 32,768 candidates. Initial `ReachableFrom` work records 16.78M site-defined traversal units (N²R on this outgoing-star fixture), compared with 32,768 initial units for the `Not Exists` family; post-delete units are zero. This adds interior traversal evidence while showing the expensive repeated root query is not amortized across bindings. V1's initial-audit omission and retained capture are disclosed in the amendment ([results](SUBSTRATE_WHERE_READER_TERM_FANOUT_V1_1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_WHERE_READER_TERM_FANOUT_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_WHERE_READER_TERM_FANOUT_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260928.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_where_reader_term_fanout_v1_1_analysis_20260928.json)).

**Repeated ReachableFrom cache v1 (2026-09-28):** following that cache-off baseline, a fresh 27-worker paired panel toggles the experimental same-graph memo and crosses N=32/128/512 with R=1/16/64. All nine cells match exact N²R off and N on adjacency-work counts; at N=512,R=64 the counter falls from 16,777,216 to 512. Final graph and exact runtime access traces match, and an edge-insertion control changes the rule outcome after mutation in both arms. Audited median wall time is lower in every cell but remains descriptive, and the feature stays default-off. This establishes an optimization opportunity for repeated identical typed queries in an unchanged graph epoch; natural reuse prevalence, memory cost, concurrency, and other mutation routes remain open ([results](SUBSTRATE_REACHABLE_FROM_CACHE_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_REACHABLE_FROM_CACHE_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_reachable_from_cache_v1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_reachable_from_cache_v1_analysis_20260928.json)).

**Source-authored browser `ReachableFrom` cache v1 (2026-09-28):** the 24-worker panel loads both rules verbatim from `seeds/browser_affordance_reach.json` and crosses 2/8/32/128 nested affordances with one/four top-level wrappers. All 10 runner gates and 8 independent analysis checks pass, including exact final-graph, progress, matcher-counter, and runtime-access-trace parity. At N=128, traversal work falls 2,097,280→257 (one wrapper) and 587,776→260 (four wrappers); instrumented median wall speedup is about 2.57× in each cell. **Reachability-cache applicability source census (2026-09-28):** one executable seed Term AST uses `ReachableFrom`; the browser affordance rules are the only located seed-rule consumer. Two direct Python query call sites were found in grounding and frozen-seed closure, but `PySubstrate.evaluate` allocates a fresh default-off cache on each call, and the high-level Python wrapper does not expose `set_reachable_cache`. The script records exact locations and source hashes; this is static coverage, not activation prevalence ([results](SUBSTRATE_REACHABLE_FROM_CACHE_USAGE_CENSUS_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/audit_reachable_from_cache_usage_v1.py), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_reachable_from_cache_usage_v1_20260928.json)). The subsequent profile and mutation gates are recorded below; wrapper exposure remains deferred pending broader internal-effect and rule-family coverage.

A 24-worker N=2/8/32/128 × B=1/4 panel has exact graph, progress, matcher-counter, runtime-trace parity, and zero-work terminal probes. At N=128, traversal visits fall from 2,097,280→257 (B=1) and 587,776→260 (B=4); full tick wall medians improve 2.67×/2.76× under audit instrumentation. **Browser-profile cache telemetry v1.1 (2026-09-28):** the instrumented rerun passes 24 source-locked workers and 12 independent checks. Hit+miss counters account for every `ReachableFrom` Term call. At N=128, peak payload estimates are 8.46 KB over two simultaneous entries (B=1) and 8.91 KB over five entries (B=4), with 16.4k–16.8k hits and 2–5 misses. The cache is empty at tick completion after mutation-driven clearing; bytes exclude bucket/allocator overhead and are not RSS ([results](SUBSTRATE_BROWSER_PROFILE_REACHABLE_CACHE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_BROWSER_PROFILE_REACHABLE_CACHE_V1_1_PREREG_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_browser_profile_reachable_cache_v1_1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_browser_profile_reachable_cache_v1_1_analysis_20260928.json)). **Browser-profile cache hit-path cost v1.2 (2026-09-28):** after the internal mutation repair, the shared-footprint cache panel passes 13 run gates and 12 independent checks over 24 fresh workers and 96 ticks. Exact outcomes and audit traces are preserved. With audits disabled, N=128 tick medians improve 12.34× (B=1) and 7.10× (B=4); at N=2, B=4 pays fixed overhead. Peak estimated payload at N=128 is 8.51/9.03 KB over two/five entries. This establishes an in-fixture quiet-path gain, not a general performance guarantee ([results](SUBSTRATE_BROWSER_PROFILE_REACHABLE_CACHE_V1_2_RESULTS_20260928.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_BROWSER_PROFILE_REACHABLE_CACHE_V1_2_PREREG_20260928.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_browser_profile_reachable_cache_v1_2.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_browser_profile_reachable_cache_v1_2_analysis_20260928.json)).

**Public mutation freshness v1 (2026-09-28):** the ten-case, 30-worker matrix passes nine independent checks. Each case begins with a live memo, so the post-mutation miss directly verifies that the prior result was invalidated before rule reevaluation; expected result cardinality and cache-off parity also hold. The cases include checked and unchecked insertion, single and batch edge deletion, node insertion/deletion, scalar/bulk attrs, and type change. This closes the tested public mutation matrix for the browser rule family. The browser rule still leaves a derived mirror edge when reachability becomes false; cache behavior is correct in both arms, but truth maintenance is incomplete. Internal rule-effect mutation/clear ordering was then tested by the falsifier below.

**In-pass mutation falsifier and repair (2026-09-28):** a five-worker minimal counterexample showed the cache-on engine could return an incomplete fixed point after a same-pass add-only edge write. The engine now clears graph-dependent evaluation memos after each progressing rule. The post-fix five-worker replay reaches exact cache-on/off graph and progress parity; the public mutation matrix still passes, and the cache performance panel was rerun with gains retained at N=32/128. A targeted 40-worker follow-up also passes eight core graph/attribute effect classes. ## General capability activation baseline — conversation panel v1.1 (2026-09-28)

The first task-level extension of the source/module inventory is complete. Twelve provenance/integrity checks pass, and the task oracle passes 8/10: four routes pass both replicates; concern authoring fails both. Within each route, activated module/function/call-edge sets replicate exactly. The measured traces span 25–32 domain modules and 3,240–83,070 Python domain calls. A post-hoc source-inventory join passes five checks: all 40 distinct observed modules occur in the 833-file census, but only 3 have direct capability-map links. This concretely identifies a map coverage gap without treating each module as an independent capability ([crosswalk](../../../evaluation/reports/conversation_task_module_source_crosswalk_v1_20260928.json), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_substrate_conversation_task_module_source_crosswalk_v1.py)). This closes only a narrow route-activation gap: Python traces are not causal necessity or native-work attribution, the panel does not estimate natural task prevalence, and profiled times are not calibrated service costs. Next gate: extend locked paired task/negative-control panels into structured perception, relational reasoning, learning/induction, and planning/action; add independent oracles and native-work counters, calibrate profiling overhead, and keep warmed task cost separate from cold startup.

## LS20 decision ambiguity and recognition noise (2026-09-28)

A source-locked 120-world paired panel held the quanta router and world fixed while varying one versus six stations and clean/noisy recognition (Gaussian pixel sigma 0/8/12). All independent transform, one-correct-station, route-reachability, uniqueness, native-freshness, and source-stability gates passed. Clean and sigma-8 arms succeeded 20/20 in every cell. At sigma 12 the recognizer refused six cases with one station and three with six stations; these refusals were all `req_key=None`, and each led to `no_waypoint`. No wrong-key execution or noisy rescue was observed. The one-station 14/20 success contrast is an initial signal (exact paired p=0.03125); six-station success was 17/20 (p=0.25). With n=20/cell, do not infer that station count changes the noise response. This locates an initial conservative-refusal boundary, not a reliable noise threshold. Replicate on fresh seeds with adequate per-cell power and include adversarially confusable transforms before estimating calibration or generalizing ([results](SUBSTRATE_LS20_DECISION_AMBIGUITY_NOISE_V1_RESULTS_20260928.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_LS20_DECISION_AMBIGUITY_NOISE_V1_PREREG_20260928.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_LS20_DECISION_AMBIGUITY_NOISE_V1_AMENDMENT_20260928.md), [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/ls20_decision_ambiguity_noise_v1/capture.json), [independent analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/ls20_decision_ambiguity_noise_v1_independent_analysis.json)).

## LS20 multi-seed recognition-noise replication (2026-09-28)

A four-seed, operator-balanced follow-up completed 640 paired worlds (80 per station × noise stratum; 1,280 episode executions) with a fixed quanta router. All clean arms succeeded 80/80. Noisy arms succeeded 80/80 at sigma 8; at sigma 10/12 they succeeded 76/80 and 64/80 with one station, and 71/80 and 59/80 with six stations; at sigma 14 they succeeded 1/80 and 5/80. All 120 noisy failures were recognizer refusals followed by no waypoint; no wrong non-null transform key occurred. Holm-adjusted paired tests separate sigma 12 and 14 effects from clean controls in both station conditions, while sigma 10 is significant only with six stations. The station-count differences themselves were not tested and should not be inferred. The worker's final source/build lock, 640 unique world/task oracles, route reachability, and all 32 operator-balance blocks pass. The initial independent analysis had a family-versus-operator counting error and its first correction expected 16 instead of 32 blocks; both are preserved and disclosed. The final v2.2 analysis lock verifies the corrected 32-block count and all other integrity gates. The finding supports fail-closed behavior on this generated vision/planning family, not calibrated confidence or general robustness. Next: inspect decoder candidate/margin observability, preregister a held-out shape-family transfer evaluation with wrong-key cost, and continue distinct long-horizon planning and scaling gates ([results](SUBSTRATE_LS20_DECISION_AMBIGUITY_NOISE_V2_RESULTS_20260928.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_LS20_DECISION_AMBIGUITY_NOISE_V2_PREREG_20260928.md), [analysis amendment](SUBSTRATE_LS20_DECISION_AMBIGUITY_NOISE_V2_AMENDMENT_20260928.md), [count amendment](SUBSTRATE_LS20_DECISION_AMBIGUITY_NOISE_V2_2_AMENDMENT_20260928.md), [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/ls20_decision_ambiguity_noise_v2/capture.json), [final analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/ls20_decision_ambiguity_noise_v2_2_analysis.json)).

## Transform recognition confidence observability (2026-09-28)

Source review of `TransformDecode`, `DimInfer`, and `ShapeDecode` confirms that the current transform path emits categorical explanation/refusal, selected hypotheses, residuals, and candidate-work counts, but no runner-up score or candidate margin. `checked` measures attempts; `ShapeDecode.total_fit` ranks a selected plan and is not defined as confidence. The separate Blink temporal extrapolator does return a support/gap confidence, but it is not transform confidence and must not be reused as one. The LS20 noise panel therefore supports a fail-closed refusal finding only; it does not demonstrate calibrated confidence. Next measure transfer on a held-out shape family. Any candidate-diagnostic instrumentation should preserve winner/status parity, have an overhead measurement, and calibrate selective risk on disjoint calibration and sealed test sets ([source audit](SUBSTRATE_RECOGNITION_CONFIDENCE_OBSERVABILITY_AUDIT_20260928.md), [LS20 v2 results](SUBSTRATE_LS20_DECISION_AMBIGUITY_NOISE_V2_RESULTS_20260928.md)).

## Held-out transform transfer on polyomino shapes (2026-09-29)

A current-source locked panel tests 12 connected, asymmetric polyomino orbits absent from the six-shape LS20 corpus across rotation, reflection, and recolouring. At the task adapter boundary, canonical-key returns are 71/72 clean, 284/288 at sigma 8, and 273/288 at sigma 12. A post-hoc source-locked replay of 756 saved observations across 85 distinct perceived-signature pairs finds 636 positive `recognized_transformed`, 12 positive exact `recognized`, and 108 added-cell `minted` outcomes. The H06_C/180-degree case and seven noisy repeats are valid `cycle4` aliases the adapter cannot label; twelve sigma-12 key misses are exact identity after perception. A side-effect replay of the 12 distinct added-cell inputs finds one new `CapabilityAxis` in every fresh graph, linked via `minted`, while `codebook_epoch` remains unchanged. The control is a known-transform negative and novelty-positive case, so its mint outcome must be evaluated for acquisition quality and persistence rather than counted as a refusal. These findings refine the adapter-only exact-key result and show that transfer, aliasing, perception collapse, and novelty side effects need separate outcomes ([preregistration](SUBSTRATE_HELDOUT_POLYOMINO_TRANSFORM_TRANSFER_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [adapter results](SUBSTRATE_HELDOUT_POLYOMINO_TRANSFORM_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [graph replay results](SUBSTRATE_HELDOUT_POLYOMINO_TRANSFORM_TRANSFER_V1_GRAPH_REPLAY_RESULTS_20260929.md), [mint side-effect results](SUBSTRATE_HELDOUT_POLYOMINO_V1_NEGATIVE_MINT_SIDE_EFFECT_RESULTS_20260929.md), [replay protocol](SUBSTRATE_HELDOUT_POLYOMINO_TRANSFORM_TRANSFER_V1_GRAPH_REPLAY_DIAGNOSTIC_20260929.md), [graph analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/heldout_polyomino_transform_transfer_v1_graph_replay_analysis.json), [graph capture](../../../evaluation/reports/heldout_polyomino_transform_transfer_v1_graph_replay/graph_replay.json), [mint side-effect capture](../../../evaluation/reports/heldout_polyomino_transform_transfer_v1_graph_replay/negative_mint_side_effects.json)). **Next gate:** preregister paired one-off perceptual-noise and true-novelty observations. ### Shared-graph recurrence and predicate-key collision

A source-locked probe sends 15 two-observation sequences through `reflective_faculty.induce_concern` in one graph per sequence. Five exact-repeat controls and ten order-balanced distinct-shape pairs all follow `minted` (one axis) then `recognized_duplicate` (zero new axes). All five targets are distinct under exact coordinates and D4 symmetry, but the current predicate-derived key is identical for every seven-cell signature: `induced_cell_cell_cell_cell_cell_cell_cell`. Thus exact recurrence is suppressed as intended on this sample, while distinct shape structures with the same predicate multiset are also suppressed. This is an observed identity collision under shape-specific acquisition, not yet a judgment that the broad predicate-level key is wrong for every concern domain. The locked panel and its limits are documented in the [recurrence protocol](SUBSTRATE_POLYOMINO_CONCERN_KEY_RECURRENCE_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_POLYOMINO_CONCERN_KEY_RECURRENCE_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/polyomino_concern_key_recurrence_v1/analysis.json). **Gate:** all 15 first/second status patterns are stable and all source/input locks match; no downstream correctness or natural collision-rate claim follows.

The paired follow-up keeps the same 15 sequences and graph-native `induce_concern` path, comparing the default predicate key with a D4-canonical shape key passed through existing `name_hint`. Both variants suppress exact repeats in 5/5 sequences; the default suppresses distinct shapes in 10/10, while the structure-key arm mints each distinct second shape in 10/10. This confirms key choice causes the measured distinction on the frozen family, but the candidate key is computed by the harness and no production caller has been changed. Its median computation was 53 μs versus a 4 μs predicate-key proxy; `induce_concern` medians were 6.16/6.32 ms, with candidate key computation outside the latter number. Do not generalize the timing or choose a global key policy from this panel. A static AST census finds 204 direct calls in 97 Python files: nine omit `name_hint`, 157 pass literals, and 38 pass expressions. All 16 domain-level calls use explicit hints; reviewed hints include content-hashed shape identities, pattern/family labels, fixed faculty names, feature names, and caller-owned names. Immediate consumers divide into nine concern-to-composer grounders, six local-library installation paths, and one gap-verdict pass-through. Thus axis-key identity and local vocabulary identity are separate contracts on several paths. The census and consumer trace are static and do not prove runtime reachability or downstream compatibility ([key caller census](SUBSTRATE_INDUCE_CONCERN_KEY_CALLER_CENSUS_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [machine-readable census](../../../evaluation/reports/induce_concern_key_census_v1.json), [census runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/induce_concern_key_census_v1.py)). Next extend the paired identity tests across representative grounder, local-library, and pass-through callers using repeated, distinct, value-varied, transformed, and noisy inputs. Preserve current hints as a separate arm and measure downstream grounding/recognition, false coalescence/splitting, and persistent axis/codebook changes before any global implementation ([comparison protocol](SUBSTRATE_POLYOMINO_CONCERN_KEY_IDENTITY_COMPARISON_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_POLYOMINO_CONCERN_KEY_IDENTITY_COMPARISON_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/polyomino_concern_key_identity_comparison_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_polyomino_concern_key_identity_comparison_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/polyomino_concern_key_identity_comparison_v1_lock_20260929.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/polyomino_concern_key_identity_comparison_v1/capture.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/polyomino_concern_key_identity_comparison_v1/analysis.json)). **Gate:** 60/60 paired calls, identical signatures per pair, one predicate key and five D4 structure keys; this is not downstream utility or production compatibility evidence.

**Downstream gap-grounder collision v1 (2026-09-29):** a source-locked shared-graph panel sends two distinct same-faculty `CapabilityGap` fixtures through `extend_for_gap(..., verify=True)`. Exact repeats retain their initial composed/rejected-primitive route and add no second axis. Cross-fixture order changes routing: B alone is rejected as a primitive but B after A enters composition; A alone enters composition but A after B creates a primitive request. All observations share `gap_shared_family` and the second is marked `recognized_duplicate`; both isolated outcomes that return verification report rejection. This demonstrates fixture-specific identity collision and route interference, not successful acquisition, general domain failure, or natural prevalence. Next compare faculty-only keys with a faculty-plus-canonical-operation candidate across grounder, local-library, and pass-through consumers, preserving repeats and value-varied equivalence controls; score verification, state changes, persistence, and reuse. No production key change until this gate is met ([results](SUBSTRATE_GAP_GROUNDER_KEY_COLLISION_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GAP_GROUNDER_KEY_COLLISION_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/gap_grounder_key_collision_v1/analysis.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/gap_grounder_key_collision_v1/capture.json), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/gap_grounder_key_collision_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/gap_grounder_key_collision_v1_lock_20260929.json)). **Gate:** 10/10 calls, six frozen sequences, distinct A/B observation signatures, and exact pre/post source-lock match; verification did not accept any composed route.

**Operation-family identity comparison v1 (2026-09-29):** in 22 source-locked calls across two key arms, appending the sorted relation-head multiset to the faculty key separates A/B in both orders while matching each later result to its isolated route. Exact B repeats and a B variant with renamed arguments both deduplicate under the candidate, while their full observation signatures differ. Isolated A/B/B-value outcomes are unchanged. The apparent verification rejections were invalid readbacks because the gate was not registered on WorldAdapter; the corrected-verifier reruns are recorded in v1.1 and current-binary v1.2 below. The candidate ignores role wiring and topology. Next hold out a same-head/different-wiring collision, a second domain family, and shared-state controls that isolate the B→A regression; report verification and downstream reuse independently ([results](SUBSTRATE_GAP_GROUNDER_OPERATION_KEY_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GAP_GROUNDER_OPERATION_KEY_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/gap_grounder_operation_key_v1/analysis.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/gap_grounder_operation_key_v1/capture.json), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/gap_grounder_operation_key_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/gap_grounder_operation_key_v1_lock_20260929.json)). **Gate:** 22/22 calls, 14 fresh graphs, matching pre/post lock, repeat and value-rename suppression with both cross-order identities separated. Verification readbacks are superseded by the adapter gate diagnostic; rerun this A/B after the integration correction.

**Verifier integration correction (2026-09-29):** source tracing and graph/native snapshots show the preceding false verdicts were invalid readbacks: `self_verify_gate` existed as a graph Rule but was not registered in the native rule vector used by `WorldAdapter.tick()`. Registering the normalized rule (`effect`→`effects`) fixes the execution path without changing the gate. A source-locked positive/negative replication passes 6/6: three actual pipeline compositions accepted with all gates true, and three known-fake mechanisms rejected; graph verdict matches the API result and each graph/native registry has one gate rule. This validates one integration path, not general verifier soundness ([diagnostic result](SUBSTRATE_SELF_VERIFICATION_ADAPTER_GATE_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SELF_VERIFICATION_ADAPTER_GATE_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/self_verification_adapter_gate_v1/analysis.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/self_verification_adapter_gate_v1/capture.json), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/self_verification_adapter_gate_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/self_verification_adapter_gate_v1_lock_20260929.json)).

The faculty-only key again merges A/B: in A→B, B is marked duplicate, routed to composition, and rejected although isolated B reaches an accepted primitive builder. Faculty-plus-operation identity separates A/B in A→B and routes B to the accepted primitive builder, while preserving exact-repeat and renamed-argument B deduplication. **Same-head role-wiring counterexample v1.3 (2026-09-29):** a 16-call locked panel compares forward signal→spectrum B with magnitude-spectrum→signal C using identical operation heads but distinct observation signatures and I/O contracts. # Measurement update — semantic validation of acquired primitives (2026-09-29)

The same-head role-wiring counterexample has now received a frozen independent numerical oracle and a matched correction panel. The v1.4 baseline demonstrates the testable failure (6/6 forward artifacts oracle-correct; 6/6 magnitude-only inverse artifacts falsely accepted as the forward term). The v1.5 guard replication preserves 6/6 valid forward cases and honestly refuses 6/6 inverse requests, with matching source locks and a verified non-identifiability witness. An AST audit finds only one buildable computational family in `substrate_extension.build_primitive`, so a second-family replication requires adding or locating another family; the audit excludes rule minting and shape/dimension learners. Next capability work should either measure an independently audited acquisition path outside this registry or expand the registered family set, then repeat semantic oracles with held-out task/port variants before treating constructor guards as a semantic-verification solution. Track the registry limitation in the [audit result](SUBSTRATE_EXTENSION_CONSTRUCTION_REGISTRY_AUDIT_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md) and the spectral evidence in the [v1.4 result](SUBSTRATE_SPECTRAL_IO_ORACLE_V1_4_RESULTS_20260929.md) and [v1.5 result](SUBSTRATE_SPECTRAL_IO_ORACLE_V1_5_RESULTS_20260929.md).

The fixed-width ladder evidence has now been extended to a locked width-by-length grid sweep. The exactness gates pass against an independent DP oracle, while the observed cost confirms the expected boundary sensitivity and exposes min-fill overestimation and ordering overhead. Next add an adversarial topology family with the same q but different separator profiles, and test the production `treewidth_bound_check` refusal/accept path against exact width labels before making a frame-locality claim. See [grid scale results](CAN_GRID_BOUNDARY_WIDTH_SCALE_V1_2_RESULTS_20260929.md) and the retained [v1.1 gate correction record](CAN_GRID_BOUNDARY_WIDTH_SCALE_V1_2_AMENDMENT_20260929.md).

The first production-gate relabelling panel now passes at the default width bound: all 48 q≤4 grids are accepted and independently oracle-correct; all q=5/6 controls are safely refused, with no returned state or mutation. Twelve insertion-order variants per width did not change this grid family’s decision. The next structural gate should vary topology at matched node count and certified width (including irregular/chordal and adversarial elimination profiles), then compare production refusal and cost; natural-task frame prevalence remains unmeasured. See [gate relabelling results](CAN_PRODUCTION_TREEWIDTH_GATE_RELABELLING_V1_1_RESULTS_20260929.md).

The matched-width topology gate has now been executed. It finds substantial false refusal on q=5/6 grids but none on three q-tree structures at the same certified width, while all estimates remain safe upper bounds. Next test non-chordal irregular graphs with controlled edge counts and separator profiles, and evaluate recovery using supplied/decomposed certificates versus min-fill-only discovery. This quantifies the gap between known frame locality and the current heuristic's ability to find it; it still does not establish that natural task graphs have such locality. See [matched topology results](CAN_MATCHED_WIDTH_TOPOLOGY_ENVELOPE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260929.md) and the retained [v1.1 generator amendment](CAN_MATCHED_WIDTH_TOPOLOGY_ENVELOPE_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260929.md).

An edge-matched non-chordal control shows the grid refusal pattern survives exact node/edge matching: q=5/6 grids are often overestimated, while same-N/E sparse partial q-trees are not. Exact inference on both families matches the independent oracle. The v1.2 replication now captures complete bag/separator/child profiles and source-aligned work proxies. These explain why the certified order's smaller maximum bag can still run slower: its profile predicts more loop work on the q=5/6 grids. Source tracing confirms the JT computation is pure Python after graph extraction, so per-call `tracemalloc` plus process-level RSS is appropriate; a native JT allocator measure does not apply to this code path. The corrected degree-profile v1.1 comparison adds a hub-concentrated partial q-tree at matched N/E/q: all 54 workers pass exactness and lock checks, and hub max degree 119 contrasts with sparse q-tree medians 33.5–36.5. Grids still run about 1.9–3.6x slower than the sparse q-trees; the hub profile raises message-entry counts but q=5/6 wall medians remain close to the sparse family, so total messages alone is not a universal latency predictor. The original v1 harness error is disclosed and its capture excluded from degree claims ([v1.1 results](CAN_EDGE_MATCHED_DEGREE_PROFILE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [amendment](CAN_EDGE_MATCHED_DEGREE_PROFILE_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260929.md), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/can_edge_matched_degree_profile_v1_1_20260929.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/can_edge_matched_degree_profile_v1_1_lock_20260929.json)). A fresh 48-worker runtime-derived scale panel now settles native rules on width-1 paths and width-2 banded graphs through N=256. Exact JT tracks N closely (7.7–8.6x time for 8x N), while native closure grows from 15–24 ms at N=32 to 8.8–21.5 s at N=256 despite low progress counts. A paired 16-worker audit attribution now shows that doubling N from 128 to 256 multiplies candidate pairs by 10.4–10.8x in the path/banded CAN cells. Hebbian reweight, Hebbian mint, and coactivation account for 99.96% of Term evaluations; audited and uninstrumented state/progress parity passes throughout. A first match-order sensitivity panel now tests an in-memory sparse-first join for the two dominant Hebbian rules: across 16 workers it preserves canonical whole-graph and state parity, cuts target candidate pairs 27–66x and uninstrumented closure time 3.5–4.1x. The seed remains unchanged. The held-out CAN replay now passes all eight gates on replicates 2/3: candidate work falls 26–66× and instrumentation-off closure time 3.50–4.04×, with graph/state/progress parity. The second authored family, a current-source four-edge anaphora task, passes all 293 analyzer checks and shows 8–16 candidate tests across only eight distinct installed orders from 24 requested permutations; its audit-on timing is diagnostic, not an ordinary speed claim ([held-out CAN results](CAN_RUNTIME_MATCH_ORDER_SENSITIVITY_V1_1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [held-out protocol](CAN_RUNTIME_MATCH_ORDER_SENSITIVITY_V1_1_HELDOUT_PREREG_20260929.md), [held-out raw](../../../evaluation/reports/can_runtime_match_order_sensitivity_v1_1_20260929.json), [anaphora results](SUBSTRATE_TASK_DERIVED_ANAPHORA_JOIN_ORDER_V1_2_CURRENT_SOURCE_RESULTS_20260929.md), [anaphora protocol](SUBSTRATE_TASK_DERIVED_ANAPHORA_JOIN_ORDER_V1_2_CURRENT_SOURCE_PREREG_20260929.md), [anaphora analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_task_derived_anaphora_join_order_v1_2_analysis_20260929.json)). This establishes order sensitivity in two authored rule families but not an automatic optimizer or representative task prevalence. A bounded estimator replay now passes 472/472 checks across 174 workers and three context sizes: it reaches the minimum exact candidate work in 4/6 task/replicate cells (median regret 1.00×, maximum 1.12×), but all requested reorders collapse to one installed order at D=2 and D=4. After charging planning, installation, and plain closure, median combined cost is 19.20–22.68× source-order closure, with no winning cell. It is therefore a negative result for this small-closure envelope, not a production optimizer result ([estimator results](SUBSTRATE_TASK_DERIVED_ANAPHORA_ORDER_ESTIMATOR_V1_3_RESULTS_20260929.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_TASK_DERIVED_ANAPHORA_ORDER_ESTIMATOR_V1_2_PREREG_20260929.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/anaphora_order_estimator_v1_3_analysis_20260929.json)). The native `Substrate::add_rule` already greedily orders match clauses by current relation-edge cardinality ([implementation](../../../runners/dsl/src/substrate.rs), [reorder routine](../../../runners/dsl/src/rewrite.rs)); the estimator replay therefore tests an external planner against an existing install-time heuristic. Its D=2 case shows the cardinality proxy can realize a 12% candidate-work loss against untouched source order. Next measure the native heuristic’s selection quality and installation cost on larger task-derived joins, then determine whether bounded sampling adds value after restricting scores to realizable orders and charging total policy cost across another rule family. ## Production visual image-ingress scope pilot v1.1 (2026-09-29)

The source-stable 32-worker repeat exercises `WaveWorld.step(frame=...)` on three independently adapted shared-sheet checkpoints, with four iterative grating phases per condition, blank sibling input, and two owner-edge omission controls. The corrected independent analysis passes 12/12 integrity/sensitivity checks. Image values reach `lum_raw` exactly in all 256 adapter calls. Across 24 matched comparisons, root-scoped sibling `act`/`act_next`/`rate` is exactly invariant (max difference 0), while global settlement changes the sibling in all 24 (max difference 43.23). The target’s dominant orientation is seed-dependent (45°, 135°, 0° across the three seeds) and identical across scope arms; this is descriptive response structure, not recognition accuracy. Median worker wall/CPU time is 0.390 s global versus 0.309 s scoped over eight sequential calls; peak RSS is about 131 MiB. These are small-fixture descriptive measurements.

The first capture is censored because `rewrite.rs` changed during execution; after `scripts/engine_build.sh`, v1.1 passed two 20-second-separated source-lock probes. The first v1.1 analyzer incorrectly compared a graph digest with the checkpoint file hash; the original output is preserved and the corrected analyzer validates both hashes separately. The exact internal rate-write phase is unavailable through the default adapter: among 4,096 final samples with equal `act_step`/`rate_step`, 1,208 differ from `max(act-theta,0)` by more than 1e-9. Treat this as a diagnostic, not a same-phase equation failure or pass. The next gate is phase-local observation proven equivalent to default `WaveWorld.step`, followed by a larger image-family and frame-discovery-cost study. See [v1.1 results](SUBSTRATE_VISION_PRODUCTION_INGRESS_SCOPE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [analysis amendment](SUBSTRATE_VISION_PRODUCTION_INGRESS_SCOPE_V1_1_ANALYSIS_AMENDMENT_20260929.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_VISION_PRODUCTION_INGRESS_SCOPE_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_production_ingress_scope_v1_1_20260929_raw.json), [corrected analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_production_ingress_scope_v1_1_corrected_analysis_20260929.json), and [source lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/vision_production_ingress_scope_v1_1_20260929_lock.json).

## Native whole-rule phase trace v1 (2026-09-29)

The opt-in observer inside the default native cycle path passes 10/10 checks across six checkpoint/scope pairs. Default and traced `WaveWorld.step(frame=...)` executions have exact graph parity after both image calls; the observer captures 1,001 events, including one successful `oo_sunit_rate` event on every call, without truncation. At whole-rule granularity, 88/384 matching activation/rate stamps differ from `max(act-theta,0)` at 1e-9 (median residual zero, maximum 1.47329). Because snapshots follow all bindings of a rule, this is an unresolved per-binding phase ambiguity, not an equation failure verdict. Median worker wall/CPU time rises from 0.299/0.298 s to 0.305/0.305 s in this small fixture. The instrumentation gap is narrowed, but natural-image accuracy, natural task prevalence, frame discovery, and scaling remain open. Next: extend to independently labeled natural and compositional image families; capture per-binding write provenance or a rule-local before/after delta sufficient to adjudicate the equation; measure frame discovery and boundary width separately; then scale graph size under both global and scoped settlement. See [native trace results](SUBSTRATE_VISION_NATIVE_RULE_PHASE_TRACE_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_VISION_NATIVE_RULE_PHASE_TRACE_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_native_rule_phase_trace_v1_20260929_raw.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/vision_native_rule_phase_trace_v1_20260929_analysis.json), and [source lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/vision_native_rule_phase_trace_v1_20260929_lock.json).

## Natural-image transformation task pilot (2026-09-29)

The next 48-worker task panel uses eight held-out BSDS300 photographs, exact 180° image transforms, independent blank baselines, three adapted checkpoints, and global/root-scoped settlement. All 10 corrected integrity checks pass. Blank-subtracted `act` maps under root-scoped settlement favor the known 180° spatial permutation over an unchanged-map control on 24/24 image/checkpoint combinations (8/8 within each checkpoint); global `act` favors the unchanged map on 24/24. `rate` also favors the unchanged map on 24/24 in both scopes. The original analyzer incorrectly joined a graph digest to a checkpoint file hash and scored raw output magnitudes; its failed report is retained, and the corrected analysis links by graph digest and subtracts blank-arm state. Next determine why `act` transformation behavior in scoped settling does not carry into `rate`, then expand to additional rotations/reflections and independently labeled visual tasks. ## Independent QuickDraw graph-Term task family (2026-09-29)

A source/runtime/data-locked 100-episode, 8-way one-shot panel evaluates the existing ordered-DTW, point-set, and deformable graph Terms on new single-stroke drawings from eight fixed QuickDraw classes. Each method scores 4,000 shared queries. PointSetDist is 45.7% (95% class-cluster interval 33.9–57.9%; chance 12.5%), ordered DTW 37.1%, and DeformDist 35.9%; the independent analyzer passes all six integrity gates. Parsing and feature preparation take 1.39 s; full capture takes 4.76 s. This is the first separate task-family result after Omniglot, but it tests held-structure application, not new-class induction. QuickDraw contributor identifiers are absent, classes are fixed, and the uncertainty has only eight class clusters. Next use creator-separated data and label-held-out combinations, then measure acquisition/application cost on a learning-capable route ([results](SUBSTRATE_QUICKDRAW_ONE_SHOT_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_QUICKDRAW_ONE_SHOT_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_quickdraw_one_shot_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_substrate_quickdraw_one_shot_v1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/quickdraw_one_shot_v1_20260929_analysis.json), [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/quickdraw_one_shot_v1_20260929_raw.jsonl), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/quickdraw_one_shot_v1_20260929_lock.json)).


## Current-source replication of nonlinear dimension induction (2026-09-29)

The v1.2.1 source-refresh replication repeats the registered 60-case linear/quadratic/piecewise transfer design against current Rust source and the matching native binary. All 12 integrity/semantic gates pass; all 60 cells match the earlier v1.1 process replicate on status, quantum count, and final generator state. Linear induction/transfer succeeds 10/10; neither nonlinear family is acquired (0/10), and the quadratic miss remains costly at 1,066.69 ms median closure (2,104.29 ms maximum) versus 0.473 ms frozen. A v1.2 raw attempt and analyzer false-negative are preserved and disclosed; the v1.2.1 amendment fixed the incomplete source-hash comparison and a fresh capture passed. This refreshes a bounded current-source capability result, not a general nonlinear learner or independent-host scaling estimate. The next third-family probe then tested `T(x,y)=(x+xy,y+x²)` in 10 enabled replicates: no valid operator acquisition or exact transfer occurred, while the linear positive control succeeded 10/10. Enabled nonlinear transfer closure averaged 1,909.989 ms versus 0.420 ms frozen. Treat `minted` statuses in this run as unsuccessful for the target capability: no target-compatible generator was acquired. The next step is to inspect candidate enumeration/rejection and budget behavior, then preregister and evaluate a richer bounded grammar with hard budgets and matched controls ([v1.2.1 results](SUBSTRATE_NONLINEAR_DIMENSION_INDUCTION_V1_2_1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [v1.3 results](SUBSTRATE_NONLINEAR_DIMENSION_INDUCTION_V1_3_RESULTS_20261005.md), [v1.3 protocol](SUBSTRATE_NONLINEAR_DIMENSION_INDUCTION_V1_3_PREREG_20261005.md), [v1.3 analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_3_analysis_20261005.json), [v1.3 capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_3_20261005.json), [v1.3 lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_3_lock_20261005.json), [v1.2.1 amendment](SUBSTRATE_NONLINEAR_DIMENSION_INDUCTION_V1_2_1_AMENDMENT_20260929.md), [comparison](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_nonlinear_dimension_induction_current_source_comparison_v1_20260929.json), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_2_1.py), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_substrate_nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_2_1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_2_1_analysis_20260929.json), [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_2_1_20260929.json), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/nonlinear_dimension_induction_v1_2_1_lock_20260929.json)).

The v1.5 follow-up now measures actual GenInfer work at the native operation site. In ten enabled coupled-quadratic transfer runs it observes ten kernel calls over 20 eligible bases at B=12 and exactly 7,812,480 matrix attempts; every attempt reaches residual validation and fails. Training observes 48,000 attempts across 20 bases at B=3. The linear control acquires/transfers in 10/10, with 20 cache hits from 40 GenInfer requests during training; frozen arms have zero requests.
