## SynthEnumerate nonlinear-map result and next learning gate (2026-09-29)

A fresh 40-cell, source/native-locked probe demonstrates bounded nonlinear executable-Term acquisition when the caller supplies grammars containing the required operators: each acquired linear, quadratic, hinge, and absolute-value map transfers exactly to all six held-out points in 5/5 repetitions. Omitting the required multiplication, maximum, or absolute-value operator causes all 15 corresponding cases to refuse at the size boundary. For acquired Terms, median 100-call native application is 4.70–5.72 microseconds. The v1 application-cost report had a unit-label defect; the preserved v1.1 repeat corrects it, and a separate audit recomputes per-call microseconds from raw nanoseconds. This narrows the claim to caller-supplied bounded grammar search and subsequent exact-Term use. It does not show automatic grammar choice, residual-driven routing, `DimensionGenerator` mint/adoption, natural task prevalence, or general nonlinear induction ([results](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHENUMERATE_NONLINEAR_MAP_V1_1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHENUMERATE_NONLINEAR_MAP_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHENUMERATE_NONLINEAR_MAP_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260929.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/synthenumerate_nonlinear_map_v1_1_20260929_analysis.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/synthenumerate_nonlinear_map_v1_1_20260929_raw.jsonl), [comparison audit](../../../evaluation/reports/synthenumerate_nonlinear_map_capture_comparison_v1_20260929.json)).

**Next gate:** preregister a small family of residual-producing tasks, candidate grammar-selection rules and their cost, one bounded search/refusal budget, and a downstream held-out oracle. Compare the current fixed-basis transformation route, the caller-supplied SynthEnumerate route, and a residual-triggered route. Charge grammar proposal and verification separately from candidate enumeration and post-acquisition application. Require exact source/native/task lock, positive and negative controls, fresh repetitions, and a non-regression criterion for false acceptance. A successful task Term must be shown to enter the actual concept/dimension representation and be reused by a later task before counting as Rung 3/4 integration evidence.

## Integrated Rung 3 nonlinear-map panel (2026-09-29)

A source-locked end-to-end panel exercises `ensure_program_synthesis` → `ingest_spec` → the graph-authored `pump` route → reflected-Program `ProgEval` on six heldouts, with five fresh processes per map. The final tuple-correct v1.1.1 capture passes source, schedule, route, terminal-status, and linear-control checks. Ten linear/quadratic programs transfer exactly (10/10); five hinge requests accept the same threshold-predicate shortcut and fail all 30 holdout predictions; five absolute-value requests hit the 200,000-candidate cap and gap. Thus the route's acceptance rate on the 20 fixed requests is 15/20, while exact heldout correctness is 10/20, and one family shows systematic accepted overgeneralization. Median end-to-end `pump` wall time is 1.2 s for linear/quadratic/hinge and 1.61 s for absolute-value failures on this host; this includes route/adapter work and is not a pure enumerator timer. The analyzer reports 9/10 gates: the data and route are valid, but the preregistered all-accepted-transfer gate fails. V1's list/tuple serialization defect and v1.1's post-success `NodeID` capture failure are separately preserved and disclosed; neither is pooled with v1.1.1 ([results](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_RUNG3_NONLINEAR_MAP_V1_1_1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [initial protocol](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_RUNG3_NONLINEAR_MAP_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [amendments](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_RUNG3_NONLINEAR_MAP_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260929.md), [capture repair](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_RUNG3_NONLINEAR_MAP_V1_1_1_AMENDMENT_20260929.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_rung3_nonlinear_map_v1_1_1_20260929_analysis.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_rung3_nonlinear_map_v1_1_1_20260929_raw.jsonl), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/synthesis_rung3_nonlinear_map_v1_1_1_20260929_lock.json)).

**Next gate:** test generalization with threshold-balanced examples and a preregistered heldout-region oracle; include candidates that are deliberately indistinguishable on training rows but diverge off-support. Preserve the current broad-grammar arm and charge its search cost. Add measures for residual-triggering, verifier outcome, representation adoption, persistence, and reuse by a later task. Success requires transfer and durable downstream use, not merely a fitting candidate or accepted status.

## Hinge grammar breadth contrast (2026-09-29)

A five-pair-per-arm source-locked Rung 3 contrast uses eight threshold-balanced training examples and six disjoint holdouts. The default grammar path hits 200,000 candidates and gaps in 5/5 workers (median `pump` 1.804 s); a manually injected four-operator `Plus/Minus/Max/TupleOf` grammar accepts and transfers in 5/5, with all 30 holdout predictions exact (median 61,384 candidates; median `pump` 650 ms). All eight capture-integrity checks and the three preregistered contrast thresholds pass. The comparison isolates grammar restriction as both a capability and tractability lever on this task; the successful arm receives oracle task information and does not establish learned operator selection. This helps explain the preceding broad-grammar false hinge acceptance and balanced-data cap exhaustion, but does not validate the same policy on independent task families ([results](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_RUNG3_HINGE_GRAMMAR_CONTRAST_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_RUNG3_HINGE_GRAMMAR_CONTRAST_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_rung3_hinge_grammar_contrast_v1_20260929_analysis.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_rung3_hinge_grammar_contrast_v1_20260929_raw.jsonl), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/synthesis_rung3_hinge_grammar_contrast_v1_20260929_lock.json)).

**Next gate:** specify an operator-shape selection rule before selecting a new task family, test it on cases not used to author its triggers, and compare learned selection, broad-default search, and oracle-bounded grammar. Require balanced training, disjoint holdouts, negative tasks with plausible but wrong fitting candidates, and the same per-worker cap/cost/false-accept reporting. Count operator selection as learned only when the substrate selects it from task evidence without harness-injected operator facts.

## Authored operator-shape selector transfer (2026-09-29)

A current-source preregistered repeat compares trigger wording with a neutral lexical ablation for two scalar piecewise-scaling tasks at thresholds 5 and 7. The normal graph-authored selector chooses `thresholded_greater_branch` and `Times/Gt/IfThenElse` in 10/10 trigger workers; every selected Program transfers on all 60 holdout points. Without trigger terms, the selector chooses no shape and the broad default reaches its 200,000-candidate cap in 10/10 workers. Search work falls about 1.9× per task, although end-to-end `pump` time does not consistently decrease. All eight integrity and ten behavioral gates pass for final v1.1.1. V1 and v1.1 captures are preserved and excluded because their analyzers reconstructed the registered schedule incorrectly; the final amendment records order explicitly and verifies the exact schedule. This supports only one authored grammar-shape rule across two parameterizations; selection remains token-triggered and does not demonstrate novel rule induction ([results](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_OPERATOR_SHAPE_TRANSFER_V1_1_1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_OPERATOR_SHAPE_TRANSFER_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [amendments](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_OPERATOR_SHAPE_TRANSFER_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260929.md), [final amendment](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_OPERATOR_SHAPE_TRANSFER_V1_1_1_AMENDMENT_20260929.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_operator_shape_transfer_v1_1_1_20260929_analysis.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_operator_shape_transfer_v1_1_1_20260929_raw.jsonl), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/synthesis_operator_shape_transfer_v1_1_1_20260929_lock.json)).

**Next gate:** run the corresponding below-threshold shape on a separate task with fresh parameters, counterbalanced trigger and neutral descriptions, and disjoint holdouts; then test an unsupported task family to measure selector refusal and default-budget cost. Treat shape coverage as bounded to the authored ontology until novel operator families are selected and validated without supplied rules.

## Lower-than operator-shape transfer (2026-09-29)

A second preregistered selector panel tests `thresholded_lower_branch` on threshold-4 and threshold-6 piecewise scaling, with five workers per task and wording condition. Trigger wording selects `Times/Lt/IfThenElse` and transfers exactly in 10/10 workers; neutral wording selects no shape and reaches the 200,000-candidate cap in 10/10. The threshold-4 candidate reduction is 3.96×; threshold-6 is 1.44× and fails the preregistered ≥1.5× requirement. All eight capture integrity checks pass, while 9/10 behavioral gates pass. This is a bounded result for a second authored shape, not general grammar learning; candidate work varies materially by task despite a fixed four-operation selection. Keep the failed threshold-6 margin visible and use it to choose the next scale/cost gate, without post-hoc budget changes ([results](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_LOWER_SHAPE_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_LOWER_SHAPE_TRANSFER_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_lower_shape_transfer_v1_20260929_analysis.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_lower_shape_transfer_v1_20260929_raw.jsonl), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/synthesis_lower_shape_transfer_v1_20260929_lock.json)).

**Next gate:** challenge both authored shapes with a third operation family and negative tasks that resemble their language but require unsupported behavior; measure selector choice, cap/refusal, accepted false generalization, and cost. Report trigger coverage as a fixed-ontology capability until a novel shape is selected and validated without a registered rule.

## Unshaped clamp synthesis transfer (2026-09-29)

A third scalar task-family panel tests `Min(upper, Max(x, lower))` for bounds `[0,5]` and `[-2,4]`, with five fresh workers per function, six training rows, and six disjoint holdouts. The standard Rung 3 route selects no authored operator shape, accepts and transfers in 10/10 workers (60/60 holdout points), and uses 8,230/6,663 median candidates. Median end-to-end `pump` wall times are 34.2/27.0 ms; peak process RSS is about 43.8 MB. All nine integrity and both transfer gates pass. This is evidence for small compositions from the fixed numeric operator ontology outside the threshold-shape rules; it does not show broad default-grammar scaling, robustness to competing fitting programs, or primitive induction ([results](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_UNSHAPED_CLAMP_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20260929.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_UNSHAPED_CLAMP_TRANSFER_V1_PREREG_20260929.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_unshaped_clamp_transfer_v1_20260929_analysis.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_unshaped_clamp_transfer_v1_20260929_raw.jsonl), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/synthesis_unshaped_clamp_transfer_v1_20260929_lock.json)).

**Next gate:** raise expression depth and create training sets with multiple valid candidates that disagree off-support; preregister an independent holdout oracle and candidate/size cap. Record whether the default Occam ordering selects the intended composition, whether it falsely accepts alternatives, and how costs grow. Include a gap/refusal arm and preserve a fixed-grammar oracle as a diagnostic upper bound.

### Off-support ambiguity v1.1 result (2026-10-01)

The follow-up completes the ambiguity gate with 15 fresh workers and 10/10 independent integrity/behavior gates. On examples compatible with both identity and square, default enumeration accepts identity in 5/5 workers and gets 0/20 analytic square holdouts correct. This is a predictive failure against the declared target, not evidence that the sparse examples identify the target. With square-disambiguating examples, all 5 workers transfer exactly on 20/20 heldouts (median 61 candidates). Contradictory labels produce a gap only after the 200,000-candidate cap in 5/5 workers (median 266 ms). See [v1.1 results](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_OFFSUPPORT_AMBIGUITY_V1_1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_OFFSUPPORT_AMBIGUITY_V1_PREREG_20261001.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_OFFSUPPORT_AMBIGUITY_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20261001.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_synthesis_offsupport_ambiguity_v1_1.py), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_substrate_synthesis_offsupport_ambiguity_v1_1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/synthesis_offsupport_ambiguity_v1_1_20261001_lock.json), [raw](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_offsupport_ambiguity_v1_1_20261001_raw.jsonl), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_offsupport_ambiguity_v1_1_20261001_analysis.json). V1's missing PID gate remains disclosed; it is diagnostic and not pooled.

**Next gate:** specify the policy for multiple fitting programs: explicit-prior selection, a discriminating query, or a gap. Implement and compare these against default Occam and broad enumeration under matched grammar/cost budgets. Score predictive accuracy separately from intended-rule identification, and report cap/refusal cost. No query-selection capability is established yet.
# Overall goal status

The current programme status, measured progress, evidence limitations, and next gated work are summarized in [Substrate capability and tractability: overall status](SUBSTRATE_CAPABILITY_AND_TRACTABILITY_OVERALL_STATUS_20260929.md). The overall goal remains active: bounded operating regimes are increasingly characterized, while natural cheap-cut prevalence, enforceable closure termination, autonomous structural induction, and broad controlled scaling remain open.
## Current thoughtexperiment throughput work (2026-09-30)

The working objective is to make exploration cheap enough to run broad candidate panels against one immutable primary revision, while preserving exact outcome/residual parity and auditable branch isolation. A refreshed measured six-candidate fixed-revision batch achieves 1.61–1.79× the throughput of six standalone rehearsals at 771–10,771 nodes; a separate 50,771-node capture gives 1.50×. The batch uses one shared baseline and O(1) graph/rule revision checks. Each candidate still takes about 0.1–0.16 s, and only one of six candidates succeeds on the current synthetic task. CoW remains a general-purpose substrate feature for isolation and shared immutable bases across future consumers; the current task-specific speed results constrain its performance claims, not the value of the capability itself.

**Thoughtexperiment phase attribution v1 (2026-09-30):** optional instrumentation separates candidate branch snapshot/setup, candidate rule patch, and model-after prediction. The source-locked six-candidate batch runner records these timings without changing semantic parity rows. Two measured repeats plus one warmup at 0/1k/10k unrelated nodes pass exact batch/standalone result parity and primary-state guards. Batch medians are 734/409/649 ms; standalone medians are 1,221/631/1,042 ms (1.66×/1.54×/1.61×). Candidate phase medians across the six branches are 12.70/7.11/12.04 ms snapshot/setup, 14.02/7.31/11.65 ms rule patch, and 76.24/42.96/65.91 ms model-after prediction. The repeat count is small and elapsed-time variation is visible; prediction is the largest of these three measured candidate phases, so eliminating only the outer branch copy will not yield an order-of-magnitude total speedup. These phase boundaries are intentionally coarse: model-after includes structural prediction and nested bounded looks, which should be split in a subsequent profile before selecting an optimization. The capture is [compressed to preserve full trial data](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_six_candidate_phase_profile_v1.json.gz); source runner is [here](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_six_candidate_batch_v1.py).

**Nested prediction phase profile v1 (2026-09-30):** source-locked timing splits candidate model-after prediction into structural frontier scanning, bounded forward look, and trace minting; each nested imagination is further split into branch/rule setup, preparation, collapse tick, residual readout, and trace minting. At 0/1k/10k unrelated nodes, five measured repeats plus two warmups give 58–64 ms bounded-look medians and 17–20 ms structural-scan medians; trace minting is below 0.1 ms. Each look runs three rounds, with nested branch/rule setup at 12–14 ms per round, collapse around 1.2 ms, and readout around 1.4–1.5 ms. Batch/standalone medians are 750–781/1,182–1,314 ms (1.55×–1.75×); exact output parity and primary-state isolation pass. Repeated internal branch creation is an immediate CoW target, while frontier scans need separate optimization. This remains one synthetic graph family and one host. The [compressed raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_six_candidate_prediction_phase_v1.json.gz) preserves detailed trials; the [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_six_candidate_batch_v1.py) fixes protocol and source hashes.

**Native persistent-page primitive probe v1 (2026-09-30):** an isolated Rust `CowPagedVec<T>` prototype uses a shared radix root and 64-slot pages. The source-locked probe compares root fork, first write, fork-plus-sparse-write, reads, and drop against `Vec<u64>::clone` at four sizes (771–50,771), five branch fanouts (1/2/4/8/32), and 25 repeats per cell. All 20 cells pass exact value checks, isolation from the base, divergent writes in sibling branches, and shared untouched-page checks. At 50,771/fanout 32, fork-plus-one-write is 35.22 μs versus 8,138.31 μs for clone-plus-write; at 771/fanout 32 it is slower (10.36 versus 3.71 μs). Reads cost about 5.2–18.4 ns/op versus about 0.5–1.7 ns/op on `Vec`, and branch drops are also slower. Base conversion is excluded, payload is a fixed `u64`, indexes are not represented, and memory allocation is not yet measured. Thus the prototype demonstrates cheap large sparse branches with the expected read and reclamation costs, not graph integration or end-to-end speed. Next: measure realistic `NodeData`/`EdgeData` pages, bytes copied and allocation counts, then integrate slabs and indexes as one branch-local semantic unit. See the [prototype](../../../runners/dsl/src/cow_paged_vec.rs), [Rust probe](../../../runners/dsl/src/bin/cow_paged_vec_probe.rs), [source-locked runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/cow_paged_vec_probe_v1.py), and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/cow_paged_vec_probe_v1.json).

**Partial graph slab-sharing comparison v1 (2026-09-30):** the eager-copy control now explicitly deep-materializes node/edge pages, while a second `Substrate` fork shares only those pages and copies query indexes. The same randomized six-candidate runner compares `native_full_copy_scoped` and `native_shared_slab_scoped` at 0/1k/10k unrelated nodes. Five measured repeats plus two warmups pass exact cross-backend results/residuals and primary-state isolation. Paired shared/eager batch-time ratios are 0.99/1.19/0.94 at those sizes; five paired blocks show substantial spread, so this is no stable end-to-end win. Per-candidate outer snapshot/setup medians are 16.36/15.00, 14.98/12.21, and 19.65/13.86 ms (eager/shared). The partial CoW route improves that phase at +1k/+10k but remains noisy and does not share adjacency/index maps, which are the next integration surface. Memory, realistic payloads, larger graphs, and independent hosts remain unmeasured. See the [source-locked capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_cow_shared_slab_comparison_v1.json.gz), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_six_candidate_batch_v1.py), and [implementation design](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_COW_SUBSTRATE_DESIGN.md).

Next work should lower *marginal* rehearsal cost so the same wall-time budget buys much larger candidate diversity. A matched six-candidate native-copy/process-CoW comparison passes exact nested-result parity and primary isolation, but fork-per-candidate throughput is 0.58×/0.62×/0.75× native at 771/1,771/10,771 nodes and 0.70× at 50,771 nodes. Process is slower in 17 of 18 paired measured blocks. It removes the outer eager branch clone but retains native copies for each internal predictive look to preserve semantics, and pays six fork/wait/pipe round trips. A separate branch-creation-only comparison (eight measured blocks, two warmups) finds process-CoW slower through 10,771 nodes but 1.91× faster at 50,771 nodes (6.83 ms versus 13.06 ms); visible focus scope and primary state match exactly. The crossover shows that large-state copy cost can matter while the full-batch result shows it is not yet the dominant total cost. Extending the full native batch to 50,771 nodes gives 956 ms versus 1,436 ms standalone (1.50×), with candidate medians in the capture; the matched process-CoW batch takes 1,348 ms versus 941 ms native (0.70×). Thus copy cost is not the only or current leading end-to-end bottleneck. The next architectural gate is a native immutable-base/branch-local-overlay prototype that treats CoW as a general isolation and shared-state capability, and makes candidate and internal-look semantics explicit. The existing `GraphMutationLog` is a readout journal, not a complete rollback log: edge before-images record prior existence rather than prior attributes, and the journal does not capture allocator/free-list or all derived-index state. Extend or replace that contract before using journal replay to recycle a branch; prove exact node-ID and rule-order behavior as well as residual parity. Measure mutation/read costs and memory as well as fork cost; maintain exact branch residuals without graph-wide scans, including deletes and nested derived state; reuse immutable rules, terms, and baseline prediction safely; broaden the task panel to independent correction/transformation families; and report peak RSS/private dirty memory and candidates at fixed time and memory budgets. The 10× marginal-cost target remains open. The [CoW design proposal](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_COW_SUBSTRATE_DESIGN.md) defines the reusable snapshot/branch/result contract, field policies, storage tradeoffs, and gates before a native implementation. See the native [batch runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_six_candidate_batch_v1.py), [native captures](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_six_candidate_batch_v1.json), [50k native capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_six_candidate_batch_50k_v1.json), the [process-CoW batch runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_process_cow_batch_v1.py) and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_process_cow_batch_v1.json), [50k process-CoW capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_process_cow_batch_50k_v1.json), and [branch setup runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_branch_creation_cost_v1.py) and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_branch_creation_cost_v1.json).

**Full-process CoW memory measurement (2026-09-30):** fresh Python/native processes capture Linux RSS/PSS and clean/dirty private/shared pages at baseline, after branch creation, after one isolated branch write, and after drop/GC. The 45 measured cells cover 771, 10,771 and 50,771 nodes for eager, shared-record-page, and shared graph-page forks, with five randomized-order repeats per cell after one warmup. All primary graph/rule revision and branch-local mutation checks pass. At 50,771 nodes, median branch-creation RSS/PSS deltas are 11,308 KiB eager, 4,868 KiB shared records, and 4,448 KiB shared graph pages; at baseline and 10,771 nodes the observed deltas are similar across routes (about 212 KiB and 1,272 KiB). The process-level memory result therefore supports a large-state advantage in this fixture, while showing no meaningful low-state benefit at this granularity. The small single-node mutation is below measurable `smaps_rollup` resolution. These are whole-process resident deltas on one Linux host, not native allocation attribution; allocator retention and runtime effects limit the drop measurement. CoW remains useful as a general immutable-state/isolation interface that can serve thought experiments and future batched inference or vLLM-style consumers; this benchmark establishes neither a vLLM integration nor general workload speedups. See [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_full_substrate_pss_v1.py) and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_full_substrate_pss_v1.json).

**Graph-page CoW mixed-mutation semantics v1 (2026-09-30):** a new source-locked Rust evaluation applies attribute insert/update/removal, node retyping, edge deletion, cascading node deletion, recycled-ID node append, edge append, nested fork, and divergent sibling writes to eager, shared-record, and shared-graph-page forks at 771/10,771/50,771 nodes. All nine backend × size rows match the eager branch's canonical live nodes and outgoing-edge structure/attributes; primary-state, nested-fork, sibling-isolation, and delete/append ID-reuse gates pass. This strengthens graph-level semantic evidence for general isolated branches beyond sparse edge insertion. It is one directed-path fixture and does not compare every derived index, concurrent mutations, arbitrary operation permutations, full `Substrate` state, timings, or memory. See the [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/typed_graph_cow_mutation_semantics_v1.py), [Rust probe](../../../runners/dsl/src/bin/typed_graph_cow_mutation_semantics_probe.rs), and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_mutation_semantics_v1.json).

**Graph-page CoW derived-index mutation semantics v2 (2026-09-30):** the follow-up to v1 declares attribute indexes on both original and retyped node classes and compares derived query signatures across eager, shared-record, and shared-graph-page branches at the same three graph sizes. The oracle exercises indexed-value updates, type-index migration on retype, deletion and ID reuse, edge deletion/append in type buckets, incoming/outgoing neighbour lists, nested forks, and divergent siblings. All nine rows pass exact signature parity and the existing base/isolation gates. This strengthens evidence that derived maps copied eagerly remain coherent when paged records/adjacency use CoW. It is still one path topology with selected declared indexes and no concurrent or randomized-order mutations, full Substrate audit, timing, or memory measure. See the [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/typed_graph_cow_mutation_semantics_v2.py), [Rust probe](../../../runners/dsl/src/bin/typed_graph_cow_mutation_semantics_probe_v2.rs), and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_mutation_semantics_v2.json).

**Graph-page CoW topology and mutation-order replication v3 (2026-09-30):** 81 source-locked rows cross three graph sizes, three topology families (path, star-augmented, grid-augmented), three mutation schedules, and three fork backends. The schedules move independent attribute, type, and edge operations around node deletion/reuse while preserving necessary dependencies. All rows pass canonical graph and selected derived-index parity against same-schedule eager controls; base, nested-branch, and sibling isolation plus ID reuse pass. A no-build replay reproduces all semantic rows and all source/runner/binary hashes. This adds controlled topology/order robustness but all fixtures share a path backbone and remain synthetic. Independent graph families, concurrent mutation, full Substrate semantics, and cross-host replication remain open. See the [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/typed_graph_cow_mutation_semantics_v3.py), [Rust probe](../../../runners/dsl/src/bin/typed_graph_cow_mutation_semantics_probe_v3.rs), and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_mutation_semantics_v3.json).

**GenMint process-restart persistence/reuse v1 (2026-09-30):** the preregistered six matrix/layout cells × three arms × five repeats completed all 90 sequences with no worker failures. An amended independent analysis passes 15 integrity/semantic gates, including exact randomized schedule and input reconstruction, unique producer/consumer PIDs, exact graph/grammar restore, semantic native-rule restore, checkpoint hash/byte reconciliation, and continuous/restart output parity. The enabled learner acquires the intended matrix in 25/30 sequences; shearB × adjacent layout fails 0/5 despite `recognized_transformed`. For acquired sequences, all 400/400 held-out calls route through the training-acquired generator and match independent targets after restart. The 80 calls in acquisition-failure cells use another expected-matrix generator and are not credited as acquired reuse. Median checkpoint size/write/restore are 392 KB/5.30 ms/132.9 ms. Median whole-sequence wall is 422 ms continuous-enabled, 840 ms restart-enabled, 871 ms restart-disabled; restart adds about 410 ms versus continuous, while paired restart-enabled is modestly faster than disabled (−28.8 ms median, 19/30 pairs; among acquired pairs −44.6 ms, 19/25). This demonstrates bounded object-level persistence and selected reuse, not self-improvement or broad transfer; aggregate economic benefit remains small and family-dependent. The first analyzer expected labels in the wrong place; that full initial pilot and its lock are preserved, and the final panel reran under a refreshed source lock. See [results](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_PROCESS_RESTART_REUSE_V1_RESULTS_20260930.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENMINT_PROCESS_RESTART_REUSE_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20260930.md), [runner](../../../scripts/genmint_process_restart_reuse_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/genmint_process_restart_reuse_v1_lock_20260930.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/genmint_process_restart_reuse_v1_20260930.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/genmint_process_restart_reuse_v1_1_analysis_20260930.json).

**General-purpose CoW capability gate (2026-09-30):** evaluate snapshot/branch as a reusable substrate contract, not as a synonym for thoughtexperiment speedup. Require immutable snapshot identity and revision, isolated independent/nested branches, cancellation/drop with bounded reclamation, deterministic receipts, explicit revision-conflict handling, and opt-in adoption, all parity-checked against eager copying. Exercise one base snapshot through at least two distinct consumers and one read-only shared-base consumer while keeping backend choice invisible to callers. The current `fork_*_experiment` methods are prototype entry points, and graph-page measurements establish neither this complete contract nor vLLM compatibility. A vLLM-style shared-prefix/KV-block adapter remains a separate future workload gate.

**Program IR candidate-snapshot transfer v1 (2026-09-30):** a source-locked 10-worker panel tests the standard scalar Rung 3 route on two clamp functions. All ten workers acquire exactly one graph-resident Program with one IR root; all 60 held-out values match the independent clamp oracle, with zero accepted false predictions. Eager-copy and shared-graph-page children match outputs, traps, Program/IR identity, and canonical resulting graph/grammar/rule digest; candidate and primary snapshots remain unchanged. Frozen and examples-ingested/no-pump controls contain no task-specific executable Program. Median synthesis pump is 95.3 ms; median validation branch wall is 81.6 ms eager and 70.6 ms shared pages, descriptive only. This adds a second, independent object-level acquisition representation next to GenMint’s `DimensionGenerator`; both remain shallow authored families and do not establish natural-task prevalence, forgetting resistance, process durability, formal P3-E1, or general CoW speed. See [results](SUBSTRATE_PROGRAM_IR_CANDIDATE_SNAPSHOT_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20260930.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_PROGRAM_IR_CANDIDATE_SNAPSHOT_V1_PREREG_20260930.md), [runner](../../../scripts/program_ir_candidate_snapshot_transfer_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/program_ir_candidate_snapshot_transfer_v1_20260930_lock.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/program_ir_candidate_snapshot_transfer_v1_20260930_raw.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/program_ir_candidate_snapshot_transfer_v1_analysis_20260930.json).

**Rung 3 ambiguity and counterexample response v1 (2026-09-30):** 15 source-locked workers compare sparse hinge examples, one externally selected distinguishing counterexample under the broad default grammar, and the same correction with an oracle-supplied compact grammar. Sparse/default accepts a predicate shortcut in all five workers; it fits all 30 training observations but makes 30/30 held-out errors. Adding `(0,3) → (2,3)` yields no accepted program and reaches the 200,000-candidate cap in all five broad-grammar workers; the error is converted to an honest gap. With `Plus, Minus, Max, TupleOf` supplied, the corrected task is accepted in 5/5 and transfers exactly on 30/30 holdout points after 58,824 candidates median. Eager and shared-page candidate branches have exact evaluation and complete state-digest parity, with primary/candidate isolation. This quantifies the tradeoff between ambiguity, a single useful query, and default search tractability, but the query and grammar are supplied by the experimenter; it provides no autonomous query/grammar-selection result. See [results](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_AMBIGUITY_COUNTEREXAMPLE_V1_RESULTS_20260930.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_SYNTHESIS_AMBIGUITY_COUNTEREXAMPLE_V1_PREREG_20260930.md), [runner](../../../scripts/synthesis_ambiguity_counterexample_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/synthesis_ambiguity_counterexample_v1_20260930_lock.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_ambiguity_counterexample_v1_20260930_raw.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/synthesis_ambiguity_counterexample_v1_analysis_20260930.json).

**Counterexample repair and query-selection audit (2026-09-30):** the existing 125-task `repair_oracle_feedback` arm feeds the first failing heldout row to `ingest_counterexample` after an accepted holdout failure. This was an explicit secondary oracle-feedback protocol, not a primary autonomous learner condition. It feeds a counterexample on 19 tasks; one reaches `accepted_holdout_ok`, two remain holdout failures, and 16 become gaps (the repair rule refuses or cannot complete most repairs). It was measured 2026-07-31 against an older source revision, so it is historical baseline evidence, not current-source replication. A separate, real query-selection mechanism exists in `domains/cegis_faculty.py::cegis_synthesize`: `find_counterexample` scans a supplied ordered input family and returns the first input on which the current MDL recipe differs from the oracle, then the loop adds that row and resynthesizes. This is a domain-general *first-disagreement* policy, not zero-query-selection. Its limits are material: family order is supplied, the oracle is callable while the scan proceeds (the policy is not label-blind for unselected points), one surviving recipe is used rather than an explicit version space, and no policy comparison or cost-of-query benchmark is registered. The next gate should compare this first-disagreement baseline with seeded-random disagreement, a candidate-set disagreement/information score computed only from current hypotheses and already revealed rows, and an oracle-best upper bound. Keep answers hidden until a query is committed; compare query utility, exact heldout accuracy, false acceptance, gaps, oracle calls, total work, and wall time on fresh functions and permuted family orders. Existing P7 oracle-feedback counts measure downstream repair, not query choice; do not pool the two claims. See `domains/cegis_faculty.py::cegis_synthesize` / `find_counterexample`, its callers `scripts/cegis_faculty_on_sum_of_n.py` and `scripts/cegis_faculty_on_variance.py`, and the P7-D capture `results/prog_synthesis_battery.json` (`p7_verdicts.h7b_repair`).

**CEGIS family-order sensitivity v1 (2026-09-30):** five paired fresh-process runs compare the current ascending-family first-disagreement policy against seeded permutations on the existing triangular-number task. All ten workers pass the independent integrity gates. Query sequences differ in all five pairs, while both policies converge to the same formula and score all six heldouts exactly. Ascending order adds three counterexample rows; each permutation adds two. Median family-oracle calls are 20 versus 16 and total CEGIS oracle calls 26 versus 21; median wall time is 6.78 versus 3.35 s. These cost differences are confounded: generator search constants are derived from the observed outputs, so different selected labels alter the search space. This is evidence of order sensitivity, not a random-policy advantage or information-gain result. The next gate must hold the literal set/search space fixed independently of query labels, reveal only committed query labels, charge oracle calls and selection work, and include multiple functions. See [results](CEGIS_QUERY_ORDER_SENSITIVITY_V1_RESULTS_20260930.md), [preregistration](CEGIS_QUERY_ORDER_SENSITIVITY_V1_PREREG_20260930.md), [runner](../../../scripts/cegis_query_order_sensitivity_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/cegis_query_order_sensitivity_v1_20260930_lock.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/cegis_query_order_sensitivity_v1_20260930_raw.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/cegis_query_order_sensitivity_v1_20260930_analysis.json).

**CEGIS family-order sensitivity v2 (2026-09-30):** five paired fresh-process runs repeat the order contrast with an identical 15-literal vocabulary fixed for every synthesis call, independent of selected labels. All ten workers pass integrity checks and converge to the same formula with exact 6/6 heldout transfer. Ascending input order selects three counterexamples in every replicate; seeded permutations select two, with varying values. Median family-oracle calls are 20 versus 16, candidates explored 3.38M versus 2.76M, and synthesis time 151.96 versus 102.23 s. This removes the v1 vocabulary confound and supports material order sensitivity on this task, but does not establish a generally superior random policy or learned information-gain selection. The fixed vocabulary makes search much costlier than the default, exposing a grammar/search-size tradeoff. Next, repeat across task functions and candidate families, then compare a label-sealed substrate selector against these order baselines under charged query/search budgets. See [results](CEGIS_QUERY_ORDER_SENSITIVITY_V2_RESULTS_20260930.md), [preregistration](CEGIS_QUERY_ORDER_SENSITIVITY_V2_PREREG_20260930.md), [runner](../../../scripts/cegis_query_order_sensitivity_v2.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/cegis_query_order_sensitivity_v2_20260930_lock.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/cegis_query_order_sensitivity_v2_20260930_raw.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/cegis_query_order_sensitivity_v2_20260930_analysis.json).

**Cross-task CEGIS family-order sensitivity v1 (2026-09-30):** the follow-up tests five paired schedules on a triangular-number task and five on population variance. The shared literal set is held at `{-1,0,1,2}` by a source-locked target wrapper, preventing output labels from expanding the grammar. All 20 workers pass integrity checks. Queries differ across all pairs. On triangular numbers both policies score 5/5 exact heldout workers; seeded order uses one versus two counterexamples median and takes 0.40 versus 0.58 s. On variance, fixed order gives 5/5 exact heldout outcomes, seeded order 4/5; both use two versus one query median, but native search is much more expensive (2.81M versus 2.77M candidates; 118 versus 84 s median) and one permuted run does not find a final program. The query-order effect transfers across these two authored families, but seeded selection is not uniformly reliable. Raw callback logs capture queried inputs; deterministic labels are reconstructable from locked oracles, though a future panel should capture callback outputs explicitly. Next, add fresh functions per family and compare selectors while enforcing answer/candidate-query budgets and treating cap hits as ordinary outcomes. See [results](CEGIS_CROSS_TASK_QUERY_ORDER_V1_RESULTS_20260930.md), [protocol](CEGIS_CROSS_TASK_QUERY_ORDER_V1_PREREG_20260930.md), [runner](../../../scripts/cegis_cross_task_query_order_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/cegis_cross_task_query_order_v1_20260930_lock.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/cegis_cross_task_query_order_v1_20260930_raw.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/cegis_cross_task_query_order_v1_20260930_analysis.json).

**Label-blind finite-pool query ranking v1 (2026-09-30):** a new substrate-side selector ranks candidates by predictive entropy over four explicit hypotheses using native Term evaluation; it has no oracle input. A source-locked 120-worker panel across scalar triangular numbers, population variance, and Euler characteristic passes all 2,707 independent integrity/label/survivor checks. After one oracle answer, the entropy selector uniquely identifies the correct hypothesis in 10/10 runs for all three tasks. Fixed-first is also sufficient for triangular number and variance, but never uniquely identifies Euler among its four hypotheses (0/10); seeded random does so 2/10, entropy does so 10/10. Ranking 11–13 candidates costs 44–52 hypothesis evaluations and 0.77–1.20 ms median; each eligible policy consumes one oracle call. This establishes a bounded query-ranking mechanism, not hypothesis generation or full CEGIS integration. The hypotheses and task families are authored, and equal weights are assumed. Initial constructor/setup failures and excluded smoke runs are documented and retained. Next, connect the ranker to a substrate-maintained candidate/version set, compare on fresh functions with matched search cost, and measure whether query answers reduce subsequent synthesis work. See [results](SUBSTRATE_LABEL_BLIND_QUERY_RANKING_V1_RESULTS_20260930.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_LABEL_BLIND_QUERY_RANKING_V1_PREREG_20260930.md), [selector](../../../domains/query_selection.py), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_label_blind_query_ranking_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_label_blind_query_ranking_v1_20260930_lock.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_label_blind_query_ranking_v1_20260930_raw.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_label_blind_query_ranking_v1_20260930_analysis.json).

**Generated-pool active querying and serial branch reuse (2026-09-30):** an opt-in generated-pool Euler experiment now combines bounded native synthesis with iterative entropy, fixed-first, and seeded-random querying. Under three authored anchors, generated pools of 218–662 hypotheses are complete at size 5, and each contains a behavior that is exact on six held-out complexes. Entropy isolates that behavior in 2–3 oracle calls across all three anchors, versus 5–7 for fixed-first and a median 4 for seeded random over 60 runs. This reduces query count but increases local compute: median selection-plus-oracle time is 31.8 ms versus 3.2/3.4 ms for fixed/random because entropy evaluates 6,026 hypothesis/query predictions. A corrected cached index preserves exact query and survivor parity; a separate 1/5/20-branch serial reuse panel finds the cache loses at one branch but is 2.70×/6.53× faster at 5/20 branches, with an estimated 642 KB retained Python heap. Every one of 390 hidden branch targets remains in both survivor sets; 357 are unique and 33 remain tolerance-equivalent. This is a bounded, one-family generated version-space mechanism, not integration into the production `cegis_synthesize` loop, independently authored task-family generality, concurrent Rust CoW, or end-to-end learner efficiency. Next compare complete, budgeted generated-pool active querying with the current resynthesis loop on fresh task functions and held-out inputs; charge pool construction, cache build/use, oracle calls, memory, and resynthesis, and count incomplete pools as ordinary failures. See the [Euler results](SUBSTRATE_GENERATED_EULER_ACTIVE_QUERY_V1_2_1_RESULTS_20260930.md), [branch reuse results](SUBSTRATE_QUERY_INDEX_BRANCH_REUSE_V1_1_RESULTS_20260930.md), [active-query analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_generated_euler_active_query_v1_2_1_20260930_analysis.json), and [branch analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_query_index_branch_reuse_v1_1_20260930_analysis.json).

**Generated-pool active query versus iterative MDL resynthesis v1.5 (2026-10-01):** a source-locked five-block panel compares triangular numbers, scalar squares, and Euler characteristic across inline MDL resynthesis, generated-pool entropy, fixed-first, and five seeded-random query orders (60 fresh workers). All 215 integrity/semantic checks pass; every arm is exact on held-out inputs in 5/5 blocks per task, and all complete pools contain the target behavior (9/1/34 behaviors; 8,709/945/10,269 enumerated terms explored). Entropy needs 1/0/2 labels versus MDL CEGIS's 11/10/17 candidate labels; however, charged learner wall (pool construction + selection/filter + labeled oracle calls) is about 6×/77×/32× higher for entropy, with similar costs for fixed/random pool arms because enumeration dominates. Entropy matches random query count on these three tasks; fixed-first uses more queries on triangular/Euler. Thus complete-pool selection has no end-to-end efficiency win here despite reducing labels. The CEGIS control is an inline replay rather than a call to `cegis_synthesize`, because the production API does not expose matched grammar controls. These are three authored small tasks, not general learner evidence. The next useful gate is to reduce/version pool construction incrementally and repeat under larger hypothesis-space/input-size ladders; keep incomplete-pool rate, held-out exactness, and total charged work as outcomes before integrating into the production loop. See [results](SUBSTRATE_GENERATED_POOL_CEGIS_COMPARISON_V1_5_RESULTS_20261001.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_GENERATED_POOL_CEGIS_COMPARISON_V1_PREREG_20261001.md), [v1.5 amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENERATED_POOL_CEGIS_COMPARISON_V1_5_AMENDMENT_20261001.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_generated_pool_cegis_comparison_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_generated_pool_cegis_comparison_v1_5_20261001_lock.json), [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_generated_pool_cegis_comparison_v1_5_20261001_raw.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_generated_pool_cegis_comparison_v1_5_20261001_analysis.json).

**Generated-pool batch/stream comparison v1.1 (2026-10-02):** 54 paired fresh-process rows compare `domains.generator.synthesize` batch versus streaming cohort registration at size caps 5/6/7 and 4/8/12 unlabeled probes, with one triangular-number training example. The corrected analyzer passes all 10 gates; every pair has exact hypothesis-digest, stop, count, and held-out coverage parity, and all pools complete. Exploration steps from 945 to 8,629–8,709 at size 7; median synthesis is 0.22–0.58 s. Streaming does not reliably reduce wall time; process peak RSS is 4–8% lower in the size-7 cells, with interpreter/native baseline included. The sole finite held-out-exact behavior is present in all size-7 repetitions and absent at sizes 5/6. This is a small one-family result, not an incremental search implementation or broad rung-three tractability result. Two runner/analyzer pilot defects and the post-capture analysis correction are disclosed. Next test a larger size ladder with a parent process cap, record incomplete cohorts without retry, and evaluate whether indexed/incremental collection can reduce total work and memory ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENERATOR_STREAM_SCALE_V1_1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENERATOR_STREAM_SCALE_V1_1_PREREG_20261002.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_generator_stream_scale_v1_2_analysis_20261002.json)).

**Generated-pool stress scale v1.2 (2026-10-02):** a preregistered 12-worker follow-up compares size caps 7/9 under batch and streaming collection, fixed at 12 unlabeled probes, with 10-second internal and 15-second parent caps. The corrected 10-check analysis passes; all workers complete and paired pools/held-out outcomes are identical. At size 9, exploration reaches 88,069 terms and 1,306 fitting hypotheses in about 7.1 s. Streaming lowers process peak RSS from 71,956 to 53,948 KiB (25%) with no stable wall-time advantage. No cap or timeout boundary was reached, so size 11 with stricter memory/time limits is next. This remains one arithmetic family and one anchor, not a general induction tractability result ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENERATOR_STREAM_SCALE_V1_2_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENERATOR_STREAM_SCALE_V1_2_PREREG_20261002.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_generator_stream_scale_v1_3_analysis_20261002.json)).

**Generated-pool stress boundary v1.3 (2026-10-02):** under a 12-second internal timeout, 16-second parent cap, and 2 GiB address-space limit, all three size-9 batch/stream pairs complete with exact pool parity, while all six size-11 workers explicitly return incomplete `timeout` pools. Streaming explores about 12% more terms and reduces median process peak RSS from 338 MiB to 99 MiB (about 71%); the size-11 partial pools differ, so neither receives parity credit. Three finite-heldout-exact hypotheses remain in each partial pool, which does not certify grammar coverage. No parent timeout or address-space failure occurred. This identifies an actual time-driven completeness boundary and a workload-specific streaming memory advantage, not asymptotic or cross-task tractability. Next test independently authored task families, multiple anchors, and resumable/incremental generation; never treat partial-pool target presence as learner adequacy ([results](SUBSTRATE_GENERATOR_STREAM_SCALE_V1_3_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENERATOR_STREAM_SCALE_V1_3_PREREG_20261002.md), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_generator_stream_scale_v1_4_analysis_20261002.json)).

**CoW capability framing:** treat copy-on-write as a general isolation and compatibility capability with independent value, even when a workload does not get faster. Keep the caller-facing snapshot/branch/receipt contract independent of the backing representation so future consumers can use it for thoughtexperiments, search, simulations, speculative execution, sandboxing, and shared-prefix or KV-block serving patterns. A vLLM-style adapter is a distinct integration target: validate block ownership, prefix reuse, mutation isolation, cancellation/reclamation, and backend-independent behavior before making compatibility claims. The current graph-page results establish neither a KV-cache adapter nor vLLM compatibility.

**Adoption integration follow-up (2026-10-02):** a locked three-process seeded `WorldAdapter` panel now exercises the strict opt-in receipt guard at `teach_write_shape_from_example`'s actual `teach()` boundary. Rejected, ambiguous, incomplete, invalid-provenance, and missing receipts all preserve codebook shapes and epoch; accepted evidence adds one shape and advances the epoch once. Median full-seed boot is 17.57 s, refusal handling 3.4–5.8 ms, and accepted teaching/adoption 32.7 ms. The initial incomplete-evidence fixture was corrected under a recorded amendment and refreshed lock. Candidate identity binds source bytes, parsed name/arguments/Term, request text, and lesson provenance. The gate checks consistency, not label-provider identity or truth; provenance identifiers remain caller-declared. Legacy behavior remains available unless strict mode is requested. Persistence/restart and stale-source/request replay are covered in the follow-up below; independent label audit and cross-task/host replication remain open. See [integration results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_RECEIPT_ADOPTION_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_RECEIPT_ADOPTION_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20261002.md), and linked raw/analysis artifacts.

**Persistence/restart follow-up (2026-10-02):** the persistence and replay gate is now measured in three writer/reader subprocess pairs with a full seed boot on each side. The v1.2 amended analysis passes 21 checks: exact candidate attributes restore, same-receipt replay is live and durable-state idempotent, and stale source/request identities refuse without codebook mutation. The first run exposed duplicate live nodes on replay; `domains.teach.teach()` now reuses exact existing `(type, attrs)` nodes. Current medians are 59.5 ms for accepted teach plus durable write and 32.8 ms for replay; writer/read boots are 16.67/19.42 s. This remains one authored function with harness-supplied labels. The cost follow-up attributes the old multi-second component to whole-rule-store JSON export inside information-commitment loading; prefix export now leaves the end-to-end persisted teach at 59.5 ms. Direct prefix timing is order sensitive, and the earlier 3.315 s writer timing came from a failed replay capture without a direct source hash for that module, so it is not a formal paired speedup estimate. Remaining work is receipt revocation/competing-candidate behavior, independent label audit, persistence costs across task families, and cross-host replication. See [results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_RECEIPT_PERSISTENCE_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [v1.1 idempotency amendment](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_RECEIPT_PERSISTENCE_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20261002.md), [v1.2 performance amendment](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_RECEIPT_PERSISTENCE_V1_2_AMENDMENT_20261002.md), and linked capture/analysis.
**Cross-task adequacy-gated acquisition follow-up (2026-10-02):** three fresh full-seed workers exercised the same strict adoption boundary on parity and clamp, plus an identity candidate mislabeled as square. Both positive tasks accepted fresh-probe receipts and transferred exactly through native Terms and emitted Python on 183/183 held-outs. The identity candidate matched its one acquisition example but was rejected by fresh square probes without codebook growth. Each label is recomputed from a separate, source-hashed oracle module; this establishes reproducible lineage, not an authenticated external oracle. Median boot is 16.68 s, refusal 5.84 ms, and positive teach/adoption 21.57/22.24 ms. This upgrades mechanism evidence across two authored examples but leaves autonomous example discovery, broader transfer, natural-task prevalence, and independent oracle governance unmeasured. Next use previously uninspected task families with a separately maintained oracle, include label noise and domain shift, and compare gated acquisition against ungated and frozen-codebook arms under equal search and acquisition budgets. See [results](SUBSTRATE_INDEPENDENT_ADEQUACY_CODEWRITE_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_INDEPENDENT_ADEQUACY_CODEWRITE_TRANSFER_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), and linked raw/analysis artifacts.
**Probe-domain coverage A/B (2026-10-02):** three matched strict/ungated pairs now show the gate's domain dependency at the real `teach()` boundary. With identical evidence restricted to the sole fresh point `x=1`, the false identity-as-square candidate is accepted and both arms score 0/4 held-outs. With identical evidence selected from `{x=1,2,3,4}`, strict mode rejects in 3/3 while ungated controls adopt and score 0/4. All 29 gates pass, and request/receipt/label hashes match within each pair. This is an authored adversarial control, not a prevalence estimate; it establishes that caller-chosen finite domains can defeat a validly implemented adequacy check. Next evaluate domain selection under bounded search cost, off-distribution probes, noisy labels, and newly authored task families; report false acceptance and useful-adoption rates jointly. See [results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROBE_COVERAGE_AB_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROBE_COVERAGE_AB_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), and linked raw/analysis artifacts.

**Probe selection under a fixed evidence budget (2026-10-02):** a corrected source/native-locked 720-cell panel finds that maximum prediction entropy over a candidate and supplied alternatives selects the only witness in 30/30 repetitions per broad-domain case. At budget one, seeded hash sampling falsely accepts 56/60 wrong candidates; entropy selection falsely accepts 0/60, while accepting the correct candidate in 30/30 and preserving its held-out behavior. If the admissible domain contains only alias points, both policies falsely accept 30/30. The timed median entropy decision is approximately 0.4 ms versus 0.0009 ms for hash selection, but the latter excludes one-time domain-order preprocessing; treat these as marginal decision costs. The v1 no-fresh-input and v1.1 integer-overflow captures are explicitly diagnostic and excluded. This supports a candidate-challenger probe strategy under a supplied model set, not a production change or general adequacy claim. The follow-up measured early stopping and a second Term family; see [early-stop transfer results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_EARLY_STOP_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md).

**Early stopping and task-family transfer (2026-10-02):** a source/native-locked 1,440-cell panel adds immediate stop on the first candidate residual and a second, two-variable arithmetic family. At budgets 1/2/4, entropy selection falsely accepts 0/60 broad-domain wrong candidates per family, compared with 54/60→39/60 for polynomial and 56/60→46/60 for vector arithmetic under seeded sampling. Entropy needs one label in every broad wrong-candidate repetition, versus mean 3.53/3.65 labels for hash at budget 4; correct-candidate controls pass 30/30 in both families. Alias-only domains still falsely accept 30/30 under both strategies. The marginal selector/evaluation cost remains higher for entropy, about 0.43–0.50 ms versus 0.14–0.25 ms at budget 4, before external oracle latency. This confirms a controlled strategy tradeoff across two Term families, not production effectiveness or natural-task prevalence. The selector-to-receipt-to-adoption path is now exercised separately on full-seed `teach()` workers; see below. See [results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_EARLY_STOP_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_EARLY_STOP_TRANSFER_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), and linked runner/analysis artifacts.

**Challenger selector, receipt, and write-shape adoption integration (2026-10-02):** a new target-blind selector API in `domains/adequacy_probe_selection.py` is exercised through the existing audit request and receipt code and the actual `teach_write_shape_from_example` boundary in nine source-stable fresh full-seed processes. Correct square shapes are accepted/adopted with exact 4/4 held-outs in 3/3 workers; broad-domain identity-as-square candidates are rejected in 3/3, with no codebook epoch growth; a singleton alias domain accepts/adopts identity in 3/3 and fails all held-outs. Six independent gates pass. This proves integration at one write-shape boundary and directly preserves the finite-domain counterexample. The selector, challenger list, domain, and oracle remain caller/harness supplied; the receipt binds the candidate and selected descriptor but does not authenticate the selector or label source. Next test provider authentication and independently authored task families before broader production routing. See [results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_SELECTOR_RECEIPT_ADOPTION_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_SELECTOR_RECEIPT_ADOPTION_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [selector API](../../../domains/adequacy_probe_selection.py), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_selector_receipt_adoption_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_selector_receipt_adoption_v1_lock_20261002.json), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_substrate_adequacy_selector_receipt_adoption_v1.py), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_selector_receipt_adoption_v1_analysis_20261002.json).

**Label-provider spoof at adoption (2026-10-02):** a matched six-process full-seed attack reuses the exact candidate, request, distinguishing `x=2` probe, provider ID, and oracle hash. The honest square label 4 is rejected for identity and causes no adoption in 3/3 runs; a forged value 2 under the same claimed provider identity is accepted and adopted in 3/3, then fails all four held-outs. The accepted receipt passes its own digest/candidate-integrity verifier, confirming that current “provenance” provides internal consistency but no provider authentication. This is a controlled caller-spoof result, not a real service error-rate estimate. Before trusting adequacy receipts, define a pinned provider-key registry, signatures bound to request/probe/value, and registry ownership/key lifecycle; none is implemented here. See [results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROVIDER_SPOOF_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROVIDER_SPOOF_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_provider_spoof_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_provider_spoof_v1_lock_20261002.json), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_substrate_adequacy_provider_spoof_v1.py), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_provider_spoof_v1_analysis_20261002.json).

**HMAC provider-authentication prototype (2026-10-02):** a source/native/seed-locked 12-worker full-seed panel crosses unsigned forgery, truthful evidence, a trusted-but-incorrect signed label, and a correct signed candidate. The opt-in `teach_write_shape_from_example_authenticated` wrapper refuses unsigned forgeries before adoption; all 36/36 tamper, request-replay, and unknown-provider controls fail verification. Truthful evidence rejects the wrong identity in 3/3, and signed correct-square evidence adopts with 4/4 held-outs in 3/3. A configured key signs a false label and it is accepted/adopted in 3/3, showing authentication does not establish correctness. This is a stdlib HMAC prototype with caller-passed key mapping; fixture keys are not deployment keys, the registry is not isolated, and the legacy receipt-only teach path remains callable. Next define a service-owned key registry and rotation/revocation, then replicate across independent candidate/task families before treating this as a trusted gate. See [results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROVIDER_AUTH_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROVIDER_AUTH_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [wrapper](../../../domains/adequacy_provider_auth.py), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_provider_auth_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_provider_auth_v1_lock_20261002.json), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_substrate_adequacy_provider_auth_v1.py), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_provider_auth_v1_analysis_20261002.json).

**HMAC provider-authentication hardening v1.1 (2026-10-02):** the follow-up adds a zero-probe request control after review found the first verifier accepted empty evidence vacuously. The core receipt API indeed accepts the internally consistent empty request; the authenticated wrapper now refuses it explicitly. All 48 tamper, replay, unknown-provider, and empty-probe controls fail closed across 12 fresh workers. The four semantic cases reproduce v1: unsigned spoof blocked, truthful residual refused, correct candidate transfers, trusted-but-incorrect signature still falsely adopts. This closes the empty-set gap in the opt-in path only; no service-owned keyring, key lifecycle, or legacy-path enforcement exists. See [v1.1 results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROVIDER_AUTH_V1_1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_PROVIDER_AUTH_V1_1_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_provider_auth_v1_1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_provider_auth_v1_1_lock_20261002.json), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_substrate_adequacy_provider_auth_v1_1.py), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_provider_auth_v1_1_analysis_20261002.json).

**Reusable snapshot API and lifecycle probe v1 (2026-09-30):** the initial native and Python prototype exposed backend-selecting `snapshot(backend)` and `snapshot.fork()` over an immutable captured graph/rule revision; the application API has since hidden backend selection. A source-locked release probe at 10,000 path nodes, five repeats, and fanout 1/4/16/32 passes all 12 backend/fanout cells for sibling isolation, primary isolation, and read-only access to the captured base. Shared-graph-page fork medians are 0.25–0.27 ms at fanout through 16 and 0.74 ms at fanout 32; eager-copy fork is 2.0–4.1 ms and slab-sharing fork is 1.2–1.4 ms in this fixture. The larger-graph result supports a reusable API and a lower graph-page fork cost, but it is not an end-to-end Thoughtexperiment result. Non-graph `Substrate` state and most graph hash indexes still copy eagerly; typed out/in adjacency bucket maps now share persistent shards. Drop/reclamation, concurrent fanout, cancellation, adoption, revision conflicts, residual receipts, and memory accounting remain open. The [source-locked runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_snapshot_fork_contract_v1.py) and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_snapshot_fork_contract_v1.json) start the lifecycle gate. Future vLLM-style shared-prefix use remains a separate adapter/workload gate; the shared immutable-base abstraction is useful, but graph state is not model KV-cache state.

**Selective graph-index CoW and Thoughtexperiment scaling v1 (2026-10-01):** a 64-shard persistent map now backs the high-cardinality typed `out_by_type`/`in_by_type` indexes in the shared-graph-page route. The source-locked profile shows, at 50,771 path nodes, map fork costs of 0.04–0.05 μs versus 2.32–2.92 ms to materialize eager copies. A 100k-query 50/50 hit/miss stream measures 4.4–5.2 ns per lookup against a flat map's 3.4–3.7 ns; a hash-based shard selector had been 5–8× slower and was replaced before the final measurement. Across path/star/grid, 50k clone medians are 39–83 μs shared versus 11.2–15.8 ms eager; one-edge mutation takes 53–94 μs and 1%-edge mutation 0.71–1.83 ms. Clone-only allocator retention is 0.39–0.95 MiB versus 9.08–11.07 MiB eager, while 1%-write retention is 2.74–4.10 MiB; all 12 cells reclaim branch bytes after drop. All 81 mutation-order/derived-query parity cells pass.

The source-locked six-candidate Substrate batch matches exact outcomes/residuals across eager, direct shared-page, and reusable-snapshot backends. At baseline/+1k, direct shared-page timing has no stable advantage; at +10k it wins all five measured randomized blocks, median 1.16× versus eager. At +50k it wins 5/5 at 1.81× (1,097 ms eager versus 629 ms shared-page median). All arms produce one useful candidate out of six, so this is more throughput for the same bounded synthetic outcome, not better candidate quality. Reusable snapshots preserve the residual contract but do not show a consistent further speedup over direct graph-page forks. This is one synthetic task family/host; the 10× marginal-cost goal, natural-task frequency, broader utility-per-time, peak Substrate memory, independent-host replication, concurrency, and read/write tradeoffs remain open. The current read probe finds a small 1.0–1.6× lookup penalty depending on topology, which must be replicated in actual engine workloads. See the [index profile](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_index_clone_profile_v1.json), [fork/write capture](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_graph_pages_probe_v1.json), [allocator capture](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_graph_pages_memory_probe_v1.json), [81-cell semantics capture](../../../evaluation/reports/typed_graph_cow_mutation_semantics_v3.json), [0/+1k/+10k Thoughtexperiment capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_cow_sharded_indexes_batch_v1.json.gz), and [50k capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_cow_sharded_indexes_50k_batch_v1.json.gz).

**Reusable snapshot Thoughtexperiment integration v1 (2026-09-30):** the six-candidate fixed-revision batch can now choose `native_reusable_snapshot`; one shared immutable base is checked against the post-baseline revision and forked by each candidate. With 2 measured repeats plus 1 warmup at 0 and 1k unrelated nodes, exact candidate outcomes, nested residuals, and primary isolation match `native_shared_graph_pages_scoped` in all cells. Reusable/direct shared-page batch medians are 686.7/639.3 ms at baseline and 608.2/587.5 ms at +1k, with one useful candidate in each batch. The 0.3–0.4 ms base capture is not the dominant cost; remaining graph indexes, wider substrate copies, and nested prediction setup remain. This does not show a throughput improvement and the low repeat count on one synthetic family is directional. It does establish that the reusable interface composes with actual candidate residual readout without changing outputs. Next measure the cost by substrate component, make remaining indexes and rule/term state shareable under the same branch-local semantic contract, then rerun larger fanout and workload panels with memory accounting. See the [batch runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_fixed_revision_six_candidate_batch_v1.py) and compressed [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_reusable_snapshot_batch_v1.json.gz).

**Offline candidate-snapshot efficacy v1 (2026-09-30):** a 30-worker source-locked panel compares an acquired GenMint candidate snapshot against frozen and equal-exposure/no-consolidation branches. See [v4 results](SUBSTRATE_ALL_QUEUE_SCOPED_FALLBACK_V4_RESULTS_20261001.md), [protocol correction](SUBSTRATE_ALL_QUEUE_SCOPED_FALLBACK_V4_1_AMENDMENT_20261001.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_ALL_QUEUE_SCOPED_FALLBACK_V4_PREREG_20261001.md), [runner](../../../scripts/substrate_all_queue_scoped_fallback_v4.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/all_queue_scoped_fallback_v4_lock_20261001.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/all_queue_scoped_fallback_v4_workers_20261001.json), and [strict analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/all_queue_scoped_fallback_v4_analysis_20261001.json).
