## Copy-on-write as a general-purpose capability: next work

Treat CoW as a general isolation and lifecycle capability, with thoughtexperiment as its first consumer rather than its scope. The synthetic shared-prefix consumer passes 30 source-locked workers across three graph sizes and two backends, and the native concurrent lifecycle panel passes 60 paired waves with exact sibling isolation and zero mutation-adjusted allocator residual after drop. The connected-topology follow-up crosses path/star/grid, 10k/50k nodes, 1%/10% writes, and fanout 4/16 in 144 waves; all semantic and lifecycle gates pass. Shared branches use 1.73×–3.12× less total live allocation and win the full-wave timing in all 24 cells. Yet at 50k/fanout16/10% writes, mutation-only allocation is 85.9–110.8 MiB shared versus 6.9–19.3 MiB eager: dense first writes erode the fork advantage even though total live bytes remain lower in these cells. The follow-up placement study crosses four degree profiles with clustered/spread/low-degree/high-degree target selection in 384 waves. With uniform degree four, clustered writes use 62.0 MiB shared total-live allocation versus 128.7 MiB spread; on a 50k star, the hub-including spread case uses 101.2 MiB versus 34.5 MiB for a contiguous leaf cluster. This separates page locality from node degree and shows both affect branch costs. All 64 cells still favor shared snapshot on total memory and median wave time, but results remain synthetic one-host evidence. Next use randomized degree distributions and target sets, then expand task-generated receipt coverage to independent task families and test concurrent commit/conflict handling; actual vLLM/KV integration still requires a named runtime and separate workload evidence. Do not conflate graph CoW pages with KV blocks. See [degree/placement results](COW_CONCURRENT_DEGREE_PLACEMENT_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [topology/write-density results](COW_CONCURRENT_MUTATION_SCALE_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [concurrent lifecycle results](COW_CONCURRENT_BRANCH_LIFECYCLE_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), and [CoW design](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_COW_SUBSTRATE_DESIGN.md).

**CoW capability scope and evaluation:** treat copy-on-write as a reusable substrate primitive for isolation, backend compatibility, and a storage-independent consumer contract, with performance as an additional measured outcome rather than its justification. Preserve an opaque snapshot/fork API and run a shared conformance suite for source immutability, branch/sibling independence, cancellation/drop reclamation, revision-checked residual return, and observable parity across supported storage backends. Track consumer integrations as separate adapters against that contract; vLLM-style prefix/KV serving is one candidate, not the definition of the capability. For each adapter, measure integration coverage and lifecycle correctness separately from speed, memory, and workload throughput. Keep client APIs independent of graph page or allocator representation so future consumers can reuse the boundary without inheriting storage details. Current evidence covers multiple graph consumers, a synthetic shared-prefix lifecycle shape, and 200 high-churn native branch waves with zero adjusted post-drop residual; it does not establish a KV-cache adapter or serving-runtime compatibility.

**High-churn lifecycle v1:** a locked 200-wave native panel retains one primary and reusable snapshot across 25 repeated waves per size/fanout cell. All semantic, primary/later-fork, branch-ID parity, cancellation, and adjusted reclamation gates pass. Across N=10k/50k and fanout 4/16, shared snapshots use 16.0×–22.8× less live requested allocator payload and finish the full concurrent wave 7.7×–13.2× faster than eager copy. This is synthetic node-only evidence on one host, not a leak-freedom proof, natural-task estimate, process-memory result, concurrent commit gate, or serving-runtime result. The within-cell all-live allocation is identical at the first and final wave, and all 200 mutation-adjusted post-drop deltas are zero. See [results](COW_HIGH_CHURN_LIFECYCLE_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [protocol](COW_HIGH_CHURN_LIFECYCLE_V1_PREREG_20261001.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/cow_high_churn_lifecycle_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../scripts/analyze_cow_high_churn_lifecycle_v1.py), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/cow_high_churn_lifecycle_v1.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/cow_high_churn_lifecycle_v1_analysis.json).


## Copy-on-write mutation density and locality gate complete

The fixed-size graph sweep now measures branch writes at 1%, 10%, 50%, and 100% density, with contiguous and evenly spaced active edges for the first three densities, at 10,771 and 50,771 nodes. All 70 fresh-process workers and 14 cells pass semantic and isolation gates. At 50,771 nodes CoW fork remains near 0.1 ms versus 11.5–14.2 ms eager, and CoW concurrent wall time wins 34/35 paired rows at each size. The mutation closure itself can be slower under CoW for sparse, spread writes; PSS advantage changes by treatment. This supports CoW's reusable-isolation/fork capability while identifying branch-local mutation as a separate cost surface. Next, measure the full thoughtexperiment harness under matched candidate workloads and expose branch write/touched-page costs in its receipt; separately specify a storage-independent shared-prefix lifecycle before implementing any serving adapter. See [COW_SNAPSHOT_WRITE_DENSITY_LOCALITY_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md](COW_SNAPSHOT_WRITE_DENSITY_LOCALITY_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md).


## Full Thoughtexperiment reusable-snapshot workload gate complete

The five-repeat +10k/+50k live-harness comparison covers eager, direct shared-page, and reusable snapshot branches with exact outcomes/residual parity across all backends. At +50k, direct and reusable shared-page batch medians are 420 and 423 ms versus 768 ms eager; direct wins 3/5 paired blocks against reusable. Reusable capture costs about 0.28 ms. The exact graph `conclusions` and `derived_only` deltas are empty for all six candidates, so this is real candidate-prediction throughput evidence but not a nonzero graph writeback or touched-page measurement. Next add a productive candidate fixture with a guaranteed nonempty graph residual, then compare extraction and explicit adoption separately under eager/direct/reusable isolation and exact-parity gates. Do not use the empty residual result to claim writeback is cheap. See [v2 results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_REUSABLE_SNAPSHOT_BATCH_V2_RESULTS_20261001.md) and [preregistration](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_REUSABLE_SNAPSHOT_BATCH_V2_PREREG_20261001.md).


## Productive residual branch and adoption gates complete

The amended 15-worker productive-residual panel executes a real hypothesis-triggered native rule across eager, direct shared-page, and reusable snapshot branches at 0/10k/50k unrelated nodes. All 225 executions return the same nonempty total and derived-only residual, change one Fact, add a Conclusion, delete the stale fact, and pass one-step convergence plus terminal no-progress checks. At 50k, five reusable branches take 0.987 ms median plus 0.074 ms snapshot capture, versus 60.072 ms eager and 2.445 ms direct-page batching ([results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_PRODUCTIVE_RESIDUAL_SNAPSHOT_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md)).

The new revision-checked `apply_experiment_graph_delta` path then passes all 9 gates over 15 fresh workers at the same sizes. Accepted `conclusions` receipts match an independent full-primary graph-delta oracle exactly; stale revisions and corrupted before-images reject with no primary graph change. The post-API-encapsulation and edge-attribute rerun measures median apply at 0.380/0.791/1.474 ms and stale rejection at 0.164/0.306/0.316 ms for 0/10k/50k nodes. A key receipt-shape finding: `derived_only` can contain edges referencing injected hypothesis nodes that it omits, so it is not necessarily a closed adoptable delta. Full `conclusions` is the tested receipt. The exactness oracle applies the receipt to full primary state because branch aperture serialization exposes only scoped edges. These timings are descriptive for one authored family. The revision-token audit fixed the `set_rule_area` epoch omission, made semantic stores crate-private with read-only public accessors and tracked writers, and measured/rejected full-state hashing as too costly for the hot path ([audit](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_REVISION_TOKEN_AUDIT_20261001.md)). A five-worker mechanism probe additionally passes added/removed/changed edge-attribute adoption, sparse journal round-trip, and malformed-before-image atomicity ([runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_edge_attr_delta_v1.py), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_edge_attr_delta_v1.json)). A separate five-worker/16-check probe now verifies that hypothesis nodes/edges remain noncommittable, edge changes reground against live before-images, the default gate refuses writes, and explicit approval writes the reviewed edge delta. Next specify deletion-proposal and concurrent-commit atomicity, then test natural-task utility and a storage-independent shared-prefix lifecycle. See [adoption preregistration](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_RESIDUAL_ADOPTION_V1_PREREG_20261001.md), [adoption results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_RESIDUAL_ADOPTION_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), and the [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_residual_adoption_v1.json).


## Thoughtexperiment mixed writeback and incident-edge locality (2026-10-01)

A five-worker source-locked mixed-commit probe passes 20/20 checks per worker. One approved batch combines a node attribute change, node and edge addition, and edge and node deletion through the native expected-revision staged graph-delta transaction. Injected late before-image corruption and an interleaved writer reject the batch without partial content writeback; authorization and application are reported separately. See [mixed commit results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_DELETION_COMMIT_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md).

To avoid whole-graph serialization during node-deletion regrounding, a native O(degree) incident-edge accessor now supplies exact edge attributes. Its preregistered five-worker probe passes local and full-scan oracle parity at (0,4), (10k,4), (50k,4), and (50k,32) background-node/target-degree cells. At 50k nodes, local read medians are 0.064–0.106 ms versus 708–710 ms for full serialization, a 6,687–11,090× difference in these synthetic conditions. This measures the accessor path, not complete regrounding. See [incident-edge results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_INCIDENT_EDGE_REGROUND_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md) and [preregistration](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_INCIDENT_EDGE_REGROUND_V1_PREREG_20261001.md).

Next: expand mixed receipt combinations and graph sizes; integrate protected-operation policy and deletion-hook semantics; add randomized differential coverage against an independent graph oracle; measure full reground latency over deletion counts and topologies; then evaluate proposal generation/adoption on held-out tasks. Keep mechanism correctness separate from proposal usefulness.


## Full node-deletion reground scaling panel (2026-10-01)

Three fresh workers across six graph/deletion treatments all match the survivor oracle. Full `reground()` median is 6.193 ms for 50k chain nodes and 128 degree-2 deletions, 5.535 ms for 50k star nodes and 128 leaf deletions, and 267.783 ms for deleting the 49,999-edge hub in a 50k star. This shows that deletion aperture matters alongside graph and receipt size; the treatments do not establish an asymptotic law or natural-task envelope. The three-worker p95 proxy is only the maximum worker median. Next cross deletion count with graph size while holding topology and degree constant, then add randomized oracle and mixed-conflict cells. ## Generated residual commit phase attribution (2026-10-01)

The source-locked 72-trial profile passes all full-graph, authorization, isolation, and effect-kind gates. For 1,000-node fixtures, the `graph_to_dict()` call inside `commit_imagination` costs 11–42 ms median and dominates all eight cells; staged graph-delta application costs 1.2–1.8 ms. On 64-node fixtures, `information_commitment.assess` costs 12.5–16.9 ms and dominates. Thus the measured commit cost has two separate sources: whole-graph materialization that grows with fixture size and a nearly size-independent manifold-assessment cost. Nested instrumented phase totals overlap and include wrapper overhead; they are not additive partitions. ## Independent targeted-commit factorial v1.1 (2026-10-01)

A corrected 3×3×4 factorial independently crosses 256/1,000/5,000 live nodes, background out-degree 0/2/8, and deletion aperture 1/4/32/128. Every non-focal node, including hub spokes, participates in the density-controlled ring, keeping background edge count fixed as aperture changes. Three fresh workers provide 12 paired trials per cell (432 total), with four interior/trailing/mixed tombstone layouts represented in every cell. All full-graph oracles, write-kind checks, rehearsal/refusal isolation gates, and same-ID parity pass. A further 108 injected competing writers reject atomically and preserve the concurrent update.

When pooling four aperture levels per node/density pair, targeted/legacy medians are 6.19/7.63, 7.56/10.69, and 7.09/20.97 ms at 256 nodes and out-degree 0/2/8; 6.75/11.11, 6.53/21.13, and 8.31/59.79 ms at 1,000; and 7.19/32.05, 8.72/99.21, and 15.34/324.73 ms at 5,000. At 5,000 nodes/out-degree 8, targeted commit is 18.55–25.74× faster across the four aperture cells, with 12/12 pair wins in each. This shows that avoiding full-graph materialization helps increasingly as unrelated graph state grows; it remains a one-host circulant result, not a complexity bound. Target cost rises at larger apertures in some cells but is not monotonic; aperture needs additional topologies and repeats. The preceding v1 diagnostic capture varied the number of density-eligible nodes with aperture and is not used for these independent-factor conclusions. Next add a second topology and another host, then replay task-generated receipts with the same stale-writer and tombstone gates. See [v1.1 results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_TARGETED_COMMIT_FACTORIAL_V1_1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [preregistration](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_TARGETED_COMMIT_FACTORIAL_V1_1_PREREG_20261001.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_targeted_commit_factorial_v1_1.py), and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_targeted_commit_factorial_v1_1.json).

### Receipt edge-order contract audit

Two task fixtures show per-event serialized edge-order divergence under receipt adoption (32/80 and 72/80 event states) while canonical facts, task outcomes, and branch-to-primary semantics pass. The source-locked mixed-act diagnostic localizes the first mismatch to event 1 and finds incident-edge sequence differences in 72/80 checkpoints, but no mismatch in 26,968 public typed-neighbor buckets. Its sole direct `incident_edges()` production caller compares keyed maps and is order-insensitive. The frozen full-seed census reports 224/8,340 named ownership groups under multiple distinct microtheories. Corpus-derived probes showed first-owner attribution can change under receipt adoption with canonical facts unchanged, and one of 14 selected shapes used an ambiguous source. The identity-based fix now carries the selected Concept/Rule node ID through owner lookup. Direct and receipt arms choose Concept 15504 / `computer_vision`; an actual `differentiate()` analysis accepts its shape only under the matching lineage. A three-worker held-out `sift` continuation then passes all eight gates through `synthesize_gaps()`: both branches derive the same `speaker normalization / formant ratio` gap through the scale-cancellation shape, while surface-only controls do not. The earlier v2 expectation of machine-learning transfer failed because it encoded the old false attribution, and remains disclosed. Next enable normal selector pruning and evaluate an outcome against a blinded held-out utility oracle; audit `source_node_id` and owner-candidate consumers and replay task receipt oracles. Separately settle the public graph ordering contract; the attribution fix does not resolve serialized edge-order differences. See the [edge-order diagnostic](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_RECEIPT_EDGE_ORDER_DIAGNOSTIC_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [ownership census](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_OWNERSHIP_ORDER_CENSUS_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [lineage v2 results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_HARVEST_SHAPE_RECEIPT_LINEAGE_V2_RESULTS_20261001.md), and [held-out postulate results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_HELDOUT_POSTULATE_RECEIPT_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md).

### Held-out selector outcome

The selector-on three-worker `sift` panel passes nine gates: derivation-only retains one scale-cancellation implication, normal `prune=True` synthesis returns zero gaps in both Direct and receipt arms, and surface-only controls remain empty. Direct/receipt outputs and canonical graph facts match. A full-boot selector-reason probe identifies `already in speech codebase` at `domains/sound_graph.py` as the rejection reason. Treat this as evidence that openness pruning closes an already implemented capability, not as a new learning or utility gain. Next choose an uncovered shape/postulate pair and preregister an independent held-out task utility oracle before proposing implementation changes. Keep derivability, openness, and utility gates distinct. See [selector results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_HELDOUT_POSTULATE_SELECTOR_V2_RESULTS_20261001.md).

### Candidate discovery and semantic novelty gate

An exploratory full-boot scan of the 33 computer-vision postulates uses the exact default 24-shape harvested library and normal selector. Three retain order-1 gaps: two generic compositional-generation derivations (`diffusion_model_vision`, `variational_autoencoder`) and reliability-weighted fusion for `vision_language_model`. Source inspection finds reliability-weighted fusion already represented in `domains/combinatorial_recognizer.py`; the VLM gap therefore exposes a selector false-open risk, while the visual front end remains a distinct acquisition need. The two generative postulates still lack a claim-specific task oracle. Do not select a gain target from retained gaps alone. Next measure false-open/false-covered rates on audited implemented and absent mechanisms and choose a task whose executable capability and independent utility oracle are both specified before transfer. The batch discovery runner computes the coverage index and default harvested shapes once for a fixed graph; ordinary `synthesize_gaps` calls retain the original recompute default. A three-worker parity panel confirms complete default/cached output equality and graph non-mutation; the observed 4–7% per-call speed difference is descriptive only. See [discovery results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_OPEN_GAP_DISCOVERY_CV_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [cache parity results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_COVERAGE_CACHE_PARITY_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [discovery protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_OPEN_GAP_DISCOVERY_CV_V1_20261001.md), and [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_open_gap_discovery_cv_v1_raw_20261001.json).

### Selector calibration: source-backed present/absent cases

A three-worker audit compares two implemented mechanisms against two absent ones. The selector correctly closes speaker scale normalization and leaves the absent diffusion-image and VAE mechanisms open, but it falsely leaves reliability-weighted cue fusion open. The source miss is diagnosed: `_live_speech_globs()` omits `domains/combinatorial_recognizer.py` because its filename does not match the speech-file markers; `_codebase_has()` consequently returns no match despite source implementations of the exact weighted-fusion scorer and predictor. This selected panel has 1/2 recall for known implemented cases and 2/2 open decisions for absent cases, not population estimates. Next broaden selector evidence in a domain-aware way, preserve these four cases as a regression panel, and remeasure both false-open and false-covered rates before using candidate gaps for utility studies. See [calibration results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_SELECTOR_CALIBRATION_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_SELECTOR_CALIBRATION_V1_PREREG_20261001.md), and [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_selector_calibration_v1_raw_20261001.json).

An all-domain measurement override scans 806 Python modules and closes both known implemented mechanisms while leaving both absent controls open in three fresh workers. It establishes a promising lookup scope for these four distinctive mechanism labels, not a production-default decision. The fusion hit establishes only that reliability-weighted channel fusion exists; the visual input path and complete VLM capability remain separate. Also, `is_gap` treats a match on one `name_key` as sufficient to close an implication, so compound/multi-key gaps need a partial-coverage policy. Next expand the audit set with partial implementations and other domains, then compare explicit domain-aware scope to the broad scan before adopting either. See [all-domain surface results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_SELECTOR_DOMAIN_SURFACE_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_SELECTOR_DOMAIN_SURFACE_V1_PREREG_20261001.md), and [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_selector_domain_surface_v1_raw_20261001.json).

The actual VLM synthesis path now confirms the mechanism-level interpretation: under all-domain lookup, derivation-only still yields one Kalman-to-cue-fusion implication, while normal pruning returns zero. The selector points to `domains/combinatorial_recognizer.py`, and source/graph identity gates pass in three workers. The earlier speech-scoped scan's retained VLM result is therefore a scope artifact for this fusion operator; it says nothing about the absent visual pathway. Do not report it as a novel VLM capability. Next decide and measure a domain-aware implementation index, then run partial-coverage and task-level utility gates separately. See [VLM transfer results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_VLM_DOMAIN_SELECTOR_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md) and [protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_VLM_DOMAIN_SELECTOR_TRANSFER_V1_PREREG_20261001.md).

### VLM facet inventory and task protocol

The source audit finds existing image ingestion/visual processing, standalone text processing, symbol-to-speech association, and reliability-weighted acoustic-channel fusion. It does not establish image-text alignment, joint image-language scoring, or zero-shot image classification. The held VLM Concept's definition is therefore stronger than the current source evidence. A source-linked facet inventory and proposed image-caption retrieval / zero-shot benchmark now separate these claims and define unimodal, shuffled-pair, and modality-corruption controls. No VLM benchmark has run because the required substrate-held image-text scorer is not identified. Next define a minimal scoring operator and benchmark custody, then preregister its held-out test before implementation or proposal evaluation. See [VLM facet audit and benchmark protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_VLM_FACET_AUDIT_AND_BENCHMARK_V1_20261001.md).

As a measured visual baseline, the source-locked Omniglot grapheme runner scores 77/80 (96.25%) in each of three fresh workers on one alphabet with held-out writers. A separate graph-native co-presentation task uses the repository-local 3,000-recording FSDD release and reaches 32/40 read-aloud (80%) and 28/40 dictation (70%) in every worker, binding 10/10 pairs. A paired cyclic-shift control preserves the recognizers and binding rule but rotates learned labels; the correct mapping beats this arm by 80 and 70 percentage points respectively across all three workers. This gives causal evidence for the narrow grapheme↔spoken-digit association on this task, not for VLM capability. The nominal `run_cross_modal` dispatch aliases grapheme-only recognition and is not the result source. Preserve the distinction from image-text alignment and keep the VLM benchmark gated on a scorer plus unimodal/shuffle controls. See [Omniglot results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_OMNIGLOT_GRAPH_RECOGNITION_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [binding results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_GRAPHEME_AUDIO_BINDING_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), and [permuted-binding results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_GRAPHEME_AUDIO_PERMUTED_BINDING_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md).

## Concurrent same-revision receipt adoption (2026-10-01)

Three fresh workers ran 30 barrier-synchronized races (90 submissions) in which three isolated branches each returned a nonempty receipt from one shared primary revision. Exactly one receipt committed and the other two were rejected as stale in every race; the complete graph always matched an independent oracle containing only the winner's write. This directly covers concurrent API submissions for the strict-revision contract. Calls go through Python/Rust and may be serialized by the Python GIL; this is not evidence of parallel native execution, disjoint-receipt merging, fairness, or throughput under service load. Median race time was 0.950 ms including thread scheduling. This supplements earlier competing-writer atomicity probes. Next replay a third task family through branch receipt adoption, audit real edge-order-sensitive consumers, and connect proposal selection to a blinded held-out task-utility oracle. ## Graph-authored correction rank and held-out continuation (2026-10-01)

A source-locked six-episode panel across three fresh workers now exercises the actual graph-authored self-correction composer, candidate rank Program, isolated rehearsal, adoption, and a third wave of new observation signatures. All 14 gates pass. The graph-cost rank arm chooses the zero-cost `signature->residual` edit, which fails the correction probe, then adopts the successful `dedup_identity_fix`; the default candidate order tries that repair first. Both arms pass an independent continuation oracle: no held-out observation remains pending, exactly one induced axis exists per new signature, and native closure is at a fixed point. Median attempts are 2 for graph cost ranking versus 1 for default order; median correction time is 1,154 ms versus 705 ms. The structural-cost prior adds search work on this family without changing utility. This is a single authored task and three workers, not a ranking-quality estimate. The evaluation also exposed that the graph-authored composer Rule had been loaded only as graph data; the adapter now activates the exact seed Rule and runs bounded native rule closure, allowing the graph composer to emit its gate and rank Program. The first harness invocation accidentally ran 18 rather than the preregistered six episodes and failed the count gate; it was superseded by the corrected six-episode capture without changing the protocol. Next make the graph rank policy consume persisted experiment outcomes and compare it with default, random, and frozen policies on genuinely fresh correction families. See [results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_GRAPH_AUTHORED_CORRECTION_RANK_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_GRAPH_AUTHORED_CORRECTION_RANK_V1_PREREG_20261001.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_graph_authored_correction_rank_v1.py), and [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_graph_authored_correction_rank_v1_raw_20261001.json).


## Correction outcome transfer v1 (2026-10-01)

Three fresh workers each ran a training correction, a cold rank episode, and an experience-informed episode on distinct substrate instances. All 8/8 gates pass. The training record set includes an actually rehearsed failed edit and the adopted repair; after explicit transport as typed `CorrectionOutcome` graph nodes, the graph-authored rank Program moves `dedup_identity_fix` ahead of the failed edit in all three workers. Candidate attempts fall from 2 to 1, while both arms adopt the repair and pass all three held-out continuation oracles. This is a useful first delegated-boundary result: the outside process supplies outcome records, the substrate's authored Program changes action ordering. It does not show autonomous persistence, acquisition, or broad learning: training and evaluation repeat one authored correction family, and evidence transport is explicit. Next test transfer across correction families with blinded utility labels, compare rank scoring against random/default/frozen controls, and measure whether outcome records are correctly attributed under repeated/noisy results. ## Cross-family idempotence outcome transfer v1 (2026-10-01)

The correction generator now emits a second task-shaped `dedup_identity_fix` for the recurrence-ledger offer rule, and both it and the shape-axis repair carry the authored `idempotent_mint_guard` outcome class. ## Cross-family idempotence transfer v2: discriminating utility panel (2026-10-01)

The v1 panel showed that outcome-class evidence crossed target rules but cold ranking already chose correctly. V2 adds a staged second recurrence candidate so two plausible fixes differ in task utility: the smaller episode-scoped guard suppresses a later valid offer, while the candidate-scoped guard preserves one offer per candidate. In three fresh workers, all 9/9 gates pass. Cold ranking selects the episode-scoped guard first; its independent oracle reads `[1, 0]` and fails, then the candidate-scoped repair passes on attempt two. Transferred evidence records one cross-target success, ranks the candidate-scoped repair first, and passes `[1, 1]` on attempt one. This is the first measured search-effort benefit from the explicit outcome-class pathway: 2 attempts cold versus 1 with history. The second candidate was staged after settling the first because the matcher evaluates same-pass bindings before effects; an initial simultaneous-candidate fixture did not distinguish the guards and is disclosed in the [amendment](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_CROSS_FAMILY_IDEMPOTENCE_TRANSFER_V2_AMENDMENT_20261001.md). Both task families, candidate classes, fixes, and utility labels are authored; evidence transport is host-managed. The result does not establish autonomous invention or natural-task generalization. See [results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_CROSS_FAMILY_IDEMPOTENCE_TRANSFER_V2_RESULTS_20261001.md), [protocol](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_CROSS_FAMILY_IDEMPOTENCE_TRANSFER_V2_PREREG_20261001.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_cross_family_idempotence_transfer_v2.py), and [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_cross_family_idempotence_transfer_v2_raw_20261001.json).

## Outcome contamination and adverse-transfer sensitivity v1 (2026-10-01)

Three fresh workers compare the automatically trained experience branch against the same branch plus one deliberately false positive for the smaller `episode_scoped_offer_guard`. All 9/9 gates pass. Clean history ranks `dedup_identity_fix` first and passes the staged `[1, 1]` oracle in one trial. The single contaminated record flips the graph-authored ranking: the episode-scoped guard runs first and yields `[1, 0]`; fallback then passes the oracle on trial two. This is direct evidence that current class-level utility aggregation can be dominated by one false attribution in this small candidate set. The injected corruption is an adversarial sensitivity probe, not an estimate of naturally occurring label noise. Next measure dose-response, false-negative and mixed-noise cases, repeated evidence aggregation, and an uncertainty-aware policy against the frozen ranker on independently authored tasks. See [results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_OUTCOME_CONTAMINATION_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [preregistration](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_OUTCOME_CONTAMINATION_V1_PREREG_20261001.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_outcome_contamination_v1.py), and [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_outcome_contamination_v1_raw_20261001.json).

## Outcome noise dose-response v1 (2026-10-01)

The five-arm, three-worker panel passes all 9 gates. With clean production evidence, the policy selects `dedup_identity_fix` and succeeds in one trial. One false positive for the episode guard changes the first choice and causes a two-trial recovery; a second such record increases that class's observed positive count from one to two but does not worsen task behavior. Changing the authentic positive repair outcome to a false negative also removes its ranking advantage and yields the same first-choice error. The mixed condition remains adverse. Thus, in this fixture, the current class-level score has a one-record decision threshold and saturates behaviorally after that threshold; the panel does not estimate field noise rates. This is the clearest measurement basis so far for evaluating a confidence-aware graph-authored rank Program against the current policy. Next preregister that policy comparison with the five noise conditions, more independent task families, and controls for ranking without outcome history. See [results](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_OUTCOME_NOISE_DOSE_RESPONSE_V1_RESULTS_20261001.md), [preregistration](THOUGHTEXPERIMENT_OUTCOME_NOISE_DOSE_RESPONSE_V1_PREREG_20261001.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/thoughtexperiment_outcome_noise_dose_response_v1.py), and [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/thoughtexperiment_outcome_noise_dose_response_v1_raw_20261001.json).

## TypedGraph CoW large-scale extension v1 (2026-10-01)

A pre-run source/binary lock covers 100k and 200k-node path, star, and grid graphs; six cells with five alternating-order repeats each pass exact query and sibling isolation checks. Shared-slab clone is faster than eager clone in all six cells (1.53–1.98×); clone plus one attribute write improves 1.26–1.80×, and clone plus spaced 1%-of-nodes writes improves 1.33–1.59×. ## GIL-release intervention: graph-then-struct cycle (2026-10-01)

Source inspection found that `tick_graph_then_struct` retained the GIL around a mutex-protected native cycle, unlike `run_rules`; the binding now releases the GIL around that same cycle. A locked 12-process v2 fanout-8 replay passes all seven task, parity, isolation, and provenance gates. This isolated change does not improve measured CPU overlap: aggregate worker CPU/wall remains 0.98–1.00×, and concurrent throughput does not improve relative to the v1 baseline. V2 still spends substantial per-branch wall time in snapshot/setup, candidate patch, and prediction; the targeted cycle boundary alone is insufficient. Timing changes are not interpreted as regressions with three repeats and host variability. System `perf` counters are unavailable under `perf_event_paranoid=4`. Next profile GIL-held Python work in-process or implement a native batch path across snapshot, patch, prediction, and readout with identical semantic gates. ## Code-write contract coverage v1 (2026-10-01)

An adversarial, source-locked four-worker panel probes whether contract validation establishes task correctness or only agreement on supplied points. The wrong `identity` function is taught as `square` using `0→0` and `1→1`; both workers accept and select it, but it gets 0/8 held-out square outputs right. Adding the distinguishing `2→4` case makes both workers refuse before a `taught_identity` construction appears. Thus contracts mitigate false acquisition only to the extent that observations distinguish competing programs. The engine currently does not select such inputs. The result motivates a measured active-probe gate: compare substrate-selected contrast/boundary probes, random probes, and caller-selected probes under an independent sealed labeler; score distinguishing power, query cost, and false admission across several operators. Aggregate shape-count deltas in this capture cannot be attributed because the runner lacks a post-read/pre-teach snapshot; the result limits claims to the specifically named construction. ## Contract query selection v1.1 (2026-10-01)

Added `domains.contract_query.select_discriminating_input`, which filters a finite supplied set of Terms against prior observations, evaluates survivors with the native Term runtime, and picks an unused input maximizing prediction-partition entropy. In eight fresh locked workers, the selector identified all six small-family targets in one query; seeded random did nearly as well there (mean 1.071). On an added sparse-information set of eight hypotheses, it selected `[-5,-4,-3]` and identified the target in three queries in both repetitions; 4,000 random sequences averaged 7.496 queries and none succeeded in one. Median measured selection-loop time was 168.6 microseconds. This is first evidence that substrate-side query choice can reduce label-query cost when informative inputs are sparse. Hypotheses and the input grid remain harness-authored, and an external oracle supplies every label. Next scale hypothesis count/expression depth and include misspecified hypothesis sets before integrating this into acquisition. The initial random-seed analyzer mismatch was corrected and disclosed in the amendment. ## Contract query scaling and misspecification v1 (2026-10-01)

A source-locked 10-worker panel scales binary-coded Term hypothesis sets from H=8 to 128 while expression depth grows K=3→7 and candidate grids grow 12→28. The selector identified each closed-set target using K queries; random median query counts were 10/18/26. Median native evaluation calls rose 226→1,638→9,434 and median loop time 2.16→22.85→178.59 ms. This is a measured work envelope for one nested synthetic family, not an asymptotic result. The selector therefore cannot certify model adequacy. Next scale candidate count and expression depth independently, vary input-grid size and partial domains, and add a residual/model-adequacy gate before treating a singleton as acquired knowledge. Fourteen source-locked workers vary candidate count, neutral Term depth, and input-grid size independently around H=32/D=0/N=20. ## Contract query memoization intervention (2026-10-02)

The 24-worker v1.2 source-locked comparison preserves identical query histories, predictions, labels, and final candidates across no-cache, JSON, fingerprint, and identity caches. Cache arms reduce native evaluator calls by 1.96–2.59× but increase median wall time: identity cache is 1.51–1.66× slower than no cache, fingerprint cache 1.54–1.72× slower, and JSON lookup 2.50–2.78× slower. The callback-backed graph-dependent `Holds` control bypasses all three caches. Keep these paths opt-in; this finite pure-Term benchmark does not rule out memoization where each native evaluation is more expensive. For this selector, the next performance intervention should change evaluation organization: precompute a prediction matrix and update candidate partitions incrementally, or add a native batch scorer. Compare against the uncached baseline with the same exact-history and open-world false-singleton checks. Do not treat lower evaluator-call counts as a speedup. See [results](SUBSTRATE_CONTRACT_QUERY_MEMOIZATION_V1_2_RESULTS_20261002.md), [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_CONTRACT_QUERY_MEMOIZATION_V1_2_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_contract_query_memoization_v1_2.py), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_substrate_contract_query_memoization_v1_2.py), and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_contract_query_memoization_v1_2_raw_20261002.json).

## Contract query batched prediction matrix (2026-10-02)

After memoization reduced native calls but increased elapsed time, the selector gained an opt-in sequence-local `TermPredictionMatrix`. The eager v1.1, 18-worker source/native-locked panel passes exact query-history, entropy, prediction, oracle, terminal, source-lock, and independent-oracle gates. Median end-to-end speedups over the uncached selector are 1.87× at H=32/N=500, 1.78× at H=128/N=28, and 1.87× at H=512/N=36, with peak RSS ratios 0.99–1.02×. That eager revision computes H×(N+1) predictions once per sequence, including the initial observation, and reuses them as evidence arrives. Both arms still return the same false singleton when the target differs from a supplied hypothesis only at an unqueried off-grid point; no model-adequacy claim follows. A later partial-domain/operator panel replaced eager population with lazy survivor-first evaluation; it preserves exact behavior, but its one-query H=8 cases are slower than uncached. The earlier large-workload speedup is not evidence for the current lazy revision, whose large-scale crossover remains to be measured. Keep matrix selection opt-in. V1's first capture is diagnostic due to a wrong analyzer matrix-cell count; v1.1 amended the protocol accounting and captured a fresh lock. ## Lazy prediction matrix crossover (2026-10-02)

The 36-worker H=128/512 × initial survivor fraction × uncached/lazy-matrix panel passes exact semantic, accounting, source-lock, and misspecification gates. At H=128, the lazy route is 1.79× faster with 7 follow-up queries and 1.51× with 3; at H=512 it is 1.98× faster with 9 queries and 1.99× with 5. Native evaluation calls fall 2.5–4.4×. If initial observations already identify the target, no candidate matrix is evaluated, but cache-mediated filtering is still slower: 0.63×/0.75× speed ratios at H=128/512. Peak RSS is indistinguishable (1.00×) at this host's process sampling resolution. Thus reuse pays when several selection rounds remain; keep it opt-in for multi-query pure-Term sequences and use uncached selection for already-resolved/zero-query cases. The target is in a finite binary-coded family; the same false singleton at off-grid x=999 remains. Next repeat over task-generated hypothesis pools and more Term depths/operators. See [results](SUBSTRATE_CONTRACT_QUERY_LAZY_MATRIX_CROSSOVER_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_CONTRACT_QUERY_LAZY_MATRIX_CROSSOVER_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_contract_query_lazy_matrix_crossover_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_contract_query_lazy_matrix_crossover_v1_lock_20261002.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_contract_query_lazy_matrix_crossover_v1_analysis_20261002.json).


## Generated-pool query transfer v1 completed (2026-10-02)

The lazy sequence-local Term prediction matrix was compared with uncached selection on pools generated by the substrate's bounded synthesizer for triangular numbers, scalar squares, and Euler characteristic (three fresh workers each). The pools were complete at H=9/1/34. An independent analyzer reproduced every selector decision and oracle label; both arms had exact semantic parity and all final survivors were correct on the locked held-outs. Native selector calls fell 18.8% on the one-query triangular task and 39.4% on the two-query Euler task. Wall time tied on triangular and improved 1.30× on Euler. Pool generation took 46–683 ms while query selection took 0.9–3.6 ms, so the result transfers a selector work reduction to generated Terms but does not improve end-to-end acquisition cost measurably. Square is only a zero-query singleton control. These are three previously authored finite tasks, not fresh-domain generalization. Next hold the task families out from protocol construction, expand generated pool size and query depth, include a target outside the grammar, and measure total synthesis-plus-selection cost under equal work and time budgets. See [results](SUBSTRATE_CONTRACT_QUERY_GENERATED_POOL_TRANSFER_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_CONTRACT_QUERY_GENERATED_POOL_TRANSFER_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_contract_query_generated_pool_transfer_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_substrate_query_generated_pool_transfer_v1.py), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_contract_query_generated_pool_transfer_v1_analysis_20261002.json).

## Generated-pool grid and misspecification stress v1 completed (2026-10-02)

A preregistered nine-worker panel crosses two cubic probe grids at Term size 7 with an absolute-value target outside the arithmetic hypothesis vocabulary. Broad-grid cubic produces H=66, takes 670 ms to synthesize, and resolves in one query with exact held-outs; a one-point grid produces H=27, takes 141 ms, and also resolves in one query on this deliberately informative point. For `|x|`, the H=9 arithmetic pool has no held-out-exact model; the selected negative probe eliminates all candidates in all three workers, yielding explicit empty-version-space refusal. Lazy evaluation reduces native calls 16.7%, 50%, and 30.8% respectively, but wall time is flat or slightly worse except the sparse cubic case (0.832→0.691 ms); full synthesis dominates. This is one successful misspecification-control case, not a calibrated adequacy detector, and sparse-grid success does not address false singletons when wrong models agree on every offered point. Next vary grid points adversarially to create aliasing, expand grammars/pools and task families, and measure refusal/miss rates with sealed held-out labels under total acquisition budgets. ## Generated cubic finite-grid alias counterexample v1 completed (2026-10-02)

A preregistered three-worker counterexample fixes cubic target `x³`, knowns at 0 and 1, and a one-point candidate grid at −1. Every generated complete pool has 12 terms but omits the cubic representative because `x` and `x³` agree on the finite training/probe inputs. Both selector arms ask `x=−1`, return the same singleton linear `x`, and then score 0/4 on sealed held-outs in all three workers. Independent replay passes; median pool generation is 99.20 ms, and the lazy matrix halves query evaluator calls (72→36) without changing this failure. This is direct evidence that entropy selection cannot repair target loss during finite-grid pool deduplication. Held-out validation catches it only after the false acquisition; the selector has no adequacy signal. Before singleton adoption, the learner needs a substrate-side residual or independently selected adequacy probes. Next measure such a gate against true singleton, contradictory-pool, and finite-alias controls, including its false refusal and false acceptance rates across multiple generated task families. ## Independent post-selection adequacy gate v1 completed (2026-10-02)

A source/input-locked audit replay covers 24 captured outcomes: three repeats each for six represented task configurations, the generated cubic false-singleton case, and an empty out-of-grammar absolute-value version space. Fresh descriptors are mechanically checked to be absent from each task's known, candidate, query, and held-out rows; the corrected Euler probes use distinct scalar descriptors. The simple accept-only-if-all-fresh-labels-match gate rejects all three alias singletons after one new label, while all 18 positive controls pass and all three empty pools remain refused. With no audit labels, the 3/3 alias singletons are accepted vacuously. The measured native evaluation cost is 21 calls / 0.20 ms total at k=1 and 84 calls / 0.29 ms at k=4. This makes one counterexample detectable cheaply but does not establish rates or general correctness; labels remain external and the gate is not integrated into production acquisition/adoption. Next build a substrate-owned, provenance-bound residual path that obtains or requests audit evidence, then test it on independently authored tasks with noisy/ambiguous evidence, false-refusal controls, and a predeclared deployment decision rule. ## Selected-probe adoption transfer across task families (2026-10-02)

The strict live adoption route requires an authenticated evidence receipt plus a recomputable nonzero-entropy probe selected over a supplied challenger and admissible domain. ## Independent threshold family: shifted inputs and signed-label noise (2026-10-02)

A new source-locked live-route panel uses `left + right > limit`, with probe inputs in a small integer range and 100 held-out triples including out-of-range values. The v1.2 replay passes 14/14 independent checks across 15 fresh workers. The authored task, provider keys, domain, and oracle are harness supplied; the noisy-label case does not estimate prevalence. ## Stochastic signed-label noise dose response (2026-10-02)

A source-locked mechanism panel tested correct and constant-false candidates on parity and threshold, with independent Bernoulli flip rates 0/0.1/0.5 and 1/3/5 simulated providers: 2,160 trials across three fresh processes, with all 48 independent gates passing. Receipts follow an exact fail-closed policy: disagreements are ambiguous; unanimous labels matching the candidate can pass if the selected probe is discriminating. For a correct candidate, eligibility follows `(1-p)^m`; for a wrong candidate, false eligibility follows `p^m`. At p=0.1 and five sources this lowers theoretical false eligibility to 0.00001 but also lowers correct eligibility to 0.590; at p=0.5 both become 0.03125. This is a quantified false-adoption/refusal tradeoff under stipulated independent noise, not a real-provider noise estimate or evidence that quorum establishes truth. The measurement uses receipt/eligibility outcomes rather than repeated graph writes. Next test correlated/burst errors and domain shift across more independently authored task families with label and compute costs. See [results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_STOCHASTIC_NOISE_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_STOCHASTIC_NOISE_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_STOCHASTIC_NOISE_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_stochastic_noise_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_substrate_adequacy_stochastic_noise_v1.py), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_stochastic_noise_v1_analysis_20261002.json).

## Common-mode provider-noise dose response (2026-10-02)

A follow-up adds a mixture correlation parameter ρ=0/0.5/1 while holding task, candidate quality, marginal error probability, and provider count fixed. Across parity and threshold, p=0.1/0.5, m=1/3/5, and 4,320 trials in three fresh workers, all 84 replay and cell-consistency gates pass. With five providers and p=0.5, empirical false eligibility rises 4/120→31/120→55/120 from ρ=0→0.5→1; correct adoption rises 2/120→32/120→57/120. The model predicts the correlation floor `ρp + (1−ρ)p^m`; at full common mode extra provider IDs give no protection. At p=0.1 counts are sparse and remain descriptive. This is a simulated mixture, not a natural correlation estimate, and it measures receipt eligibility rather than live graph writes. Next measure burst/clustered error and quality strata across additional domains, charging equal label and compute budgets. See [results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_CORRELATED_NOISE_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_CORRELATED_NOISE_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_correlated_noise_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_substrate_adequacy_correlated_noise_v1.py), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_correlated_noise_v1_analysis_20261002.json).

## Offline evidence-policy tradeoff sensitivity (2026-10-02)

A preregistered deterministic replay evaluates unanimity, majority, and 80% agreement on the same 6,480 signed trials from the independent- and common-mode panels (19,440 decisions, 327/327 checks). At five independent providers and p=0.1, correct eligibility was 72/120, 113/120, and 119/120; wrong-candidate false eligibility was 0/120, 2/120, and 6/120. At p=0.5, majority accepts correct and wrong candidates at approximately equal rates. Under fully common-mode error, additional provider IDs add no information for any threshold. This describes an evidence/coverage frontier under synthetic assumptions; the policies are not implemented and CPU cost/live graph adoption was not measured. Do not change the production unanimity rule from this replay. Next acquire additional task/provider-quality strata and benchmark actual decision CPU and live write/refusal effects under matched label budgets. Median adoption-boundary times are 0.483–0.526 ms across the three tasks. This replicates the transaction invariant beyond square, but remains a one-host, three-family mechanism result. ## Cold initialization versus warmed full conversation (2026-10-02)

A matched 18-worker panel crosses parity, clamp, and square with truthful adoption versus missing-evidence refusal. The first `converse("hello")` call takes 94.6–100.3 ms median wall time per cell; the subsequent target conversation takes 111.2–116.0 ms. The 8/8 semantic checks pass: accepted evidence adopts one shape, missing evidence produces no codebook growth, and accepted native predictions match the independent oracle. However, aggregate process CPU medians for the target turn are 1.65–1.70 seconds, far above wall time. This process-time measure includes CPU across worker threads; the Rust matcher has a Rayon path, but per-rule/worker attribution was not captured. Full target graph changes include ordinary conversation state and continue after the initial warm-up, so they remain descriptive. The post-capture amendment discloses that receipt construction occurred after the cold warm-up timer and before the target timer, contrary to the preregistered construction order; neither timed interval contains receipt construction. Next trace per-rule/worker CPU and work counts, repeat under constrained thread counts, and separate aggregate CPU from wall latency and core budget. This is one host and three authored tasks, not a general live-request cost estimate. See [results](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_WARM_CONVERSE_COST_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_WARM_CONVERSE_COST_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_ADEQUACY_WARM_CONVERSE_COST_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_adequacy_warm_converse_cost_v1.py), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_adequacy_warm_converse_cost_v1_analysis_20261002.json).

This small diagnostic finds no process-level latency or thread-count reduction and leaves aggregate CPU attribution unresolved; it does not show that Rayon ignored the setting, because the process includes other pools. The raw sample contains 26 thread instances in the capped-Rayon arm and 49 in the default arm, with 0.69–1.13 s sampled thread runtime against 1.07–1.28 s aggregate process CPU, but these figures are not an accepted attribution result: in-process sampler starvation and coarse interval boundaries leave unknown CPU. **Thread-origin and OpenBLAS intervention (2026-10-02):** symbolized `pthread_create` stacks on 12 fresh workers pass all 12 corrected review gates. The target calls create 23 threads from NumPy's bundled OpenBLAS initialization when its thread cap is unset, and zero under `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1`. Under interposition, process CPU medians fall from 1.24/1.33 s to 0.125/0.110 s when OpenBLAS is capped at one; instrumentation affects timing, so this is causal diagnostic evidence, not a production speedup claim. The follow-up uninstrumented six-process panel passes 9/9 gates and confirms a route-specific 13.35× process CPU reduction (1,359.5 ms to 101.8 ms), while median wall falls from 129.9 ms to 103.8 ms. This identifies OpenBLAS parallel work as the main source of the earlier CPU/wall discrepancy for this one host and route, not as a general speedup claim. The parser-thread churn remains a distinct cost target. Next benchmark a reusable stack-safe JSON parse worker against per-call threads with exact semantic parity, then repeat the BLAS comparison on another task family or host. **Raw residual-to-composer grounding boundary v1 (2026-10-02):** four paired navigation workers execute a faulted rule and pass the resulting actual/expected action fields to `induce_concern`, without a caller-supplied name hint or edit cue. All four mint the generic `induced_actual_expected` axis; all four then stop at `ground_concern`'s held-relation wall and emit no proposal. A fresh matched context with the authored A8 cue builds the expected `flip_comparison` proposal for `hop_descend_gradient` in all four workers. Primary rules stay unchanged in both branches. This pins down the current transition gap: learning can record a novel observation, while translating raw outcome semantics to a useful structural vocabulary still requires interpretation/cue engineering. The positive cue's task utility was measured independently in A8 v1.4; this boundary experiment adds no new utility claim. Next candidate improvement is a gated residual-grounding layer that derives task-relevant predicates from the discrepancy and retains abstention on ambiguous mappings ([protocol](RESIDUAL_TO_COMPOSER_GROUNDING_BOUNDARY_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/measure_residual_to_composer_grounding_boundary_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_residual_to_composer_grounding_boundary_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/residual_to_composer_grounding_boundary_v1_lock_20261002.json), and [results](../../../evaluation/reports/residual_to_composer_grounding_boundary_v1_20261002.json)).

**Residual-to-composer cue derivation v1 preregistered (2026-10-02):** the next learning gate specifies an explicit state/action-geometry bridge from error residuals to an operator-level cue. It includes inverted-action positives, ordinary/ambiguous residual abstention controls, unrelated-target grounding, and primary-rule isolation. This is a proposed mechanism, not yet implementation or evidence of self-improvement; build the source-locked runner and independent analyzer before making a capability claim ([protocol](RESIDUAL_TO_COMPOSER_CUE_DERIVATION_V1_PREREG_20261002.md)).

**Residual-to-composer cue derivation v1 (2026-10-02):** 13 fresh source-locked workers pass all gates: four cardinal inversion cases derive the known cue, produce the expected `flip_comparison` proposal, and pass held-out navigation; four valid non-inversions and four malformed/underdetermined residuals abstain; and the absent-target control yields no candidate. Median induction/grounding times are 5.86/0.285 ms. This demonstrates a hand-coded action-geometry bridge to an existing operator class, not substrate induction of the cue or general self-improvement. Full rule-store capture also finds 24 lazy reflective/shape-decode rules added on every worker and five additional rules in cue-positive contexts (two keyed to the residual). Target-rule preservation therefore does not imply a mutation-free experiment; next run this path in the copy-on-write Thoughtexperiment branch and measure full graph deltas/adoption ([results](RESIDUAL_TO_COMPOSER_CUE_DERIVATION_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](RESIDUAL_TO_COMPOSER_CUE_DERIVATION_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/measure_residual_to_composer_cue_derivation_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_residual_to_composer_cue_derivation_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/residual_to_composer_cue_derivation_v1_lock_20261002.json), and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/residual_to_composer_cue_derivation_v1_20261002.json)).

**Residual-to-composer CoW branch isolation v1 (2026-10-02):** the follow-up preserves the same 13-case panel, but runs induction and grounding inside a `snapshot().fork()` branch after the task outcome has been observed. All 13 primary graph/rule/revision states are unchanged during exploration; each returns exactly one residual node while every prior primary node, edge, and rule remains intact. Four opposite-action branches produce the same held `flip_comparison` repair and pass held-out checks; all nine non-inversion/ambiguous controls abstain, including the absent-target case. Branch-local initialization adds 24 rules in abstention paths and 29 in cue-positive paths. This verifies containment and a useful return payload for an authored decoder, not target-blind diagnosis: the action-vector-to-cue mapping is still in the harness. Median snapshot-fork time is 0.263 ms on this fixture and is descriptive only. Next remove the host-authored cue mapping and test competing/misleading write causes with independent primary/branch oracles ([results](RESIDUAL_TO_COMPOSER_BRANCH_ISOLATION_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](RESIDUAL_TO_COMPOSER_BRANCH_ISOLATION_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/measure_residual_to_composer_branch_isolation_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_residual_to_composer_branch_isolation_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/residual_to_composer_branch_isolation_v1_lock_20261002.json), and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/residual_to_composer_branch_isolation_v1_20261002.json)).

**Residual CoW return v1 (2026-10-02):** 26 paired rows compare deep-copy branches with the existing shared-graph-pages branch. Both reproduce all four held-out-positive proposals, abstain on nine controls, and leave the host graph/rule store unchanged until residual return. After positive candidate scoring, the journal returns a median 40-node/2-edge post-induction graph delta; exact revision-checked application reproduces the branch facts and does not merge native rule-vector additions. Shared-page fork median is 0.246 ms versus 0.515 ms for deep copy on this small one-host fixture; other operation costs are similar, so no general speedup is inferred. The returned graph delta has not yet been shown independently executable. Next test post-return residual usability, cleanup/reclamation, and larger graph sizes with the copy arm retained ([results](RESIDUAL_COW_RETURN_V1_RESULTS_20261002.md), [protocol](RESIDUAL_COW_RETURN_V1_PREREG_20261002.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/measure_residual_cow_return_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_residual_cow_return_v1.py), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/residual_cow_return_v1_lock_20261002.json), and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/residual_cow_return_v1_20261002.json)).

**Residual CoW candidate rehydration v1 (2026-10-02):** four source-locked positive workers serialize the held-out-passing candidate into a graph residual, return it through the shared-page branch, deserialize it on the host, and reproduce exact candidate digests and held-out outcomes (4/4). A deliberately stale host revision is rejected without a partial graph write; retrying with the current revision succeeds. **LLM transport treewidth scaling v1 (2026-10-02):** a three-worker k={1,2,4,6,8,10} sweep covers all ten L12→L13 held-out transitions. **Qwen3 cross-model transport v1 (2026-10-02):** the new hashed 70-text fixture was encoded with both local tokenizers; each model's 60/10 split was fit independently. Three workers per model passed 480 exact-inference cells each, including oracle/rescore, certified-width, source-stability, topology-repeatability, and graph-isolation gates. Widths at fan-in 1/2/4/8 are 1/2/4–6/8 in both models. The median of hop-level JT medians is 0.153/0.367/9.16/539.1 ms for 0.6B and 0.153/0.378/8.88/537.0 ms for 1.7B; top-2 reduces this graph-solving time about 1,412×/1,405× relative to top-8. This supports cross-scale repeatability of the explicit fan-in cost effect, not natural frame discovery or language utility. ### Edge/access audit follow-up (2026-10-03)


### Connected-conversation runtime access panel v1.3 (2026-10-03)

Three fresh workers replayed four conversation cases with concrete runtime tracing off/on from fresh worlds. Across 12 paired worker/cases and 198 closure checkpoints per arm, all checkpoint and final graph digests match; all goals resolve and closures reach fixed points. The trace-on arm records 6,240 event occurrences, all attributed to four bounded discourse-rule signatures, with no dropped rows. Of these, 5,520 accesses connect one task-owned endpoint to shared/unowned state and 720 remain within one frame; none directly join differently owned task nodes. This validates trace-on/off state parity for this workload and build. The trace implementation remains partial, and rule traces do not account for all host/native work. Shared state makes the selected frame interaction graph complete, so this does not establish safe factorization, semantic parity of partitioned closure, speedup, or natural-task prevalence. The API-fit audit confirms current Microtheory scoping does not represent task-frame ownership by default and that the delta report cannot certify complete notifications or queue settlement by itself. A first pilot now adds explicit ownership edges symmetrically and globally resweeps two Microtheory roots. It passes exact closure parity on one two-goal workload in 3/3 workers and all 24 checkpoints, but requires 132 scoped calls and is slower on this tiny case. This is a parity positive control only; the matcher still sees the full graph. Next gate: broaden exact parity to common-ground stress and 4/8-goal cases, dynamic ownership/deletion/reuse, and adversarial cross-frame dependencies; account for matcher/read work, interface cost, and scheduling overhead before proposing factorized execution. V1.1 independently verifies all 48 per-scope quiescence records show zero progress and no pending deferred work, while the engine still reports notification completeness as false. See [pilot results](SUBSTRATE_CONVERSATION_TASK_SCOPE_PARITY_PILOT_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md), [v1.1 amendment](SUBSTRATE_CONVERSATION_TASK_SCOPE_PARITY_PILOT_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20261003.md), [pilot method](SUBSTRATE_CONVERSATION_TASK_SCOPE_PARITY_PILOT_V1_METHOD_20261003.md), [API-fit audit](SUBSTRATE_CONVERSATION_PARTITION_API_FIT_AUDIT_20261003.md), [trace results](SUBSTRATE_CONNECTED_CONVERSATION_ACCESS_TRACE_PANEL_V1_3_RESULTS_20261003.md), [trace method](SUBSTRATE_CONNECTED_CONVERSATION_ACCESS_TRACE_PANEL_V1_METHOD_20261003.md), [pilot capture](../../../evaluation/reports/conversation_task_scope_parity_pilot_v1_20261003.json), and [pilot analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/conversation_task_scope_parity_pilot_v1_analysis_20261003.json).

The source-locked 45-worker sweep covers 0, 256, 1,024, 4,096, and 16,384 shared-event decoys across three orderings and three replicates. Exact state/lifecycle and trace parity pass; fallback isolation and anchor path coverage pass. At 16,384 decoys anchor reduces work by one-third against fallback but still costs 2.73× monolithic work. Aggregate anchor wall time is 15% below fallback and 7.25× monolithic. A post-capture v1.1 analyzer fixes a replicate-label validation error in the first analyzer; the original capture/lock and analyzer remain preserved. `ru_maxrss` is contaminated by trace data and retained output snapshots (2.5 GB raw capture), so substrate memory scaling is not established. Next isolate each arm in a fresh process, disable traces, stream lightweight summaries, and measure peak RSS; afterward transfer the size study to natural task graphs with independently labeled ownership. See [protocol](SUBSTRATE_CONVERSATION_TASK_SCOPE_SIZE_MEMORY_V1_PREREG_20261003.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_CONVERSATION_TASK_SCOPE_SIZE_MEMORY_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/conversation_task_scope_size_memory_v1.py), [source lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/conversation_task_scope_size_memory_v1_lock_20261003.json), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/conversation_task_scope_size_memory_v1_20261003.json.gz), and [amended analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/conversation_task_scope_size_memory_v1_amended_analysis_20261003.json).

### Memory-isolated matcher scaling v1.1 (2026-10-03)

The v1 rerun corrects the v1 RSS contamination: one isolated worker per size/order/replicate, traces disabled, each arm's full output discarded after compacting checkpoint digests/counters, and only small worker summaries retained. All 45 exact-state and source-lock gates pass. Median whole-worker peak RSS rises 32.6→222.1 MiB over 0→16,384 shared-event decoys, approximately 11.8 KiB per decoy for this complete Python/native workload. This is an end-to-end maximum across three arms, not a per-arm or native allocation measure. At maximum size anchor is 2.73× monolithic work and 6.61× its wall time, despite 19% lower time than fallback. The v1 contaminated RSS is withdrawn; its compressed raw capture is retained and verified. Next isolate each arm in its own process, then test natural task graphs with independently labeled ownership. ### Per-arm process memory v1.2 (2026-10-03)

The amended run uses 135 fresh processes, one per size/order/replicate/arm, and independently confirms exact matched state/lifecycle parity plus scope-path isolation. Across all five graph sizes, per-arm median RSS differs by at most 0.62 MiB. At 16,384 decoys, medians are 201.6 MiB monolithic, 202.0 MiB fallback, 201.9 MiB anchor. The process footprint therefore appears dominated by graph materialization/runtime for this authored family; native-only and per-structure allocation remain unmeasured. Anchor is 17% faster than fallback at the largest size, while still 7.11× monolithic wall time. This supersedes combined-arm memory estimates in v1.1 and the contaminated v1 series. Next apply the isolation and semantic gates to naturally harvested graphs with independently reviewed ownership labels. ### Live task-graph ownership census v1 (2026-10-03)

Ten fresh full-seed replays capture five live request routes and pass source stability, graph completeness, unique PID, and exact same-prompt replicate digest gates. The independently derived frame uses only Message/Goal/Event identity relations. Only two of five conditions expose any Goal-to-prompt ownership; one is the wrong Goal kind, and three have zero assignable Goals despite a prompt Message. The single-request design necessarily yields one frame, so its zero interframe edges/treewidth zero do not establish locality. Each task frame contains one or five nodes in a ~25k-node graph and touches 16–30 unique unowned neighbors. Current task outcomes are 6/10; the scene route now fails by selecting self-report. The original analyzer omitted an import; the separately hashed v1.1 analysis passes, with the original lock and capture preserved. Next audit explicit identity links and then capture multi-turn sequences where multiple frames coexist. ### Live multi-turn frame scale v1 (2026-10-03)

Twelve fresh workers replayed N=1/2/4/8 identical self-report turns, three per size. All source-lock, distinct-PID, per-turn ownership/route, and v1.1 semantic replicate gates pass. Raw digests differ at N≥2 only because generated `SystemModel` timing fields vary; the original v1 raw-digest failure remains recorded. With identity-based ownership, each frame has six owned nodes. Boundary coupling grows to a complete eight-frame interaction graph (28 pairwise edges, exact treewidth 7) at N=8, despite only seven directly cross-owned edges. This is a concrete counterexample to assuming low-width frame interaction for persistent repeated discourse state; it is one repetitive authored route, not a general workload conclusion. Peak RSS is ~1.72 GiB and dominated by full-seed startup/base state; later turn wall time is generally 130–160 ms. Next use semantically distinct independent and dependent task sequences with explicit oracles and compare boundary-induced versus direct interaction. A reproducible read-only audit validates both source-locked captures and confirms the boundary: nine live workers have zero `EpisodicEvent`, `MemoryContext`, `MemorySchema`, `MemoryRetrievalRequest`, `RecallCandidate`, or `RecallOutcome` nodes; the nine structured workers explicitly instantiate and use them. ### Semantic ingress source contract (2026-10-03)

Source inspection confirms `WorldAdapter.ingest_semantic_event()` is an explicit adapter API, not the raw-text bridge: it consumes a pre-adapted mapping, rejects strings, does not create a turn or reply, and has no production caller elsewhere under `substrate/`. An optional neutral proposition payload can be materialized with provenance, but the caller supplies its predicate and role arguments; truth uptake remains separate. Therefore the interface offers a viable seam for gradual transfer of execution and evidence handling to the substrate, while extraction and provider trust remain upstream responsibilities. The next evaluation should score raw-text extraction, explicit neutral ingress, and integrated memory/query behavior as separate stages. See the [source audit](SUBSTRATE_SEMANTIC_INGRESS_SOURCE_AUDIT_20261003.md) and its [API test](../../../tests/test_semantic_event_ingress.py).

The corrected full production-loop comparison passes all 69 cases: 279/279

### GenInfer scope provenance enforcement probe (2026-10-03)

The source-locked 36-worker panel confirms that native GenInfer does not
validate `FrameScope` provenance records. Matching `scope_id` attributes cause
12/12 exact acquisitions in each of the valid, absent, and contradictory
record conditions. Thus the existing required-scope behavior means “a token
must be present and match eligible parts”; provenance integrity and boundary
assignment are not enforced by the Term. This qualifies v1.3's synthetic
scope-locality result. Next decide and specify the authority model for scope
assignment, then evaluate the mechanism that enforces it, including stale,
missing, conflicting, and cross-frame assignments. See [results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_SCOPE_PROVENANCE_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md), [amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_EXPLICIT_SCOPE_V1_3_1_AMENDMENT_20261003.md), and [preregistration](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_SCOPE_PROVENANCE_V1_PREREG_20261003.md).

### GenInfer cross-frame dependency boundary v1 (2026-10-03)

The 36-case paired production-path panel separates local basis, explicitly
included cross-frame basis, and a valid basis excluded by scope. Global exact
acquisition is 36/36; scoped exact acquisition is 24/24 when dependency
coverage is explicit and 0/12 when the required basis is excluded. At K=16,
local and included-dependency closure are about 4.5× faster, while excluded
scope is 13.3× faster only because it returns without the valid explanation.
This qualifies frame-scope speedups: preserving capability requires boundary
coverage, and the engine currently receives caller-assigned tokens. Next
measure boundary/dependency discovery and assignment errors against a
counterbalanced oracle, include ambiguous and shared interfaces, then scale to
independently authored tasks and larger graphs. See [results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_CROSS_FRAME_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md), [protocol](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_CROSS_FRAME_V1_PREREG_20261003.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/substrate_geninfer_cross_frame_v1.py), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_geninfer_cross_frame_v1_analysis_20261003.json).

### GenInfer frame-selection implementation boundary (2026-10-03)

Source-linked review confirms that the substrate consumes caller-supplied
`scope_id` attributes but has no producer that derives scopes from graph
structure or checks `FrameScope` provenance. Recent exactness/speed results
measure scoped execution with evaluator-authored partitions. The missing
capability is safe partition discovery with dependency coverage. Gate any
implementation on held-out graph families with oracle boundaries and
cross-frame dependencies; report partition precision/recall, dependency
coverage, false-split/missed-explanation rates, discovery cost, and scoped-first
global-retry cost. Require semantic parity on connected and high-coupling
controls before native scaling claims. See [source audit](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_FRAME_SELECTION_SOURCE_AUDIT_20261003.md), [structural census](SUBSTRATE_TASK_GRAPH_STRUCTURAL_CENSUS_V1_3_RESULTS_20261003.md), and [cross-frame evaluation](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_CROSS_FRAME_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md).
