# Current gate update — predecessor interfaces and thought experiments

The 2026-10-03 predecessor-interface captures supply rule-level and scoped
closure evidence. The standard communication seed path has been restored by
registering manifest version 1.4.17. Scoped closure matches monolithic carry
in 10/10 paired cases when the predecessor is outside ownership but remains
visible in the shared graph. It rejects wrong-speaker, topic-interruption, and
omitted-interface controls. The first capture supplies rule-level
positive/control evidence: the rule carried the target in 10/10 retained
cases, rejected four continuity/interface controls in 10/10 each, and
propagated across an eligible topicless chain in 10/10. Existing
thoughtexperiment studies already exercise shared-page CoW branches, residual
extraction/return, primary isolation, and million-node hosts in bounded
candidate-evaluation workloads; those are measured capabilities, not pending
implementation. The remaining integration gate is to combine those branch
semantics with predecessor-dependent frame execution and measure branch
allocation, closure work, residual contents, and merge-back parity together.
For the partition gate, require canonical full-graph parity whenever semantic
dependencies are retained, explicit expected residuals when an interface is
withheld, and no unintended cross-frame effects.

Follow-on result: a 70-case source-locked closure panel now covers the second
multi-edge rule, correction grounding. Monolithic and scoped results agree on
all positive/negative outcomes; the current event and effect target are owned
by the frame, while the predecessor is outside ownership and visible in the
shared graph. A subsequent production-materialized trace replays 1/2/4/8
instruction/correction pairs across 2/4/8/16 frames, three sweep orders, and
nine fresh processes (36 paired closures). Canonical full graph parity and
exact correction evidence hold in every cell. V1.0's N=8 scoped timing was
16.6× monolithic; corrected v1.1 measures 25.3 ms scoped versus 2.48 ms
monolithic (10.2×). Candidate enumeration (14.5×) and Term evaluation
(13.4×) ratios reproduce across captures; serialization order diverges in
some sweep orders despite equal canonical graph facts. This demonstrates
selected trace parity, while showing
the current repeated full-graph scoped matcher is not an efficient partition
algorithm. An opt-in declared anchor was then tested against the same-source
fallback on this 36-cell trace. It preserves canonical graph state in all
arms, but the proof guard falls back for most scope/rule evaluations because
each event can participate as the next event's predecessor. At eight pairs the
anchor reduces Candidate and Term work by only 0.5% and 0.7%, respectively;
both remain about 14× the monolithic counts. Do not treat this as a useful
optimization on a chained transcript. Next investigate a sound multi-role
ownership index or independent discourse frames, then repeat against the
lifecycle panel; keep CoW residual integration separate.

Audit amendment: v1.0 mislabeled the ownership count and its analyzer check was
invalid. V1.1 supersedes that metadata and timing capture. It records actual
members returned by native `neighbours(root, "has_concept")` queries, with two
semantic nodes plus the scope root in each frame, then independently checks
frame count, unique IDs, types, and counts. The original v1.0 artifact is
retained only as a diagnostic. V1.1 preserves all graph/semantic outcomes and
work counts; its corrected median N=8 timing is 25.3 ms scoped versus 2.48 ms
monolithic (10.2×). The declared-anchor capture remains separately locked to
the unchanged v1.0 runner and is unaffected by this amendment.

### Declared-anchor topology comparison on correction traces (2026-10-03)

An exploratory 72-cell comparison replays the same correction pairs in one
chained `DiscourseState` or in independent states, with monolithic, generic
scoped, and declared-anchor scoped closure. All cells preserve exact evidence
and canonical graph parity. At eight pairs, independent states raise target
rule anchor-path use from 3/56 to 24/56 evaluations, but reduce total Candidate
and Term work only 5.1% and 5.4%, with no end-to-end speed gain; rule
enumerations remain unchanged. This confirms topology affects proof-guard
eligibility while demonstrating that current scoped whole-graph matching
dominates cost. Next build and measure sound multi-role dependency indexing
over predecessor lifecycle cases, including index construction, cross-frame
communication, omitted-interface residuals, and exact full-graph parity. Then
integrate that path with the existing thoughtexperiment CoW branch and residual
return harness. ## 2026-10-03 Synthesized-hypothesis active-query gate

The current active-query gate measures a finite version space produced by `domains.generator.synthesize`, not only a host-listed candidate set. Across five source-locked numeric-relation workers, the maximum-entropy selector uses a median of two locally simulated labels versus one for fixed-first and four for seeded-random; all policies identify a survivor that is exact on the disjoint 1,296-case grid and 13-case navigation panel. Maximum entropy has higher selector latency (3.13 ms median) and no advantage over fixed-first on this design. The median synthesis cost is 5.83 s and remains the dominant cost. This is a small, harness-specified relation with 9–10 hypotheses and does not estimate real oracle expense or general learning. Next vary hypothesis ambiguity, model misspecification, and task families while preserving exact source and held-out isolation. See [results](NUMERIC_OPPOSITION_ACTIVE_QUERY_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md), [preregistration](NUMERIC_OPPOSITION_ACTIVE_QUERY_V1_PREREG_20261003.md), [implementation amendment](NUMERIC_OPPOSITION_ACTIVE_QUERY_V1_AMENDMENT_20261003.md), [source lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/numeric_opposition_active_query_v1_lock_20261003.json), and [independent analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/numeric_opposition_active_query_v1_analysis_20261003.json).


## 2026-10-03 Order-balanced active-query replication

The follow-up to numeric active-query v1 corrects its fixed-order comparison: each of five generated 9–10-hypothesis pools is replayed across 30 pre-frozen randomized input orders, pairing max-entropy and sequential selection on the identical order. Maximum entropy uniquely identifies an exact survivor in 150/150 order blocks; sequential randomized order does so in 111/150. Worker-level median savings range from zero to two oracle labels. The selector costs 3.74 ms median versus 0.40 ms sequential, so economic benefit depends on a real oracle's cost and cannot be inferred from these locally generated labels. This supports a bounded useful response to candidate-order balance on one synthetic relation family. Next increase ambiguity, introduce observational aliases and out-of-grammar targets, and replicate across independent task families. ## 2026-10-03 Out-of-grammar active-query checkpoint

Five source-locked additive-conservation panels test the native Term version
space and entropy selector under a target absent from Neg/Eq/And. All 31
synthesized hypotheses are wrong on disjoint fractional holdouts; one panel
has no fit. The current entropy selector emits no query in the four nonempty
panels because at least one candidate fails evaluation at each available
input. Sequential selection can end at a false singleton (3/5 panels). This
is a useful negative capability result and identifies the next engineering
measurement: make candidate evaluation errors explicit prediction outcomes,
then repeat the exact panels before widening to unrelated target relations.
The raw result, protocol, source lock, and analyzer are listed in
[the result report](NUMERIC_OPPOSITION_MODEL_MISSPECIFICATION_V1_RESULTS_20261003.md).

The v1.1 selector-error control confirms explicit exception prediction and
elimination using an injected evaluator failure. Natural generated terms in
the five additive panels did not trigger this path, so this verifies the API
contract rather than field prevalence. The corrected panel still returns false
singletons in 3/5 draws for both policies. Keep those claims separate in later
experiments; prioritize an adequacy criterion and unrelated target relations.

**2026-10-03 model-adequacy gate:** A corrected source-locked audit spans additive and product targets outside the Neg/Eq/And grammar plus an in-grammar opposition control. Challenge queries leave false additive singletons in 2/5 panels, empty product candidates in 5/5, and retain an exact opposition candidate in 5/5. The control uses 16 coverage-directed examples rather than four, so this is not sample-size matched. The next capability step is to evaluate a policy that selects among further querying, grammar widening, and requesting help, with held-out labels hidden from that policy; score correct resolution, false singleton, empty-set, label cost, synthesis work, and wall/CPU time across multiple task families. See [results](NUMERIC_RELATION_MODEL_ADEQUACY_AUDIT_V1_1_RESULTS_20261003.md), [protocol](NUMERIC_RELATION_MODEL_ADEQUACY_AUDIT_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20261003.md), [lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/numeric_relation_model_adequacy_audit_v1_1_lock_20261003.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/numeric_relation_model_adequacy_audit_v1_1_analysis_20261003.json).

**2026-10-03 finite behavior-class return policy replay:** A source-bound secondary analysis applies a class-return rule to the same 25 query panels. With zero-aware probes, all panels end in one finite class; all members are exact on the 6,560-case heldout grid in 25/25, while the current help trigger makes five unnecessary opposition-family requests (6.55 s total measured hint synthesis). Returning the class would replace those hints with 2,560 candidate-probe evaluations, whose latency was not measured. The original nonzero domain is a safety counterexample: five inequality panels appear to be one class but include false candidates on heldout, yielding 5/25 harmful returns. This supports only a coverage-qualified class-return experiment, not universal equivalence or deployment. Next preregister a live comparison with measured class-evaluation cost, a help arm, and broader independent domains; require abstention when probe coverage is inadequate. **2026-10-03 prospective finite-class policy gate:** A fresh 25-panel source-locked comparison passes independent replay. Zero-aware finite-class return yields heldout-safe results in 24/25 panels at 18 total oracle labels; zero-aware query+help is safe in 19/25 at 56 labels; nonzero-only class return is safe in 20/25 and harmful on every inequality panel. The remaining zero-aware inequality case still requests help and returns one exact plus ten false candidates, so help is not a complete ambiguity resolver. Class partitioning costs 81 ms total (2.08 ms median/panel) across 8,448 candidate-probe evaluations; four grammar searches cost 209.3 s aggregate, dominating the run. Five unnecessary opposition hints are avoided relative to query+help, with no rule adoption. This supports a coverage-qualified class-return capability on these authored functions and makes candidate acquisition the measured cost center; it does not establish natural-task efficacy or universal equivalence. Next use independently structured task families and larger probe domains, add help-quality/selection metrics, and integrate class return into an isolated thoughtexperiment branch before any persistent adoption. **2026-10-03 inference evidence reconciliation (supersedes the immediately preceding next-step sentence):** The proposed controlled exact-versus-oracle and BP/topology work is already substantially executed. Current evidence includes (a) 48-worker, 40-check exact MAP comparisons against an independent factor-table oracle at fixed N=120, certified widths q=6–9, and matched grid/sparse q-tree topology; (b) 36-worker node scaling at q=6/9 through N=504 with 56 independent analysis checks; (c) paired binary/ternary inference at q=4–6; (d) runtime-generated native-rule-settled paths/banded graphs through N=256; and (e) 180 LLM-derived bipartite cells with exhaustive conditional-source oracles and exact/BP agreement measured through width 10. Separate two-model transport results replicate the explicit fan-in cost effect. These are strong, source-locked synthetic/derived-graph results, not natural-task prevalence or autonomous cut discovery. The earlier recommendation to create another controlled exact-vs-oracle panel is redundant and is withdrawn.

The next inference gate should sample factor graphs from a preregistered, task-selected corpus of live substrate workloads (including failures and high-ambiguity cases), without filtering on width. Record extraction success/failure, variable/factor/domain definitions, connected components, certified or conservative width with the decomposition method, exact feasibility/cost where oracle-backed, and BP convergence plus exact agreement on the feasible subset. Then separately evaluate whether a frame/partition proposal made without access to exact heldout answers reduces boundary width and preserves task-level decisions. This targets the actual missing link between demonstrated conditional bounded-width tractability and the cheap-cut hypothesis. **2026-10-04 natural-graph ownership audit:** Re-read the retained live conversation harvest and its independent v1.1 analysis. The archive contains ten usable final graphs from five authored prompts, each repeated twice, with 25,036–25,216 nodes and 11,445–11,722 edges. Explicit prompt-linked task ownership is recovered in only two of the five conditions (`scene_description` and `self_report_action`); the other three have no directly linked prompt Goal under the analyzer's conservative rule. Every analyzed graph currently collapses to one frame, so the sample cannot estimate multi-frame cheap-cut prevalence or demonstrate that task frames can be discovered automatically. Treat these graphs as a rehydration and ownership-coverage diagnostic, not as the natural-task transfer benchmark itself. Next establish a blinded, independently reviewed task-to-goal mapping for an expanded task panel; report mapping coverage and disagreement, preserve unmapped nodes as shared, and only then run current-source paired monolithic/fallback/anchor replay with coupled-dependency controls and charged frame-discovery cost.

**2026-10-04 typed anchor-path diagnostic:** A reproducible retrospective analyzer now reports shortest typed paths from each inbound prompt Message to Goal/DiscourseEvent nodes, with and without high-degree intermediate nodes. At cutoff 100, `scene_description` reaches five Goals without a hub, including the intended `describe_scene` Goal through `about → Scene → describes`, but also three `produce_utterance` Goals and a `report_self` Goal. The direct `comprehends` rule selects only `report_self`. The other four prompt conditions each reach their prompt DiscourseEvent but no Goal without a hub; `self_report_action` alone also has a directly comprehended `report_self` Goal. This demonstrates both undercoverage by direct links and false-ownership risk from broad reachability. The paths are candidate evidence only, not ownership labels or task frame discovery. Next compare candidate mapping policies against independently reviewed node-level annotations, including explicit false-positive/abstention accounting, before charging any partitioned execution as a frame-locality result. See [path analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_live_conversation_task_anchor_paths_v1.py) and [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/live_conversation_task_anchor_paths_v1_20261004.json).

The packet is an annotation instrument only: it contains no reviewer labels, has five authored prompts, and includes bounded candidate context rather than the full graph. **2026-10-04 provisional ownership annotation diagnostic:** A single-pass annotation was added with separate labels for request scope and whether the interpreted task aligns with the prompt. On the six non-uncertain Goal candidates, the bounded typed-path policy covers all six request-associated Goals (1.00 precision/recall against these provisional labels), while direct `comprehends` links cover two (1.00 precision, 0.33 recall). For task alignment, the broader path policy includes the misinterpreted `report_self` Goal in the scene-description case (0.83 precision, 1.00 recall); the direct-link policy has 0.50 precision and 0.20 recall. These numbers mainly show why task relevance and task correctness must be scored separately. There are no true-negative Goal labels in this six-item set, the labels and policy design are not independent, and one annotator over five prompts cannot validate the policy. **2026-10-04 distinct-Term class positive control:** A new source-locked five-panel run supplies `ax == -ex`, `-ax == ex`, and a same-sign control. In all five cases, the policy returns exactly the two structurally distinct equivalent Terms after one label and one coverage expansion; an independent analyzer verifies transitions and rescoring across the registered 6,560-case holdout and 3,024 separate balanced wide-range/boundary cases per member. ### Continuous singleton audit and next learning gate (2026-10-04)

On 20 fixed proposals, task-conditioned continuous examples rejected all
seven false acceptances made by the two-label integer policy, accepted the 12
holdout-correct candidates, and requested help on eight panels total. It used
62 labels versus 38 for the integer policy. This does not establish a general
adequacy detector because example generation was informed by the task family
and the audit did not trigger resynthesis. The next gate is to compare generic
domain sampling, Term-directed probe proposals, and abstention on held task
families without a task-informed generator; then feed observed residuals into
resynthesis and measure end-to-end quality, false adoption, and cumulative
compute/query cost. ### Generic continuous singleton audit (2026-10-04)

Task-agnostic uniform sampling from the continuous four-variable box did not
find any of the seven false candidates at 4, 16, or 64 labels per candidate:
all caps leave 12 correct and seven false acceptances plus one no-candidate
help. The cap-64 policy spends 1,216 labels. Task-conditioned probing rejects
all seven false candidates in 62 labels total, but uses task-informed examples.
This quantifies why untargeted sampling is a poor substitute in this fixture;
per-query time is unmeasured. Next add candidate-Term-directed, task-blind probe
proposals and compare on held task variants with abstention, then feed
mismatches back into resynthesis and measure end-to-end gains and cost. See

and account for end-to-end cost and adoption quality. ### Term-directed floating-point edge probes (2026-10-04)

The previously unresolved three-Term pool contains a real finite-precision
false candidate: `ax*ax == ex*ex` agrees with absolute equality on the ordinary
holdout but underflows for `ax=1e-200`, `ex=2e-200`. A task-blind probe slate
constructed from Term variable pairs selects this counterexample with one
oracle label in both search arms, removes the false Term, and returns the two
survivors as one binary behavior class. They have zero mismatches on a separate
4,096-case log-scale/ULP stress holdout; the squared candidate has 520. Policy
construction uses 218–221 native Term evaluations and 1.72–2.09 ms on this
single panel. This is a narrow probe-policy result, not universal equivalence
or generic self-improvement. Next transfer to other operators/domains and
include IEEE edge policies and adversarial class controls. The v2 bitwise-disjoint study passes nine analyzer gates. It reproduces
one-label rejection for the Abs/Times underflow candidate and one-label

structured control falsifies finite-class acceptance: a literal-guard false
candidate agrees on every variable-pair edge probe, is accepted with zero
labels, and has two errors on the 4,096-row holdout. This demonstrates that
finite observed-class agreement is not a safe acceptance guarantee. Next add
Term-literal-directed proposals, compare to edge-only probes on this exact
control, and request help when no query splits a class. ## Clause contradiction and aliasing v1 (2026-10-04)

The twelve-panel extension passes nine independent replay gates. The solver proves three unary conjunctions empty over finite binary64 values: contradictory bounds, no representable float between adjacent endpoints, and a lower bound above the largest finite float. Repeated compatible bounds use one oracle label, reusing a base-slate query. Direct cross-variable aliasing remains unresolved and correctly triggers help while its false candidate survives. In a mixed unsatisfiable-plus-alias disjunction, one base query removes the false candidate, after which the remaining identity can be accepted. The pairwise controls still falsely accept higher-arity intervals, unsupported arithmetic, and unresolved aliases; the clause-aware policy has no holdout false acceptances in this panel. This is a narrow unary-comparison proof fragment, not general Term equivalence. Next test generated formulas and independently check proof classifications across a wider finite-float boundary suite. ## Thoughtexperiment revision/receipt validation v1 (2026-10-04)

A source-locked 16-worker paired panel compares the existing full-digest lifecycle with O(1) graph/rule revision checks and journal receipts at 200k/1m nodes, both snapshot backends, and two replicates per cell. Every worker passes semantic selection, isolation, rule preservation, stale-receipt, quiescence, and exact post-lifecycle branch/primary parity gates; all match an independent monolithic oracle. The fast path removes five full graph exports/digests from the candidate lifecycle. Lifecycle-only median speedup is 28.2×/122.8× (full-copy/shared-pages) at 200k and 33.7×/319.8× at 1m. Including a timed exact branch/primary digest audit lowers this to 2.33×/2.42× and 2.47×/2.50×. Therefore high hot-loop throughput is supported only when revision/journal guarantees carry routine validation and full parity audits run separately; exact audit every batch still shows a measured 2.3–2.5× reduction on this task. This is conditional on tracked semantic writes and complete journal coverage; it remains one sparse synthetic workload, two replicates/cell, and one host. ## 2026-10-04 current-source finite-key closure theorem envelope

The finite-key monotone insertion result is explicitly narrower than weak
acyclicity: positive edge matches; fixed finite literal mint keys;
`add_node_if_absent`; empty-attribute edge insertion; no deletion,
replacement, external state, or rule mutation during closure. Current-source
v1.3 replay passes 25 generated grammar cases (15 admitted native fixed
points with exact independent terminal graphs and bound checks; 10 refused
forms). A separate source-locked scale v1.2 sweep passes 90 cases through
N=256 on cycles and dense directed graphs. For M=4 dense inputs, measured
setup/closure/export medians are 26 ms, 119 ms, and 544 ms at N=64/128/256,
while progress stays at seven firings. The near-4x time increase per N
doubling tracks this synthetic workload's quadratic edge growth; it is not a
uniform wall-time theorem. Next vary rule-body arity, edge-type count, and
interacting positive rule families under the same independent graph oracle,
then test the admission gate against the full runtime syntax. See [grammar
results](SUBSTRATE_FINITE_KEY_GENERATED_GRAMMAR_V1_3_RESULTS_20261004.md) and
[scale results](SUBSTRATE_FINITE_KEY_CLOSURE_SCALE_V1_2_RESULTS_20261004.md).

## 2026-10-04 native per-rule closure counter validation

A source-locked 180-pair audit-off/on replay validates native per-rule candidate, clause, edge, and global counter conservation on the circulant three-rule family. All 360 closures match an independent monotone oracle; paired graph equality, zero audit-off counters, unambiguous semantic rule IDs, no unattributed matcher/Term counts, and rule-order invariance pass. The median paired audit-on/off end-to-end time ratio is 1.104, with noisy one-host timing. This is direct counter evidence for the tested matcher path; it does not prove universal instrumentation coverage. ## 2026-10-05 synthesis-to-query integration gate

A source-locked prospective integration now feeds generated version spaces into the existing disagreement selector on two scalar components of the coupled-quadratic map. Both generated pools contain two training-consistent terms, including one exact held-out term and one shortcut. Across 20 grid permutations per task, maximum entropy selects a distinguishing query and retains the exact program in 20/20 runs for both tasks. Fixed-first uses 1.2/1.3 labels on average and seeded random 1.1/1.2, versus one for entropy. However, entropy takes about 0.32–0.36 ms and evaluates 72 hypothesis/input pairs, while baseline policies take about 0.01 ms and evaluate two pairs. The selector is useful for label efficiency here but not compute efficiency under this cheap oracle. This closes a narrow integration demonstration; query-domain discovery, oracle cost/reliability, graph-resident version-space management, grammar choice, and task-family diversity remain open. The full evidence and limitations are in [v1.1 results](GENERATED_QUADRATIC_QUERY_TRANSFER_V1_1_RESULTS_20261005.md).

**2026-10-05 synthesis-to-query replication v1.2:** The independent analysis now reports timing directly, and a fresh source-locked 120-cell replication passes all eight gates. The result reproduces 20/20 exact survivors per policy/task and the one-label entropy result. Measured entropy decisions are 0.381/0.572 ms median per task against 0.012/0.016 ms fixed-first, with 72 versus two Term evaluations; synthesis is 8.91/13.66 ms. This sharpens the cost conclusion: entropy saves a fraction of an oracle call on the authored permutation set, at materially higher CPU cost. The integration works, but this selection policy is not compute-efficient for the current cheap oracle. See [v1.2 results](GENERATED_QUADRATIC_QUERY_TRANSFER_V1_2_RESULTS_20261005.md) and its [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/generated_quadratic_query_transfer_v1_2_20261005_analysis.json).

## 2026-10-05 finite-key termination extension triage

The source-locked core-seed census contains 209 active-rule instances and 800 effect occurrences: `set_attr` 370, `add_edge` 282, unconditional `add_node` 106, `del_node` 28, `del_edge` 11, and `net_collapse` 3. The core profiles use `set_attr_if_different` zero times. Therefore adding only the existing idempotent `SetAttrIfDifferent` effect to the static checker would not admit any new core rule; it would improve the checker’s proof vocabulary but not address the measured profile-coverage failure. Unconditional node minting and deletion/replacement remain substantive nonmonotone or unbounded behaviors, and 206 rule instances carry fields outside the checker’s `name/match/effects` schema. Counts overlap by rule and are descriptive syntax frequency, not disjoint rejection classes. Evidence is the preserved raw census and per-rule decisions in [core seed admission results](SUBSTRATE_CORE_SEED_PROFILE_ADMISSION_CENSUS_V1_RESULTS_20261005.md) and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/substrate_core_seed_profile_admission_census_v1_analysis_20261005.json).

Do not prioritize a checker-only `SetAttrIfDifferent` extension as a route to core termination coverage. The next termination gate should either (a) identify an actual useful seed profile wholly expressible in a broader formally justified monotone fragment, or (b) define an opt-in restricted operating profile and measure the resulting capability loss, initialization cost, rejected-rule rate, and enforcement coverage at every rule mutation/import/restore boundary. Until a nonempty profile is admitted and enforced, the finite-key result is a conditional theorem for authored experiments, not an engine-wide closure guarantee.

The locked v1.2 census expands profile coverage from the 17 core roots to all 117 current registry IDs. It boots 112 roots (82 nonempty profiles, 30 empty); one root lacks a manifest and four roots have a missing `core.json` dependency, all retained explicitly. None of 1,803 active-rule instances passes the current finite-key checker, and no nonempty profile passes. The independent predicate agrees on every decision; seven integrity checks pass. This does not imply the rejected programs diverge. Next author an explicit, useful, finite-key profile and measure its task behavior and coverage against a matched unrestricted baseline; then enforce profile membership on rule insertion, patch, seed load, restore, and self-mint paths. ## 2026-10-05 authored finite-key operating profile

To test whether the proven fragment can host a useful behavior at all, an explicit two-rule profile derives transitive `reachable` edges from `link`. Its complete rule set passes the finite-key checker; an unconditional fresh-node negative control is refused. Across 36 locked path/tree/four-layer-DAG cases at N=8–64, all closures reach fixed point within the profile's progress bound, and the materialized relation matches both independent DFS and native `ReachableFrom` outputs exactly. At N=64, path closure costs 40.45 ms for 2,016 pairs versus 0.836 ms for one `ReachableFrom` query per source; the binary-tree and layered DAG cases also make materialization more expensive for one all-source sweep. Thus the fragment supports a useful bounded relation-derivation task, but this form is not a single-query speedup; repeated downstream reuse and break-even remain unmeasured. This authored profile is not a registered boot mode and has no universal runtime admission enforcement. Next retain it as the positive workload for a profile enforcement gate, then measure downstream reuse against repeated direct queries. See [results](FINITE_KEY_REACHABILITY_PROFILE_V1_RESULTS_20261005.md), [protocol](FINITE_KEY_REACHABILITY_PROFILE_V1_PREREG_20261005.md), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/finite_key_reachability_profile_v1_20261005.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/finite_key_reachability_profile_v1_analysis_20261005.json).

## 2026-10-05 authored finite-key profile reuse result

The v1.1 preregistered reuse sweep completes 36 locked cases, each with Q=1,2,4,8 batches querying every source. Independent DFS confirms exact direct and materialized results throughout; all fixed points meet the finite progress bound, and all nine analysis gates pass. End-to-end materialization is below the direct-query total only in binary-tree N=64 at Q=8 (3.224 ms vs 4.198 ms median; 0.77× profile/direct). The other 11 topology/size cells remain slower through Q=8; the N=64 path is 7.29× slower at Q=8. This is a narrow candidate crossover with short, potentially noisy timings, not a general performance claim. The positive signal is that reuse can repay setup on one tested shape; the open gap is whether this survives independent workloads and larger sizes, and how often such reuse arises naturally. Next preregister a held-out topology/size replication and a query-count sweep extending beyond eight batches only for cells with an observed near-crossover, while retaining matched semantic checks and full cost accounting. See [v1.1 results](FINITE_KEY_REACHABILITY_PROFILE_V1_1_RESULTS_20261005.md), [protocol](FINITE_KEY_REACHABILITY_PROFILE_V1_1_PREREG_20261005.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/finite_key_reachability_profile_v1_1.py), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/finite_key_reachability_profile_v1_1_analysis_20261005.json).

## 2026-10-05 authored finite-key profile crossover replication

The v1.2 locked timing replication passes all nine semantic and integrity gates over 60 cases, 15 fresh substrates per tree topology/size cell, and alternating direct/materialized timing order. It does not reproduce the v1.1 crossover: binary-tree N=64, Q=8 has median paired ratio 1.37 and only 1/15 favorable repetitions. No cell meets the preregistered rule of ratio below one and at least 12/15 wins. Binary-tree N=128 and ternary-tree N=128 approach parity at Q=32 (ratios 0.992 and 0.990), but each favors materialization in only 8/15 repetitions. Treat the original apparent crossover as noise or an unstable local result. The remaining hypothesis is that larger reuse counts may repay setup; measure Q=64,128,256 with more paired repetitions on the N=128 near-parity cells before making that claim. ## 2026-10-05 high-reuse finite-key profile follow-up

The v1.3 locked follow-up passes all nine gates on 60 cases: two N=128 tree shapes, 30 paired repetitions each, and Q=32–256 all-source batches. No cell meets the preregistered robust-crossover criterion (median paired ratio below one and at least 24/30 repetitions favoring the profile). At Q=256, binary-tree medians are 184.348 ms direct versus 175.990 ms profile (paired ratio 0.941; 23/30 favorable); ternary-tree medians are 174.837 versus 170.350 ms (0.955; 20/30). Next inspect current task routes for repeated derived-relation queries, then preregister a representative live-task test that measures relation construction/maintenance, repeated consumers, semantic parity, and the direct-query baseline. ## 2026-10-05 rule-path cache versus explicit reachability materialization

A source audit found the existing experimental `ReachableFrom` same-graph cache, which shares results inside native rule execution but is not used by direct `PySubstrate.evaluate()` calls (each direct call creates a fresh EvalCache). This means the earlier materialization timing compared against an uncached host-query route; it did not compare with the strongest existing rule-engine optimization. The corrected v1.2 three-arm replay passes ten checks over 60 cases. Repeated no-op rule consumers match DFS; the cache produces exactly N−1 misses and (N−1)(R−1) hits due the matcher’s injective-binding exclusion of the root self-pair. At R=16, cache-on reduces end-to-end total 9–35% versus cache-off; explicit materialization is 1.28–1.54× slower than cache-on in all cells. At R=1 the cache can add overhead, consistent with no repeated key. Thus materialization does not beat the current opt-in memoization for this rule workload, though the profile result remains relevant to host queries that cannot share the cache. Existing browser-profile v1.3 measurements also show 7.46–12.81× quieter tick improvements at N=128 on synthetic DOM-shaped tasks. Next audit repeated-key incidence and cache telemetry over independently authored active task routes, while retaining the distinction between synthetic profile gains and natural prevalence. Preserve v1/v1.1 failed analysis artifacts with the v1.2 correction record. See [comparison results](REACHABILITY_CACHE_MATERIALIZATION_COMPARISON_V1_2_RESULTS_20261005.md), [amendment](REACHABILITY_CACHE_MATERIALIZATION_COMPARISON_V1_2_AMENDMENT_20261005.md), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/reachability_cache_materialization_comparison_v1_2_20261005.json), [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/reachability_cache_materialization_comparison_v1_2_analysis_20261005.json), and [browser-profile cache v1.3](SUBSTRATE_BROWSER_PROFILE_REACHABLE_CACHE_V1_3_RESULTS_20260928.md).

It finds two typed `ReachableFrom` Terms, both in the two-rule `browser_affordance_reach` family; three Python literal references; and five helper calls (three `grounding_reach`, one `flag_ungrounded_confident`, one `seed_dependency_closure`). Direct `PySubstrate.evaluate()` still constructs a fresh default cache, and the high-level wrapper still exposes no cache toggle. The existing browser-profile cache factorial remains synthetic DOM-shaped, not a live page. Therefore the next gate is to instrument an actual BrowserWorld session across stable and changing graph phases and compare cached/uncached semantics, hit/miss volume, payload, and tick cost; broaden to other routes if current typed-consumer inventory changes. ## 2026-10-05 frame-boundary size reanalysis

A deterministic reanalysis of the 78 typed interaction snapshots reconstructs 6,363 annotated frames and independently matches every labeled-node and edge-occurrence count. Bigville dynamic-link frames have size five and median two distinct external graph-node neighbors (p90 three, maximum 100), with median five unassigned-endpoint incidences per frame. Connected-conversation frames have size nine, median four shared-membership nodes, and 27 distinct external neighbors (p90 47); discourse frames have size 11, median four shared nodes, and 19 external neighbors (p90 25). These runtime-labeled boundaries do not support a blanket “small separator” assumption for the selected conversation/discourse graphs. However, they are only graph-node adjacency, not factor scopes or task-relevant interfaces, and the three families are selected/generated rather than a natural prevalence sample. Advance the gate by projecting actual typed rule/factor scopes and runtime read/write channels onto these boundaries, including all unassigned nodes; do not infer treewidth or exact-inference cost from these counts. See [post-hoc results](SUBSTRATE_TASK_FRAME_BOUNDARY_SIZES_POSTHOC_V1_RESULTS_20261005.md), [script](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/posthoc_task_frame_boundary_sizes_v1.py), and [machine output](../../../evaluation/reports/task_frame_boundary_sizes_posthoc_v1_20261005.json).

## 2026-10-05 GenInfer scope-index lifecycle confirmatory

The amended 36-worker full-Substrate evaluation separates traced work attribution from untraced closure timing. GenInfer scope indexing removes population visits (76/4,076/40,076 to zero at 0/1k/10k unrelated codebook decoys) while preserving four parsed parts, 9,600 search candidates, exact outputs, and branch/restore parity. Closure medians remain effectively equal between scan and indexed arms at all sizes, so the local operation-count reduction has not produced a demonstrated end-to-end speedup. Index build/rebuild reaches about 0.5/1.0 ms at 10k; graph restore itself is around 69 ms. Scope IDs and decoys are harness-authored, the work family is one synthetic 2-D linear route, and only three untraced replicates per cell were run. Keep index admission opt-in; the post-hoc helper attribution shows ShapeDecode, TransformDecode, and DimInfer retain 75% of measured population visits, and candidate-loop counts are unchanged. Next establish whether those helpers receive valid frame provenance, then test scoped lookup and candidate-loop cost on representative codebooks with exact parity. See [amendment](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_SCOPE_INDEX_LIFECYCLE_V1_1_AMENDMENT_20261005.md), [results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_SCOPE_INDEX_LIFECYCLE_V1_1_RESULTS_20261005.md), [source lock](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/geninfer_scope_index_lifecycle_v1_1_lock_20261005.json), [raw capture](../../../evaluation/reports/geninfer_scope_index_lifecycle_v1_1_20261005.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/geninfer_scope_index_lifecycle_v1_1_analysis_20261005.json).

## 2026-10-06 higher-dimensional GenInfer solver feasibility

The current native GenInfer enumerates only 2×2 integer maps and skips other coordinate dimensions. A standalone exact-rational prototype recovers full-rank 1-D, 2-D, and 3-D maps, verifies every training point, transfers to held-out points, and abstains on rank-deficient controls. At the authored 3-D data bound B=4, the existing exhaustive formula implies 387,420,488 matrix candidates. The independent analyzer passes exact-output, rank-control, formula, and source-hash checks. This establishes only that an exact full-rank solver route is implementable; it is not native substrate capability or natural workload evidence. Next integrate an opt-in native path, preserve current 2-D selection semantics, require integrality/full-data checks, and report abstention for underdetermined cases pending a separate prior/search strategy. See [results](GENINFER_FULL_RANK_MATRIX_SOLVER_FEASIBILITY_V1_RESULTS_20261006.md), [protocol](GENINFER_FULL_RANK_MATRIX_SOLVER_FEASIBILITY_V1_PREREG_20261006.md), [runner](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/geninfer_full_rank_matrix_solver_feasibility_v1.py), [analyzer](../../../evaluation/substrate_capability/analyze_geninfer_full_rank_matrix_solver_feasibility_v1.py), [capture](../../../evaluation/reports/geninfer_full_rank_matrix_solver_feasibility_v1_20261006.json), and [analysis](../../../evaluation/reports/geninfer_full_rank_matrix_solver_feasibility_v1_analysis_20261006.json).

The corrected native full-rank path passes its prospectively locked 96-worker replication: three repetitions each for 1-D, existing 2-D, three distinct 3-D integer matrices, and rank-deficient, nonlinear, and ambiguous-ID controls, with audit on/off and both source-matched builds. ## 2026-10-06 exact-linear prefilter implementation checkpoint

The v1 prefilter is now implemented behind both the preregistered Cargo feature
and a separate `agent.gen_linear_exact_enabled` runtime field, defaulting off.
On eligible 2-D frames it hashes typed predicate-plus-id keys, uses a linear
scan to find two independent source displacements, solves the bounded integer
map with checked arithmetic, and verifies all aligned rows. Ambiguous keys,
rank deficiency, unsupported values, and arithmetic uncertainty fall back to
the historical enumerator. Three feature-gated Rust tests pass, including all
625 integer 2x2 matrices with entries in [-2,2] on a full-rank corpus; these
test exact-map recovery, not full native GenInfer parity. Default and feature-on
library checks pass. The prefilter has not yet received proof/fallback audit
counters, matched native binaries, a locked runtime panel, or the high-bound
stress capture, so it has no admitted speedup claim. Next complete those
observability and source-lock pieces, run the frozen differential and native
panels, then update the capability assessment from their results. See the
[implementation status](SUBSTRATE_NONLINEAR_DIMENSION_INDUCTION_V2_IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS_20261006.md)
and [prefilter preregistration](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_EXACT_LINEAR_PREFILTER_V1_PREREG_20261006.md).

**2026-10-06 GenInfer exact-linear prefilter v1:** The locked three-build,
480-worker panel completed with zero failures and passed all 15 independent
integrity and semantic gates. Audit-on/off and quadratic/prefilter projections
matched, held-out rows matched the oracle, and the prefilter had no false
quadratic mints. It recorded 30 exact solves, 220 proven no-fits, and 30
conservative fallbacks across 80 audited workers. Median clean closure fell
from 78 ms to 2.5 ms on the linear positive and from seconds to low
milliseconds on several conditions; rank-deficient closure remained expensive
(111 s baseline, 70 s prefilter). The gains primarily reflect sound early
no-fit proofs, not general nonlinear learning. Natural-task prevalence and
rung-three tractability remain unmeasured. See [v1 results](SUBSTRATE_GENINFER_EXACT_LINEAR_PREFILTER_V1_RESULTS_20261006.md),
[locked capture](../../../evaluation/reports/geninfer_exact_linear_prefilter_v1_raw_20261006.json),
